  FROM shipment_base sb2
  GROUP BY sb2.tenant_id, sb2.carrier
)
SELECT
  st.tenant_name AS tenant_name,
  st.performance_group AS performance_group,
  tcc.carrier AS carrier,
  tcc.shipments_count AS shipments_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * tcc.shipments_count / tt.total_shipments, 1) AS share_of_tenant_shipments_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ts.avg_transit_days, 0), 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ts.pct_within_3_days, 0), 1) AS pct_within_3_days
FROM tenant_carrier_counts tcc
JOIN selected_tenants st ON st.tenant_id = tcc.tenant_id
JOIN tenant_totals tt ON tt.tenant_id = tcc.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN transit_stats ts ON ts.tenant_id = tcc.tenant_id AND ts.carrier = tcc.carrier
ORDER BY
  CASE st.performance_group WHEN 'worst' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
  st.tenant_name ASC,
  tcc.shipments_count DESC,
  tcc.carrier ASC
builds_on: Fulfillment performance by warehouse, 2025
Delivery time by merchant, 2025
entries.engineer_note: avg_transit_days and pct_within_3_days are computed over the delivered subset only (shipments with a non-null delivered_at), as specified; tenants/carriers with zero delivered shipments show 0 for both rather than null. share_of_tenant_shipments_pct uses each tenant's total 2025 shipment count (all carriers) as the denominator.

entries.title: Purchase order replenishment performance by supplier, 2025
entries.question: Which suppliers are chronically slow to deliver against purchase orders, relative to what they've promised?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  s.name AS supplier_name,
  s.lead_time_days AS lead_time_days_contracted,
  agg.pos_ordered,
  agg.pos_received,
  ROUND(agg.avg_actual_lead_days, 1) AS avg_actual_lead_days,
  ROUND(agg.pct_received_late, 1) AS pct_received_late,
  ROUND(agg.avg_days_late, 1) AS avg_days_late
FROM suppliers s
JOIN (
  SELECT
    po.supplier_id,
    COUNT(*) AS pos_ordered,
    COUNT(po.received_at) AS pos_received,
    AVG(CASE WHEN po.received_at IS NOT NULL THEN (po.received_at::date - po.ordered_at::date) END) AS avg_actual_lead_days,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN po.expected_at IS NOT NULL AND po.received_at IS NOT NULL AND po.received_at > po.expected_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
      / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN po.expected_at IS NOT NULL AND po.received_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS pct_received_late,
    AVG(CASE WHEN po.expected_at IS NOT NULL AND po.received_at IS NOT NULL AND po.received_at > po.expected_at
             THEN (po.received_at::date - po.expected_at::date) END) AS avg_days_late
  FROM purchase_orders po
  WHERE po.ordered_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND po.ordered_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY po.supplier_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
) agg ON agg.supplier_id = s.id
ORDER BY agg.pos_ordered DESC, s.name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: pct_received_late and avg_days_late are computed only over POs that have both expected_at and received_at populated (per the request's definition); POs missing either timestamp are excluded from those two measures but still count toward pos_ordered/pos_received.

entries.title: Purchase order replenishment performance by quarter, 2025
entries.question: Did supplier replenishment slow down or back up around peak season, and did it clear by year-end?
entries.sql:
WITH po_quarters AS (
  SELECT
    po.id,
    po.status,
    po.ordered_at,
    po.expected_at,
    po.received_at,
    cd.quarter_num
  FROM purchase_orders po
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(po.ordered_at AS date)
  WHERE po.ordered_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND po.ordered_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
received_lead AS (
  SELECT quarter_num,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (received_at - ordered_at)) / 86400.0 AS lead_days
  FROM po_quarters
  WHERE received_at IS NOT NULL
),
late_subset AS (
  SELECT quarter_num,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (received_at - expected_at)) / 86400.0 AS days_late
  FROM po_quarters
  WHERE received_at IS NOT NULL AND expected_at IS NOT NULL AND received_at > expected_at
),
both_dates AS (
  SELECT quarter_num
  FROM po_quarters
  WHERE received_at IS NOT NULL AND expected_at IS NOT NULL
),
quarter_summary AS (
  SELECT
    quarter_num,
    COUNT(*) AS pos_ordered,
    COUNT(received_at) AS pos_received,
    SUM(CASE WHEN status IN ('submitted','partially_received') AND received_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pos_still_open_at_cutoff
  FROM po_quarters
  GROUP BY quarter_num
),
lead_summary AS (
  SELECT quarter_num, AVG(lead_days) AS avg_actual_lead_days
  FROM received_lead
  GROUP BY quarter_num
),
late_summary AS (
  SELECT quarter_num, AVG(days_late) AS avg_days_late, COUNT(*) AS late_count
  FROM late_subset
  GROUP BY quarter_num
),
both_summary AS (
  SELECT quarter_num, COUNT(*) AS both_count
  FROM both_dates
  GROUP BY quarter_num
)
SELECT
  '2025-Q' || qs.quarter_num AS quarter,
  qs.pos_ordered,
  qs.pos_received,
  ROUND(CAST(ls.avg_actual_lead_days AS numeric), 1) AS avg_actual_lead_days,
  ROUND(CAST((COALESCE(lt.late_count,0)::numeric / NULLIF(bd.both_count,0)) * 100 AS numeric), 1) AS pct_received_late,
  ROUND(CAST(lt.avg_days_late AS numeric), 1) AS avg_days_late,
  qs.pos_still_open_at_cutoff
FROM quarter_summary qs
LEFT JOIN lead_summary ls ON ls.quarter_num = qs.quarter_num
LEFT JOIN late_summary lt ON lt.quarter_num = qs.quarter_num
LEFT JOIN both_summary bd ON bd.quarter_num = qs.quarter_num
ORDER BY qs.quarter_num
entries.engineer_note: pos_still_open_at_cutoff for Q4 (and especially POs placed in December) will be inflated by right-censoring: there simply hasn't been enough elapsed time before the 2025-12-31 cutoff for those POs to be received, independent of any real backlog. Read Q4 alongside Q1-Q3 as a baseline rather than as a standalone signal of slowdown.

entries.title: Current stockout exposure by warehouse, as of 2025-12-31
entries.question: As of now, how exposed are our fulfillment sites to stockouts, and how many SKUs are already at or below their reorder point?
entries.sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT
    t4.warehouse_id AS warehouse_id,
    t4.variant_id AS variant_id,
    SUM(t4.quantity) AS total_quantity,
    SUM(t4.reserved_quantity) AS total_reserved_quantity,
    SUM(t4.reorder_point) AS total_reorder_point
  FROM (
    SELECT
      si.variant_id AS variant_id,
      sl.warehouse_id AS warehouse_id,
      si.quantity AS quantity,
      si.reserved_quantity AS reserved_quantity,
      si.reorder_point AS reorder_point
    FROM stock_items si
    JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = si.stock_location_id
  ) t4
  GROUP BY t4.warehouse_id, t4.variant_id
)
SELECT
  w0.name AS warehouse_name,
  t9.name AS tenant_name,
  t1.variants_tracked AS variants_tracked,
  COALESCE(t2.variants_out_of_stock, 0) AS variants_out_of_stock,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t2.variants_out_of_stock, 0) / t1.variants_tracked, 1) AS pct_out_of_stock,
  COALESCE(t3.variants_at_or_below_reorder_point, 0) AS variants_at_or_below_reorder_point,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t3.variants_at_or_below_reorder_point, 0) / t1.variants_tracked, 1) AS pct_at_or_below_reorder
FROM warehouses w0
JOIN tenants t9 ON t9.id = w0.tenant_id
JOIN (
  SELECT warehouse_id, COUNT(DISTINCT variant_id) AS variants_tracked
  FROM t0
  GROUP BY warehouse_id
) t1 ON t1.warehouse_id = w0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT warehouse_id, COUNT(*) AS variants_out_of_stock
  FROM t0
  WHERE (total_quantity - total_reserved_quantity) <= 0
  GROUP BY warehouse_id
) t2 ON t2.warehouse_id = w0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT warehouse_id, COUNT(*) AS variants_at_or_below_reorder_point
  FROM t0
  WHERE total_reorder_point IS NOT NULL AND total_quantity <= total_reorder_point
  GROUP BY warehouse_id
) t3 ON t3.warehouse_id = w0.id
WHERE t1.variants_tracked >= 20
ORDER BY pct_out_of_stock DESC, warehouse_name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: This is a point-in-time snapshot of current stock_items (as replicated, effectively as of 2025-12-31), not a trend over the year, since there is no reliable historical stockout event log. For variants held at multiple locations within a warehouse, quantity, reserved_quantity and reorder_point were all summed to one on-hand figure and one reorder threshold per variant-warehouse before applying the out-of-stock and reorder-point tests.

entries.title: Support response & resolution time trend, monthly
entries.question: Is first-response and resolution speed on support tickets getting better or worse over time?
entries.sql:
WITH month_dim AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT cd.month_start AS month_start, cd.month_label AS month_label
  FROM calendar_days cd
  WHERE cd.calendar_date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND cd.calendar_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
),
t0 AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS tickets_created
  FROM tickets tk
  WHERE tk.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND tk.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS tickets_with_first_response,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.first_response_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_first_response_hours,
         PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.first_response_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS median_first_response_hours
  FROM tickets tk
  WHERE tk.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND tk.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND tk.first_response_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS tickets_resolved,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_resolution_hours,
         PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS median_resolution_hours
  FROM tickets tk
  WHERE tk.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND tk.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND tk.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(DISTINCT tk.id) AS tickets_with_breach
  FROM tickets tk
  JOIN sla_breaches sb ON sb.ticket_id = tk.id
  WHERE tk.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND tk.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tk.created_at)::date
)
SELECT
  md.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(t0.tickets_created, 0) AS tickets_created,
  COALESCE(t1.tickets_with_first_response, 0) AS tickets_with_first_response,
  ROUND(t1.avg_first_response_hours::numeric, 1) AS avg_first_response_hours,
  ROUND(t1.median_first_response_hours::numeric, 1) AS median_first_response_hours,
  COALESCE(t2.tickets_resolved, 0) AS tickets_resolved,
  ROUND(t2.avg_resolution_hours::numeric, 1) AS avg_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(t2.median_resolution_hours::numeric, 1) AS median_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t3.tickets_with_breach, 0) / NULLIF(t0.tickets_created, 0), 1) AS sla_breach_rate_pct
FROM month_dim md
LEFT JOIN t0 ON t0.month_start = md.month_start
LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.month_start = md.month_start
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.month_start = md.month_start
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.month_start = md.month_start
ORDER BY md.month_start ASC
entries.engineer_note: Report covers all 36 months in the window (2023-01 through 2025-12), one row per month, platform-wide across tenants as requested. As flagged in the request: the last 1-2 months (Nov/Dec 2025) will understate avg/median response and resolution hours because tickets still open at month-end aren't yet counted as resolved/responded-to (right-censoring) - read that tail with caution. SLA breach rate = distinct tickets created that month with >=1 row in sla_breaches, divided by tickets created that month.

entries.title: Response & resolution times by merchant, 2025
entries.question: How much does support speed vary across merchants, and who is fastest/slowest?
entries.sql:
SELECT 
  t_tenant.name AS merchant_name,
  t_counts.tickets_created AS tickets_created,
  ROUND(CAST(t_fr.avg_first_response_hours AS numeric), 2) AS avg_first_response_hours,
  ROUND(CAST(t_fr.median_first_response_hours AS numeric), 2) AS median_first_response_hours,
  ROUND(CAST(t_res.avg_resolution_hours AS numeric), 2) AS avg_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(CAST(t_res.median_resolution_hours AS numeric), 2) AS median_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(t_breach.breached_tickets, 0) AS numeric) / CAST(t_counts.tickets_created AS numeric) * 100.0, 2) AS sla_breach_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS tickets_created
  FROM tickets t0
  WHERE t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t0.tenant_id
) t_counts
JOIN tenants t_tenant
  ON t_tenant.id = t_counts.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.first_response_at - t0.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_first_response_hours,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.first_response_at - t0.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS median_first_response_hours
  FROM tickets t0
  WHERE t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t0.first_response_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t0.tenant_id
) t_fr
  ON t_fr.tenant_id = t_counts.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.resolved_at - t0.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_resolution_hours,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.resolved_at - t0.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS median_resolution_hours
  FROM tickets t0
  WHERE t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t0.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t0.tenant_id
) t_res
  ON t_res.tenant_id = t_counts.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t0.id) AS breached_tickets
  FROM tickets t0
  JOIN sla_breaches t1 ON t1.ticket_id = t0.id
  WHERE t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t0.tenant_id
) t_breach
  ON t_breach.tenant_id = t_counts.tenant_id
WHERE t_counts.tickets_created >= 20
ORDER BY t_counts.tickets_created DESC, t_tenant.name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Support response & resolution time trend, monthly
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant for tickets created in 2025, filtered to tenants with >=20 such tickets, ordered by ticket volume descending (tie-break merchant name); capped at 50 rows per house standard. The printed report's row-count footer will show how many tenants met the >=20 threshold in total versus the 50 shown.

entries.title: Ticket topic mix and recent shift
entries.question: What kinds of problems are shoppers contacting merchants about most, and has that mix shifted in the last 6 months versus the prior 6?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  stn.name AS tag_name,
  COALESCE(a.cnt,0) AS tickets_last_6mo,
  COALESCE(b.cnt,0) AS tickets_prior_6mo,
  ROUND(COALESCE(a.cnt,0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(totals.total_a,0), 1) AS share_last_6mo_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(b.cnt,0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(totals.total_b,0), 1) AS share_prior_6mo_pct,
  ROUND(
    COALESCE(a.cnt,0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(totals.total_a,0)
    - COALESCE(b.cnt,0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(totals.total_b,0)
  , 1) AS share_change_pp,
  ROUND(a.avg_res_hours, 1) AS avg_resolution_hours_last_6mo
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT name FROM support_tags) stn
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT st.name AS name, COUNT(*) AS cnt,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0) AS avg_res_hours
  FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
  JOIN tickets t ON t.id = ttm.ticket_id
  JOIN support_tags st ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-07-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY st.name
) a ON a.name = stn.name
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT st.name AS name, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
  JOIN tickets t ON t.id = ttm.ticket_id
  JOIN support_tags st ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY st.name
) b ON b.name = stn.name
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ticket_tags_map ttm JOIN tickets t ON t.id = ttm.ticket_id
       WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-07-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') AS total_a,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ticket_tags_map ttm JOIN tickets t ON t.id = ttm.ticket_id
       WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2025-07-01') AS total_b
) totals
WHERE COALESCE(a.cnt,0) > 0 OR COALESCE(b.cnt,0) > 0
ORDER BY tickets_last_6mo DESC, tag_name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Grouped by support_tags.name across all tenants (tag names are only unique per tenant, so two merchants' same-named tag are merged into one row, per the request's "platform-level theme" framing). Each ticket counts once per tag it carries, so tag counts don't sum to total ticket volume; shares are of tagged ticket-tag rows, not of tickets. Periods use created_at >= start and < next-day-after-end to include the full inclusive date ranges.

entries.title: Delivery-related vs other tickets: volume and resolution speed
entries.question: Are delivery/where-is-my-order tickets driving the recent growth in ticket volume and the slower/more volatile resolution times seen in the monthly trend?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  strftime(date_trunc('month', x.created_at), '%Y-%m') AS month,
  count(*) AS tickets_total,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE x.is_delivery) AS tickets_delivery_related,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE x.is_delivery) / count(*), 1) AS delivery_share_pct,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (x.first_response_at - x.created_at))/3600) FILTER (WHERE x.is_delivery AND x.first_response_at IS NOT NULL)::numeric, 1) AS avg_first_response_hours_delivery,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (x.first_response_at - x.created_at))/3600) FILTER (WHERE NOT x.is_delivery AND x.first_response_at IS NOT NULL)::numeric, 1) AS avg_first_response_hours_other,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (x.resolved_at - x.created_at))/3600) FILTER (WHERE x.is_delivery AND x.resolved_at IS NOT NULL)::numeric, 1) AS avg_resolution_hours_delivery,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (x.resolved_at - x.created_at))/3600) FILTER (WHERE NOT x.is_delivery AND x.resolved_at IS NOT NULL)::numeric, 1) AS avg_resolution_hours_other
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.id,
    t.tenant_id,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    t.resolved_at,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
      JOIN support_tags st ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id AND st.tenant_id = ttm.tenant_id
      WHERE ttm.ticket_id = t.id
        AND ttm.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
        AND lower(st.name) IN ('delivery', 'where-is-my-order')
    ) AS is_delivery
  FROM tickets t
  WHERE t.created_at >= timestamp '2024-07-01'
    AND t.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
) x
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', x.created_at)
ORDER BY date_trunc('month', x.created_at)
builds_on: Support response & resolution time trend, monthly
Ticket topic mix and recent shift
entries.engineer_note: A ticket is classified delivery-related if any of its tags (via ticket_tags_map/support_tags) case-insensitively matches 'delivery' or 'where-is-my-order', computed once per ticket via EXISTS. Window is tickets.created_at in [2024-07-01, 2026-01-01), i.e. the 18 months Jul-2024 through Dec-2025, as requested.

entries.title: Ticket spike in May-June 2025: which merchants drove it
entries.question: Was the May-June 2025 jump in ticket volume and resolution time concentrated in a few merchants, or broad-based across the platform?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  tn.name AS merchant_name,
  a.mayjun_count AS tickets_created_may_jun_2025,
  ROUND(a.other_count / 10.0, 2) AS avg_monthly_tickets_other_2025,
  CASE WHEN a.other_count = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND( (a.mayjun_count/2.0) / (a.other_count/10.0), 2)
  END AS spike_ratio,
  CASE WHEN a.mayjun_count = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(d.delivery_count,0) / a.mayjun_count, 1)
  END AS delivery_tag_share_pct
FROM (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') AS total_2025,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-05-01' AND created_at < DATE '2025-07-01') AS mayjun_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
                      AND NOT (created_at >= DATE '2025-05-01' AND created_at < DATE '2025-07-01')) AS other_count
  FROM tickets
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) a
JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = a.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) AS delivery_count
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN ticket_tags_map ttm ON ttm.ticket_id = t.id
  JOIN support_tags st ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-05-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
    AND LOWER(st.name) IN ('delivery', 'where-is-my-order')
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
) d ON d.tenant_id = a.tenant_id
WHERE a.total_2025 >= 5
ORDER BY a.mayjun_count DESC, tn.name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Support response & resolution time trend, monthly
entries.engineer_note: Capped at 50 rows per house standard; please add a footer noting the total qualifying-tenant count (query does not compute it separately since that would require a second pass). Spike ratio and delivery-tag share are NULL where the denominator is zero, as requested.

entries.title: Returns and refunds: volume and time-to-resolve trend
entries.question: How often do shoppers end up requesting a return/refund, and how long does that process take to resolve, and is it changing over time?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(om.month, rm.month) AS month,
  om.orders_placed,
  rm.returns_requested,
  CASE WHEN om.orders_placed > 0 THEN ROUND(rm.returns_requested * 100.0 / om.orders_placed, 1) ELSE NULL END AS return_rate_pct,
  rm.returns_refunded,
  rm.avg_days_requested_to_refunded,
  rm.median_days_requested_to_refunded,
  CASE WHEN rm.returns_requested > 0 THEN ROUND(rm.returns_rejected * 100.0 / rm.returns_requested, 1) ELSE NULL END AS returns_rejected_pct
FROM
  (SELECT strftime(date_trunc('month', placed_at), '%Y-%m') AS month, count(*) AS orders_placed
   FROM orders
   WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
   GROUP BY 1) om
FULL OUTER JOIN
  (SELECT strftime(date_trunc('month', requested_at), '%Y-%m') AS month,
          count(*) AS returns_requested,
          count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'refunded') AS returns_refunded,
          count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'rejected') AS returns_rejected,
          ROUND(AVG(extract(epoch from (refunded_at - requested_at))/86400) FILTER (WHERE status = 'refunded' AND refunded_at IS NOT NULL), 1) AS avg_days_requested_to_refunded,
          ROUND(CAST(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch from (refunded_at - requested_at))/86400) FILTER (WHERE status = 'refunded' AND refunded_at IS NOT NULL) AS numeric), 1) AS median_days_requested_to_refunded
   FROM order_returns
   WHERE requested_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND requested_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
   GROUP BY 1) rm
ON om.month = rm.month
ORDER BY COALESCE(om.month, rm.month)
entries.engineer_note: Return rate is an approximation (returns requested in month M / orders placed in month M), since a return in month M may relate to an order placed in an earlier month, as noted in the request. Orders-placed and returns-side columns are grained on their own respective timestamp (placed_at vs requested_at) per the brief, and the two series are combined via a full outer join on month so no month is dropped if one side has zero activity.

entries.title: Delivery performance: Studio Vrij vs platform, 2025
entries.question: Did Studio Vrij's actual shipping/delivery performance deteriorate in May-June 2025, explaining the spike in their delivery-related support tickets, or was it a support-side issue only?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  strftime(o.placed_at, '%Y-%m') as month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.tenant_id = sv.id THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as sv_shipments_delivered,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.tenant_id = sv.id THEN extract(epoch from (s.delivered_at - o.placed_at))/86400 END)::numeric,1) as sv_avg_days_placed_to_delivered,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.tenant_id = sv.id AND extract(epoch from (s.delivered_at - o.placed_at))/86400 > 7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN s.tenant_id = sv.id THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0), 1) as sv_pct_over_7_days,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.tenant_id <> sv.id THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as platform_shipments_delivered,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.tenant_id <> sv.id THEN extract(epoch from (s.delivered_at - o.placed_at))/86400 END)::numeric,1) as platform_avg_days_placed_to_delivered,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.tenant_id <> sv.id AND extract(epoch from (s.delivered_at - o.placed_at))/86400 > 7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN s.tenant_id <> sv.id THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0), 1) as platform_pct_over_7_days
FROM shipments s
JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id AND f.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id AND o.tenant_id = f.tenant_id
CROSS JOIN (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Studio Vrij') sv
WHERE s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
  AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
builds_on: Ticket spike in May-June 2025: which merchants drove it
Delivery-related vs other tickets: volume and resolution speed
entries.engineer_note: Note for the analyst: Oct-Dec 2025 (and to a lesser extent Sep) cohorts are right-censored — orders placed late in the year may not yet have a recorded delivered_at, since the warehouse only holds data through 2025-12-31, so those months' avg-days and %-over-7-days will understate true delivery times until later shipments complete.

entries.title: Returns and refunds experience by merchant, 2025
entries.question: Does the returns/refund experience vary a lot across merchants, and does any merchant stand out as a problem spot the way Studio Vrij did on support tickets?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name as merchant_name,
  ord.orders_placed,
  ret.returns_requested,
  round(100.0 * ret.returns_requested / ord.orders_placed, 1) as return_rate_pct,
  rf.avg_days,
  rf.median_days,
  round(100.0 * coalesce(rej.rejected_count,0) / ret.returns_requested, 1) as returns_rejected_pct
FROM tenants t
JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as orders_placed FROM orders WHERE placed_at >= '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY tenant_id) ord ON ord.tenant_id = t.id
JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as returns_requested FROM order_returns WHERE requested_at >= '2025-01-01' AND requested_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY tenant_id) ret ON ret.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, round(avg(days),1) as avg_days, round(cast(percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by days) as numeric),1) as median_days
           FROM (SELECT tenant_id, extract(epoch from (refunded_at - requested_at))/86400 as days FROM order_returns WHERE status='refunded' AND refunded_at IS NOT NULL AND requested_at >= '2025-01-01' AND requested_at < '2026-01-01') x
           GROUP BY tenant_id) rf ON rf.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as rejected_count FROM order_returns WHERE status='rejected' AND requested_at >= '2025-01-01' AND requested_at < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY tenant_id) rej ON rej.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE ret.returns_requested >= 20
ORDER BY ret.returns_requested DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Returns and refunds: volume and time-to-resolve trend
Response & resolution times by merchant, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Orders-placed and returns-requested are counted independently by their own 2025 date windows (per the stated caveat, a return's order may fall outside 2025), so return rate is a rough proxy. Tenants with no refunded returns in 2025 show null avg/median days; the printed row count vs. total qualifying tenants (returns_requested>=20) should be noted from the query's actual row count at print time.

entries.title: Shopper satisfaction (CSAT) trend, monthly
entries.question: How satisfied are shoppers with support interactions overall, and is satisfaction trending up or down?
entries.sql:
select
  strftime(date_trunc('month', submitted_at), '%Y-%m') as month,
  count(*) as csat_responses,
  round(avg(score)::numeric, 2) as avg_score,
  round(percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by score)::numeric, 1) as median_score,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when score >= 4 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_satisfied,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when score <= 2 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_dissatisfied
from csat_responses
where submitted_at >= timestamp '2023-01-01' and submitted_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
group by date_trunc('month', submitted_at)
order by month asc
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide monthly CSAT trend from csat_responses.submitted_at, Jan 2023 - Dec 2025 (36 rows expected, one per month, well under the 50-row page limit).

entries.title: Shopper satisfaction (CSAT) by merchant, 2025
entries.question: Which merchants have the weakest shopper satisfaction, and how much does it vary across the platform?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.id AS tenant_id,
  t0.name AS merchant_name,
  t1.response_count,
  t2.avg_score,
  t3.median_score,
  t4.pct_satisfied,
  t5.pct_dissatisfied
FROM tenants t0
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS response_count
  FROM csat_responses
  WHERE submitted_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND submitted_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, ROUND(AVG(score)::numeric, 2) AS avg_score
  FROM csat_responses
  WHERE submitted_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND submitted_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY score)::numeric, 1) AS median_score
  FROM csat_responses
  WHERE submitted_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND submitted_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.id
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN score >= 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_satisfied
  FROM csat_responses
  WHERE submitted_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND submitted_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) t4 ON t4.tenant_id = t0.id
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN score <= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_dissatisfied
  FROM csat_responses
  WHERE submitted_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND submitted_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) t5 ON t5.tenant_id = t0.id
ORDER BY t2.avg_score ASC, t0.name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Shopper satisfaction (CSAT) trend, monthly
Response & resolution times by merchant, 2025
entries.engineer_note: One row per tenant with >=10 CSAT responses in 2025, ordered worst-average first; printed to 50 rows. Note in the report footer the total count of qualifying tenants (i.e. the full row count before the LIMIT 50) so the analyst can see if any were cut off.

entries.title: CSAT score by ticket resolution-time bucket
entries.question: Does a slower ticket resolution actually translate into a lower satisfaction score?
entries.sql:
with resolved_tickets_with_csat as (
    select
        t.id as ticket_id,
        c.score as csat_score,
        extract(epoch from (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 as resolution_hours
    from tickets t
    join csat_responses c
        on c.ticket_id = t.id
    where t.resolved_at is not null
        and t.created_at >= timestamp '2023-01-01'
        and t.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
),
bucketed_tickets as (
    select
        ticket_id,
        csat_score,
        case
            when resolution_hours < 4 then '<4h'
            when resolution_hours < 24 then '4-24h'
            when resolution_hours < 72 then '1-3 days'
            when resolution_hours < 168 then '3-7 days'
            else '>7 days'
        end as resolution_bucket,
        case
            when resolution_hours < 4 then 0
            when resolution_hours < 24 then 4
            when resolution_hours < 72 then 24
            when resolution_hours < 168 then 72
            else 168
        end as bucket_sort_key
    from resolved_tickets_with_csat
),
bucket_summary as (
    select
        resolution_bucket,
        bucket_sort_key,
        count(*) as ticket_count,
        round(avg(csat_score)::numeric, 2) as avg_csat_score,
        round(100.0 * sum(case when csat_score >= 4 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_satisfied,
        round(100.0 * sum(case when csat_score <= 2 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_dissatisfied
    from bucketed_tickets
    group by resolution_bucket, bucket_sort_key
)
select
    resolution_bucket as resolution_time_bucket,
    ticket_count as tickets,
    avg_csat_score as avg_csat_score,
    pct_satisfied as pct_satisfied,
    pct_dissatisfied as pct_dissatisfied
from bucket_summary
order by bucket_sort_key
builds_on: Shopper satisfaction (CSAT) trend, monthly
Support response & resolution time trend, monthly
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide (all tenants pooled) since the request didn't scope to a merchant; resolution_hours computed from created_at to resolved_at as specified, with exactly the 5 requested buckets.

entries.title: Product review ratings trend, monthly
entries.question: What are shoppers' product review ratings telling us, and does the pattern echo the dips we see in support CSAT?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', t.created_at) AS month_start,
    t.rating,
    t.is_verified_purchase
  FROM product_reviews t
  WHERE t.is_approved = true
    AND t.created_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  strftime(t0.month_start, '%Y-%m') AS month,
  t0.review_count AS reviews_submitted,
  t1.avg_rating,
  t2.median_rating,
  t3.pct_low_rating,
  t3.pct_high_rating,
  t3.pct_verified_purchase
FROM (
  SELECT month_start, COUNT(*) AS review_count
  FROM base
  GROUP BY month_start
) t0
JOIN (
  SELECT month_start, ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating
  FROM base
  GROUP BY month_start
) t1 ON t1.month_start = t0.month_start
JOIN (
  SELECT month_start, ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY rating)::numeric, 1) AS median_rating
  FROM base
  GROUP BY month_start
) t2 ON t2.month_start = t0.month_start
JOIN (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN rating IN (1,2) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_low_rating,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN rating IN (4,5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_high_rating,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_verified_purchase THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_verified_purchase
  FROM base
  GROUP BY month_start
) t3 ON t3.month_start = t0.month_start
ORDER BY t0.month_start ASC
builds_on: Shopper satisfaction (CSAT) trend, monthly
entries.engineer_note: Report is platform-wide review ratings only, at the requested grain and columns (36 monthly rows expected, 2023-01 through 2025-12). The CSAT comparison mentioned in the question isn't included as a column here since that would be a second metric/grain bundled into this report; if the analyst wants a side-by-side with support CSAT, that should be its own request (or a follow-up report joining metrics_daily/csat_responses).

entries.title: Website traffic channel mix, 2025 vs 2024
entries.question: Which acquisition channels bring the most site traffic across all merchants, and how has that mix shifted versus a year ago?
entries.sql:
select
  channel,
  sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end) as sessions_2025,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end)
    / nullif(sum(sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end)) over (), 0), 1) as share_of_2025_sessions_pct,
  sum(case when started_at >= date '2024-01-01' and started_at < date '2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end) as sessions_2024,
  round(100.0 * (
    sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end)
    - sum(case when started_at >= date '2024-01-01' and started_at < date '2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end)
  ) / nullif(sum(case when started_at >= date '2024-01-01' and started_at < date '2025-01-01' then 1 else 0 end), 0), 1) as yoy_change_pct,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' and is_bounce then 1 else 0 end)
    / nullif(sum(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then 1 else 0 end), 0), 1) as bounce_rate_2025_pct,
  round(avg(case when started_at >= date '2025-01-01' and started_at < date '2026-01-01' then page_view_count end), 1) as avg_page_views_2025
from (
  select
    coalesce(nullif(trim(utm_source), ''), 'direct/none') as channel,
    started_at,
    is_bounce,
    page_view_count
  from web_sessions
) s
group by channel
order by sessions_2025 desc, channel asc
limit 12
entries.engineer_note: Channel mix and YoY shift across all merchants, top 12 channels by 2025 sessions; bounce rate and avg page views cover 2025 only as requested.

entries.title: Which marketing channels drive orders and revenue
entries.question: Among orders marketing can take credit for, which campaign channels generate the most attributed orders and revenue, and what's the resulting average order value?
entries.sql:
WITH attr AS (
  SELECT
    c.channel AS channel,
    a.order_id AS order_id,
    a.attributed_revenue AS attributed_revenue,
    CASE WHEN a.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS fx_rate
  FROM attributions a
  JOIN campaigns c ON c.id = a.campaign_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = a.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(a.occurred_at AS date)
  WHERE a.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND a.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND a.order_id IS NOT NULL
),
per_channel AS (
  SELECT
    channel,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS attributed_orders,
    SUM(attributed_revenue / fx_rate) AS attributed_revenue_eur
  FROM attr
  GROUP BY channel
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(attributed_revenue_eur) AS total_revenue_eur FROM per_channel
)
SELECT
  pc.channel,
  pc.attributed_orders,
  ROUND(pc.attributed_revenue_eur, 0) AS attributed_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(pc.attributed_revenue_eur / t.total_revenue_eur * 100, 1) AS share_of_revenue_pct,
  ROUND(pc.attributed_revenue_eur / pc.attributed_orders, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur
FROM per_channel pc
CROSS JOIN totals t
ORDER BY attributed_revenue_eur DESC, channel ASC
entries.engineer_note: EUR conversion uses exchange_rates with base_code='EUR', quote_code=currency_code, as_of=date of occurred_at (rate=1 for EUR); if a rate is missing for a given currency/day the row's revenue will be null in the sum rather than silently dropped, worth a data-quality check if totals look off.

entries.title: Discounting baseline: monthly coupon usage and discount rate
entries.question: How much discounting is happening platform-wide each month, and how often are coupon codes actually used?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label AS month
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE year_num = 2025
),
order_calc AS (
  SELECT
    strftime(o.placed_at, '%Y-%m') AS month,
    o.grand_total / CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS revenue_eur,
    o.discount_total / CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS discount_eur,
    CASE WHEN o.discount_total > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_discount
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = date(o.placed_at)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
order_agg AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
    SUM(has_discount) AS orders_with_discount_count,
    SUM(revenue_eur) AS total_order_revenue_eur,
    SUM(discount_eur) AS total_discount_amount_eur
  FROM order_calc
  GROUP BY month
),
coupon_agg AS (
  SELECT
    strftime(cr.redeemed_at, '%Y-%m') AS month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cr.coupon_id) AS distinct_coupons_used
  FROM coupon_redemptions cr
  WHERE cr.redeemed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND cr.redeemed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
  m.month,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_with_discount_count, 0) AS orders_with_discount_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.orders_with_discount_count, 0)::numeric * 100.0 / NULLIF(oa.orders_count,0), 1) AS discount_rate_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.total_order_revenue_eur,0)::numeric, 0) AS total_order_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.total_discount_amount_eur,0)::numeric, 0) AS total_discount_amount_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.total_discount_amount_eur,0)::numeric * 100.0 / NULLIF(oa.total_order_revenue_eur + oa.total_discount_amount_eur, 0), 1) AS discount_share_of_gmv_pct,
  COALESCE(ca.distinct_coupons_used, 0) AS distinct_coupons_used,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.total_discount_amount_eur,0)::numeric / NULLIF(oa.orders_with_discount_count,0), 0) AS avg_discount_per_discounted_order_eur
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.month = m.month
LEFT JOIN coupon_agg ca ON ca.month = m.month
ORDER BY m.month
entries.engineer_note: EUR conversion uses exchange_rates (base=EUR, quote=order currency, as_of=placed_at date); EUR-denominated orders use rate 1 directly since EUR/EUR is not guaranteed to be stored. All 12 months of 2025 are included via calendar_days even if an month had zero qualifying orders/redemptions (shown as 0/NULL rate).

entries.title: Direct traffic concentration by merchant
entries.question: Is the dominant 'direct/none' traffic channel spread evenly across merchants, or concentrated in a handful of them?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.name AS tenant_name,
  COALESCE(t1.total_sessions_2025, 0) AS total_sessions_2025,
  COALESCE(t2.direct_sessions_2025, 0) AS direct_sessions_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.direct_sessions_2025, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COALESCE(t1.total_sessions_2025, 0), 0), 1) AS direct_share_of_tenant_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.direct_sessions_2025, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t3.platform_direct_sessions_2025, 0), 1) AS pct_of_platform_direct_sessions
FROM tenants t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_sessions_2025
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS direct_sessions_2025
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND (utm_source IS NULL OR TRIM(utm_source) = '')
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS platform_direct_sessions_2025
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND (utm_source IS NULL OR TRIM(utm_source) = '')
) t3
ORDER BY direct_sessions_2025 DESC, tenant_name ASC
LIMIT 15
builds_on: Website traffic channel mix, 2025 vs 2024
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant, top 15 by direct_sessions_2025 descending as requested; the 2025 date filter is implemented as started_at >= 2025-01-01 and < 2026-01-01 to include all of Dec 31 2025.

entries.title: Do discounted orders look healthy, or just cheaper?
entries.question: Compared to full-price orders, do discounted orders in 2025 have a healthy order value, basket size, and return/cancellation rate, or do they look worse on the metrics that matter?
entries.sql:
SELECT order_group, orders_count, avg_order_value_eur, avg_items_per_order, return_rate_pct, cancelled_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    case when o.discount_total > 0 then 'discounted' else 'full price' end as order_group,
    count(*) as orders_count,
    round(avg(o.grand_total / case when o.currency_code = 'EUR' then 1 else er.rate end)::numeric, 0) as avg_order_value_eur,
    round(avg(coalesce(oi.item_qty,0))::numeric, 1) as avg_items_per_order,
    round(100.0 * sum(case when ret.order_id is not null then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as return_rate_pct,
    round(100.0 * sum(case when o.status = 'cancelled' then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as cancelled_rate_pct
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er on er.base_code = 'EUR' and er.quote_code = o.currency_code and er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
  LEFT JOIN (select order_id, sum(quantity) as item_qty from order_items group by order_id) oi on oi.order_id = o.id
  LEFT JOIN (select distinct order_id from order_returns) ret on ret.order_id = o.id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= date '2025-01-01' and o.placed_at < date '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY case when o.discount_total > 0 then 'discounted' else 'full price' end
) t
ORDER BY (case when order_group = 'discounted' then 0 else 1 end)
builds_on: Discounting baseline: monthly coupon usage and discount rate
entries.engineer_note: Orders with no order_items rows are counted with 0 items in the basket-size average (rather than being excluded), and orders with no exact-currency exchange rate (should not occur per the nightly rate feed) would be dropped from the EUR average via the inner join to exchange_rates for non-EUR currencies.

entries.title: Which merchants drove the January and July discount-rate spikes
entries.question: The platform-wide discount rate jumped from a ~35% baseline to 53-59% in January and July 2025 with no increase in average discount size — was that driven by a handful of merchants running sitewide promotions in those two months?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.name AS tenant_name,
  t0.industry AS industry,
  COALESCE(t1.orders_jan_jul, 0) AS orders_jan_jul_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t1.discount_orders, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t1.orders_jan_jul, 0), 1) AS discount_rate_jan_jul_pct,
  COALESCE(t2.orders_other, 0) AS orders_other_months_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.discount_orders, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t2.orders_other, 0), 1) AS discount_rate_other_months_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t1.discount_orders, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t1.orders_jan_jul, 0), 1)
    - ROUND(COALESCE(t2.discount_orders, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(t2.orders_other, 0), 1) AS delta_pct_points
FROM tenants t0
JOIN (
  SELECT
    o1.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_jan_jul,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o1.discount_total > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS discount_orders
  FROM orders o1
  WHERE o1.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o1.placed_at) = 2025
    AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o1.placed_at) IN (1, 7)
  GROUP BY o1.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    o2.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_other,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o2.discount_total > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS discount_orders
  FROM orders o2
  WHERE o2.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o2.placed_at) = 2025
    AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o2.placed_at) NOT IN (1, 7)
  GROUP BY o2.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
WHERE t1.orders_jan_jul >= 20
ORDER BY delta_pct_points DESC, orders_jan_jul_2025 DESC
LIMIT 15
builds_on: Discounting baseline: monthly coupon usage and discount rate
entries.engineer_note: Discount rate is defined on raw (unconverted) discount_total > 0 per the request's "Source: orders table" instruction, so no currency conversion was applied since the measure is a boolean share, not a summed amount. Tenants with fewer than 20 orders in the Jan/Jul 2025 bucket are excluded per spec; the report does not separately print the excluded count.

entries.title: Are discounted orders healthier across verticals, or just in B2B?
entries.question: Does the 'discounted orders have higher AOV, bigger baskets, and fewer returns' pattern hold in consumer verticals, or is it mainly an artifact of B2B wholesale contract pricing?
entries.sql:
WITH order_items_agg AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS item_qty
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
),
order_returns_flag AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id FROM order_returns
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    t.industry AS industry,
    CASE WHEN o.discount_total > 0 THEN 'discounted' ELSE 'full price' END AS order_group,
    o.status AS status,
    o.grand_total AS grand_total,
    o.currency_code AS currency_code,
    o.placed_at AS placed_at,
    COALESCE(oi.item_qty, 0) AS item_qty,
    COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS eur_rate
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN order_items_agg oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  b.industry AS industry,
  b.order_group AS order_group,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
  ROUND(AVG(b.grand_total / b.eur_rate), 0) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(b.item_qty), 1) AS avg_items_per_order,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN rf.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS return_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS cancelled_rate_pct
FROM base b
LEFT JOIN order_returns_flag rf ON rf.order_id = b.order_id
GROUP BY b.industry, b.order_group
ORDER BY b.industry ASC, b.order_group ASC
builds_on: Do discounted orders look healthy, or just cheaper?
Which merchants drove the January and July discount-rate spikes
entries.engineer_note: Industry comes from tenants.industry (free-text field set per merchant), so groupings reflect whatever values merchants have on file rather than a fixed vertical taxonomy; EUR conversion uses the exchange rate as of each order's placed_at date (EUR/EUR treated as rate 1).

entries.title: Email/campaign engagement baseline by channel
entries.question: How much campaign messaging goes out, and is anyone opening or clicking — is this a strength or a weak spot across the platform?
entries.sql:
WITH messages AS (
  SELECT
    cm.sent_at,
    cm.delivered_at,
    cm.opened_at,
    cm.clicked_at,
    cm.bounced_at,
    cm.unsubscribed_at,
    c.channel
  FROM campaign_messages cm
  JOIN campaigns c ON c.id = cm.campaign_id
  WHERE cm.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND cm.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    channel,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL) AS messages_sent,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS delivered_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND opened_at IS NOT NULL) AS opened_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND clicked_at IS NOT NULL) AS clicked_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL AND bounced_at IS NOT NULL) AS bounced_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sent_at IS NOT NULL AND unsubscribed_at IS NOT NULL) AS unsubscribed_count
  FROM messages
  GROUP BY channel
)
SELECT
  channel,
  messages_sent,
  ROUND(100.0 * delivered_count / NULLIF(messages_sent, 0), 1) AS delivered_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * opened_count / NULLIF(delivered_count, 0), 1) AS open_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * clicked_count / NULLIF(delivered_count, 0), 1) AS click_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * bounced_count / NULLIF(messages_sent, 0), 1) AS bounce_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * unsubscribed_count / NULLIF(messages_sent, 0), 1) AS unsubscribe_rate_pct
FROM agg
ORDER BY messages_sent DESC, channel ASC
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide (no tenant filter), filtered on campaign_messages.created_at in 2025 as requested. Delivered/open/click rates use delivered_at-not-null as the denominator basis (open and click also require delivered_at not null per spec); bounce and unsubscribe rates use sent_at-not-null as denominator.

entries.title: Do loyalty program members behave differently from other shoppers?
entries.question: Among shoppers who actually place orders, do loyalty-program members order more often or spend more per order than non-members?
entries.sql:
SELECT segment, users_count, orders_count_2025, avg_orders_per_user, avg_order_value_eur, total_revenue_eur
FROM (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la
      WHERE la.user_id = o.user_id AND la.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    ) THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id) AS users_count,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count_2025,
    ROUND(COUNT(*)::numeric / COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id), 2) AS avg_orders_per_user,
    ROUND(AVG(o.grand_total / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END))::numeric, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur,
    ROUND(SUM(o.grand_total / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END))::numeric, 0) AS total_revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la
      WHERE la.user_id = o.user_id AND la.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    ) THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END
) seg
ORDER BY CASE WHEN segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
entries.engineer_note: Grand_total converted to EUR via exchange_rates(base_code='EUR', quote_code=order currency, as_of=order date); EUR-denominated orders are treated as rate 1 when no explicit EUR/EUR row exists. If a non-EUR order's date is missing a rate row, that order is excluded from the EUR average/sum (but still counted in users_count/orders_count_2025).

entries.title: Is loyalty members' lower spend a within-industry effect or a merchant-mix effect?
entries.question: Within the same industry, do loyalty-program members actually order more or spend more than non-members, or does the platform-wide 'members look worse' result just reflect which verticals have more loyalty members enrolled?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.industry AS industry,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN o.user_id END) AS members_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NULL THEN o.user_id END) AS nonmembers_count,
  ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN o.id END)::numeric
        / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN o.user_id END), 0), 2) AS avg_orders_per_member,
  ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NULL THEN o.id END)::numeric
        / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NULL THEN o.user_id END), 0), 2) AS avg_orders_per_nonmember,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NOT NULL
                 THEN o.grand_total / (CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END)
            END), 0) AS avg_order_value_member_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN dla.user_id IS NULL
                 THEN o.grand_total / (CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END)
            END), 0) AS avg_order_value_nonmember_eur
FROM orders o
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_accounts) dla
  ON dla.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND dla.user_id = o.user_id
LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
  ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  AND t.industry IN (
    SELECT DISTINCT t2.industry
    FROM tenants t2
    JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.tenant_id = t2.id
    WHERE lp.is_active = true
  )
GROUP BY t.industry
ORDER BY t.industry
builds_on: Do loyalty program members behave differently from other shoppers?
entries.engineer_note: Membership is defined as any loyalty_accounts row for that user+tenant (deduplicated so multi-program enrollees aren't double-counted), independent of whether that specific program is active; industry eligibility is still restricted to industries with at least one tenant having an active loyalty_programs row. EUR conversion uses exchange_rates as of the order's placed_at date, with EUR orders treated as rate 1.

entries.title: Do referred or referring shoppers spend differently than everyone else?
entries.question: Among shoppers who place orders, do people who were referred in, or who refer others, show different order frequency or spend than everyone else?
entries.sql:
WITH classified AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.grand_total, o.currency_code, o.placed_at,
    CASE WHEN rr.referred_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'referred'
         WHEN rf.referrer_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'referrer'
         ELSE 'neither' END AS segment
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, referred_user_id FROM referral_redemptions) rr
    ON rr.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND rr.referred_user_id = o.user_id
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, referrer_user_id FROM referrals) rf
    ON rf.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND rf.referrer_user_id = o.user_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
converted AS (
  SELECT c.*,
    CASE WHEN c.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN c.grand_total
         ELSE c.grand_total / er.rate END AS grand_total_eur
  FROM classified c
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = c.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(c.placed_at AS date)
)
SELECT segment,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id || ':' || user_id) AS users_count,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_count_2025,
  ROUND(COUNT(*)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id || ':' || user_id),0), 2) AS avg_orders_per_user,
  ROUND(AVG(grand_total_eur)::numeric, 0) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(grand_total_eur)::numeric, 0) AS total_revenue_eur
FROM converted
GROUP BY segment
ORDER BY CASE segment WHEN 'referred' THEN 1 WHEN 'referrer' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END
entries.engineer_note: Classified by user_id scoped to tenant_id (same user_id can repeat across tenants, so users are counted as tenant+user_id pairs). EUR conversion divides each order's grand_total by that day's EUR→currency rate from exchange_rates (rate=1 implied for orders already in EUR).

entries.title: Do we run A/B tests, and do we act on the results?
entries.question: How many A/B tests has the platform run, in what state are they, and how often does a test actually end with a declared winner?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.status,
  t.tests_count,
  ROUND(t.tests_count * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ab_tests), 1) AS share_of_tests_pct,
  t.tests_with_winner_declared_count,
  ROUND(t.avg_variants_per_test, 1) AS avg_variants_per_test,
  ROUND(t.avg_duration_days, 1) AS avg_duration_days
FROM (
  SELECT
    a.status,
    COUNT(*) AS tests_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.winner_variant_id IS NOT NULL) AS tests_with_winner_declared_count,
    AVG(vc.variant_count) AS avg_variants_per_test,
    AVG(CASE WHEN a.started_at IS NOT NULL AND a.ended_at IS NOT NULL
         THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (a.ended_at - a.started_at)) / 86400.0 END) AS avg_duration_days
  FROM ab_tests a
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT ab_test_id, COUNT(*) AS variant_count
    FROM ab_variants
    GROUP BY ab_test_id
  ) vc ON vc.ab_test_id = a.id
  GROUP BY a.status
) t
ORDER BY t.tests_count DESC, t.status ASC
entries.engineer_note: One row per ab_tests.status across all tenants, all-time, per spec. avg_variants_per_test averages the per-test count of linked ab_variants rows (0 for tests with none, via LEFT JOIN); avg_duration_days only considers tests with both started_at and ended_at set.

entries.title: Test
entries.question: Test question
entries.sql:
select
    t.id as tenant_id,
    t.name as a,
    count(o.id) as b
from tenants t
left join orders o on o.tenant_id = t.id
group by t.id, t.name
order by t.id
entries.engineer_note: This request ("Test"/"Test question", columns "a" and "b") had no concrete business meaning to report on, so I produced a minimal one-row-per-tenant placeholder (tenant name as "a", lifetime order count as "b"). Please resubmit with the actual question and named metrics you want.

entries.title: Merchant size and recent growth trend
entries.question: How big is each merchant's business on Tidewick, and is it growing, flat, or shrinking over the last quarter?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.name AS merchant_name,
  t0.industry AS industry,
  t0.employee_count AS employee_count,
  COALESCE(t1.orders_last90, 0) AS orders_last_90_days,
  COALESCE(t1.revenue_last90_eur, 0) AS gross_revenue_eur_last_90_days,
  COALESCE(t2.orders_prior90, 0) AS orders_prior_90_days,
  COALESCE(t2.revenue_prior90_eur, 0) AS gross_revenue_eur_prior_90_days,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t2.revenue_prior90_eur,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(((COALESCE(t1.revenue_last90_eur,0) - t2.revenue_prior90_eur) / t2.revenue_prior90_eur) * 100, 1)
  END AS revenue_growth_pct,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t2.orders_prior90,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(((COALESCE(t1.orders_last90,0) - t2.orders_prior90) / CAST(t2.orders_prior90 AS decimal)) * 100, 1)
  END AS order_growth_pct
FROM tenants t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o1.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
         COUNT(*) AS orders_last90,
         SUM(o1.grand_total / er1.rate) AS revenue_last90_eur
  FROM orders o1
  JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er1.quote_code = o1.currency_code
   AND er1.as_of = CAST(o1.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o1.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o1.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-03 00:00:00'
    AND o1.placed_at <  TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY o1.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o2.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
         COUNT(*) AS orders_prior90,
         SUM(o2.grand_total / er2.rate) AS revenue_prior90_eur
  FROM orders o2
  JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = o2.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = CAST(o2.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o2.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o2.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-07-05 00:00:00'
    AND o2.placed_at <  TIMESTAMP '2025-10-03 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY o2.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
ORDER BY gross_revenue_eur_last_90_days DESC, t0.id ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Revenue is converted to EUR using the daily exchange_rates (EUR base) matched to each order's placed_at date. Growth pct is left NULL (rather than a misleading number) for merchants with zero prior-period orders/revenue, since growth is undefined in that case. All 120 merchants fit within the 50-row cap only if there are ≤50 tenants with last-90-day revenue; the report notes total row count as usual.

entries.title: Top merchants: year-over-year holiday-quarter growth
entries.question: For the biggest merchants, is Oct-Dec revenue really growing year over year, or is the recent growth just holiday seasonality?
entries.sql:
SELECT t0.id AS tenant_id, t0.name AS merchant_name, t0.industry,
  COALESCE(t1.revenue_eur_a, 0) AS revenue_eur_2025,
  COALESCE(t2.revenue_eur_b, 0) AS revenue_eur_2024,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t2.revenue_eur_b, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(((COALESCE(t1.revenue_eur_a, 0) - t2.revenue_eur_b) / t2.revenue_eur_b) * 100, 1)
  END AS revenue_yoy_growth_pct,
  COALESCE(t3.orders_a, 0) AS orders_2025,
  COALESCE(t4.orders_b, 0) AS orders_2024,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t4.orders_b, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(((COALESCE(t3.orders_a, 0) - t4.orders_b)::numeric / t4.orders_b) * 100, 1)
  END AS order_yoy_growth_pct
FROM tenants t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id AS tenant_id, SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS revenue_eur_a
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id AS tenant_id, SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS revenue_eur_b
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2024-10-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_a
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_b
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2024-10-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t4 ON t4.tenant_id = t0.id
ORDER BY COALESCE(t1.revenue_eur_a, 0) DESC, t0.id ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Merchant size and recent growth trend
entries.engineer_note: Revenue uses orders.grand_total converted to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=order currency, matched by placed_at date); growth % is blank (NULL) when the prior-year base is zero, as requested.

entries.title: Merchant risk signals: refunds, cancellations, unpaid invoices, shopper drop-off
entries.question: Which merchants show warning signs right now: rising refunds or cancellations, unpaid invoices, or falling shopper activity?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  round(coalesce(rr.refund_rate_last, 0) * 100, 2) AS refund_rate_last_90d_pct,
  round(coalesce(rr.refund_rate_prior, 0) * 100, 2) AS refund_rate_prior_90d_pct,
  round(coalesce(cr.cancel_rate_last, 0) * 100, 2) AS cancellation_rate_last_90d_pct,
  round(coalesce(cr.cancel_rate_prior, 0) * 100, 2) AS cancellation_rate_prior_90d_pct,
  round(coalesce(ov.overdue_eur, 0), 2) AS overdue_invoice_amount_eur,
  coalesce(ws.sessions_last, 0) AS web_sessions_last_90d,
  coalesce(ws.sessions_prior, 0) AS web_sessions_prior_90d,
  round(
    CASE WHEN coalesce(ws.sessions_prior, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE (ws.sessions_last - ws.sessions_prior) * 100.0 / ws.sessions_prior
    END, 2
  ) AS session_growth_pct
FROM tenants t
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ra.tenant_id,
         ra.refund_last_eur / NULLIF(ca.captured_last_eur, 0) AS refund_rate_last,
         ra.refund_prior_eur / NULLIF(ca.captured_prior_eur, 0) AS refund_rate_prior
  FROM (
    SELECT tenant_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN processed_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS refund_last_eur,
           SUM(CASE WHEN processed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND processed_at < DATE '2025-10-03' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS refund_prior_eur
    FROM (
      SELECT pr.tenant_id, pr.processed_at,
             pr.amount / COALESCE(er.rate, 1) AS amount_eur
      FROM payment_refunds pr
      LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
      WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
        AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    ) ra_inner
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  ) ra
  JOIN (
    SELECT tenant_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN captured_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS captured_last_eur,
           SUM(CASE WHEN captured_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND captured_at < DATE '2025-10-03' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS captured_prior_eur
    FROM (
      SELECT p.tenant_id, p.captured_at,
             p.amount / COALESCE(er.rate, 1) AS amount_eur
      FROM payments p
      LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
      WHERE p.status = 'captured'
        AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    ) ca_inner
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  ) ca ON ca.tenant_id = ra.tenant_id
) rr ON rr.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01' AND status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::decimal
           / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS cancel_rate_last,
         SUM(CASE WHEN placed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND placed_at < DATE '2025-10-03' AND status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::decimal
           / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN placed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND placed_at < DATE '2025-10-03' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS cancel_rate_prior
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) cr ON cr.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT i.tenant_id,
         SUM(i.amount_due / COALESCE(er.rate, 1)) AS overdue_eur
  FROM invoices i
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = (
        SELECT MAX(er2.as_of) FROM exchange_rates er2
        WHERE er2.base_code = 'EUR' AND er2.quote_code = i.currency_code AND er2.as_of <= DATE '2026-01-05'
      )
  WHERE i.status = 'past_due' OR (i.status = 'open' AND i.due_at < DATE '2026-01-05')
  GROUP BY i.tenant_id
) ov ON ov.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN started_at >= DATE '2025-10-03' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sessions_last,
         SUM(CASE WHEN started_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND started_at < DATE '2025-10-03' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sessions_prior
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-07-05' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) ws ON ws.tenant_id = t.id
ORDER BY overdue_invoice_amount_eur DESC, refund_rate_last_90d_pct DESC, t.id
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Merchant size and recent growth trend
entries.engineer_note: Overdue invoice EUR conversion uses the most recent exchange rate on or before the reporting date 2026-01-05 (data only runs through 2025-12-31, so effectively 2025-12-31's rate is used); all other metrics use the FX rate on the transaction's own date as specified.

entries.title: Merchant customer base health: repeat purchase rate
entries.question: For each merchant, how much of their customer base is repeat buyers versus one-and-done, over the last 12 months?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.id AS tenant_id,
  t0.name AS merchant_name,
  t0.industry AS industry,
  t1.distinct_customers AS distinct_customers,
  COALESCE(t2.repeat_customers, 0) AS repeat_customers,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.repeat_customers, 0) * 100.0 / t1.distinct_customers, 1) AS repeat_purchase_rate_pct,
  COALESCE(t3.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders_last_12_months,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t3.total_orders, 0) * 1.0 / t1.distinct_customers, 2) AS avg_orders_per_customer
FROM tenants t0
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id) AS distinct_customers
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT x.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS repeat_customers
  FROM (
    SELECT o.tenant_id, o.user_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    GROUP BY o.tenant_id, o.user_id
  ) x
  WHERE x.order_count >= 2
  GROUP BY x.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.id
ORDER BY distinct_customers DESC, repeat_purchase_rate_pct DESC, t0.id ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Used placed_at between 2025-01-01 and 2026-01-01 (calendar year 2025, the warehouse's last full 12 months) as the "last 12 months" window, excluding cancelled orders as specified; merchants with zero orders in the period are omitted since repeat/average rates would be undefined for them.

entries.title: DSAR volume and timeliness by month
entries.question: How many data subject requests do we receive each month, how quickly are they resolved relative to their due date, and how many are currently open — on time or overdue?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t0.month_start, t0.month_label
  FROM calendar_days t0
  WHERE t0.month_start BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-01'
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(r.requests_received,0) AS requests_received,
  COALESCE(ot.completed_on_time,0) AS completed_on_time,
  COALESCE(lt.completed_late,0) AS completed_late,
  COALESCE(nd.still_open_not_due,0) AS still_open_not_due,
  COALESCE(od.still_open_overdue,0) AS still_open_overdue,
  ROUND(avgc.avg_days_to_complete,1) AS avg_days_to_complete,
  ROUND(medc.median_days_to_complete,1) AS median_days_to_complete,
  ROUND( CASE WHEN (COALESCE(ot.completed_on_time,0)+COALESCE(lt.completed_late,0))=0 THEN NULL
    ELSE 100.0*COALESCE(ot.completed_on_time,0)/(COALESCE(ot.completed_on_time,0)+COALESCE(lt.completed_late,0))
  END, 1) AS pct_on_time
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t1.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS requests_received
  FROM data_subject_requests t1
  GROUP BY 1
) r ON r.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t2.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS completed_on_time
  FROM data_subject_requests t2
  WHERE t2.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND t2.completed_at <= t2.due_at
  GROUP BY 1
) ot ON ot.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t3.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS completed_late
  FROM data_subject_requests t3
  WHERE t3.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND (t3.completed_at > t3.due_at OR t3.due_at IS NULL)
  GROUP BY 1
) lt ON lt.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t4.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS still_open_not_due
  FROM data_subject_requests t4
  WHERE t4.completed_at IS NULL AND (t4.due_at IS NULL OR t4.due_at >= DATE '2025-12-31')
  GROUP BY 1
) nd ON nd.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t5.received_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS still_open_overdue
  FROM data_subject_requests t5
  WHERE t5.completed_at IS NULL AND t5.due_at < DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY 1
) od ON od.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t6.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t6.completed_at - t6.received_at))/86400.0) AS avg_days_to_complete
  FROM data_subject_requests t6
  WHERE t6.completed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
) avgc ON avgc.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT month_start, PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days) AS median_days_to_complete
  FROM (
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', t7.received_at)::date AS month_start,
      EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t7.completed_at - t7.received_at))/86400.0 AS days
    FROM data_subject_requests t7
    WHERE t7.completed_at IS NOT NULL
  ) sub
  GROUP BY month_start
) medc ON medc.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start
entries.engineer_note: "Completed" is determined directly by completed_at IS NOT NULL (per the request's own definitions for on-time/late), not by the status column, so no separate status-code lookup was needed; this matches data_subject_requests regardless of its status string values. Expect 36 rows, one per month from 2023-01 to 2025-12, all tenants combined.

entries.title: Staff access currency by account status
entries.question: Among internal staff users, how much elevated/role-based access exists today, and do deactivated or suspended staff still retain active role grants rather than having access revoked promptly?
entries.sql:
WITH staff AS (
  SELECT id, status, last_login_at
  FROM users
  WHERE is_staff = true AND deleted_at IS NULL
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    s.id AS user_id,
    s.status,
    s.last_login_at,
    ur.id AS user_role_id,
    ur.created_at AS role_granted_at,
    r.is_system
  FROM staff s
  LEFT JOIN user_roles ur ON ur.user_id = s.id
  LEFT JOIN roles r ON r.id = ur.role_id
)
SELECT
  status,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS staff_user_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE user_role_id IS NOT NULL) AS users_with_any_role,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE user_role_id IS NOT NULL)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id),0), 4) AS pct_with_any_role,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE is_system = true) AS users_with_system_role,
  ROUND(COUNT(user_role_id)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id),0), 2) AS avg_roles_per_user,
  ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(role_granted_at AS date))) FILTER (WHERE user_role_id IS NOT NULL), 1) AS median_days_since_role_granted,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE last_login_at IS NULL)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id),0), 4) AS pct_never_logged_in,
  ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(last_login_at AS date))) FILTER (WHERE last_login_at IS NOT NULL), 1) AS median_days_since_last_login
FROM joined
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'active' THEN 1 WHEN 'invited' THEN 2 WHEN 'suspended' THEN 3 WHEN 'deactivated' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END, status
entries.engineer_note: This is a current-state snapshot of user_roles as of 2025-12-31 (the schema has no revocation/end-date on role grants), so it shows what access exists today rather than how quickly past revocations happened; please flag any non-trivial users_with_any_role/users_with_system_role in the suspended/deactivated rows as a stale-access signal.

entries.title: Audit log volume and actor identification by month
entries.question: Is our audit trail continuous over time with no unexplained gaps, and are logged actions reliably tied to an identifiable actor rather than null/system placeholders?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start <= DATE '2025-12-01'
),
live AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start,
         count(*) AS live_events,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_user_id IS NULL) AS live_null_actor,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_type IN ('system','api_key','service_account')) AS live_system_api
  FROM audit_log
  GROUP BY 1
),
archive AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start,
         count(*) AS archived_events,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_user_id IS NULL) AS archived_null_actor,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_type IN ('system','api_key','service_account')) AS archived_system_api
  FROM audit_log_archive
  GROUP BY 1
),
actor_types AS (
  SELECT month_start, actor_type
  FROM (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start, actor_type FROM audit_log
    UNION ALL
    SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start, actor_type FROM audit_log_archive
  ) t
  GROUP BY month_start, actor_type
),
distinct_actor_types AS (
  SELECT month_start, count(*) AS distinct_actor_type_values
  FROM actor_types
  GROUP BY month_start
),
access AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start, count(*) AS access_events
  FROM access_log
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  coalesce(l.live_events,0) AS audit_log_live_events,
  coalesce(a.archived_events,0) AS audit_log_archived_events,
  coalesce(l.live_events,0) + coalesce(a.archived_events,0) AS total_audit_events,
  round(
    CASE WHEN (coalesce(l.live_events,0)+coalesce(a.archived_events,0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (coalesce(l.live_null_actor,0)+coalesce(a.archived_null_actor,0))::numeric / (coalesce(l.live_events,0)+coalesce(a.archived_events,0))
    END, 4) AS pct_actor_user_id_null,
  coalesce(dat.distinct_actor_type_values,0) AS distinct_actor_type_values,
  round(
    CASE WHEN (coalesce(l.live_events,0)+coalesce(a.archived_events,0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (coalesce(l.live_system_api,0)+coalesce(a.archived_system_api,0))::numeric / (coalesce(l.live_events,0)+coalesce(a.archived_events,0))
    END, 4) AS pct_actor_type_system_or_api,
