  coalesce(acc.access_events,0) AS access_log_events
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN live l ON l.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN archive a ON a.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN distinct_actor_types dat ON dat.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN access acc ON acc.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start
entries.engineer_note: Report is platform-wide (not per-tenant) since the question concerns overall audit-trail integrity across all merchants; months with zero events show 0 counts and null percentages rather than being dropped, so true logging gaps are visible as explicit rows.

entries.title: DSAR backlog reconciliation by status and request type
entries.question: Do the data subject requests that look 'open and overdue' by timestamp actually carry an open status, or is that an artifact of missing completed_at values on closed requests — and is the due_at SLA window itself consistent?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  status,
  request_type,
  COUNT(*) AS count_requests,
  COUNT(completed_at) AS count_with_completed_at,
  COUNT(*) - COUNT(completed_at) AS count_without_completed_at,
  SUM(CASE WHEN completed_at IS NULL AND due_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_overdue_open,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN due_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_due_at_null,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN due_at IS NOT NULL THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (due_at - received_at)) / 86400.0 END), 1) AS avg_sla_window_days,
  MIN(CASE WHEN completed_at IS NULL THEN received_at END) AS oldest_open_received_at
FROM data_subject_requests
WHERE received_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND received_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY status, request_type
ORDER BY status, request_type
builds_on: DSAR volume and timeliness by month
entries.engineer_note: oldest_open_received_at is NULL (not blank) for any status/request_type group where every row has a completed_at, since SQL has no blank/empty concept for timestamps. count_overdue_open uses the literal cutoff due_at < 2025-12-31 as requested, not today's date.

entries.title: Elevated access by permission category and staff status
entries.question: Which permission categories represent real elevated/admin-type access, how many staff users hold each, and do any non-active (invited/suspended/deactivated) staff still hold them?
entries.sql:
WITH staff_totals AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS total_staff
  FROM users
  WHERE is_staff = true AND deleted_at IS NULL
),
cat_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.category, u.id AS user_id, u.status
  FROM permissions p
  JOIN role_permissions rp ON rp.permission_id = p.id
  JOIN user_roles ur ON ur.role_id = rp.role_id
  JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = true AND u.deleted_at IS NULL
),
cat_perm_counts AS (
  SELECT category, count(DISTINCT code) AS distinct_permission_codes
  FROM permissions
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT
  cu.category,
  count(*) AS staff_users_with_category,
  round(100.0 * count(*) / st.total_staff, 2) AS pct_of_all_staff,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE cu.status = 'active') AS active_count,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE cu.status IN ('invited','suspended','deactivated')) AS non_active_count,
  cpc.distinct_permission_codes
FROM cat_users cu
CROSS JOIN staff_totals st
JOIN cat_perm_counts cpc ON cpc.category = cu.category
GROUP BY cu.category, st.total_staff, cpc.distinct_permission_codes
ORDER BY staff_users_with_category DESC, cu.category
builds_on: Staff access currency by account status
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per permissions.category, counting distinct is_staff=true/non-deleted users who hold at least one role granting a permission in that category (via user_roles -> role_permissions -> permissions). This is a current-state snapshot (no time dimension in users/roles to bound as of 2025-12-31, so it reflects the latest replicated state). distinct_permission_codes counts all permission codes defined in that category, independent of whether staff currently hold them.

entries.title: Role grant and revocation activity over time
entries.question: Is staff access actively granted and revoked over time (evidence of ongoing access management), and can we attribute those changes to an identifiable actor?
entries.sql:
WITH combined_log AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, action, actor_user_id, entity_table, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log
  UNION ALL
  SELECT tenant_id, action, actor_user_id, entity_table, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log_archive
),
role_changes AS (
  SELECT
    occurred_at,
    action,
    actor_user_id
  FROM combined_log
  WHERE entity_table = 'user_roles'
    AND action IN ('create', 'delete')
    AND occurred_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
monthly_changes AS (
  SELECT
    strftime(occurred_at, '%Y-%m') AS month_label,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'create') AS role_grants_created,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE action = 'delete') AS role_grants_removed,
    count(DISTINCT actor_user_id) AS distinct_actor_user_id,
    count(*) AS total_changes,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE actor_user_id IS NULL) AS null_actor_changes
  FROM role_changes
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  months.month_label AS month,
  coalesce(monthly_changes.role_grants_created, 0) AS role_grants_created,
  coalesce(monthly_changes.role_grants_removed, 0) AS role_grants_removed,
  coalesce(monthly_changes.role_grants_created, 0) - coalesce(monthly_changes.role_grants_removed, 0) AS net_change,
  coalesce(monthly_changes.distinct_actor_user_id, 0) AS distinct_actor_user_id,
  CASE WHEN coalesce(monthly_changes.total_changes,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE round(100.0 * monthly_changes.null_actor_changes / monthly_changes.total_changes, 1)
  END AS pct_actor_user_id_null
FROM months
LEFT JOIN monthly_changes ON months.month_label = monthly_changes.month_label
ORDER BY months.month_label
builds_on: Audit log volume and actor identification by month
Staff access currency by account status
entries.engineer_note: Combines audit_log and audit_log_archive (entity_table='user_roles', actions create/delete) across all tenants, since the question is about overall access-management practice rather than a specific merchant; months with zero activity are shown via a calendar spine with 0s, and pct_actor_user_id_null is left null for months with no changes (undefined rate) rather than 0.

entries.title: Audit log coverage for identity and access-control tables
entries.question: Which identity/access-control tables and actions actually appear in the audit trail, and under what naming — specifically, are role/permission grant and revocation events logged at all?
entries.sql:
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT entity_table, action, entity_id, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log
  WHERE occurred_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT entity_table, action, entity_id, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log_archive
  WHERE occurred_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  entity_table,
  action,
  COUNT(*) AS row_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT entity_id) AS distinct_entity_id_count,
  MIN(occurred_at) AS min_occurred_at,
  MAX(occurred_at) AS max_occurred_at
FROM combined
WHERE entity_table IN (
  'users','user',
  'roles','role',
  'user_roles','user_role',
  'role_permissions','role_permission',
  'permissions','permission',
  'teams','team',
  'team_members','team_member',
  'api_keys','api_key',
  'invitations','invitation',
  'mfa_devices','mfa_device',
  'sessions','session',
  'service_accounts','service_account',
  'personal_access_tokens','personal_access_token'
)
GROUP BY entity_table, action
ORDER BY entity_table, action
builds_on: Role grant and revocation activity over time
entries.engineer_note: Grain is entity_table x action, counted across audit_log UNION ALL audit_log_archive for 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31. To catch spelling mismatches, the entity_table filter includes both the exact 13 requested table names and their singular/plural counterpart (e.g. both 'user_roles' and 'user_role', 'role' and 'roles'), so any variant spelling will show up as its own row rather than being silently excluded.

entries.title: MFA device adoption by user segment and status
entries.question: What share of staff and customer accounts are protected by a confirmed MFA device, and does that differ by account status?
entries.sql:
WITH user_mfa AS (
  SELECT user_id, tenant_id,
         max(case when confirmed_at is not null then 1 else 0 end) as has_confirmed,
         1 as has_any
  FROM mfa_devices
  GROUP BY user_id, tenant_id
)
SELECT
  u.is_staff,
  u.status,
  count(*) as total_users,
  sum(case when um.has_confirmed = 1 then 1 else 0 end) as users_with_confirmed_mfa,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when um.has_confirmed = 1 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_with_confirmed_mfa,
  sum(case when um.has_any = 1 then 1 else 0 end) as users_with_any_mfa_device,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when um.has_any = 1 then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_with_any_mfa_device
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN user_mfa um ON um.user_id = u.id AND um.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
WHERE u.deleted_at is null
GROUP BY u.is_staff, u.status
ORDER BY u.is_staff desc, u.status
entries.engineer_note: This is a current-state snapshot across all tenants (no date filter applied beyond excluding deleted users), since users/mfa_devices have no period column to bound as of 2025-12-31 and the warehouse already ends there. Percentages are rounded to 1 decimal place.

entries.title: Failed login attempts and suspicious access patterns by month
entries.question: How much login activity fails, is there visible evidence of brute-force-style patterns, and are access-denied events actually being captured as suspicious activity over time?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
),
login_month AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start,
         email,
         succeeded
  FROM login_attempts
),
login_agg AS (
  SELECT month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS total_login_attempts,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE succeeded = false) AS failed_login_attempts
  FROM login_month
  GROUP BY month_start
),
brute_force AS (
  SELECT month_start, COUNT(DISTINCT email) AS emails_with_5plus_failed
  FROM (
    SELECT month_start, email, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM login_month
    WHERE succeeded = false AND email IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY month_start, email
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
  ) t
  GROUP BY month_start
),
audit_combined AS (
  SELECT occurred_at, action FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'access_denied'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT occurred_at, action FROM audit_log_archive WHERE action = 'access_denied'
),
audit_agg AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date AS month_start,
         COUNT(*) AS audit_access_denied_events
  FROM audit_combined
  GROUP BY month_start
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(la.total_login_attempts, 0) AS total_login_attempts,
  COALESCE(la.failed_login_attempts, 0) AS failed_login_attempts,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN COALESCE(la.total_login_attempts,0) = 0 THEN 0
       ELSE 100.0 * la.failed_login_attempts / la.total_login_attempts END, 2) AS pct_failed,
  COALESCE(bf.emails_with_5plus_failed, 0) AS emails_with_5plus_failed_in_month,
  COALESCE(aa.audit_access_denied_events, 0) AS audit_access_denied_events
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN login_agg la ON la.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN brute_force bf ON bf.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN audit_agg aa ON aa.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start
builds_on: MFA device adoption by user segment and status
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide monthly series, all months 2023-01..2025-12 included via calendar_days even if zero activity. login_attempts and the audit_log/audit_log_archive access_denied signal are aggregated independently per month (not row-joined), as requested, so they can be compared side by side but are not causally linked.

entries.title: Retention policy coverage for audit and compliance-relevant tables
entries.question: Do we have retention policies actually defined, active, and consistently enforced for the tables that matter most to this questionnaire (audit log, access log, change history, DSARs, compliance events, login attempts), and could any of them be purging data sooner than the history we'd want to cite?
entries.sql:
select
  entity_table,
  count(distinct tenant_id) as tenants_with_policy,
  round(100.0 * count(distinct tenant_id) / 120, 1) as pct_tenants_with_policy,
  round(avg(retention_days), 1) as avg_retention_days,
  min(retention_days) as min_retention_days,
  max(retention_days) as max_retention_days,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when is_active then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_policies_active,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when last_run_at >= date '2025-10-03' then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_policies_run_in_last_90_days
from retention_policies
where entity_table in ('audit_log', 'access_log', 'change_history', 'data_subject_requests', 'compliance_events', 'login_attempts')
group by entity_table
order by entity_table
builds_on: Audit log volume and actor identification by month
Audit log coverage for identity and access-control tables
entries.engineer_note: One row per entity_table as requested, aggregated across all tenants' retention_policies rows; a table only appears here if at least one tenant has defined a policy row for it, so missing rows in the printed report (expect up to 6) mean zero tenants have ever configured a policy for that table.

entries.title: Storefront-to-order funnel for top merchants, Q4 2025
entries.question: Where do shoppers drop off between landing on the storefront and placing a paid order, and does the shape differ across our biggest merchants?
entries.sql:
WITH paid_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS paid_order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND status NOT IN ('pending', 'cancelled')
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
top_tenants AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, paid_order_count
  FROM paid_orders
  ORDER BY paid_order_count DESC, tenant_id ASC
  LIMIT 10
),
visits AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS visit_count
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
carts_created AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS cart_count
  FROM carts
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
orders_placed AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
assembled AS (
  SELECT
    t.id AS tenant_id,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    COALESCE(v.visit_count, 0) AS visits,
    COALESCE(c.cart_count, 0) AS carts_created,
    COALESCE(o.order_count, 0) AS orders_placed,
    tt.paid_order_count AS orders_paid
  FROM top_tenants tt
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tt.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN visits v ON v.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN carts_created c ON c.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN orders_placed o ON o.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  visits,
  carts_created,
  orders_placed,
  orders_paid,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN visits > 0 THEN 100.0 * carts_created / visits ELSE NULL END, 1) AS visit_to_cart_pct,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN carts_created > 0 THEN 100.0 * orders_placed / carts_created ELSE NULL END, 1) AS cart_to_order_pct,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN orders_placed > 0 THEN 100.0 * orders_paid / orders_placed ELSE NULL END, 1) AS order_to_paid_pct,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN visits > 0 THEN 100.0 * orders_paid / visits ELSE NULL END, 1) AS overall_visit_to_paid_pct
FROM assembled
ORDER BY overall_visit_to_paid_pct DESC NULLS LAST, tenant_name ASC
entries.engineer_note: Each funnel stage (visits, carts, orders, paid orders) is counted independently per tenant over Q4 2025, as requested — there is no row-level link between web_sessions, carts and orders to trace individual shoppers through the funnel, so the percentages are stage-level conversion ratios, not tracked-visitor conversion rates.

entries.title: Checkout funnel by device type and arrival channel
entries.question: Once a cart is created, is the drop-off to a paid order a single cliff or a slow bleed across stages, and does it differ by device or by how the shopper arrived?
entries.sql:
SELECT 
  device_type,
  channel,
  COUNT(*) AS carts_started,
  SUM(CASE WHEN subtotal > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS carts_with_items,
  SUM(CASE WHEN order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_placed,
  SUM(CASE WHEN order_status IS NOT NULL AND order_status NOT IN ('pending','cancelled') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_paid,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN subtotal > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 1) AS cart_to_item_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN subtotal > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0), 1) AS item_to_order_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_status IS NOT NULL AND order_status NOT IN ('pending','cancelled') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0), 1) AS order_to_paid_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_status IS NOT NULL AND order_status NOT IN ('pending','cancelled') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 1) AS overall_cart_to_paid_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    cb.cart_id,
    cb.subtotal,
    cb.device_type,
    CASE
      WHEN cb.raw_channel = 'direct' THEN 'direct'
      WHEN cb.raw_channel = 'unknown' THEN 'unknown'
      WHEN cb.raw_channel IN (
        SELECT all_channels.raw_channel
        FROM (
          SELECT
            COALESCE(
              (SELECT CASE WHEN ws2.utm_source IS NULL OR TRIM(ws2.utm_source) = '' THEN 'direct' ELSE ws2.utm_source END
               FROM web_sessions ws2
               WHERE ws2.tenant_id = c2.tenant_id AND ws2.user_id = c2.user_id
                 AND ws2.started_at <= c2.created_at
                 AND CAST(ws2.started_at AS date) = CAST(c2.created_at AS date)
               ORDER BY ws2.started_at DESC LIMIT 1),
              'unknown'
            ) AS raw_channel
          FROM carts c2
          WHERE c2.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND c2.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
        ) all_channels
        WHERE all_channels.raw_channel NOT IN ('direct','unknown')
        GROUP BY all_channels.raw_channel
        ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
        LIMIT 6
      ) THEN cb.raw_channel
      ELSE 'other'
    END AS channel,
    (SELECT o.id FROM orders o WHERE o.cart_id = cb.cart_id AND o.tenant_id = cb.tenant_id ORDER BY o.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS order_id,
    (SELECT o.status FROM orders o WHERE o.cart_id = cb.cart_id AND o.tenant_id = cb.tenant_id ORDER BY o.created_at DESC LIMIT 1) AS order_status
  FROM (
    SELECT
      c.id AS cart_id,
      c.tenant_id,
      c.user_id,
      c.created_at,
      c.subtotal,
      COALESCE(
        (SELECT CASE
                  WHEN ws.user_agent ILIKE '%tablet%' OR ws.user_agent ILIKE '%ipad%' THEN 'tablet'
                  WHEN ws.user_agent ILIKE '%mobile%' OR ws.user_agent ILIKE '%android%' OR ws.user_agent ILIKE '%iphone%' THEN 'mobile'
                  WHEN ws.user_agent IS NOT NULL THEN 'desktop'
                  ELSE 'unknown'
                END
         FROM web_sessions ws
         WHERE ws.tenant_id = c.tenant_id AND ws.user_id = c.user_id
           AND ws.started_at <= c.created_at
           AND CAST(ws.started_at AS date) = CAST(c.created_at AS date)
         ORDER BY ws.started_at DESC LIMIT 1),
        'unknown'
      ) AS device_type,
      COALESCE(
        (SELECT CASE WHEN ws.utm_source IS NULL OR TRIM(ws.utm_source) = '' THEN 'direct' ELSE ws.utm_source END
         FROM web_sessions ws
         WHERE ws.tenant_id = c.tenant_id AND ws.user_id = c.user_id
           AND ws.started_at <= c.created_at
           AND CAST(ws.started_at AS date) = CAST(c.created_at AS date)
         ORDER BY ws.started_at DESC LIMIT 1),
        'unknown'
      ) AS raw_channel
    FROM carts c
    WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  ) cb
) final
GROUP BY device_type, channel
ORDER BY carts_started DESC, device_type, channel
entries.engineer_note: Device/channel are approximated by matching each cart's user_id to their most recent same-day web_sessions row (fallback 'unknown' if none); please flag in the printed notes if 'unknown' dominates the rows, since that would mean the user-to-session match is too sparse to trust for this cohort. Channel buckets to top-6 utm_source values (by cart count) + 'other', with 'direct' and 'unknown' as separate buckets.

entries.title: Repeat purchase rate and time-to-repeat by first-order cohort month
entries.question: Of shoppers who place a first order, how many come back and how long does it take?
entries.sql:
WITH paid_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, id, placed_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id, user_id ORDER BY placed_at, id) AS rn
  FROM orders
  WHERE status NOT IN ('pending','cancelled')
    AND placed_at IS NOT NULL
),
first_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, placed_at AS first_placed_at
  FROM paid_orders WHERE rn = 1
),
second_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, placed_at AS second_placed_at
  FROM paid_orders WHERE rn = 2
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    f.tenant_id,
    f.user_id,
    f.first_placed_at,
    s.second_placed_at,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', f.first_placed_at)::date AS cohort_month,
    CASE WHEN s.second_placed_at IS NOT NULL
         THEN (s.second_placed_at::date - f.first_placed_at::date)
    END AS days_to_second
  FROM first_orders f
  LEFT JOIN second_orders s
    ON f.tenant_id = s.tenant_id AND f.user_id = s.user_id
)
SELECT
  strftime(cohort_month, '%Y-%m') AS cohort_month,
  COUNT(*) AS first_time_buyers,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_second <= 30) / COUNT(*), 1) AS repeat_within_30_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_second <= 60) / COUNT(*), 1) AS repeat_within_60_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_second <= 90) / COUNT(*), 1) AS repeat_within_90_pct,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE second_placed_at IS NOT NULL) AS repeat_buyers,
  CAST(ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_second)) AS integer) AS median_days_to_second_order
FROM joined
WHERE cohort_month >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND cohort_month <= DATE '2025-10-01'
GROUP BY cohort_month
ORDER BY cohort_month
entries.engineer_note: A "user" here is identified by (tenant_id, user_id) since user_id is only unique per tenant; the first/second paid order per user is determined by placed_at order (ties broken by order id). Days-to-second-order is a whole-day calendar difference between placed_at dates; median is computed only over users who did place a second order.

entries.title: Session-tracking coverage vs order volume for top merchants, 2025
entries.question: Does the >100% visit-to-cart ratio in the Q4 funnel reflect real shopper behavior, or is web-session tracking sparse relative to order volume for certain merchants (e.g. subscription sellers), making 'visits' an unreliable denominator for them?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.industry,
  COALESCE(v.visits_2025, 0) AS visits_2025,
  COALESCE(o.orders_2025, 0) AS orders_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(v.visits_2025, 0)::numeric / NULLIF(COALESCE(o.orders_2025, 0), 0), 2) AS visits_per_order,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(s.sub_linked_orders, 0) / NULLIF(COALESCE(o.orders_2025, 0), 0), 1) AS subscription_linked_orders_pct,
  COALESCE(a.active_subscriptions, 0) AS active_subscriptions
FROM tenants t
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS visits_2025
  FROM web_sessions
  WHERE started_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND started_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) v ON v.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_2025
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) o ON o.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o2.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS sub_linked_orders
  FROM orders o2
  WHERE o2.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o2.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM invoices i
      WHERE i.order_id = o2.id AND i.subscription_id IS NOT NULL
    )
  GROUP BY o2.tenant_id
) s ON s.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS active_subscriptions
  FROM subscriptions
  WHERE status = 'active'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) a ON a.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE t.name IN (
  'Brennquell Kaffee', 'Spice Route Box', 'Grind Collective', 'Honeycomb Larder',
  'Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane',
  'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik'
)
ORDER BY visits_per_order ASC, tenant_name ASC
builds_on: Storefront-to-order funnel for top merchants, Q4 2025
entries.engineer_note: Visits and orders are raw counts (not currency, so no FX conversion needed). Visits-per-order and subscription-linked % are NULL-safe (divide-by-zero guarded via NULLIF) in case any of the 10 tenants had zero 2025 orders.

entries.title: Where orders stall after checkout: status-transition funnel, Q4 2025
entries.question: Within the post-checkout order lifecycle, is the drop-off to a paid order a single cliff at one status or a slow bleed spread across several, and which status is it?
entries.sql:
WITH base_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.created_at AS order_created_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN (
    SELECT o2.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM orders o2
    WHERE o2.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND o2.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY o2.tenant_id
    ORDER BY order_count DESC
    LIMIT 10
  ) top_tenants ON top_tenants.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND o.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
total_orders AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders FROM base_orders
),
status_list AS (
  SELECT status_name FROM (VALUES ('pending'),('confirmed'),('paid'),('partially_fulfilled'),('fulfilled'),('cancelled'),('refunded')) AS s(status_name)
),
first_reach AS (
  SELECT bo.order_id, osh.to_status AS status_name, MIN(osh.created_at) AS first_reached_at
  FROM base_orders bo
  JOIN order_status_history osh ON osh.order_id = bo.order_id
  WHERE osh.to_status IN ('pending','confirmed','paid','partially_fulfilled','fulfilled','cancelled','refunded')
  GROUP BY bo.order_id, osh.to_status
),
status_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    sl.status_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fr.order_id) AS orders_reaching_status,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (fr.first_reached_at - bo.order_created_at)) / 3600.0)) AS median_hours
  FROM status_list sl
  LEFT JOIN first_reach fr ON fr.status_name = sl.status_name
  LEFT JOIN base_orders bo ON bo.order_id = fr.order_id
  GROUP BY sl.status_name
)
SELECT
  sm.status_name AS status,
  COALESCE(sm.orders_reaching_status, 0) AS orders_reaching_status,
  ROUND(COALESCE(sm.orders_reaching_status, 0) * 100.0 / t.total_orders, 1) AS pct_of_total_orders,
  ROUND(sm.median_hours, 1) AS median_hours_to_status
FROM status_metrics sm
CROSS JOIN total_orders t
ORDER BY pct_of_total_orders DESC, sm.status_name ASC
builds_on: Storefront-to-order funnel for top merchants, Q4 2025
entries.engineer_note: I did not have the companion Q4 funnel report's exact tenant list (no tenant names were supplied), so as a proxy I selected the 10 tenants with the most orders created in Q4 2025; please swap in the actual tenant_id list if it differs. Median hours is null for a status if no order in the base population ever reached it.

entries.title: Cart abandonment: cliff or slow bleed, Q4 2025 (non-subscription merchants)
entries.question: When a cart doesn't convert, does the shopper give up quickly within the same visit, or does the cart linger for days before being abandoned or expiring?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    c.id,
    c.status,
    c.created_at,
    c.converted_at,
    c.abandoned_at,
    c.expires_at,
    CASE
      WHEN c.converted_at IS NOT NULL OR c.abandoned_at IS NOT NULL OR c.expires_at IS NOT NULL
      THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at)) / 3600.0
      ELSE NULL
    END AS resolution_hours
  FROM carts c
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik')
    AND c.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    CASE
      WHEN resolution_hours IS NULL THEN 'unresolved/still active'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 1 THEN '<1 hour'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 24 THEN '1-24 hours'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 168 THEN '1-7 days'
      ELSE '>7 days'
    END AS duration_bucket
  FROM base
)
SELECT
  duration_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
  ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_carts,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS converted_pct
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY duration_bucket
ORDER BY
  CASE duration_bucket
    WHEN '<1 hour' THEN 1
    WHEN '1-24 hours' THEN 2
    WHEN '1-7 days' THEN 3
    WHEN '>7 days' THEN 4
    WHEN 'unresolved/still active' THEN 5
  END
builds_on: Storefront-to-order funnel for top merchants, Q4 2025
Checkout funnel by device type and arrival channel
entries.engineer_note: Resolution time = coalesce(converted_at, abandoned_at, expires_at) - created_at, computed in hours; carts with all three null fall into the 'unresolved/still active' bucket. Tenant names matched exactly as given against tenants.name.

entries.title: Where orders stall after checkout, Q4 2025 — retail merchants only (corrected)
entries.question: For the real one-off retail merchants (excluding subscription-box sellers), is the drop-off between order creation and payment a single cliff or a slow bleed, and at which status does it happen?
entries.sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
base_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.created_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN target_tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01' AND o.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
total AS (
  SELECT count(*) AS total_orders FROM base_orders
),
statuses AS (
  SELECT unnest(ARRAY['pending','confirmed','paid','partially_fulfilled','fulfilled','cancelled','refunded']) AS status
),
first_reach AS (
  SELECT bo.id AS order_id, osh.to_status AS status, min(osh.created_at) AS first_at
  FROM base_orders bo
  JOIN order_status_history osh ON osh.order_id = bo.id
  WHERE osh.to_status IN ('pending','confirmed','paid','partially_fulfilled','fulfilled','cancelled','refunded')
  GROUP BY bo.id, osh.to_status
),
joined AS (
  SELECT fr.order_id, fr.status, fr.first_at, bo.created_at,
         EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (fr.first_at - bo.created_at)) / 3600.0 AS hours
  FROM first_reach fr
  JOIN base_orders bo ON bo.id = fr.order_id
)
SELECT
  s.status,
  count(j.order_id) AS orders_reaching_status,
  round(100.0 * count(j.order_id) / NULLIF(t.total_orders, 0), 1) AS pct_of_total_orders,
  round(CAST(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY j.hours) AS numeric), 1) AS median_hours_from_order_creation
FROM statuses s
CROSS JOIN total t
LEFT JOIN joined j ON j.status = s.status
GROUP BY s.status, t.total_orders
ORDER BY pct_of_total_orders DESC, s.status ASC
builds_on: Where orders stall after checkout: status-transition funnel, Q4 2025
entries.engineer_note: Restricted to the six named tenants (looked up by tenants.name) and orders created 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31; one row per status (all 7 included, zero-filled where unreached), as specified.

entries.title: Cart abandonment timing by tenant, Q4 2025 (retail merchants)
entries.question: Is the 'slow bleed' pattern in cart abandonment (most unresolved carts linger 1 hour to 7 days rather than dying instantly) consistent across retail merchants, or is it driven by one or two tenants' cart-expiry settings?
entries.sql:
SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    b.bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY t.name), 1) AS pct_of_tenant_carts,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS converted_pct
FROM (
    SELECT
        c.tenant_id,
        c.status,
        CASE
            WHEN c.converted_at IS NULL AND c.abandoned_at IS NULL AND c.expires_at IS NULL
                THEN 'unresolved/still active'
            WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 1
                THEN '<1 hour'
            WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 24
                THEN '1-24 hours'
            WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 168
                THEN '1-7 days'
            ELSE '>7 days'
        END AS bucket
    FROM carts c
    WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
) b
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = b.tenant_id
WHERE t.name IN ('Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik')
GROUP BY t.name, b.bucket
ORDER BY t.name,
    CASE b.bucket
        WHEN '<1 hour' THEN 1
        WHEN '1-24 hours' THEN 2
        WHEN '1-7 days' THEN 3
        WHEN '>7 days' THEN 4
        WHEN 'unresolved/still active' THEN 5
    END
builds_on: Cart abandonment: cliff or slow bleed, Q4 2025 (non-subscription merchants)
entries.engineer_note: Grain is tenant x duration bucket (up to 6 tenants x 5 buckets = 30 rows), matching the bucket/window definitions from the earlier 'cliff or slow bleed' report. pct_of_tenant_carts sums to ~100% within each tenant; converted_pct is the share of converted-status carts within each tenant/bucket cell.

entries.title: Delivery speed and return rate by merchant, Q4 2025
entries.question: Do merchants whose deliveries run slower/later also see higher return rates — an early read on whether delivery experience is eroding trust?
entries.sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Brennquell Kaffee','Spice Route Box','Grind Collective','Honeycomb Larder','Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
shipment_stats AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_delivered,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at))/86400.0) AS median_delivery_days,
    AVG(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at))/86400.0 > 7 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100 AS pct_over_7
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o.tenant_id IN (SELECT id FROM target_tenants)
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
order_stats AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS q4_orders,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)) AS orders_with_return
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.tenant_id IN (SELECT id FROM target_tenants)
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
)
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
  COALESCE(ss.shipments_delivered,0) AS shipments_delivered,
  ROUND(ss.median_delivery_days::numeric,1) AS median_delivery_days,
  ROUND(ss.pct_over_7::numeric,1) AS pct_over_7_days,
  ROUND( (os.orders_with_return::numeric / NULLIF(os.q4_orders,0)) * 100, 1) AS pct_orders_with_return
FROM target_tenants t
LEFT JOIN shipment_stats ss ON ss.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN order_stats os ON os.tenant_id = t.id
ORDER BY pct_over_7_days DESC NULLS LAST, t.name ASC
entries.engineer_note: Per the request, "late" is approximated as delivery_days > 7 since there's no promised-delivery-date field in the schema; this is a generic lateness proxy, not an SLA breach measure. Returns % is at the order level (any return row), not return value/revenue.

entries.title: Late delivery and returns within apparel merchants, Q4 2025
entries.question: Within a single high-return vertical (apparel), do late-delivered orders actually have a higher return rate than on-time ones — controlling for the vertical effect that swamped the merchant-level comparison?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  base.delivery_bucket,
  count(*) AS shipments_count,
  round(
    100.0 * count(distinct case when exists (
        select 1 from order_returns orr where orr.order_id = base.order_id
      ) then base.order_id end)
    / nullif(count(distinct base.order_id), 0)
  , 1) AS pct_orders_with_return
FROM (
  select o.tenant_id, o.id as order_id,
    case when (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at) <= interval '7 days' then 'on-time' else 'late' end as delivery_bucket
  from shipments s
  join fulfillments f on f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  join orders o on o.id = f.order_id
  where s.shipped_at >= timestamp '2025-10-01'
    and s.shipped_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
    and s.delivered_at is not null
) base
join tenants t on t.id = base.tenant_id
where t.name in ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij', 'Cragsley Outfitters')
group by t.name, base.delivery_bucket
order by t.name, (case when base.delivery_bucket = 'on-time' then 0 else 1 end)
builds_on: Delivery speed and return rate by merchant, Q4 2025
entries.engineer_note: Grain is tenant x delivery bucket as requested (max 6 rows: 3 tenants x 2 buckets). shipments_count counts shipment rows in the Q4 2025 window with non-null delivered_at; pct_orders_with_return is computed over the distinct orders behind those shipments in each bucket, so an order with shipments in both buckets can contribute to both rows.

entries.title: Late delivery and repeat purchase, September 2025 shipments
entries.question: Does a late delivery visibly reduce the chance a customer buys again, compared to an on-time delivery?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  delivery_bucket,
  MAX(bucket_shipment_count) AS shipments_count,
  COUNT(*) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN min_days_to_next IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_customers_with_next_order,
  ROUND(
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY min_days_to_next) FILTER (WHERE min_days_to_next IS NOT NULL)
  , 0) AS median_days_to_next_order
FROM (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    user_id,
    delivery_bucket,
    MIN(days_to_next) AS min_days_to_next,
    MAX(bucket_shipment_count) AS bucket_shipment_count
  FROM (
    SELECT
      tenant_id,
      user_id,
      delivery_bucket,
      EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (next_order_at - delivered_at)) / 86400.0 AS days_to_next,
      COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY delivery_bucket) AS bucket_shipment_count
    FROM (
      SELECT
        o.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
        o.user_id AS user_id,
        CASE WHEN (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at) <= INTERVAL '7 days' THEN 'on-time' ELSE 'late' END AS delivery_bucket,
        s.delivered_at AS delivered_at,
        (
          SELECT MIN(o2.placed_at)
          FROM orders o2
          WHERE o2.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
            AND o2.user_id = o.user_id
            AND o2.placed_at > s.delivered_at
            AND o2.placed_at <= s.delivered_at + INTERVAL '90 days'
        ) AS next_order_at
      FROM shipments s
      JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
      JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
      JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
      WHERE t.name IN (
          'Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty',
          'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik'
        )
        AND s.delivered_at >= DATE '2025-09-01'
        AND s.delivered_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
        AND s.shipped_at IS NOT NULL
    ) shipment_level
  ) days_level
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id, delivery_bucket
) customer_level
GROUP BY delivery_bucket
ORDER BY CASE WHEN delivery_bucket = 'on-time' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, delivery_bucket
builds_on: Delivery speed and return rate by merchant, Q4 2025
entries.engineer_note: Customer-level "has next order" and "days to next order" are computed per shipment's delivered_at and then collapsed to one value per customer within the bucket (earliest qualifying next order across their September shipments), since a customer can have multiple shipments in the same bucket; shipments_count still counts all shipments in the bucket.

entries.title: Repeat purchase after a return vs. no return, 2025
entries.question: Does experiencing a return change whether, and how soon, a customer places their next order, compared to orders that had no return?
entries.sql:
WITH retail_tenants AS (
    SELECT id, name
    FROM tenants
    WHERE name IN (
        'Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty',
        'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik'
    )
),
all_orders AS (
    SELECT o.id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.placed_at
    FROM orders o
    JOIN retail_tenants rt ON rt.id = o.tenant_id
    WHERE o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
),
base_orders AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM all_orders
    WHERE placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
      AND placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01'
),
order_has_return AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id
    FROM order_returns
),
next_order_per_base_order AS (
    SELECT b.id AS order_id, MIN(a.placed_at) AS next_placed_at
    FROM base_orders b
    JOIN all_orders a
      ON a.tenant_id = b.tenant_id
     AND a.user_id = b.user_id
     AND a.placed_at > b.placed_at
    GROUP BY b.id
),
order_level AS (
    SELECT
        b.id AS order_id,
        b.tenant_id,
        b.user_id,
        CASE WHEN ohr.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'has_return' ELSE 'no_return' END AS grp,
        CASE WHEN nop.next_placed_at IS NOT NULL
             THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (nop.next_placed_at - b.placed_at)) / 86400.0
        END AS days_to_next
    FROM base_orders b
    LEFT JOIN order_has_return ohr ON ohr.order_id = b.id
    LEFT JOIN next_order_per_base_order nop ON nop.order_id = b.id
)
SELECT
    grp AS "group",
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT (tenant_id, user_id)) AS distinct_customers,
    ROUND(
        100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN days_to_next IS NOT NULL AND days_to_next <= 90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*),
        1
    ) AS pct_with_subsequent_order_within_90_days,
    ROUND(
        CAST(
            PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_next)
            FILTER (WHERE days_to_next IS NOT NULL AND days_to_next <= 90)
        AS numeric),
        0
    ) AS median_days_to_subsequent_order
FROM order_level
GROUP BY grp
ORDER BY CASE WHEN grp = 'has_return' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
entries.engineer_note: "Subsequent order" is defined as each order's nearest next order placed by the same (tenant_id, user_id), regardless of that next order's own date range (it can fall after 2025-09-30, since data runs through 2025-12-31); the 90-day and median calculations use that nearest next order's date, not just any order in the window. Return status/outcome of the order_returns row is not filtered (any row counts as "has a return").

entries.title: Monthly revenue by source
entries.question: If we ask what revenue was in a given month from four different places (orders booked, payments captured, payouts settled, invoices paid), do we get the same answer, and how far apart are they?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start, month_label
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-01'
),

orders_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', o.placed_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate), 2) AS orders_booked_revenue_eur,
         COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),

payments_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', p.captured_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(p.amount / er.rate), 2) AS payments_captured_eur,
         COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payments p
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS DATE)
  WHERE p.status = 'captured'
    AND p.captured_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),

payouts_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', po.paid_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(po.gross_amount / er.rate), 2) AS payout_gross_eur
  FROM payouts po
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = po.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(po.paid_at AS DATE)
  WHERE po.paid_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),

invoices_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', i.paid_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(i.total / er.rate), 2) AS invoice_paid_revenue_eur
  FROM invoices i
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(i.paid_at AS DATE)
  WHERE i.status = 'paid'
    AND i.paid_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),

refunds_rev AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.processed_at)::date AS month_start,
         ROUND(SUM(pr.amount / er.rate), 2) AS refunds_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
)

SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(orr.orders_booked_revenue_eur, 0) AS orders_booked_revenue_eur,
  COALESCE(pay.payments_captured_eur, 0) AS payments_captured_eur,
  COALESCE(pou.payout_gross_eur, 0) AS payout_gross_eur,
  COALESCE(inv.invoice_paid_revenue_eur, 0) AS invoice_paid_revenue_eur,
  COALESCE(ref.refunds_eur, 0) AS refunds_eur,
  COALESCE(orr.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
  COALESCE(pay.payment_count, 0) AS payment_count
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN orders_rev orr ON orr.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN payments_rev pay ON pay.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN payouts_rev pou ON pou.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN invoices_rev inv ON inv.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN refunds_rev ref ON ref.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start
entries.engineer_note: Each of the four revenue measures is converted to EUR independently using exchange_rates matched to the event's own date and currency (orders by placed_at, payments by captured_at, payouts by paid_at, invoices by paid_at), so differences between them reflect genuine timing/definition gaps (e.g. payouts net out fees/refunds and lag payment capture) rather than conversion artifacts. 36 rows, one per month, all months present via calendar_days even if a source had zero activity.

entries.title: Orders traced into captured payments
entries.question: Is there a clean, traceable link from an order to the money actually collected for it, or do orders vanish (no captured payment) or multiply (captured payments exceeding order value) along the way?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND calendar_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
),
orders_filtered AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.currency_code, o.grand_total, o.placed_at,
         strftime(o.placed_at, '%Y-%m') AS month_label
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
orders_eur AS (
  SELECT ofl.order_id, ofl.month_label,
         ofl.grand_total / er.rate AS grand_total_eur
  FROM orders_filtered ofl
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = ofl.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(ofl.placed_at AS date)
),
payments_captured AS (
  SELECT p.id AS payment_id, p.order_id, p.amount, p.currency_code, p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status = 'captured' AND p.order_id IS NOT NULL
),
payments_linked AS (
  SELECT pc.payment_id, pc.order_id, ofl.month_label,
         pc.amount / er.rate AS amount_eur
  FROM payments_captured pc
  JOIN orders_filtered ofl ON ofl.order_id = pc.order_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = pc.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(pc.captured_at, ofl.placed_at) AS date)
),
order_agg AS (
  SELECT month_label,
         COUNT(*) AS orders_count,
         SUM(grand_total_eur) AS orders_grand_total_eur
  FROM orders_eur
  GROUP BY month_label
),
order_with_payment AS (
  SELECT month_label, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_with_captured_payment_count
  FROM payments_linked
  GROUP BY month_label
),
payment_agg AS (
  SELECT month_label, SUM(amount_eur) AS captured_payment_total_eur
  FROM payments_linked
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0), 2) AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  COALESCE(owp.orders_with_captured_payment_count, 0) AS orders_with_captured_payment_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0), 2) AS captured_payment_total_eur,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) - COALESCE(owp.orders_with_captured_payment_count, 0) AS orders_without_captured_payment_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) - COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0), 2) AS gap_eur,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND((COALESCE(oa.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) - COALESCE(pa.captured_payment_total_eur, 0)) / oa.orders_grand_total_eur * 100, 1)
  END AS gap_pct
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.month_label = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN order_with_payment owp ON owp.month_label = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN payment_agg pa ON pa.month_label = m.month_label
ORDER BY m.month_label
entries.engineer_note: Captured-payment amounts are converted to EUR using the exchange rate as of their captured_at date (falling back to the order's placed_at date if captured_at is null); orders' grand_total uses the placed_at date. Months with zero qualifying orders still appear via the calendar_days spine, with all measures as 0/NULL for gap_pct.

entries.title: Payout reconciliation to gross, fees and refunds
entries.question: Do payouts consistently reconcile as net = gross minus fee, and do refunds actually reduce what we pay out, or could refunds be double-counted or missing from the payout math?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start AS month
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start <= DATE '2025-12-01'
),
payout_agg AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', COALESCE(p.paid_at, CAST(p.arrival_date AS timestamp)))::date AS month,
    SUM(p.gross_amount / er.rate) AS gross_eur,
    SUM(p.fee_amount / er.rate) AS fee_eur,
    SUM(p.net_amount / er.rate) AS net_eur
  FROM payouts p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = COALESCE(CAST(p.paid_at AS date), p.arrival_date)
  WHERE COALESCE(p.paid_at, CAST(p.arrival_date AS timestamp)) IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
),
refund_agg AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', pr.processed_at)::date AS month,
    SUM(pr.amount / er.rate) AS refunds_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  strftime(m.month, '%Y-%m') AS month,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.gross_eur,0),2) AS payout_gross_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.fee_eur,0),2) AS payout_fee_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.net_eur,0),2) AS payout_net_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.net_eur,0) - (COALESCE(pa.gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pa.fee_eur,0)),2) AS net_check_diff_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ra.refunds_eur,0),2) AS refunds_processed_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pa.net_eur,0) - (COALESCE(pa.gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pa.fee_eur,0) - COALESCE(ra.refunds_eur,0)),2) AS net_minus_refunds_diff_eur
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN payout_agg pa ON pa.month = m.month
LEFT JOIN refund_agg ra ON ra.month = m.month
ORDER BY m.month
builds_on: Monthly revenue by source
entries.engineer_note: Payout month uses paid_at, falling back to arrival_date only when paid_at is null (36 months, 2023-01 to 2025-12, all months printed since the request's range is within the 50-row limit). Refunds are matched by calendar month only (not joined to the specific payout), since payment_refunds has no payout linkage in the schema - a mismatch in net_minus_refunds_diff_eur could reflect either true timing lag between refund processing and payout settlement, or an actual accounting gap.

entries.title: Order-to-payment gap by order status, aged cohort
entries.question: Is the 20-40% gap between order value and captured payments explained by order status (i.e. structural - many orders simply never get paid), or does it look like something else, once we only look at orders old enough that timing lag can't be the excuse?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  pop.status AS order_status,
  pop.order_count,
  ROUND(pop.order_count * 100.0 / SUM(pop.order_count) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_orders,
  ROUND(pop.grand_total_eur, 2) AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  pop.orders_with_captured_payment_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pay.captured_eur, 0), 2) AS matched_captured_payment_eur,
  ROUND(pop.grand_total_eur - COALESCE(pay.captured_eur, 0), 2) AS gap_eur,
  ROUND((pop.grand_total_eur - COALESCE(pay.captured_eur, 0)) / NULLIF(pop.grand_total_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS gap_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.status,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS grand_total_eur,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'captured'
    ) THEN 1 END) AS orders_with_captured_payment_count
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY o.status
) pop
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    o.status,
    SUM(p.amount / er2.rate) AS captured_eur
  FROM payments p
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = p.order_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p.status = 'captured'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY o.status
) pay ON pay.status = pop.status
ORDER BY orders_grand_total_eur DESC, pop.status
builds_on: Orders traced into captured payments
entries.engineer_note: Grain is order status, population restricted to orders placed 2023-01-01 through 2025-06-30 inclusive as requested. EUR conversion divides each amount by the EUR→currency rate (orders by placed_at date, captured payments by captured_at date), matching the convention that exchange_rates.rate is EUR-based.

entries.title: Invoice revenue: order-linked vs subscription-only
entries.question: Is invoice revenue additional revenue on top of what we already count in orders, or does some of it double-count order revenue we've already booked?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  strftime(date_trunc('month', i.paid_at), '%Y-%m') as month,
  round(sum(case when i.currency_code = 'EUR' then i.total else i.total / er.rate end), 2) as invoice_paid_total_eur,
  round(sum(case when i.order_id is not null then (case when i.currency_code = 'EUR' then i.total else i.total / er.rate end) else 0 end), 2) as invoice_order_linked_eur,
  round(sum(case when i.order_id is null and i.subscription_id is not null then (case when i.currency_code = 'EUR' then i.total else i.total / er.rate end) else 0 end), 2) as invoice_subscription_only_eur,
  round(sum(case when i.order_id is null and i.subscription_id is null then (case when i.currency_code = 'EUR' then i.total else i.total / er.rate end) else 0 end), 2) as invoice_other_eur,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when i.order_id is not null then (case when i.currency_code = 'EUR' then i.total else i.total / er.rate end) else 0 end)
        / nullif(sum(case when i.currency_code = 'EUR' then i.total else i.total / er.rate end), 0), 1) as pct_order_linked
FROM invoices i
LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
  ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
  AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
  AND er.as_of = date(i.paid_at)
WHERE i.status = 'paid'
  AND i.paid_at >= date '2023-01-01'
  AND i.paid_at < date '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', i.paid_at)
ORDER BY date_trunc('month', i.paid_at)
builds_on: Monthly revenue by source
entries.engineer_note: EUR-currency invoices are summed directly (no FX join needed); all other currencies convert via exchange_rates matched on invoices.currency_code and the paid_at date. Rows with a currency/date combination missing from exchange_rates (none expected for in-range data) would show as NULL in the EUR columns rather than being silently dropped.

entries.title: Payout net formula check via payment-linked refunds
entries.question: Once refunds are matched to the actual payments inside each payout (not just by calendar month), does net = gross - fee - refunds hold cleanly, confirming refunds are reflected once and only once in what we pay merchants?
entries.sql:
WITH payout_eur AS (
  SELECT
    po.id AS payout_id,
    cd.month_start,
    cd.month_label,
    CASE WHEN po.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN po.gross_amount ELSE po.gross_amount / er.rate END AS gross_eur,
    CASE WHEN po.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN po.fee_amount ELSE po.fee_amount / er.rate END AS fee_eur,
    CASE WHEN po.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN po.net_amount ELSE po.net_amount / er.rate END AS net_eur
  FROM payouts po
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(po.paid_at AS date)
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = po.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = cd.calendar_date
  WHERE po.paid_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND po.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
refund_eur AS (
  SELECT
    po.id AS payout_id,
    CASE WHEN pr.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pr.amount ELSE pr.amount / er.rate END AS refund_eur
  FROM payouts po
  JOIN payout_items pi ON pi.payout_id = po.id
  JOIN payment_refunds pr ON pr.payment_id = pi.payment_id AND pr.status = 'succeeded'
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE po.paid_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND po.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
payout_month_agg AS (
  SELECT month_start, month_label,
    SUM(gross_eur) AS payout_gross_eur,
    SUM(fee_eur) AS payout_fee_eur,
    SUM(net_eur) AS payout_net_eur
  FROM payout_eur
  GROUP BY month_start, month_label
),
refund_month_agg AS (
  SELECT pe.month_start, pe.month_label, SUM(re.refund_eur) AS linked_refunds_eur
  FROM refund_eur re
  JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT payout_id, month_start, month_label FROM payout_eur) pe ON pe.payout_id = re.payout_id
  GROUP BY pe.month_start, pe.month_label
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start, month_label FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start <= DATE '2025-12-01'
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_gross_eur,0),2) AS payout_gross_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_fee_eur,0),2) AS payout_fee_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_net_eur,0),2) AS payout_net_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rf.linked_refunds_eur,0),2) AS linked_refunds_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pg.payout_fee_eur,0) - COALESCE(rf.linked_refunds_eur,0),2) AS implied_net_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pg.payout_net_eur,0) - (COALESCE(pg.payout_gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pg.payout_fee_eur,0) - COALESCE(rf.linked_refunds_eur,0)),2) AS diff_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(pg.payout_net_eur,0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (COALESCE(pg.payout_net_eur,0) - (COALESCE(pg.payout_gross_eur,0) - COALESCE(pg.payout_fee_eur,0) - COALESCE(rf.linked_refunds_eur,0))) / pg.payout_net_eur * 100
    END, 1) AS diff_pct
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN payout_month_agg pg ON pg.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN refund_month_agg rf ON rf.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start
builds_on: Payout reconciliation to gross, fees and refunds
entries.engineer_note: Months with zero payouts show 0s with diff_pct left NULL (division by zero undefined). EUR amounts are passed through unconverted since exchange_rates may not carry a self-referential EUR/EUR row; all other currencies are converted via the EUR-based daily rate on the relevant date (paid_at for payouts, processed_at for refunds).

entries.title: Order-to-payment gap re-measured with refund-inclusive payment status
entries.question: How much of the gap between order value and 'captured' payments is really just that refunded/partially-refunded payments were excluded by my status filter, versus a genuine hole where money was never collected?
entries.sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT
    o0.id AS order_id,
    o0.status AS order_status,
    o0.grand_total / er0.rate AS grand_total_eur
  FROM orders o0
  JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er0.quote_code = o0.currency_code
   AND er0.as_of = CAST(o0.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o0.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND o0.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01 00:00:00'
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT
    p1.order_id AS order_id,
    p1.amount / er1.rate AS gross_eur,
    (p1.amount - p1.amount_refunded) / er1.rate AS net_eur
  FROM payments p1
  JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er1.quote_code = p1.currency_code
   AND er1.as_of = CAST(p1.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p1.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p1.order_id IN (SELECT t0.order_id FROM t0)
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    t1.order_id AS order_id,
    SUM(t1.gross_eur) AS gross_eur,
    SUM(t1.net_eur) AS net_eur
  FROM t1
  GROUP BY t1.order_id
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    t0.order_status AS order_status,
    COUNT(t0.order_id) AS order_count,
    SUM(t0.grand_total_eur) AS orders_grand_total_eur
  FROM t0
  GROUP BY t0.order_status
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT
    t0.order_status AS order_status,
    COUNT(t2.order_id) AS orders_with_money_collected_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(t2.gross_eur, 0)) AS gross_collected_eur,
    SUM(COALESCE(t2.net_eur, 0)) AS net_collected_eur
  FROM t0
  LEFT JOIN t2
    ON t2.order_id = t0.order_id
  GROUP BY t0.order_status
)
SELECT
  t3.order_status AS order_status,
  t3.order_count AS order_count,
  t3.orders_grand_total_eur AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  t4.orders_with_money_collected_count AS orders_with_money_collected_count,
  t4.gross_collected_eur AS gross_collected_eur,
  t4.net_collected_eur AS net_collected_eur,
  t3.orders_grand_total_eur - t4.gross_collected_eur AS gap_vs_gross_eur,
  ROUND(
    (t3.orders_grand_total_eur - t4.gross_collected_eur) / NULLIF(t3.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) * 100,
    1
  ) AS gap_vs_gross_pct
FROM t3
JOIN t4
  ON t4.order_status = t3.order_status
ORDER BY t3.orders_grand_total_eur DESC, t3.order_status ASC
builds_on: Order-to-payment gap by order status, aged cohort
entries.engineer_note: Grain is orders.status (8 possible rows), each order counted once for orders_with_money_collected_count even if it has multiple captured/refunded payments (gross/net are summed across all its linked payments). Money conversion uses exchange_rates on placed_at date for order totals and on captured_at date for payment amounts, per the request.

entries.title: Refund timing relative to payout settlement
entries.question: When a payment is refunded, does the refund happen before its payout settles (so it can cleanly reduce that payout) or after (so the clawback has no clean home in the payout data), and how much money is affected?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  timing_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS refund_count,
  ROUND(SUM(amount_eur), 2) AS refund_amount_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(amount_eur) / SUM(SUM(amount_eur)) OVER () * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_refund_amount,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN timing_bucket = 'refund after payout paid_at' THEN days_lag END), 1) AS avg_days_lag
FROM (
  SELECT
    pr.id,
    CASE
      WHEN po.id IS NULL THEN 'payment not yet settled in any payout'
      WHEN pr.processed_at <= po.paid_at THEN 'refund before payout paid_at'
      ELSE 'refund after payout paid_at'
    END AS timing_bucket,
    CASE WHEN pr.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pr.amount ELSE pr.amount / er.rate END AS amount_eur,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (pr.processed_at - po.paid_at)) / 86400.0 AS days_lag
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  LEFT JOIN payout_items pi ON pi.payment_id = pr.payment_id
  LEFT JOIN payouts po ON po.id = pi.payout_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = pr.processed_at::date
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
) sub
GROUP BY timing_bucket
ORDER BY refund_amount_eur DESC
builds_on: Payout net formula check via payment-linked refunds
entries.engineer_note: Grain is the three timing buckets as specified (3 rows total). A payment can appear in at most one payout (payout_items.payment_id is unique), so each refund maps to 0 or 1 payout for bucketing; avg_days_lag is NULL for the before/not-yet-settled buckets as requested.

entries.title: Customer headcount by definition
entries.question: Do different reasonable definitions of 'how many customers we have' or 'how many are active' give meaningfully different headcounts?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.definition,
  t.user_count,
  round(t.user_count * 100.0 / tot.total_count, 1) as pct_of_all_customers
FROM (
  SELECT 'All customers (ever created)' as definition,
    (SELECT count(distinct u1.id) FROM users u1
       WHERE u1.is_staff = false AND u1.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01') as user_count
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Status = active',
    (SELECT count(distinct u2.id) FROM users u2
       WHERE u2.is_staff = false AND u2.status = 'active')
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Placed at least one order, ever',
    (SELECT count(distinct u3.id) FROM users u3
       WHERE u3.is_staff = false
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o3 WHERE o3.user_id = u3.id
                       AND o3.placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Placed at least one order in trailing 12 months',
    (SELECT count(distinct u4.id) FROM users u4
       WHERE u4.is_staff = false
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o4 WHERE o4.user_id = u4.id
                       AND o4.placed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
                       AND o4.placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Has an active or trialing subscription',
    (SELECT count(distinct u5.id) FROM users u5
       WHERE u5.is_staff = false
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions s5 WHERE s5.user_id = u5.id
                       AND s5.status IN ('active','trialing')))
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Logged in within last 90 days of data',
    (SELECT count(distinct u6.id) FROM users u6
       WHERE u6.is_staff = false
         AND u6.last_login_at >= timestamp '2025-10-03'
         AND u6.last_login_at < timestamp '2026-01-01')
) t
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT count(distinct u0.id) as total_count
  FROM users u0
  WHERE u0.is_staff = false AND u0.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
) tot
ORDER BY t.user_count DESC, t.definition
entries.engineer_note: Counts are pooled across all tenants (non-staff users only), as requested. "created_at <= 2025-12-31" and "placed_at <= 2025-12-31" were implemented as "< 2026-01-01" to include the full last day.

entries.title: B2B wholesaler receivables aging
entries.question: For our B2B wholesaler merchants, how much of their outstanding receivables is genuinely overdue versus just within normal net terms lag, so we can present that line accurately in the annual accounts?
entries.sql:
WITH scoped_tenants AS (
  SELECT id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%office%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%wholesale%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%b2b%'
),
tenant_match_count AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM scoped_tenants
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    i.id,
    i.amount_due,
    i.currency_code,
    i.due_at,
    bp.net_terms_days,
    CASE
      WHEN i.due_at IS NULL OR i.due_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31' THEN 'Not yet due'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - i.due_at::date) BETWEEN 1 AND 30 THEN '1-30 days overdue'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - i.due_at::date) BETWEEN 31 AND 60 THEN '31-60 days overdue'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - i.due_at::date) BETWEEN 61 AND 90 THEN '61-90 days overdue'
      ELSE '90+ days overdue'
    END AS aging_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN i.due_at IS NULL OR i.due_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31' THEN 0
      ELSE (DATE '2025-12-31' - i.due_at::date)
    END AS days_past_due,
    er.rate AS eur_rate
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN scoped_tenants st ON st.id = i.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN billing_profiles bp ON bp.id = i.billing_profile_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
  WHERE i.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
    AND i.amount_due > 0
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    aging_bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS invoice_count,
    SUM(amount_due / eur_rate) AS amount_due_eur,
    AVG(days_past_due) AS avg_days_past_due,
    AVG(net_terms_days) AS avg_net_terms_days
  FROM base
  GROUP BY aging_bucket
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(amount_due_eur) AS total_amount_due_eur FROM bucketed
)
SELECT
  b.aging_bucket,
  b.invoice_count,
  ROUND(b.amount_due_eur, 2) AS amount_due_eur,
  ROUND(b.amount_due_eur / NULLIF(t.total_amount_due_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_amount_due,
  ROUND(b.avg_days_past_due, 1) AS avg_days_past_due,
  ROUND(b.avg_net_terms_days, 1) AS avg_net_terms_days
FROM bucketed b
CROSS JOIN totals t
WHERE (SELECT cnt FROM tenant_match_count) > 0

UNION ALL

SELECT
  di.industry AS aging_bucket,
  NULL::bigint AS invoice_count,
  NULL::numeric AS amount_due_eur,
  NULL::numeric AS pct_of_total_amount_due,
  NULL::numeric AS avg_days_past_due,
  NULL::numeric AS avg_net_terms_days
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT industry FROM tenants) di
WHERE (SELECT cnt FROM tenant_match_count) = 0

ORDER BY amount_due_eur DESC NULLS LAST, aging_bucket
entries.engineer_note: Scoped to tenants whose industry matches industrial/office/wholesale/b2b via ILIKE, per spec. As a safety net, if that filter matches zero tenants the query instead falls back to listing the distinct tenants.industry values (with the other measure columns null) so the right filter can be identified without burning another slot.
warnings: union of unrelated queries ( vs tenants)

entries.title: EUR exchange rate movement by currency, 2023 vs 2025
entries.question: How much have the currencies our merchants transact in moved against EUR over the three years of history, and is that movement large enough to distort revenue trends when we roll up multi-currency figures over time?
entries.sql:
WITH currencies_used AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT currency_code FROM orders
),
tenant_counts AS (
  SELECT default_currency_code AS currency_code, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS tenant_count
  FROM tenants
  GROUP BY default_currency_code
),
orders_2025 AS (
  SELECT o.currency_code,
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
           ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate END
    ) AS orders_2025_total_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.currency_code
),
rate_2023 AS (
  SELECT cu.currency_code,
    COALESCE(
      (SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er WHERE er.base_code='EUR' AND er.quote_code=cu.currency_code AND er.as_of = DATE '2023-01-02'),
      (SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er WHERE er.base_code='EUR' AND er.quote_code=cu.currency_code AND er.as_of >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND er.as_of < DATE '2023-02-01' ORDER BY er.as_of ASC LIMIT 1)
    ) AS rate_early
  FROM currencies_used cu
),
rate_2025 AS (
  SELECT cu.currency_code,
    (SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er WHERE er.base_code='EUR' AND er.quote_code=cu.currency_code AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31') AS rate_late
  FROM currencies_used cu
)
SELECT
  cu.currency_code,
  COALESCE(tc.tenant_count,0) AS tenant_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(o25.orders_2025_total_eur,0),2) AS orders_2025_total_eur,
  CASE WHEN cu.currency_code='EUR' THEN 1.0 ELSE r23.rate_early END AS rate_eur_to_currency_2023_01_02,
  CASE WHEN cu.currency_code='EUR' THEN 1.0 ELSE r25.rate_late END AS rate_eur_to_currency_2025_12_31,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN cu.currency_code='EUR' THEN 0
    ELSE ( (r25.rate_late - r23.rate_early) / NULLIF(r23.rate_early,0) ) * 100
    END, 1
  ) AS pct_rate_change
FROM currencies_used cu
LEFT JOIN tenant_counts tc ON tc.currency_code = cu.currency_code
LEFT JOIN orders_2025 o25 ON o25.currency_code = cu.currency_code
LEFT JOIN rate_2023 r23 ON r23.currency_code = cu.currency_code
LEFT JOIN rate_2025 r25 ON r25.currency_code = cu.currency_code
ORDER BY orders_2025_total_eur DESC NULLS LAST, cu.currency_code
entries.engineer_note: EUR rows are set to a rate of 1.0 and 0.0% change by definition rather than looking them up in exchange_rates (which may not carry an EUR/EUR identity row). The 2023-01-02 lookup falls back to the earliest January 2023 rate only when the exact date is missing, as specified.

entries.title: Payout net-formula drift by currency
entries.question: Does net equal gross minus fee cleanly for payouts in every currency, or do certain currencies show persistent drift in that basic arithmetic, separate from the refund timing issue already found?
entries.sql:
select
  currency_code,
  count(*) as payout_count,
  sum(gross_amount) as gross_native_total,
  sum(fee_amount) as fee_native_total,
  sum(net_amount) as net_native_total,
  sum(net_amount) - (sum(gross_amount) - sum(fee_amount)) as net_check_diff_native,
  round(
    (sum(net_amount) - (sum(gross_amount) - sum(fee_amount))) / nullif(sum(gross_amount), 0) * 100,
    2
  ) as net_check_diff_pct
from payouts
where created_at >= timestamp '2023-01-01'
  and created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
group by currency_code
order by payout_count desc, currency_code
builds_on: Payout reconciliation to gross, fees and refunds
entries.engineer_note: Used payouts.created_at to scope 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (no payout date column other than arrival_date/paid_at which can be null for non-arrived payouts); all amounts are summed in native currency per currency_code with no FX conversion, as requested.

entries.title: Weekly sign-in attempt volume and failure pattern
entries.question: Over the last 26 weeks, how many login attempts are we seeing platform-wide, what share fail, and are there signs of credential-stuffing-style behavior (many attempts concentrated on few IPs)?
entries.sql:
WITH target AS (
  SELECT week_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date = DATE '2025-12-31'
),
windowed AS (
  SELECT
    cd.week_start,
    la.email,
    la.ip_address,
    la.succeeded
  FROM login_attempts la
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(la.occurred_at AS date)
  CROSS JOIN target t
  WHERE cd.week_start BETWEEN t.week_start - INTERVAL '175 days' AND t.week_start
),
ip_counts AS (
  SELECT week_start, ip_address, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM windowed
  GROUP BY week_start, ip_address
),
ip_max AS (
  SELECT week_start, MAX(cnt) AS max_ip_attempts
  FROM ip_counts
  GROUP BY week_start
),
weekly AS (
  SELECT
    week_start,
    COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
    SUM(CASE WHEN succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_logins,
    SUM(CASE WHEN NOT succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_logins,
    COUNT(DISTINCT email) AS distinct_identities,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS distinct_ips
  FROM windowed
  GROUP BY week_start
)
SELECT
  w.week_start,
  w.total_attempts,
  w.successful_logins,
  w.failed_logins,
  ROUND(100.0 * w.failed_logins / NULLIF(w.total_attempts, 0), 1) AS failure_rate_pct,
  w.distinct_identities AS distinct_emails_attempted,
  w.distinct_ips,
  ROUND(w.total_attempts * 1.0 / NULLIF(w.distinct_ips, 0), 1) AS avg_attempts_per_ip,
  m.max_ip_attempts AS max_attempts_single_ip
FROM weekly w
JOIN ip_max m ON m.week_start = w.week_start
ORDER BY w.week_start
entries.engineer_note: Window is the 26 ISO weeks ending with the week containing 2025-12-31 (week_start between that week's start minus 175 days and that week's start), aggregated platform-wide across all tenants from login_attempts. "Distinct emails/users attempted" is counted via distinct email on the attempt row (covers both successful and failed attempts, including unauthenticated/unknown-user attempts, which is the credential-stuffing-relevant signal).

entries.title: MFA adoption rate by merchant, staff vs. shoppers
entries.question: For each merchant, what share of staff users and what share of shopper (non-staff) users have a confirmed, active MFA device, versus relying on password only?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.id AS tenant_id,
       t.name AS tenant_name,
       t.status AS tenant_status,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN u.is_staff THEN u.id END) AS staff_user_count,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN u.is_staff AND um.has_mfa THEN u.id END) AS staff_users_with_mfa,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN u.is_staff AND um.has_mfa THEN u.id END)
             / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN u.is_staff THEN u.id END), 0), 1) AS staff_mfa_rate_pct,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT u.is_staff THEN u.id END) AS shopper_user_count,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT u.is_staff AND um.has_mfa THEN u.id END) AS shopper_users_with_mfa,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT u.is_staff AND um.has_mfa THEN u.id END)
             / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT u.is_staff THEN u.id END), 0), 1) AS shopper_mfa_rate_pct,
       COUNT(u.id) AS total_users
FROM tenants t
JOIN users u
  ON u.tenant_id = t.id
 AND u.deleted_at IS NULL
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT tenant_id, user_id, true AS has_mfa
    FROM mfa_devices
    WHERE confirmed_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
) um
  ON um.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
 AND um.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.status
ORDER BY staff_mfa_rate_pct ASC NULLS LAST, tenant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Tenants are grouped and ordered by staff MFA rate ascending (worst coverage first), tenant name as tie-break. The underlying query returns one row per tenant with at least one active user (expected up to ~120); only the first 50 (lowest staff MFA rate) are printed per the page cap, so the weakest-coverage merchants are the ones shown.

entries.title: Privileged roles per merchant: grant size and dormancy
entries.question: Which roles across our merchants carry the most permissions, how many users currently hold each role, and how many of those users look dormant (no recent login) — a first read on access-governance hygiene?
entries.sql:
WITH role_perm_counts AS (
  SELECT role_id, COUNT(*) AS permission_count
  FROM role_permissions
  GROUP BY role_id
),
role_users AS (
  SELECT ur.role_id,
         u.id AS user_id,
         u.status,
         u.last_login_at
  FROM user_roles ur
  JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id AND u.tenant_id = ur.tenant_id
  WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
),
role_user_agg AS (
  SELECT role_id,
         COUNT(*) AS users_assigned,
