         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active') AS users_active,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active' AND (last_login_at IS NULL OR last_login_at < DATE '2025-10-05')) AS users_dormant,
         MAX(last_login_at) AS most_recent_login
  FROM role_users
  GROUP BY role_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  r.name AS role_name,
  r.is_system,
  rpc.permission_count,
  rua.users_assigned,
  rua.users_active,
  rua.users_dormant,
  rua.most_recent_login,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_qualifying_roles
FROM roles r
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
JOIN role_perm_counts rpc ON rpc.role_id = r.id
JOIN role_user_agg rua ON rua.role_id = r.id
ORDER BY rpc.permission_count DESC, rua.users_assigned DESC, t.name, r.name
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant+role, restricted to roles with ≥1 permission and ≥1 non-deleted assigned user, as requested. Added a window-function column `total_qualifying_roles` (count before the 50-row cap) so the full population size is visible on the printed page without a second query.

entries.title: Platform-wide MFA adoption trend by month, staff vs. shoppers
entries.question: What is the actual company-wide MFA adoption rate today for staff and for shoppers, and has it been improving or flat over the past year?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT month_label, MAX(calendar_date) AS month_end
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE year_num = 2025
  GROUP BY month_label
),
eligible_users AS (
  SELECT m.month_label, m.month_end, u.id AS user_id, u.is_staff
  FROM months m
  JOIN users u
    ON u.created_at <= m.month_end
   AND (u.deleted_at IS NULL OR u.deleted_at > m.month_end)
),
user_mfa AS (
  SELECT eu.month_label, eu.month_end, eu.user_id, eu.is_staff,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM mfa_devices md
      WHERE md.user_id = eu.user_id AND md.confirmed_at <= eu.month_end
    ) AS has_mfa
  FROM eligible_users eu
),
monthly_summary AS (
  SELECT month_label,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_staff) AS staff_users,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_staff AND has_mfa) AS staff_mfa_users,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_staff) AS shopper_users,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_staff AND has_mfa) AS shopper_mfa_users
  FROM user_mfa
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  month_label,
  staff_users,
  staff_mfa_users AS staff_users_with_mfa,
  ROUND(100.0 * staff_mfa_users / NULLIF(staff_users,0), 1) AS staff_mfa_rate_pct,
  shopper_users,
  shopper_mfa_users AS shopper_users_with_mfa,
  ROUND(100.0 * shopper_mfa_users / NULLIF(shopper_users,0), 1) AS shopper_mfa_rate_pct
FROM monthly_summary
ORDER BY month_label
builds_on: MFA adoption rate by merchant, staff vs. shoppers
entries.engineer_note: MFA presence is defined as any mfa_devices row with confirmed_at <= month end (one or more confirmed devices), regardless of whether the device was later removed, since mfa_devices has no deletion/status column; this matches the requested "confirmed MFA" definition.

entries.title: Login attempts by tenant during the week of 2025-11-24 spike
entries.question: The week of 2025-11-24 showed a 41% jump in total login attempts platform-wide versus the prior week — is that jump broad-based across many merchants (consistent with Black Friday/Cyber Monday shopping traffic) or concentrated in one or a few tenants with elevated failure rates or IP concentration (consistent with a credential-stuffing attempt)?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.status AS tenant_status,
  COUNT(*) AS total_login_attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN la.succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_logins,
  SUM(CASE WHEN NOT la.succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_logins,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN NOT la.succeeded THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS failure_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT la.email) AS distinct_emails_attempted,
  COUNT(DISTINCT la.ip_address) AS distinct_ip_addresses,
  (SELECT MAX(ip_count) FROM (
      SELECT COUNT(*) AS ip_count
      FROM login_attempts la2
      WHERE la2.tenant_id = la.tenant_id
        AND la2.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-24 00:00:00'
        AND la2.occurred_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-30 23:59:59'
      GROUP BY la2.ip_address
  ) ip_counts) AS max_attempts_single_ip,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (
      SELECT COUNT(*)
      FROM login_attempts la3
      WHERE la3.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-24 00:00:00'
        AND la3.occurred_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-30 23:59:59'
  ), 1) AS pct_of_platform_total
FROM login_attempts la
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = la.tenant_id
WHERE la.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-24 00:00:00'
  AND la.occurred_at <= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-30 23:59:59'
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.status, la.tenant_id
ORDER BY total_login_attempts DESC, tenant_name ASC
builds_on: Weekly sign-in attempt volume and failure pattern
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant with at least one login attempt in the 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-30 window; with ~120 tenants on the platform this should return well under the 50-row cap, but the exact row count will be visible on the printed report (dry runs can't confirm counts against real data).

entries.title: Privileged role landscape by role name, company-wide
entries.question: Beyond the default 'Owner' role (which filled the entire first page of the prior report), what other roles across merchants carry significant permissions, how widely are they assigned, and how dormant are the users holding them?
entries.sql:
WITH role_instance AS (
  SELECT r.id AS role_id, r.tenant_id, r.name, r.is_system,
         COUNT(DISTINCT rp.permission_id) AS perm_count
  FROM roles r
  JOIN role_permissions rp ON rp.role_id = r.id
  GROUP BY r.id, r.tenant_id, r.name, r.is_system
),
assigned AS (
  SELECT ur.role_id,
         COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) AS assigned_users,
         COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) FILTER (WHERE u.status = 'active' AND (u.last_login_at IS NULL OR u.last_login_at < DATE '2025-10-05')) AS dormant_users
  FROM user_roles ur
  JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id AND u.tenant_id = ur.tenant_id
  WHERE u.deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY ur.role_id
),
qualifying AS (
  SELECT ri.tenant_id, ri.name, ri.is_system, ri.perm_count,
         a.assigned_users, a.dormant_users
  FROM role_instance ri
  JOIN assigned a ON a.role_id = ri.role_id
  WHERE ri.perm_count >= 1 AND a.assigned_users >= 1
)
SELECT
  name AS role_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS tenant_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_system THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_is_system,
  ROUND(AVG(perm_count), 1) AS avg_permission_count,
  MAX(perm_count) AS max_permission_count,
  SUM(assigned_users) AS total_users_assigned,
  SUM(dormant_users) AS total_users_dormant,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(dormant_users) / NULLIF(SUM(assigned_users), 0), 1) AS dormant_rate_pct
FROM qualifying
WHERE name <> 'Owner'
GROUP BY name
ORDER BY total_users_assigned DESC, role_name
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Privileged roles per merchant: grant size and dormancy
entries.engineer_note: Excluded role_name = 'Owner' per the question's framing (it was the subject of the prior per-tenant report); the remaining population is the same qualifying set (role instances with ≥1 permission and ≥1 non-deleted assigned user), now aggregated by role name. The printed report's row-count footer will show how many distinct role names qualified in total.

entries.title: Dormant users holding Owner or Administrator access
entries.question: Specifically which accounts currently hold the two most powerful roles (Owner, Administrator) but haven't logged in recently — the concrete list of privileged accounts that look stale?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.status AS tenant_status,
  r.name AS role_name,
  u.email AS user_email,
  u.status AS user_status,
  CASE WHEN u.last_login_at IS NULL THEN 'never' ELSE CAST(u.last_login_at AS varchar) END AS last_login,
  CASE WHEN u.last_login_at IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(u.last_login_at AS date)) END AS days_since_last_login,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(u.created_at AS date)) AS account_age_days,
  COUNT(*) OVER() AS total_qualifying_rows
FROM user_roles ur
JOIN roles r ON r.id = ur.role_id
JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = u.tenant_id
WHERE r.name IN ('Owner','Administrator')
  AND u.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND u.status = 'active'
  AND (u.last_login_at IS NULL OR u.last_login_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-05')
ORDER BY u.last_login_at ASC NULLS FIRST, t.name ASC, u.email ASC, r.name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Privileged roles per merchant: grant size and dormancy
Privileged role landscape by role name, company-wide
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per (user, role) since a user can hold both Owner and Administrator and role_name is a report column; days_since_last_login is left NULL for 'never' rather than a sentinel number, with never-logged-in users sorted first via last_login_at ASC NULLS FIRST (most stale). total_qualifying_rows is a window-count column showing how many rows matched in total, since more than 50 may qualify.

entries.title: API key hygiene by merchant
entries.question: How many API keys does each merchant have, how many are active, and how many of those active keys look abandoned (never used, or unused for a long time)?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.status AS tenant_status,
  COUNT(ak.id) AS total_api_keys,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ak.status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_api_keys,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ak.status IN ('revoked','expired') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS revoked_or_expired_keys,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ak.status = 'active' AND ak.last_used_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_never_used,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ak.status = 'active' AND ak.last_used_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-05 00:00:00' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_unused_90d,
  MAX(CASE WHEN ak.status = 'active' THEN DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE) ELSE NULL END) AS oldest_active_key_age_days,
  COALESCE(sa.service_account_count, 0) AS service_accounts_count
FROM api_keys ak
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ak.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS service_account_count
  FROM service_accounts
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) sa ON sa.tenant_id = t.id
GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.status, sa.service_account_count
ORDER BY active_never_used DESC, active_unused_90d DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant (grouped internally by t.id for correctness even though not printed). "Active keys unused 90+ days" excludes never-used keys (NULL last_used_at doesn't satisfy the < comparison), so the two abandonment buckets are mutually exclusive. Report prints up to 50 of the tenants that have at least one api_keys row; total row count is shown on the printed report per house standard.

entries.title: Audit log coverage by action type
entries.question: Is the audit trail (audit_log) consistently capturing sensitive actions across all merchants and over time, or are some action types thin, recent-only, or concentrated in a handful of tenants — could we credibly reconstruct 'who did what, when' if asked?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  a.action AS action_type,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-05' AND a.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01') AS events_last_90_days,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT a.tenant_id) / t.tenant_count, 1) AS pct_of_tenants,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.actor_user_id) AS distinct_actor_users,
  MIN(a.occurred_at) AS earliest_occurred_at,
  MAX(a.occurred_at) AS most_recent_occurred_at
FROM audit_log a
CROSS JOIN (SELECT COUNT(*) AS tenant_count FROM tenants) t
WHERE a.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND a.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY a.action, t.tenant_count
ORDER BY total_events DESC, action_type ASC
entries.engineer_note: Tenant denominator is computed live as COUNT(*) FROM tenants rather than hardcoded 120, so the % column will self-correct if the actual tenant count differs; please flag if you want it pinned to exactly 120 instead.

entries.title: Audit-trail coverage of actual soft-deletions, by entity table
entries.question: For tables where the app actually soft-deletes rows (deleted_at), does audit_log's 'delete' action consistently capture those deletions, or is there a real gap between what was deleted and what the audit trail shows?
entries.sql:
SELECT entity_table,
 total_soft_deleted,
 matching_audit_rows,
 CASE WHEN total_soft_deleted = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE ROUND(LEAST(matching_audit_rows::numeric / total_soft_deleted * 100, 100), 1)
 END AS coverage_rate_pct,
 distinct_tenants,
 earliest_deleted_at,
 most_recent_deleted_at
FROM (
  SELECT 'products' AS entity_table,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL) AS total_soft_deleted,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'delete' AND entity_table = 'products') AS matching_audit_rows,
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM products WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL) AS distinct_tenants,
    (SELECT min(deleted_at) FROM products WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL) AS earliest_deleted_at,
    (SELECT max(deleted_at) FROM products WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL) AS most_recent_deleted_at
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'users',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'delete' AND entity_table = 'users'),
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT min(deleted_at) FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT max(deleted_at) FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'discounts',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM discounts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'delete' AND entity_table = 'discounts'),
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM discounts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT min(deleted_at) FROM discounts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT max(deleted_at) FROM discounts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'coupons',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM coupons WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'delete' AND entity_table = 'coupons'),
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM coupons WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT min(deleted_at) FROM coupons WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT max(deleted_at) FROM coupons WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'campaigns',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM campaigns WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'delete' AND entity_table = 'campaigns'),
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM campaigns WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT min(deleted_at) FROM campaigns WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT max(deleted_at) FROM campaigns WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'promotions',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM promotions WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT count(*) FROM audit_log WHERE action = 'delete' AND entity_table = 'promotions'),
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM promotions WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT min(deleted_at) FROM promotions WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL),
    (SELECT max(deleted_at) FROM promotions WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL)
) t
ORDER BY coverage_rate_pct ASC, entity_table ASC
builds_on: Audit log coverage by action type
entries.engineer_note: Coverage rate is capped at 100% per the request; since data only spans 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31, no additional date filter was needed on deleted_at as all rows already fall in that window. If any table's matching_audit_rows exceeds total_soft_deleted, the rate will show 100% but that itself signals an anomaly worth flagging.

entries.title: Active API key age distribution (rotation hygiene)
entries.question: Platform-wide, how old are our currently active API keys — do we have a meaningful population of long-lived, apparently never-rotated credentials, even though usage patterns look healthy?
entries.sql:
with active_keys as (
  select
    id,
    tenant_id,
    created_at,
    last_used_at,
    date '2026-01-05' - created_at::date as age_days
  from api_keys
  where status = 'active'
),
bucketed as (
  select
    *,
    case
      when age_days < 90 then '1 - under 90 days'
      when age_days < 365 then '2 - 90 days-1 year'
      when age_days < 730 then '3 - 1-2 years'
      when age_days < 1460 then '4 - 2-4 years'
      else '5 - 4+ years'
    end as bucket_sort
  from active_keys
),
totals as (
  select count(*) as total_active from bucketed
)
select
  case b.bucket_sort
    when '1 - under 90 days' then 'under 90 days'
    when '2 - 90 days-1 year' then '90 days-1 year'
    when '3 - 1-2 years' then '1-2 years'
    when '4 - 2-4 years' then '2-4 years'
    when '5 - 4+ years' then '4+ years'
  end as age_bucket,
  count(*) as active_key_count,
  round(100.0 * count(*) / t.total_active, 1) as share_pct,
  count(distinct b.tenant_id) as distinct_tenants,
  max(b.age_days) as oldest_key_age_days,
  count(*) filter (where b.last_used_at is null) as never_used_count,
  count(*) filter (where b.last_used_at is not null and b.last_used_at < timestamp '2025-10-05') as unused_90d_plus_count
from bucketed b
cross join totals t
group by b.bucket_sort, t.total_active
order by b.bucket_sort
builds_on: API key hygiene by merchant
entries.engineer_note: Age is computed as 2026-01-05 minus created_at (date), per the fixed reference date in the request. "Unused 90+ days" counts keys with a non-null last_used_at before 2025-10-05; never-used keys are reported separately in their own column rather than folded into this count.

entries.title: Compliance event resolution health by severity
entries.question: When compliance_events flags something (suspicious access, retention overruns, failed DSAR SLAs, etc.), is it actually getting resolved, or are flagged incidents piling up unresolved — is existing monitoring a real control or just theoretical?
entries.sql:
SELECT
    severity,
    COUNT(*) AS total_events,
    SUM(CASE WHEN resolved THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS resolved_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN NOT resolved THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unresolved_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN resolved THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS resolution_rate_pct,
    MAX(CASE WHEN NOT resolved THEN DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(occurred_at AS date) END) AS oldest_unresolved_age_days,
    MAX(occurred_at) AS most_recent_occurred_at
FROM compliance_events
GROUP BY severity
ORDER BY unresolved_count DESC, severity ASC
entries.engineer_note: Report covers all tenants combined (platform-wide), since the question is about whether monitoring is a real control overall, not per merchant. All-time range is naturally bounded by the data (2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31); no explicit date filter was needed since compliance_events has no earlier/later rows.

entries.title: Data subject requests: monthly volume, closure time, and overdue backlog
entries.question: How many access/erasure/portability/rectification/restriction requests are we receiving each month, how long do they typically take to close, and how many are overdue or still open?
entries.sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    tcal.month_start AS month_start,
    tcal.month_label AS month_label
  FROM calendar_days tcal
  WHERE tcal.month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND tcal.month_start <= DATE '2025-12-01'
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS requests_received
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS access_requests_received
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  WHERE tdsr.request_type = 'access'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS erasure_requests_received
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  WHERE tdsr.request_type = 'erasure'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS portability_requests_received
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  WHERE tdsr.request_type = 'portability'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
),
t5 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS rectification_restriction_requests_received
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  WHERE tdsr.request_type IN ('rectification', 'restriction')
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
),
t6 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS completed_count
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  WHERE tdsr.completed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
),
t7 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (
      ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tdsr.completed_at - tdsr.received_at)) / 86400.0
    ) AS median_days_to_close
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  WHERE tdsr.completed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
),
t8 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS still_open_count
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  WHERE tdsr.completed_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
),
t9 AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS overdue_count
  FROM data_subject_requests tdsr
  WHERE tdsr.completed_at IS NULL
    AND tdsr.due_at IS NOT NULL
    AND tdsr.due_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-05 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', tdsr.received_at)::date
)
SELECT
  t0.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(t1.requests_received, 0) AS requests_received,
  COALESCE(t2.access_requests_received, 0) AS access_requests_received,
  COALESCE(t3.erasure_requests_received, 0) AS erasure_requests_received,
  COALESCE(t4.portability_requests_received, 0) AS portability_requests_received,
  COALESCE(t5.rectification_restriction_requests_received, 0) AS rectification_restriction_requests_received,
  COALESCE(t6.completed_count, 0) AS completed_count,
  ROUND(t7.median_days_to_close, 1) AS median_days_to_close,
  COALESCE(t8.still_open_count, 0) AS still_open_count,
  COALESCE(t9.overdue_count, 0) AS overdue_count
FROM t0
LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN t4 ON t4.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN t5 ON t5.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN t6 ON t6.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN t7 ON t7.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN t8 ON t8.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN t9 ON t9.month_start = t0.month_start
ORDER BY t0.month_start ASC
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide monthly report, 36 rows (2023-01 through 2025-12), exactly as specified; median days to close computed as fractional days (EPOCH/86400) rounded to 1 decimal, null for months with zero completions.

entries.title: Consent trend by purpose and month: grants, withdrawals, and net opt-in rate
entries.question: How has the mix of granted vs. withdrawn vs. never-given consent changed over time, by purpose?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  metrics.purpose AS purpose,
  metrics.month_label AS month,
  metrics.grants_recorded AS grants_recorded,
  metrics.withdrawals_recorded AS withdrawals_recorded,
  metrics.expirations_recorded AS expirations_recorded,
  metrics.users_with_any_record AS users_with_any_record,
  metrics.net_active_optins AS net_active_optins,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN metrics.users_with_any_record = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE 100.0 * metrics.net_active_optins / metrics.users_with_any_record
    END, 1) AS active_optin_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    p.purpose AS purpose,
    m.month_start AS month_start,
    m.month_label AS month_label,
    m.month_end AS month_end,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM consent_records cr
      WHERE cr.purpose = p.purpose AND cr.status = 'granted'
        AND CAST(cr.occurred_at AS DATE) BETWEEN m.month_start AND m.month_end) AS grants_recorded,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM consent_records cr
      WHERE cr.purpose = p.purpose AND cr.status = 'withdrawn'
        AND CAST(cr.occurred_at AS DATE) BETWEEN m.month_start AND m.month_end) AS withdrawals_recorded,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM consent_records cr
      WHERE cr.purpose = p.purpose AND cr.status = 'expired'
        AND CAST(cr.occurred_at AS DATE) BETWEEN m.month_start AND m.month_end) AS expirations_recorded,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cr.user_id) FROM consent_records cr
      WHERE cr.purpose = p.purpose AND CAST(cr.occurred_at AS DATE) <= m.month_end) AS users_with_any_record,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
        SELECT cr.user_id AS user_id, cr.status AS status,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cr.tenant_id, cr.user_id, cr.purpose ORDER BY cr.occurred_at DESC) AS rn
        FROM consent_records cr
        WHERE cr.purpose = p.purpose AND CAST(cr.occurred_at AS DATE) <= m.month_end
     ) ranked WHERE ranked.rn = 1 AND ranked.status = 'granted') AS net_active_optins
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT purpose FROM consent_records) p
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT month_start, month_label, MAX(calendar_date) AS month_end
    FROM calendar_days
    WHERE year_num BETWEEN 2023 AND 2025
    GROUP BY month_start, month_label
  ) m
) metrics
ORDER BY metrics.purpose, metrics.month_start
entries.engineer_note: Active opt-in rate is left NULL for any (purpose, month) with zero users-with-any-record as of month end, since the ratio is undefined there; all other logic follows the request exactly (purposes taken from distinct consent_records.purpose, months 2023-01..2025-12 from calendar_days).

entries.title: Compliance events: monthly volume and resolution time by severity
entries.question: How many compliance incidents are being flagged each month by severity, how quickly are they resolved, and is an unresolved backlog building up?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  strftime(date_trunc('month', occurred_at), '%Y-%m') as month,
  severity,
  count(*) as incidents_detected,
  count(*) filter (where resolved) as resolved_count,
  count(*) filter (where not resolved) as unresolved_count,
  round(
    (percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by extract(epoch from (resolved_at - occurred_at))/86400.0) filter (where resolved))::numeric,
    1
  ) as median_days_to_resolve,
  count(*) filter (
    where not resolved
      and (timestamp '2026-01-05' - occurred_at) > interval '30 days'
  ) as unresolved_over_30d
FROM compliance_events
WHERE occurred_at >= timestamp '2023-01-01'
  AND occurred_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide (no tenant filter) as requested. median_days_to_resolve is computed as the median of (resolved_at - occurred_at) in fractional days over resolved=true rows only; months/severities with zero resolved incidents will show a null median rather than zero.

entries.title: Currently open data subject requests: age and overdue detail
entries.question: Which specific data subject requests are still open right now, how old are they, and which are overdue?
entries.sql:
WITH open_requests AS (
    SELECT
        dsr.public_id,
        dsr.tenant_id,
        dsr.request_type,
        dsr.status,
        dsr.received_at,
        dsr.due_at,
        dsr.assigned_to_user_id
    FROM data_subject_requests dsr
    WHERE dsr.completed_at IS NULL
),
enriched AS (
    SELECT
        r.public_id AS request_public_id,
        t.name AS tenant_name,
        r.request_type,
        r.status,
        CAST(r.received_at AS date) AS received_date,
        CAST(r.due_at AS date) AS due_date,
        DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(r.received_at AS date) AS days_since_received,
        CASE
            WHEN r.due_at IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN DATE '2026-01-05' < CAST(r.due_at AS date) THEN 0
            ELSE DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(r.due_at AS date)
        END AS days_overdue,
        COALESCE(u.full_name, 'unassigned') AS assigned_to
    FROM open_requests r
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = r.assigned_to_user_id
)
SELECT
    request_public_id,
    tenant_name,
    request_type,
    status,
    received_date AS received_at,
    due_date AS due_at,
    days_since_received,
    days_overdue,
    assigned_to
FROM enriched
ORDER BY received_at ASC, request_public_id ASC
builds_on: Data subject requests: monthly volume, closure time, and overdue backlog
entries.engineer_note: Days overdue is NULL when due_at is not set, and 0 when due_at is in the future (not yet overdue); all date math uses the literal 2026-01-05 reporting date as requested.

entries.title: Marketing-email consent opt-in trend, full history
entries.question: Has the marketing-email opt-in rate meaningfully changed over the full 3-year history, and did the early decline continue or stabilize?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT month_label, MIN(calendar_date) AS month_start, MAX(calendar_date) AS month_end
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY month_label
),
flow AS (
  SELECT cd.month_label,
         SUM(CASE WHEN cr.status = 'granted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS grants,
         SUM(CASE WHEN cr.status = 'withdrawn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS withdrawals,
         SUM(CASE WHEN cr.status = 'expired' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS expirations
  FROM calendar_days cd
  JOIN consent_records cr
    ON cr.occurred_at::date = cd.calendar_date
   AND cr.purpose = 'marketing_email'
  WHERE cd.calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY cd.month_label
),
snapshot_base AS (
  SELECT m.month_label,
         cr.user_id,
         cr.status,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.month_label, cr.user_id ORDER BY cr.occurred_at DESC, cr.id DESC) AS rn
  FROM months m
  JOIN consent_records cr
    ON cr.purpose = 'marketing_email'
   AND cr.occurred_at < (m.month_end + INTERVAL '1 day')
),
monthly_active AS (
  SELECT month_label,
         COUNT(*) AS users_with_consent,
         SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'granted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS net_active
  FROM snapshot_base
  WHERE rn = 1
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  m.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(f.grants, 0) AS grants_recorded,
  COALESCE(f.withdrawals, 0) AS withdrawals_recorded,
  COALESCE(f.expirations, 0) AS expirations_recorded,
  COALESCE(ma.users_with_consent, 0) AS users_with_any_consent,
  COALESCE(ma.net_active, 0) AS net_active_opt_ins,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(ma.net_active, 0) / NULLIF(ma.users_with_consent, 0), 1) AS active_opt_in_rate_pct
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN flow f ON f.month_label = m.month_label
LEFT JOIN monthly_active ma ON ma.month_label = m.month_label
ORDER BY m.month_label ASC
builds_on: Consent trend by purpose and month: grants, withdrawals, and net opt-in rate
entries.engineer_note: All 36 months (2023-01 through 2025-12) are included, platform-wide across all tenants, purpose fixed to marketing_email; effective status as of each month end is the latest consent_records row per user with occurred_at on or before that month's last day.

entries.title: Retention policy inventory: what rules exist and where
entries.question: What data-retention policies has Tidewick actually configured, for which entity tables, with what retention windows and expiry actions?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  rp.name AS policy_name,
  rp.entity_schema,
  rp.entity_table,
  rp.retention_days,
  rp.action_on_expiry,
  rp.is_active,
  rp.last_run_at
FROM retention_policies rp
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = rp.tenant_id
ORDER BY rp.entity_table, t.name, rp.id
entries.engineer_note: Lists every configured retention policy (active and inactive), one row per policy, ordered by entity table then tenant name, as requested. Note: this report may exceed 50 printed rows if there are more than 50 policies across all tenants; the handbook caps printed rows at 50, so the printed report will note total row count if truncated.

entries.title: Data subject request status audit: does completed_at reflect true closure?
entries.question: Across all data subject requests (not just currently open ones), which status values leave completed_at null, and is that a systemic pattern (e.g. all rejections) or isolated to a few records?
entries.sql:
select
  status,
  count(*) as total_requests,
  count(completed_at) as completed_count,
  count(*) - count(completed_at) as not_completed_count,
  min(received_at) as oldest_received_at,
  max(received_at) as newest_received_at,
  avg(case when completed_at is null then date(DATE '2026-01-05') - date(received_at) end) as avg_age_days_not_completed
from data_subject_requests
group by status
order by total_requests desc, status asc
builds_on: Currently open data subject requests: age and overdue detail
entries.engineer_note: One row per data_subject_requests.status across full history, platform-wide (no tenant filter, as requested). avg_age_days_not_completed is null when every row of that status already has completed_at set.

entries.title: Retention policy landscape: distinct rules by entity table
entries.question: What retention rules actually exist across entity tables, collapsing the one-row-per-tenant duplication, so I can see real coverage and variation?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.entity_schema AS entity_schema,
  t0.entity_table AS entity_table,
  t0.retention_days AS retention_days,
  t0.action_on_expiry AS action_on_expiry,
  COUNT(DISTINCT t0.tenant_id) AS tenant_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t0.is_active THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS active_count,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t0.last_run_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS never_run_count
FROM retention_policies t0
GROUP BY
  t0.entity_schema,
  t0.entity_table,
  t0.retention_days,
  t0.action_on_expiry
ORDER BY
  t0.entity_table ASC,
  tenant_count DESC,
  t0.entity_schema ASC,
  t0.retention_days ASC,
  t0.action_on_expiry ASC
builds_on: Retention policy inventory: what rules exist and where
entries.engineer_note: Grain is (entity_schema, entity_table, retention_days, action_on_expiry) as requested; active_count and never_run_count are counts of policy rows (one per tenant) within that combination that are active / never run, not distinct tenant counts, since a tenant could in principle differ on those flags while matching the same rule shape.

entries.title: Legal holds: active scope, coverage, and staleness
entries.question: How many legal holds are currently active, what do they cover, and are any stale (placed long ago with no recent review or release)?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
       lh.name AS hold_name,
       LEFT(lh.reason, 200) AS reason_truncated,
       lh.entity_table AS entity_table_scope,
       lh.subject_user_id,
       lh.is_active,
       CAST(lh.placed_at AS date) AS placed_at_date,
       CAST(lh.released_at AS date) AS released_at_date,
       CASE WHEN lh.is_active THEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lh.placed_at AS date)) END AS days_since_placed
FROM legal_holds lh
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = lh.tenant_id
ORDER BY lh.is_active DESC, lh.placed_at ASC, lh.id ASC
entries.engineer_note: Query returns every legal_holds row (active first, oldest placed_at first) with no artificial LIMIT; the report pipeline's standard 50-row cap and total-row note will indicate whether a narrower follow-up (e.g. active-only or per-tenant) is needed. Reason text truncated to 200 characters.

entries.title: Linking rejected erasure requests to active legal holds
entries.question: Do the 3 long-open 'rejected' data subject requests correspond to the same shopper and tenant as the 3 active legal holds for payment disputes?
entries.sql:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT
    dsr.id AS dsr_id,
    dsr.public_id AS dsar_public_id,
    dsr.tenant_id AS dsr_tenant_id,
    dsr.subject_user_id AS dsar_subject_user_id,
    dsr.request_type AS dsar_request_type,
    dsr.received_at AS dsar_received_at,
    lh.id AS lh_id,
    lh.name AS legal_hold_name,
    lh.subject_user_id AS legal_hold_subject_user_id,
    lh.reason AS legal_hold_reason,
    lh.is_active AS legal_hold_is_active,
    lh.placed_at AS legal_hold_placed_at,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY dsr.id
      ORDER BY ABS(COALESCE(DATE(lh.placed_at) - DATE(dsr.received_at), 999999))
    ) AS rn
  FROM data_subject_requests dsr
  LEFT JOIN legal_holds lh
    ON lh.tenant_id = dsr.tenant_id
   AND (
        (dsr.subject_user_id IS NOT NULL AND lh.subject_user_id = dsr.subject_user_id)
        OR
        (dsr.subject_user_id IS NULL AND ABS(DATE(lh.placed_at) - DATE(dsr.received_at)) <= 3)
   )
  WHERE dsr.status = 'rejected'
)
SELECT
  j.dsar_public_id,
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  j.dsar_subject_user_id,
  j.dsar_request_type,
  DATE(j.dsar_received_at) AS dsar_received_at,
  j.legal_hold_name,
  j.legal_hold_subject_user_id,
  LEFT(j.legal_hold_reason, 200) AS legal_hold_reason,
  j.legal_hold_is_active,
  DATE(j.legal_hold_placed_at) AS legal_hold_placed_at,
  (DATE(j.legal_hold_placed_at) - DATE(j.dsar_received_at)) AS days_between,
  CASE
    WHEN j.lh_id IS NULL THEN 'no match'
    WHEN j.dsar_subject_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'subject_user_id match'
    ELSE 'tenant + date window fallback'
  END AS join_strategy
FROM joined j
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = j.dsr_tenant_id
WHERE j.rn = 1
ORDER BY j.dsar_received_at ASC, j.dsar_public_id ASC
builds_on: Currently open data subject requests: age and overdue detail
Data subject request status audit: does completed_at reflect true closure?
Legal holds: active scope, coverage, and staleness
entries.engineer_note: Join tries the exact tenant_id + subject_user_id match first; for any dsar row where subject_user_id is null it automatically falls back to tenant_id-only matching against legal_holds placed within 3 days of received_at, picking the closest-dated hold as the candidate (join_strategy column shows which path was used, or 'no match' if neither found a hold). Reason text truncated to 200 chars for page width.

entries.title: email_log actual retention vs. the stated 730-day delete policy
entries.question: Since email_log's retention policy is configured but inactive and has never run for any tenant, how much email data are we actually still holding well past the stated 730-day window?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  strftime(t0.month_start, '%Y-%m') AS month,
  t0.email_count AS emails_logged,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - t0.month_start) AS days_old_as_of_2026_01_05,
  CASE WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - t0.month_start) > 730 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS exceeds_730_day_retention
FROM (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', t1.created_at)::date AS month_start, COUNT(*) AS email_count
  FROM email_log t1
  WHERE t1.created_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND t1.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', t1.created_at)
) t0
ORDER BY t0.month_start ASC
builds_on: Retention policy landscape: distinct rules by entity table
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide monthly counts from email_log.created_at, Jan 2023–Dec 2025 (36 rows). "Days old" is measured from each month's start to 2026-01-05 as requested, so the flag is conservative (actual oldest/newest rows within a month could differ by up to ~30 days).

entries.title: audit_log actual archiving vs. the stated 730-day archive policy
entries.question: audit_log's retention policy looks healthy on paper (active, last run 2025-12-31) — but are rows older than 730 days actually leaving the live table as the 'archive' action implies?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  strftime(date_trunc('month', occurred_at), '%Y-%m') AS month,
  COUNT(*) AS rows_in_live_table,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date) AS days_old_as_of_report_date,
  CASE WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - date_trunc('month', occurred_at)::date) > 730 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS exceeds_730_day_retention
FROM audit_log
WHERE occurred_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', occurred_at)
ORDER BY date_trunc('month', occurred_at) ASC
builds_on: Retention policy landscape: distinct rules by entity table
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide (all tenants) monthly count of audit_log rows still in the live table, with age-from-month-start and the >730-day retention flag computed against the literal report date 2026-01-05. 36 rows (2023-01 through 2025-12).

entries.title: 2025 Background Job Reliability by Month
entries.question: How did background job failure rates and run durations trend across 2025?
entries.sql:
select
  date_trunc('month', queued_at)::date as month,
  count(*) as total_job_runs,
  count(*) filter (where status = 'failed') as failed_runs,
  round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where status = 'failed') / nullif(count(*), 0), 2) as failure_rate_pct,
  count(*) filter (where status = 'cancelled') as cancelled_runs,
  round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where status = 'cancelled') / nullif(count(*), 0), 2) as cancelled_rate_pct,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (finished_at - started_at))) filter (where started_at is not null and finished_at is not null), 1) as avg_duration_seconds,
  round(percentile_cont(0.95) within group (order by extract(epoch from (finished_at - started_at))) filter (where started_at is not null and finished_at is not null)) as p95_duration_seconds
from job_runs
where queued_at >= date '2025-01-01' and queued_at < date '2026-01-01'
group by 1
order by 1 asc
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide (all tenants) monthly rollup of job_runs for 2025; duration stats computed only over runs with both started_at and finished_at set.

entries.title: Merchants Hit Hardest by Job Failures, 2025
entries.question: Which merchants had the most background job failures in 2025, and does it track with order volume?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name as tenant_name,
  jr.total_job_runs_2025,
  jr.failed_runs_2025,
  round(jr.failed_runs_2025 * 100.0 / jr.total_job_runs_2025, 1) as failure_rate_pct,
  round(jr.avg_duration_seconds_failed, 1) as avg_duration_seconds_failed,
  coalesce(o.total_orders_2025, 0) as total_orders_2025,
  case when coalesce(o.total_orders_2025, 0) = 0 then null
       else round(jr.failed_runs_2025 / o.total_orders_2025 * 1000.0, 1)
  end as failed_runs_per_1000_orders
FROM tenants t
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    count(*) as total_job_runs_2025,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') as failed_runs_2025,
    avg(duration_ms / 1000.0) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') as avg_duration_seconds_failed
  FROM job_runs
  WHERE queued_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND queued_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) jr ON jr.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as total_orders_2025
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) o ON o.tenant_id = t.id
ORDER BY jr.failed_runs_2025 DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 20
entries.engineer_note: avg_duration_seconds_failed is computed from job_runs.duration_ms/1000 (the only duration field available), averaged over failed runs only; failed_runs_per_1000_orders is left blank (NULL) when a tenant has zero 2025 orders, per the request.

entries.title: 2025 Internal Health Check Reliability by Month
entries.question: How did the rate of failed internal health checks trend across 2025?
entries.sql:
with checks_2025 as (
  select
    date_trunc('month', checked_at) as month_start,
    is_healthy,
    latency_ms,
    component
  from system_health_checks
  where checked_at >= date '2025-01-01'
    and checked_at < date '2026-01-01'
),
monthly_agg as (
  select
    month_start,
    count(*) as total_checks,
    count(*) filter (where is_healthy = false) as unhealthy_checks,
    round(avg(latency_ms))::int as avg_latency_ms,
    count(distinct component) as distinct_components_checked
  from checks_2025
  group by month_start
)
select
  strftime(month_start, '%Y-%m') as month,
  total_checks,
  unhealthy_checks,
  round(100.0 * unhealthy_checks / nullif(total_checks, 0), 2) as unhealthy_rate_pct,
  avg_latency_ms,
  distinct_components_checked
from monthly_agg
order by month_start asc
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide monthly rollup of system_health_checks for 2025, one row per month with 12 rows total; avg_latency_ms averages over non-null latency_ms values only.

entries.title: 2025 Q4 Weekly Job Reliability and Lateness
entries.question: Within the window job_runs actually covers (Oct-Dec 2025), how did failure rates and job lateness (queue delay, not just run duration) trend week by week?
entries.sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT
    t0a.id AS job_run_id,
    t0a.status AS status,
    t0a.queued_at AS queued_at,
    t0a.started_at AS started_at,
    t0a.finished_at AS finished_at,
    t0b.week_start AS week_start
  FROM job_runs t0a
  JOIN calendar_days t0b
    ON t0b.calendar_date = CAST(t0a.queued_at AS date)
  WHERE t0a.queued_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND t0a.queued_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT t1a.week_start AS week_start, COUNT(*) AS total_job_runs
  FROM t0 t1a
  GROUP BY t1a.week_start
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT t2a.week_start AS week_start, COUNT(*) AS failed_runs
  FROM t0 t2a
  WHERE t2a.status = 'failed'
  GROUP BY t2a.week_start
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    t3a.week_start AS week_start,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t3a.started_at - t3a.queued_at))) AS avg_queue_delay_seconds
  FROM t0 t3a
  WHERE t3a.started_at IS NOT NULL AND t3a.queued_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t3a.week_start
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT
    t4a.week_start AS week_start,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t4a.started_at - t4a.queued_at))) AS p95_queue_delay_seconds
  FROM t0 t4a
  WHERE t4a.started_at IS NOT NULL AND t4a.queued_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t4a.week_start
),
t5 AS (
  SELECT
    t5a.week_start AS week_start,
    COUNT(*) AS delay_denom,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t5a.started_at - t5a.queued_at)) > 300) AS over_5min_count
  FROM t0 t5a
  WHERE t5a.started_at IS NOT NULL AND t5a.queued_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t5a.week_start
),
t6 AS (
  SELECT
    t6a.week_start AS week_start,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t6a.finished_at - t6a.started_at))) AS avg_duration_seconds
  FROM t0 t6a
  WHERE t6a.finished_at IS NOT NULL AND t6a.started_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t6a.week_start
),
t_weeks AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t0.week_start AS week_start FROM t0
)
SELECT
  t_weeks.week_start AS week_start,
  COALESCE(t1.total_job_runs, 0) AS total_job_runs,
  COALESCE(t2.failed_runs, 0) AS failed_runs,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.failed_runs, 0)::numeric * 100.0 / NULLIF(t1.total_job_runs, 0), 1) AS failure_rate_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t3.avg_queue_delay_seconds, 0)::numeric, 1) AS avg_queue_delay_seconds,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t4.p95_queue_delay_seconds, 0)::numeric, 0) AS p95_queue_delay_seconds,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t5.over_5min_count, 0)::numeric * 100.0 / NULLIF(t5.delay_denom, 0), 1) AS pct_jobs_queue_delay_over_5min,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t6.avg_duration_seconds, 0)::numeric, 1) AS avg_duration_seconds
FROM t_weeks
LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.week_start = t_weeks.week_start
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.week_start = t_weeks.week_start
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.week_start = t_weeks.week_start
LEFT JOIN t4 ON t4.week_start = t_weeks.week_start
LEFT JOIN t5 ON t5.week_start = t_weeks.week_start
LEFT JOIN t6 ON t6.week_start = t_weeks.week_start
ORDER BY t_weeks.week_start ASC
builds_on: 2025 Background Job Reliability by Month
entries.engineer_note: Weeks are grouped by calendar_days.week_start (ISO week of queued_at), so the first and last printed weeks may extend a few days before Oct 1 or after Dec 31 2025 where the ISO week straddles the quarter boundary; all underlying job_runs rows are still restricted to queued_at in [2025-10-01, 2026-01-01).

entries.title: 2025 Job Failures by Job Type (Handler)
entries.question: Are job failures concentrated in a small number of job types/handlers rather than spread evenly across tenants?
entries.sql:
WITH job_runs_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    jr.id AS id,
    jr.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    jr.job_id AS job_id,
    jr.status AS status,
    jr.started_at AS started_at,
    jr.finished_at AS finished_at,
    j.handler AS handler
  FROM job_runs jr
  JOIN jobs j ON j.id = jr.job_id
  WHERE jr.queued_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND jr.queued_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  t0.handler AS handler,
  COALESCE(t1.total_runs, 0) AS total_runs,
  COALESCE(t2.failed_runs, 0) AS failed_runs,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t2.failed_runs, 0) / NULLIF(COALESCE(t1.total_runs, 0), 0), 2) AS failure_rate_pct,
  COALESCE(t3.distinct_tenants_run, 0) AS distinct_tenants_run,
  COALESCE(t4.distinct_tenants_failed, 0) AS distinct_tenants_failed,
  ROUND(t5.avg_duration_seconds_failed, 1) AS avg_duration_seconds_failed
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT handler FROM job_runs_filtered) t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT handler, COUNT(*) AS total_runs
  FROM job_runs_filtered
  GROUP BY handler
) t1 ON t1.handler = t0.handler
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT handler, COUNT(*) AS failed_runs
  FROM job_runs_filtered
  WHERE status = 'failed'
  GROUP BY handler
) t2 ON t2.handler = t0.handler
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT handler, COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants_run
  FROM job_runs_filtered
  GROUP BY handler
) t3 ON t3.handler = t0.handler
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT handler, COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants_failed
  FROM job_runs_filtered
  WHERE status = 'failed'
  GROUP BY handler
) t4 ON t4.handler = t0.handler
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT handler, AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (finished_at - started_at))) AS avg_duration_seconds_failed
  FROM job_runs_filtered
  WHERE status = 'failed'
    AND started_at IS NOT NULL
    AND finished_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY handler
) t5 ON t5.handler = t0.handler
ORDER BY failed_runs DESC, t0.handler ASC
builds_on: Merchants Hit Hardest by Job Failures, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Per the request, filtered to queued_at in 2025-10-01..2025-12-31 (the only window available for job_runs), even though the title says "2025" — full-year 2025 job_runs data is not present in the warehouse.

entries.title: 2025 Q4 Weekly Job Failures vs Health Check Alerts
entries.question: In the window where we have both job_runs and system_health_checks data, did weeks with more unhealthy health checks line up with weeks of more job failures?
entries.sql:
WITH job_week AS (
  SELECT
    cd.week_start,
    COUNT(*) AS total_job_runs,
    SUM(CASE WHEN jr.status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_job_runs
  FROM job_runs jr
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(jr.queued_at AS date)
  WHERE jr.queued_at >= DATE '2025-11-01' AND jr.queued_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY cd.week_start
),
health_week AS (
  SELECT
    cd.week_start,
    COUNT(*) AS total_health_checks,
    SUM(CASE WHEN shc.is_healthy = false THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unhealthy_health_checks
  FROM system_health_checks shc
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(shc.checked_at AS date)
  WHERE shc.checked_at >= DATE '2025-11-01' AND shc.checked_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY cd.week_start
)
SELECT
  jw.week_start,
  jw.total_job_runs,
  jw.failed_job_runs,
  ROUND(100.0 * jw.failed_job_runs / NULLIF(jw.total_job_runs, 0), 2) AS job_failure_rate_pct,
  hw.total_health_checks,
  hw.unhealthy_health_checks,
  ROUND(100.0 * hw.unhealthy_health_checks / NULLIF(hw.total_health_checks, 0), 2) AS health_check_unhealthy_rate_pct
FROM job_week jw
JOIN health_week hw ON hw.week_start = jw.week_start
ORDER BY jw.week_start ASC
builds_on: 2025 Background Job Reliability by Month
2025 Internal Health Check Reliability by Month
entries.engineer_note: Weeks are ISO weeks (calendar_days.week_start, Monday-based); only weeks with data in both job_runs and system_health_checks for Nov 1 - Dec 31 2025 are included (inner join), so a week start may be dropped if one source has no rows that week. Platform-wide totals across all tenants.

entries.title: Tenant Size vs Carts.remind Job Failure Exposure, 2025
entries.question: Were the 10 tenants hit by the November carts.remind job failures large/top-tier accounts, or did exposure look unrelated to merchant size?
entries.sql:
WITH order_rev AS (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders_2025,
    SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS total_revenue_eur_2025
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = DATE(o.placed_at)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
affected AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT jr.tenant_id
  FROM job_runs jr
  JOIN jobs j ON j.id = jr.job_id
  WHERE j.handler = 'carts.remind'
    AND jr.status = 'failed'
    AND jr.queued_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-01'
    AND jr.queued_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01'
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    t.id AS tenant_id,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    COALESCE(orv.total_orders_2025, 0) AS total_orders_2025,
    COALESCE(orv.total_revenue_eur_2025, 0) AS total_revenue_eur_2025,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(orv.total_revenue_eur_2025, 0) DESC) AS revenue_rank,
    CASE WHEN a.tenant_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS was_affected_by_nov_carts_remind_failure
  FROM tenants t
  LEFT JOIN order_rev orv ON orv.tenant_id = t.id
  LEFT JOIN affected a ON a.tenant_id = t.id
)
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  total_orders_2025,
  ROUND(total_revenue_eur_2025, 2) AS total_revenue_eur_2025,
  revenue_rank,
  was_affected_by_nov_carts_remind_failure
FROM ranked
ORDER BY was_affected_by_nov_carts_remind_failure DESC, revenue_rank ASC, tenant_name ASC
LIMIT 30
builds_on: Merchants Hit Hardest by Job Failures, 2025
2025 Job Failures by Job Type (Handler)
entries.engineer_note: Ranking and revenue cover all tenants (not just those with 2025 orders, which are coalesced to 0) so the 10 affected tenants can be compared against the full field; the report returns the 10 Nov carts.remind-failure tenants plus the ~20 next-largest unaffected tenants by 2025 EUR revenue.

entries.title: Support Ticket Volume Around the Nov 2025 Carts.remind Incident
entries.question: Did support ticket volume spike for the 10 affected tenants around the week of the carts.remind failures, compared to other tenants?
entries.sql:
WITH affected AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT jr.tenant_id
  FROM job_runs jr
  JOIN jobs j ON j.id = jr.job_id
  WHERE j.handler = 'carts.remind'
    AND jr.status = 'failed'
    AND jr.queued_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-01'
    AND jr.queued_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-01'
),
tenant_counts AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_tenants
  FROM tenants
  WHERE status IN ('trial','active','past_due','suspended','churned')
),
ticket_weeks AS (
  SELECT cd.week_start,
         t.tenant_id,
         CASE WHEN t.tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM affected) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_affected
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(t.created_at AS DATE)
  WHERE t.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-01' AND t.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  week_start,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_affected = 1) AS tickets_affected_tenants,
  ROUND(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_affected = 1) / 10.0, 2) AS avg_tickets_per_affected_tenant,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_affected = 0) AS tickets_other_tenants,
  ROUND(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_affected = 0) / (SELECT (total_tenants - 10) FROM tenant_counts), 2) AS avg_tickets_per_other_tenant
FROM ticket_weeks
GROUP BY week_start
ORDER BY week_start
builds_on: 2025 Job Failures by Job Type (Handler)
entries.engineer_note: Affected tenants = the 10 distinct tenant_ids with a failed job_runs row for jobs.handler='carts.remind' queued in Nov 2025, matching the prior request's definition. 'Other' tenant count uses all tenants with a valid status (which covers the whole tenants table) minus the 10 affected.

entries.title: 2025 Webhook Delivery Reliability Trend
entries.question: How reliable were webhook deliveries to merchants' own systems across 2025, and what time window does the data actually cover?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  date_trunc('month', created_at)::date AS month,
  count(*) AS total_deliveries,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success') AS success_count,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success') / count(*), 2) AS success_rate_pct,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') AS failed_count,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') / count(*), 2) AS failure_rate_pct,
  round(avg(duration_ms) FILTER (WHERE duration_ms IS NOT NULL)) AS avg_duration_ms,
  count(DISTINCT webhook_id) AS distinct_webhooks
FROM webhook_deliveries
WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', created_at)
ORDER BY month ASC
entries.engineer_note: Filtered on created_at as requested; the query only returns months that actually have webhook_deliveries rows within 2025 (no synthetic zero-filled months), so the row count itself shows the real coverage window.

entries.title: Support Tickets: Affected vs Other Tenants, Baseline vs Incident Period
entries.question: Was the Nov-Dec ticket rise for the 10 carts.remind-affected tenants a real spike against their own baseline, or just their normal (or seasonal) level?
entries.sql:
WITH affected AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT jr.tenant_id
  FROM job_runs jr
  JOIN jobs j ON jr.job_id = j.id
  WHERE j.handler = 'carts.remind'
    AND jr.status = 'failed'
    AND jr.queued_at >= DATE '2025-11-01' AND jr.queued_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
),
groups AS (
  SELECT t.id AS tenant_id,
    CASE WHEN a.tenant_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Affected' ELSE 'Other' END AS group_name
  FROM tenants t
  LEFT JOIN affected a ON a.tenant_id = t.id
),
tenant_counts AS (
  SELECT group_name, COUNT(*) AS tenant_count
  FROM groups
  GROUP BY group_name
),
ticket_counts AS (
  SELECT g.group_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN tk.created_at >= DATE '2025-08-01' AND tk.created_at < DATE '2025-10-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS baseline_tickets,
    SUM(CASE WHEN tk.created_at >= DATE '2025-11-01' AND tk.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS incident_tickets
  FROM groups g
  LEFT JOIN tickets tk ON tk.tenant_id = g.tenant_id
  GROUP BY g.group_name
)
SELECT
  tc.group_name,
  tcn.tenant_count,
  ROUND(tc.baseline_tickets::numeric / tcn.tenant_count / (61/7.0), 2) AS avg_weekly_tickets_per_tenant_baseline,
  ROUND(tc.incident_tickets::numeric / tcn.tenant_count / (61/7.0), 2) AS avg_weekly_tickets_per_tenant_incident,
  ROUND(
    (((tc.incident_tickets::numeric / tcn.tenant_count) - (tc.baseline_tickets::numeric / tcn.tenant_count))
     / NULLIF(tc.baseline_tickets::numeric / tcn.tenant_count, 0)) * 100
  , 1) AS pct_change
FROM ticket_counts tc
JOIN tenant_counts tcn ON tcn.group_name = tc.group_name
ORDER BY tc.group_name
builds_on: Support Ticket Volume Around the Nov 2025 Carts.remind Incident
Tenant Size vs Carts.remind Job Failure Exposure, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Affected tenants = distinct tenant_ids with a failed job_runs row (via jobs.handler='carts.remind') queued in Nov 2025, per prior reports; this should be exactly the 10 tenants referenced. Periods use created_at on tickets, both exactly 61 days as specified.

entries.title: 2025 Webhook Delivery Reliability by Endpoint
entries.question: Which individual webhook endpoints are chronically troublesome - low success rates or deliveries stuck retrying rather than resolving?
entries.sql:
select
  w.name as webhook_name,
  t.name as tenant_name,
  count(*) as total_deliveries_2025,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when wd.status = 'success' then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 2) as success_rate_pct,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when wd.status = 'failed' then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 2) as failed_rate_pct,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when wd.status in ('pending','retrying') then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 2) as pending_or_retrying_rate_pct,
  round(avg(wd.duration_ms)) as avg_duration_ms
from webhook_deliveries wd
join webhooks w on w.id = wd.webhook_id
join tenants t on t.id = w.tenant_id
where wd.created_at >= date '2025-01-01' and wd.created_at < date '2026-01-01'
group by w.id, w.name, t.name
having count(*) >= 20
order by pending_or_retrying_rate_pct desc, failed_rate_pct desc, webhook_name asc
limit 20
builds_on: 2025 Webhook Delivery Reliability Trend
entries.engineer_note: Webhook deliveries are not multi-currency so no FX conversion was needed; rates are computed per webhook over all 2025 deliveries with at least 20 total, limited to the worst 20 by stuck-retry rate then failure rate.

entries.title: Webhook Delivery Reliability: Carts.remind-Affected Tenants vs Others, 2025
entries.question: Do the 10 tenants hit by the Nov carts.remind job failures also show worse webhook delivery reliability than other tenants, suggesting clustered reliability problems on the same accounts?
entries.sql:
WITH affected AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT jr.tenant_id
  FROM job_runs jr
  JOIN jobs j ON j.id = jr.job_id
  WHERE j.name = 'carts.remind'
    AND jr.status = 'failed'
    AND jr.started_at >= DATE '2025-11-01'
    AND jr.started_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN wd.tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM affected) THEN 'Affected' ELSE 'Other' END AS group_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT wd.tenant_id) AS tenant_count,
  COUNT(*) AS total_deliveries_2025,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN wd.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS success_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN wd.status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS failed_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN wd.status IN ('pending', 'retrying') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pending_or_retrying_rate_pct
FROM webhook_deliveries wd
JOIN webhooks w ON w.id = wd.webhook_id
WHERE wd.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
  AND wd.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY group_name
ORDER BY group_name
builds_on: 2025 Webhook Delivery Reliability by Endpoint
Tenant Size vs Carts.remind Job Failure Exposure, 2025
entries.engineer_note: The "Affected" cohort is derived directly in this query as the distinct tenant_ids with a failed job_runs row for a job named 'carts.remind' in Nov 2025 (since I don't have the earlier report's exact tenant list to join against) — if that prior report used a different job name/handler key or a slightly different definition of "affected," the two numbers may not line up exactly with 10 tenants.

entries.title: Merchant Catalog Profile
entries.question: How large and content-rich is each merchant's catalog, and how does that relate to their recent sales volume?
entries.sql:
WITH products_agg AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
    count(*) AS active_product_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM product_media pm WHERE pm.product_id = p.id AND pm.is_primary = true
    )) AS products_with_primary_image,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.description IS NOT NULL AND length(trim(p.description)) > 0) AS products_with_description
  FROM products p
  WHERE p.status = 'active' AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
variants_agg AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
    count(v.id) AS active_variant_count
  FROM products p
  JOIN product_variants v ON v.product_id = p.id AND v.is_active = true AND v.deleted_at IS NULL
  WHERE p.status = 'active' AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
reviews_agg AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
    count(r.id) AS approved_review_count,
    avg(r.rating) AS avg_rating
  FROM products p
  JOIN product_reviews r ON r.product_id = p.id AND r.is_approved = true
  WHERE p.status = 'active' AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
orders_agg AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
    count(*) AS orders_last_12mo,
    sum(o.grand_total / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END)) AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  COALESCE(pa.active_product_count, 0) AS active_product_count,
  COALESCE(va.active_variant_count, 0) AS active_variant_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(va.active_variant_count, 0)::numeric / NULLIF(pa.active_product_count, 0), 2) AS avg_variants_per_product,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(pa.products_with_primary_image, 0) / NULLIF(pa.active_product_count, 0), 1) AS pct_products_with_primary_image,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(pa.products_with_description, 0) / NULLIF(pa.active_product_count, 0), 1) AS pct_products_with_description,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ra.approved_review_count, 0)::numeric / NULLIF(pa.active_product_count, 0), 2) AS avg_reviews_per_product,
  ROUND(ra.avg_rating::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_last_12mo, 0) AS orders_last_12mo,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.revenue_eur, 0), 0) AS revenue_eur_last_12mo
FROM tenants t
LEFT JOIN products_agg pa ON pa.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN variants_agg va ON va.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN reviews_agg ra ON ra.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN orders_agg oa ON oa.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE t.deleted_at IS NULL
ORDER BY revenue_eur_last_12mo DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Printed top 50 tenants by last-12mo EUR revenue (full non-deleted tenant universe is ~120 rows, per the request). Tenants with no active products/orders in the window show 0/NULL for the affected ratios (NULLIF avoids divide-by-zero); EUR amounts for orders already in EUR use rate=1 since exchange_rates has no EUR→EUR self-row.

entries.title: Catalog Richness vs Sales Performance by Image Count Bucket
entries.question: Do products with more images, a proxy for richer catalog content, see higher engagement and sales than sparser listings?
entries.sql:
WITH product_images AS (
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS image_count
  FROM product_media
  WHERE kind = 'image'
  GROUP BY product_id
),
base AS (
  SELECT p.id AS product_id,
         COALESCE(pi.image_count,0) AS image_count,
         CASE WHEN p.description IS NOT NULL AND p.description <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_description
  FROM products p
  LEFT JOIN product_images pi ON pi.product_id = p.id
  WHERE p.status = 'active' AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT product_id, has_description,
    CASE
      WHEN image_count = 0 THEN '0'
      WHEN image_count = 1 THEN '1'
      WHEN image_count BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN '2-3'
      WHEN image_count BETWEEN 4 AND 6 THEN '4-6'
      ELSE '7+'
    END AS image_count_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN image_count = 0 THEN 0
      WHEN image_count = 1 THEN 1
      WHEN image_count BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN 2
      WHEN image_count BETWEEN 4 AND 6 THEN 3
      ELSE 4
    END AS bucket_order
  FROM base
),
reviews AS (
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS review_count, AVG(rating) AS avg_rating
  FROM product_reviews
  GROUP BY product_id
),
sales AS (
  SELECT pv.product_id,
         SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold,
         SUM(oi.line_total / er.rate) AS revenue_eur
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = oi.product_variant_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = oi.currency_code AND er.as_of = DATE(o.placed_at)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY pv.product_id
)
SELECT
  b.image_count_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS product_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(b.has_description) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_with_description,
  ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(r.review_count,0)), 2) AS avg_reviews_per_product,
  ROUND(AVG(r.avg_rating), 2) AS avg_rating,
  ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(s.units_sold,0)), 2) AS avg_units_sold_per_product_last_12mo,
  ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(s.revenue_eur,0))) AS avg_revenue_per_product_eur_last_12mo
FROM bucketed b
LEFT JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = b.product_id
LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = b.product_id
GROUP BY b.image_count_bucket, b.bucket_order
ORDER BY b.bucket_order
entries.engineer_note: avg_rating is the mean of each product's own average star rating within the bucket (products with zero reviews are excluded from that average, but counted at 0 for avg_reviews_per_product and sales); revenue/units are averaged over all active products in the bucket, including those with no 2025 sales (counted as 0).

entries.title: Monthly Review Volume and Rating Trend
entries.question: How is customer review volume and average rating trending over time across the platform?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t0.month_label AS month, t0.month_start AS month_start
  FROM calendar_days t0
  WHERE t0.month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND t0.month_start < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
reviews AS (
  SELECT t1.month_label AS month, t0.rating AS rating, t0.is_verified_purchase AS is_verified_purchase
  FROM product_reviews t0
  JOIN calendar_days t1 ON t1.calendar_date = CAST(t0.created_at AS date)
  WHERE t0.is_approved = true
),
m_count AS (
  SELECT t2.month AS month, COUNT(*) AS review_count
  FROM reviews t2
  GROUP BY t2.month
),
m_avg AS (
  SELECT t3.month AS month, AVG(t3.rating) AS avg_rating
  FROM reviews t3
  GROUP BY t3.month
),
m_low AS (
  SELECT t4.month AS month, SUM(CASE WHEN t4.rating IN (1,2) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS low_count
  FROM reviews t4
  GROUP BY t4.month
),
m_five AS (
  SELECT t5.month AS month, SUM(CASE WHEN t5.rating = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS five_count
  FROM reviews t5
  GROUP BY t5.month
),
m_verified AS (
  SELECT t6.month AS month, SUM(CASE WHEN t6.is_verified_purchase THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS verified_count
  FROM reviews t6
  GROUP BY t6.month
)
SELECT
  t0.month AS month,
  COALESCE(t1.review_count, 0) AS review_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.avg_rating, 0), 2) AS avg_rating,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t3.low_count, 0) / NULLIF(t1.review_count, 0), 1) AS pct_1_2_star,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t4.five_count, 0) / NULLIF(t1.review_count, 0), 1) AS pct_5_star,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t5.verified_count, 0) / NULLIF(t1.review_count, 0), 1) AS pct_verified_purchase
FROM months t0
LEFT JOIN m_count t1 ON t1.month = t0.month
LEFT JOIN m_avg t2 ON t2.month = t0.month
LEFT JOIN m_low t3 ON t3.month = t0.month
LEFT JOIN m_five t4 ON t4.month = t0.month
LEFT JOIN m_verified t5 ON t5.month = t0.month
ORDER BY t0.month_start
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per calendar month 2023-01 through 2025-12 (36 rows), built from the full calendar so months with zero approved reviews still appear with 0/blank measures rather than being dropped; percentages are null when review_count is 0 since there's no base to divide by.

entries.title: Image-Richness vs Sales Within Apparel & Footwear
entries.question: Within a single vertical, removing the cross-vertical confound seen in the platform-wide bucket report, do products with more images actually sell better?
entries.sql:
WITH apparel_tenants AS (
    SELECT id AS tenant_id
    FROM tenants
    WHERE industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
),
base_products AS (
    SELECT p.id AS product_id,
           p.tenant_id,
           p.description
    FROM products p
    JOIN apparel_tenants t ON t.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
    WHERE p.status = 'active'
      AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
),
image_counts AS (
    SELECT bp.product_id,
           COUNT(pm.id) AS image_count
    FROM base_products bp
    LEFT JOIN product_media pm
           ON pm.product_id = bp.product_id
          AND pm.kind = 'image'
    GROUP BY bp.product_id
),
variant_counts AS (
    SELECT bp.product_id,
           COUNT(pv.id) AS variant_count
    FROM base_products bp
    LEFT JOIN product_variants pv
           ON pv.product_id = bp.product_id
          AND pv.deleted_at IS NULL
    GROUP BY bp.product_id
),
review_stats AS (
    SELECT bp.product_id,
           COUNT(pr.id) AS review_count,
           AVG(pr.rating::numeric) AS avg_rating_for_product
    FROM base_products bp
    LEFT JOIN product_reviews pr
           ON pr.product_id = bp.product_id
          AND pr.is_approved = true
    GROUP BY bp.product_id
),
order_items_in_window AS (
    SELECT oi.product_variant_id,
           oi.quantity,
           oi.line_total,
           oi.currency_code,
           o.placed_at
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
      AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
      AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
order_items_eur AS (
    SELECT oiw.product_variant_id,
           oiw.quantity,
           oiw.line_total / er.rate AS line_total_eur
    FROM order_items_in_window oiw
    JOIN exchange_rates er
           ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = oiw.currency_code
          AND er.as_of = CAST(oiw.placed_at AS date)
),
variant_product_map AS (
    SELECT pv.id AS variant_id,
           pv.product_id
    FROM product_variants pv
    JOIN base_products bp ON bp.product_id = pv.product_id
),
product_sales AS (
    SELECT vpm.product_id,
           SUM(oie.quantity) AS units_sold,
           SUM(oie.line_total_eur) AS revenue_eur
    FROM variant_product_map vpm
    JOIN order_items_eur oie ON oie.product_variant_id = vpm.variant_id
    GROUP BY vpm.product_id
),
product_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        bp.product_id,
        CASE
            WHEN ic.image_count = 0 THEN '0'
            WHEN ic.image_count = 1 THEN '1'
            WHEN ic.image_count BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN '2-3'
            WHEN ic.image_count BETWEEN 4 AND 6 THEN '4-6'
            ELSE '7+'
        END AS image_count_bucket,
        CASE WHEN bp.description IS NOT NULL AND bp.description <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_description,
        COALESCE(vc.variant_count, 0) AS variant_count,
        COALESCE(rs.review_count, 0) AS review_count,
        rs.avg_rating_for_product,
        COALESCE(ps.units_sold, 0) AS units_sold,
        COALESCE(ps.revenue_eur, 0) AS revenue_eur
    FROM base_products bp
    JOIN image_counts ic ON ic.product_id = bp.product_id
    LEFT JOIN variant_counts vc ON vc.product_id = bp.product_id
    LEFT JOIN review_stats rs ON rs.product_id = bp.product_id
    LEFT JOIN product_sales ps ON ps.product_id = bp.product_id
)
SELECT
    image_count_bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS product_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(has_description) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_with_description,
    ROUND(AVG(variant_count), 2) AS avg_variants_per_product,
    ROUND(AVG(review_count), 2) AS avg_reviews_per_product,
    ROUND(AVG(avg_rating_for_product) FILTER (WHERE review_count > 0), 2) AS avg_rating,
    ROUND(AVG(units_sold), 2) AS avg_units_sold_per_product_last_12mo,
    ROUND(AVG(revenue_eur), 0) AS avg_revenue_per_product_eur_last_12mo
FROM product_metrics
GROUP BY image_count_bucket
ORDER BY
    CASE image_count_bucket
        WHEN '0' THEN 1
        WHEN '1' THEN 2
        WHEN '2-3' THEN 3
        WHEN '4-6' THEN 4
        WHEN '7+' THEN 5
    END
builds_on: Catalog Richness vs Sales Performance by Image Count Bucket
entries.engineer_note: Replicates the night-1 image-count-bucket methodology but restricted to products of tenants with industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'. Revenue converted to EUR using exchange_rates (EUR->order currency) as of the order's placed_at date; sales window is orders placed 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31 with status not cancelled; avg_rating is the mean of each product's own average approved-review rating, computed only over products with at least one approved review, while zero-review products still contribute 0 to avg_reviews_per_product and to the sales averages.

entries.title: Review Engagement Relative to Order Volume
entries.question: Is the month-over-month growth in review counts just tracking order volume growth, or is review-per-order engagement actually increasing?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(t1.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  COALESCE(t2.review_count, 0) AS review_count,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(t1.orders_count, 0) = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE COALESCE(t2.review_count, 0)::decimal / t1.orders_count * 100
    END, 2
  ) AS reviews_per_100_orders,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t2.avg_rating, 0), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND calendar_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
) t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.placed_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_count
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o.status NOT IN ('cancelled')
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', o.placed_at)::date
) t1 ON t1.month_start = t0.month_start
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', r.created_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS review_count,
    AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating
  FROM product_reviews r
  WHERE r.is_approved = true
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', r.created_at)::date
) t2 ON t2.month_start = t0.month_start
ORDER BY t0.month_start ASC
builds_on: Monthly Review Volume and Rating Trend
entries.engineer_note: Built off calendar_days so every month 2023-01..2025-12 appears even with zero orders/reviews; reviews_per_100_orders is 0 when orders_count is 0 to avoid divide-by-zero, and avg_rating is 0 (not null) for months with no approved reviews.

entries.title: December Rating Dip by Vertical: 2024 vs 2025
entries.question: Which merchant vertical drove the platform-wide rating dip and spike in negative reviews seen in December 2025?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.industry,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE pr.created_at >= DATE '2024-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2025-01-01') AS dec2024_review_count,
  ROUND(AVG(pr.rating) FILTER (WHERE pr.created_at >= DATE '2024-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2025-01-01')::numeric, 2) AS dec2024_avg_rating,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') AS dec2025_review_count,
  ROUND(AVG(pr.rating) FILTER (WHERE pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01')::numeric, 2) AS dec2025_avg_rating,
  ROUND(
    (AVG(pr.rating) FILTER (WHERE pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01')
     - AVG(pr.rating) FILTER (WHERE pr.created_at >= DATE '2024-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2025-01-01'))::numeric
  , 2) AS rating_change_pts,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01' AND pr.rating <= 2)
    / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'), 0)
  , 1) AS dec2025_pct_1_2_star
FROM product_reviews pr
JOIN products p ON p.id = pr.product_id AND p.tenant_id = pr.tenant_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = pr.tenant_id
WHERE pr.is_approved = true
  AND (
    (pr.created_at >= DATE '2024-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2025-01-01')
    OR (pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01')
  )
GROUP BY t.industry
ORDER BY rating_change_pts ASC NULLS LAST, t.industry ASC
builds_on: Monthly Review Volume and Rating Trend
entries.engineer_note: Grouped by tenants.industry (the vertical field); verticals with zero approved reviews in both Decembers are naturally excluded since they contribute no rows. rating_change_pts and the 1-2 star share are NULL/0 only if a vertical had no reviews in the relevant month.

entries.title: Home & Living December 2025 Rating Dip: Merchant Breakdown
entries.question: Within Home & Living, is the December 2025 rating decline concentrated in a few merchants or spread across the vertical?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name AS merchant_name,
       d.review_count AS dec2025_review_count,
       d.avg_rating AS dec2025_avg_rating,
       d.pct_1_2_star AS dec2025_pct_1_2_star,
       j.avg_rating AS jan_to_nov_2025_avg_rating,
       ROUND(d.avg_rating - j.avg_rating, 2) AS rating_change_pts
FROM tenants t
JOIN (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         COUNT(*) AS review_count,
         ROUND(AVG(pr.rating), 2) AS avg_rating,
         ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN pr.rating <= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_1_2_star
