  FROM product_reviews pr
  JOIN products p ON pr.product_id = p.id
  WHERE pr.is_approved = true
    AND pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01'
    AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
) d ON d.tenant_id = t.id
JOIN (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         ROUND(AVG(pr.rating), 2) AS avg_rating
  FROM product_reviews pr
  JOIN products p ON pr.product_id = p.id
  WHERE pr.is_approved = true
    AND pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND pr.created_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
) j ON j.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE t.industry = 'Home & Living'
ORDER BY rating_change_pts ASC, d.review_count DESC
builds_on: December Rating Dip by Vertical: 2024 vs 2025
entries.engineer_note: Both dec2025_avg_rating and jan_to_nov_2025_avg_rating are rounded to 2 decimals before computing rating_change_pts, since the report is meant to show the rounded values a reader would compare on the page; merchants with 0 reviews in Jan-Nov 2025 are excluded via the inner join since no baseline exists for them.

entries.title: Lowest-Rated Products Platform-Wide With Sufficient Review Volume
entries.question: Which specific products are getting the worst customer feedback, among those with enough reviews for the rating to be meaningful?
entries.sql:
WITH reviews AS (
  SELECT product_id,
         count(*) AS review_count,
         avg(rating) AS avg_rating,
         sum(case when rating in (1,2) then 1 else 0 end)::numeric / count(*) * 100 AS pct_1_2
  FROM product_reviews
  WHERE is_approved = true
  GROUP BY product_id
),
sales AS (
  SELECT pv.product_id, sum(oi.quantity) AS units_sold
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = oi.product_variant_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY pv.product_id
)
SELECT p.name AS product_name,
       t.name AS merchant_name,
       t.industry,
       r.review_count,
       round(r.avg_rating, 2) AS avg_rating,
       round(r.pct_1_2, 1) AS pct_1_2_star,
       coalesce(s.units_sold, 0) AS units_sold_last_12mo
FROM products p
JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = p.id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = p.id
WHERE r.review_count >= 5
ORDER BY avg_rating ASC, r.review_count DESC, p.id ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Lowest-Rated Products Platform-Wide
entries.engineer_note: Report is capped at 50 rows as requested (worst avg_rating first, ties broken by review_count desc then product id); the printed report footer will show how many products in total met the review_count >= 5 threshold.

entries.title: Collections and Bundles Adoption by Merchant
entries.question: How much are merchants leaning on curated collections and bundles rather than flat product listings, and does that line up with stronger sales?
entries.sql:
WITH tenant_revenue AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
         SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS revenue_eur,
         COUNT(*) AS orders_cnt
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
active_products AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS active_product_count
  FROM products
  WHERE status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
products_in_collection AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS cnt
  FROM products p
  JOIN collection_products cp ON cp.product_id = p.id AND cp.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
  JOIN collections c ON c.id = cp.collection_id AND c.tenant_id = p.tenant_id AND c.deleted_at IS NULL
  WHERE p.status = 'active' AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
products_in_bundle AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS cnt
  FROM products p
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.product_id = p.id AND pv.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
  JOIN bundle_items bi ON bi.variant_id = pv.id AND bi.tenant_id = pv.tenant_id
  JOIN product_bundles pb ON pb.id = bi.bundle_id AND pb.tenant_id = pv.tenant_id AND pb.is_active = true
  WHERE p.status = 'active' AND p.deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
collection_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS active_collection_count
  FROM collections
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
bundle_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS active_bundle_count
  FROM product_bundles
  WHERE is_active = true
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT t.name AS merchant_name,
       t.industry,
       COALESCE(cc.active_collection_count,0) AS active_collection_count,
       ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(pic.cnt,0) / NULLIF(ap.active_product_count,0), 1) AS pct_active_products_in_a_collection,
       COALESCE(bc.active_bundle_count,0) AS active_bundle_count,
       ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(pib.cnt,0) / NULLIF(ap.active_product_count,0), 1) AS pct_active_products_in_a_bundle,
       ROUND(tr.revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur_last_12mo,
       ROUND(tr.revenue_eur / NULLIF(tr.orders_cnt,0)) AS avg_order_value_eur_last_12mo
FROM tenant_revenue tr
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tr.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN active_products ap ON ap.tenant_id = tr.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN products_in_collection pic ON pic.tenant_id = tr.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN products_in_bundle pib ON pib.tenant_id = tr.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN collection_counts cc ON cc.tenant_id = tr.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN bundle_counts bc ON bc.tenant_id = tr.tenant_id
ORDER BY revenue_eur_last_12mo DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Merchant Catalog Profile
entries.engineer_note: Revenue window and EUR conversion mirror the Merchant Catalog Profile report (orders placed 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, status <> cancelled, EUR rate as of placed_at date). Percentages are null (shown as blank) for any tenant with zero active products, since the denominator is undefined; the report prints the top 50 by revenue and will note the total row count returned.

entries.title: Poorly-Rated Product Concentration by Merchant
entries.question: Which merchants have the largest share of their reviewed catalog sitting at genuinely poor ratings, rather than a few isolated bad products?
entries.sql:
WITH revenue AS (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    SUM(
      o.grand_total / CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END
    ) AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
top50 AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, revenue_eur,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY revenue_eur DESC) AS rn
  FROM revenue
),
product_stats AS (
  SELECT
    p.tenant_id,
    p.id AS product_id,
    COUNT(pr.id) AS review_count,
    AVG(pr.rating) AS avg_rating
  FROM products p
  JOIN product_reviews pr
    ON pr.product_id = p.id
    AND pr.is_approved = true
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id, p.id
  HAVING COUNT(pr.id) >= 5
),
merchant_agg AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS products_with_5plus_reviews,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE avg_rating < 3.0) AS poor_rated_product_count
  FROM product_stats
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  COALESCE(ma.products_with_5plus_reviews, 0) AS products_with_5plus_reviews,
  COALESCE(ma.poor_rated_product_count, 0) AS poor_rated_product_count,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ma.products_with_5plus_reviews, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ROUND(ma.poor_rated_product_count::numeric / ma.products_with_5plus_reviews * 100, 1)
  END AS pct_poor_rated_products,
  ROUND(r.revenue_eur, 2) AS revenue_eur_last_12mo
FROM top50 r
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN merchant_agg ma ON ma.tenant_id = r.tenant_id
WHERE r.rn <= 50
ORDER BY
  poor_rated_product_count DESC,
  pct_poor_rated_products DESC NULLS LAST,
  merchant_name
builds_on: Lowest-Rated Products Platform-Wide With Sufficient Review Volume
Merchant Catalog Profile
entries.engineer_note: Top-50 set is independently re-derived here using the same revenue definition (orders placed 2025-01-01..2025-12-31, non-cancelled, converted to EUR via exchange_rates as of placed_at) rather than joining to a stored Merchant Catalog Profile output, so results should match that report's top-50 as long as its revenue logic is identical. Returns at most 50 rows (one per top-50 merchant); merchants with zero products having 5+ approved reviews show pct_poor_rated_products as blank/NULL.

entries.title: High-Selling Products With Few or No Reviews
entries.question: Which products sell well but have surprisingly little customer review feedback, suggesting a listing or follow-up gap rather than a demand problem?
entries.sql:
WITH order_item_sales AS (
  SELECT
    pv.product_id,
    oi.quantity,
    oi.line_total,
    o.currency_code,
    o.placed_at
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON oi.product_variant_id = pv.id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
rates AS (
  SELECT quote_code, as_of, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR'
),
sales_eur AS (
  SELECT
    s.product_id,
    SUM(s.quantity) AS units_sold,
    SUM(s.line_total / r.rate) AS revenue_eur
  FROM order_item_sales s
  JOIN rates r
    ON r.quote_code = s.currency_code
   AND r.as_of = CAST(s.placed_at AS date)
  GROUP BY s.product_id
),
reviews AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    COUNT(*) AS review_count,
    AVG(rating) AS avg_rating
  FROM product_reviews
  WHERE is_approved = true
  GROUP BY product_id
),
product_info AS (
  SELECT
    p.id,
    p.name AS product_name,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.status,
    p.deleted_at
  FROM products p
)
SELECT
  pi.product_name,
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  se.units_sold AS units_sold_last_12mo,
  ROUND(se.revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur_last_12mo,
  COALESCE(r.review_count, 0) AS review_count,
  ROUND(CAST(r.avg_rating AS numeric), 2) AS avg_rating
FROM sales_eur se
JOIN product_info pi ON pi.id = se.product_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = pi.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN reviews r ON r.product_id = se.product_id
WHERE pi.status = 'active'
  AND pi.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND se.units_sold >= 30
  AND COALESCE(r.review_count, 0) <= 2
ORDER BY se.units_sold DESC, se.revenue_eur DESC, pi.product_name
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Lowest-Rated Products Platform-Wide With Sufficient Review Volume
entries.engineer_note: Revenue uses order_items.line_total (post-discount, pre-tax) converted to EUR via the day's EUR exchange rate; "last 12mo" is read as calendar year 2025 (placed_at 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31) per the stated filter. Review count/rating are all-time across approved reviews, as specified. Results are capped at 50 rows per house standard; the report will note the total number of qualifying products.

entries.title: Catalog Structure: Top Merchants vs Long Tail
entries.question: Do our top-revenue merchants' catalogs look structurally different from the long tail in size, categorization, and media richness?
entries.sql:
with tenant_rev as (
  select
    o.tenant_id,
    sum(o.grand_total / er.rate) as revenue_eur
  from orders o
  join exchange_rates er
    on er.base_code = 'EUR'
   and er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   and er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
  where o.placed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
    and o.placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
    and o.status <> 'cancelled'
  group by o.tenant_id
),
ranked as (
  select
    t.id as tenant_id,
    coalesce(tr.revenue_eur, 0) as revenue_eur,
    row_number() over (order by coalesce(tr.revenue_eur,0) desc, t.id) as rnk
  from tenants t
  left join tenant_rev tr on tr.tenant_id = t.id
  where t.deleted_at is null
),
tiered as (
  select
    tenant_id,
    revenue_eur,
    case
      when rnk <= 10 then 'Top 10'
      when rnk <= 30 then 'Next 20'
      else 'Rest'
    end as tier,
    case
      when rnk <= 10 then 1
      when rnk <= 30 then 2
      else 3
    end as tier_order
  from ranked
),
tier_agg as (
  select tier, tier_order,
    count(distinct tenant_id) as merchant_count,
    sum(revenue_eur) as tier_revenue
  from tiered
  group by tier, tier_order
),
active_products as (
  select p.id as product_id, p.tenant_id
  from products p
  where p.status = 'active' and p.deleted_at is null
),
product_metrics as (
  select
    ap.product_id,
    ap.tenant_id,
    (select count(*) from product_variants pv
       where pv.product_id = ap.product_id and pv.is_active = true and pv.deleted_at is null) as variant_count,
    (select count(*) from product_categories pc
       where pc.product_id = ap.product_id) as category_count,
    exists (select 1 from product_media pm
       where pm.product_id = ap.product_id and pm.is_primary = true) as has_primary_image,
    (select count(*) from product_media pm2
       where pm2.product_id = ap.product_id) as media_count,
    exists (
       select 1 from collection_products cp
       join collections c on c.id = cp.collection_id and c.deleted_at is null
       where cp.product_id = ap.product_id
    ) as in_collection
  from active_products ap
),
product_agg as (
  select ti.tier,
    count(pm.product_id) as active_products,
    avg(pm.variant_count) as avg_variants,
    avg(pm.category_count) as avg_categories,
    avg(case when pm.has_primary_image then 1.0 else 0.0 end) as pct_primary_image,
    avg(pm.media_count) as avg_media,
    avg(case when pm.in_collection then 1.0 else 0.0 end) as pct_in_collection
  from tiered ti
  left join product_metrics pm on pm.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
  group by ti.tier
)
select
  ta.tier,
  ta.merchant_count,
  round(pa.active_products::numeric / ta.merchant_count, 2) as avg_active_products_per_merchant,
  round(pa.avg_variants::numeric, 2) as avg_variants_per_product,
  round(pa.avg_categories::numeric, 2) as avg_categories_per_product,
  round((100.0*pa.pct_primary_image)::numeric, 1) as pct_products_with_primary_image,
  round(pa.avg_media::numeric, 2) as avg_media_count_per_product,
  round((100.0*pa.pct_in_collection)::numeric, 1) as pct_active_products_in_a_collection,
  round((100.0*ta.tier_revenue / sum(ta.tier_revenue) over ())::numeric, 1) as revenue_share_pct
from tier_agg ta
join product_agg pa on pa.tier = ta.tier
order by ta.tier_order
builds_on: Merchant Catalog Profile
Collections and Bundles Adoption by Merchant
entries.engineer_note: Revenue ranking uses orders placed 2025-01-01..2025-12-31, status<>'cancelled', converted to EUR via exchange_rates(base=EUR, quote=order currency, as_of=placed_at date), matching the Merchant Catalog Profile definition. Product-level metrics (variants, categories, media, collection membership) are pooled across all active/non-deleted products within each tier rather than averaged merchant-by-merchant, since the request specifies them as "per product" measures.

entries.title: Discount cost vs. order volume/revenue by discount, 2025
entries.question: Which discounts (promotions/coupons) cost us the most in 2025, and how much order volume and revenue do they sit on?
entries.sql:
WITH fod AS (
  SELECT
    od.id AS od_id,
    od.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    od.order_id AS order_id,
    od.discount_id AS discount_id,
    od.coupon_id AS coupon_id,
    od.amount AS discount_amount_local,
    od.currency_code AS discount_currency_code,
    o.grand_total AS order_grand_total_local,
    o.currency_code AS order_currency_code,
    o.user_id AS user_id,
    o.placed_at AS placed_at,
    CAST(o.placed_at AS date) AS placed_date
  FROM order_discounts od
  JOIN orders o
    ON o.id = od.order_id
   AND o.tenant_id = od.tenant_id
  WHERE od.discount_id IS NOT NULL
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
discount_base AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT discount_id FROM fod
),
coupon_codes AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT fod.discount_id AS discount_id, c.code AS code
  FROM fod
  JOIN coupons c
    ON c.id = fod.coupon_id
   AND c.tenant_id = fod.tenant_id
  WHERE fod.coupon_id IS NOT NULL
),
coupon_codes_agg AS (
  SELECT
    cc.discount_id AS discount_id,
    STRING_AGG(cc.code, ', ' ORDER BY cc.code) AS coupon_codes
  FROM coupon_codes cc
  GROUP BY cc.discount_id
),
m_discount_amount AS (
  SELECT
    fod.discount_id AS discount_id,
    SUM(fod.discount_amount_local / fxd.rate) AS discount_amount_eur
  FROM fod
  JOIN exchange_rates fxd
    ON fxd.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND fxd.quote_code = fod.discount_currency_code
   AND fxd.as_of = fod.placed_date
  GROUP BY fod.discount_id
),
m_orders AS (
  SELECT
    fod.discount_id AS discount_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fod.order_id) AS order_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fod.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
    MIN(fod.placed_at) AS first_order_date,
    MAX(fod.placed_at) AS last_order_date
  FROM fod
  GROUP BY fod.discount_id
),
distinct_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    discount_id,
    order_id,
    order_grand_total_local,
    order_currency_code,
    placed_date
  FROM fod
),
m_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    do1.discount_id AS discount_id,
    SUM(do1.order_grand_total_local / fxo.rate) AS revenue_eur
  FROM distinct_orders do1
  JOIN exchange_rates fxo
    ON fxo.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND fxo.quote_code = do1.order_currency_code
   AND fxo.as_of = do1.placed_date
  GROUP BY do1.discount_id
)
SELECT
  d.name AS discount_name,
  d.kind AS discount_kind,
  COALESCE(cca.coupon_codes, 'automatic') AS coupon_codes,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mda.discount_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS discount_amount_eur,
  COALESCE(mo.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mr.revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS order_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(mr.revenue_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE 100.0 * COALESCE(mda.discount_amount_eur, 0) / mr.revenue_eur
    END, 2
  ) AS discount_pct_of_revenue,
  COALESCE(mo.distinct_customers, 0) AS distinct_customers,
  mo.first_order_date AS first_order_date,
  mo.last_order_date AS last_order_date
FROM discount_base db
JOIN discounts d ON d.id = db.discount_id
LEFT JOIN coupon_codes_agg cca ON cca.discount_id = db.discount_id
LEFT JOIN m_discount_amount mda ON mda.discount_id = db.discount_id
LEFT JOIN m_orders mo ON mo.discount_id = db.discount_id
LEFT JOIN m_revenue mr ON mr.discount_id = db.discount_id
ORDER BY discount_amount_eur DESC, d.name ASC
entries.engineer_note: Coupon codes are sourced from coupons linked via order_discounts.coupon_id actually used in 2025 (comma-joined, 'automatic' if none were used); EUR conversion applies the exchange_rates row for each order's placed_at date (weekend rows already carry forward the prior business day's rate per the warehouse convention). No LIMIT is applied in SQL - per the handbook the report print step caps output at 50 rows and notes the full row count; query is fully ordered by discount_amount_eur desc with discount_name as a deterministic tie-break.

entries.title: Discount spend concentration by tenant and vertical, 2025
entries.question: Are one or two merchants (or one vertical) responsible for most of our discount spend, relative to their share of revenue?
entries.sql:
WITH eligible_orders AS (
    SELECT
        o.id AS order_id,
        o.tenant_id,
        o.grand_total,
        o.currency_code,
        o.placed_at
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
order_revenue_eur AS (
    SELECT
        eo.tenant_id,
        eo.order_id,
        eo.grand_total / er.rate AS revenue_eur
    FROM eligible_orders eo
    JOIN exchange_rates er
      ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
     AND er.quote_code = eo.currency_code
     AND er.as_of = DATE(eo.placed_at)
),
tenant_order_totals AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        SUM(revenue_eur) AS total_revenue_eur,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count
    FROM order_revenue_eur
    GROUP BY tenant_id
),
discount_detail AS (
    SELECT
        od.tenant_id,
        od.order_id,
        od.amount / er.rate AS discount_eur,
        COALESCE(od.coupon_id::varchar, od.code) AS discount_code_key
    FROM order_discounts od
    JOIN eligible_orders eo
      ON eo.order_id = od.order_id
     AND eo.tenant_id = od.tenant_id
    JOIN exchange_rates er
      ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
     AND er.quote_code = od.currency_code
     AND er.as_of = DATE(eo.placed_at)
),
tenant_discount_totals AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        SUM(discount_eur) AS total_discount_eur,
        COUNT(DISTINCT discount_code_key) AS distinct_discount_codes
    FROM discount_detail
    GROUP BY tenant_id
),
combined AS (
    SELECT
        t.name AS tenant_name,
        t.industry AS vertical,
        COALESCE(td.total_discount_eur, 0) AS discount_eur,
        ot.total_revenue_eur AS revenue_eur,
        ot.order_count,
        COALESCE(td.distinct_discount_codes, 0) AS distinct_discount_codes
    FROM tenant_order_totals ot
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ot.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN tenant_discount_totals td ON td.tenant_id = ot.tenant_id
)
SELECT
    tenant_name,
    vertical,
    ROUND(discount_eur, 2) AS discount_amount_eur,
    ROUND(revenue_eur, 2) AS order_revenue_eur,
    ROUND(discount_eur / NULLIF(revenue_eur, 0) * 100, 2) AS discount_pct_of_revenue,
    order_count,
    distinct_discount_codes,
    ROUND(discount_eur / NULLIF(SUM(discount_eur) OVER (), 0) * 100, 2) AS share_of_company_discount_pct
FROM combined
ORDER BY discount_amount_eur DESC, tenant_name
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant (120 tenants expected; report prints the top 50 by discount EUR). Order count and revenue are based on all non-cancelled orders placed in 2025; tenants with zero discounts in the period still appear with 0 discount/share. "Distinct discount codes/coupons" counts distinct coupon_id (falling back to the free-text code when coupon_id is null).

entries.title: Coupon redemption patterns: repeat use, limit breaches and post-expiry usage, 2025
entries.question: Which coupon codes show signs of overuse or abuse — repeated redemption by the same customer, redemptions beyond stated limits, or use after the coupon's campaign window ended?
entries.sql:
WITH redemptions AS (
  SELECT
    cr.coupon_id,
    cr.user_id,
    cr.discount_amount,
    cr.currency_code,
    cr.redeemed_at,
    c.code AS coupon_code,
    c.status,
    c.usage_limit,
    c.per_customer_limit,
    c.starts_at,
    c.expires_at,
    cr.discount_amount / NULLIF(er.rate, 0) AS discount_amount_eur
  FROM coupon_redemptions cr
  JOIN coupons c ON cr.coupon_id = c.id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = cr.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(cr.redeemed_at AS date)
  WHERE cr.redeemed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND cr.redeemed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
per_customer AS (
  SELECT coupon_id, user_id, COUNT(*) AS redemption_count
  FROM redemptions
  GROUP BY coupon_id, user_id
),
customer_max AS (
  SELECT coupon_id, MAX(redemption_count) AS max_redemptions_by_customer
  FROM per_customer
  GROUP BY coupon_id
)
SELECT
  r.coupon_code AS coupon_code,
  MAX(r.status) AS status,
  MAX(r.usage_limit) AS usage_limit,
  MAX(r.per_customer_limit) AS per_customer_limit,
  COUNT(*) AS times_redeemed,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  cm.max_redemptions_by_customer AS max_redemptions_by_customer,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.redeemed_at > r.expires_at) AS redemptions_after_expiry,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.redeemed_at < r.starts_at) AS redemptions_before_start,
  ROUND(SUM(r.discount_amount_eur), 2) AS total_discount_eur
FROM redemptions r
JOIN customer_max cm ON cm.coupon_id = r.coupon_id
GROUP BY r.coupon_id, r.coupon_code, cm.max_redemptions_by_customer
ORDER BY redemptions_after_expiry DESC, max_redemptions_by_customer DESC, coupon_code ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Grouped by coupons.id (coupon_code shown as the label) since codes aren't globally unique across tenants; discount amounts were converted to EUR directly from coupon_redemptions.currency_code/redeemed_at (that table already carries both, so the orders join for currency/placed_at wasn't needed). Full 2023-2025 history was scanned as requested, with the printed table limited to the top 50 most suspicious coupons per the sort order.
warnings: columns usage_limit, per_customer_limit are mostly empty

entries.title: Order economics behind the 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)' discount
entries.question: Is the 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)' discount a real zero-margin giveaway, or does the €0 order revenue reflect that these customers actually pay via a separate subscription invoice?
entries.sql:
WITH disc_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.currency_code, o.placed_at,
         o.subtotal, o.discount_total, o.tax_total, o.shipping_total, o.grand_total
  FROM order_discounts od
  JOIN discounts d ON d.id = od.discount_id AND d.tenant_id = od.tenant_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = od.order_id AND o.tenant_id = od.tenant_id
  WHERE d.name = 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
rated AS (
  SELECT dso.*,
         er.rate,
         dso.subtotal / er.rate AS subtotal_eur,
         dso.discount_total / er.rate AS discount_total_eur,
         dso.tax_total / er.rate AS tax_total_eur,
         dso.shipping_total / er.rate AS shipping_total_eur,
         dso.grand_total / er.rate AS grand_total_eur,
         CASE WHEN EXISTS (
           SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions s
           WHERE s.tenant_id = dso.tenant_id
             AND s.user_id = dso.user_id
             AND s.status IN ('trialing','active','past_due')
             AND s.started_at <= dso.placed_at
             AND (s.ended_at IS NULL OR s.ended_at >= dso.placed_at)
         ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_active_sub
  FROM disc_orders dso
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = dso.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(dso.placed_at AS date)
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(AVG(r.subtotal_eur),2) AS avg_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(r.discount_total_eur),2) AS avg_discount_total_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(r.shipping_total_eur),2) AS avg_shipping_total_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(r.tax_total_eur),2) AS avg_tax_total_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(r.grand_total_eur),2) AS avg_grand_total_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN r.grand_total = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_zero_grand_total,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(r.has_active_sub) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_orders_with_active_subscription
FROM rated r
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
GROUP BY t.name
ORDER BY order_count DESC, tenant_name ASC
builds_on: Discount cost vs. order volume/revenue by discount, 2025
Discount spend concentration by tenant and vertical, 2025
entries.engineer_note: The "% of customers with an active subscription overlapping the order's placed_at date" is computed at order grain (share of orders whose customer had a qualifying subscription at placed_at), since overlap is order-date-dependent and a customer could qualify for some of their orders but not others; pct_zero_grand_total uses the original (pre-conversion) grand_total since 0 is currency-invariant.

entries.title: Coupons with a configured usage cap: actual breaches of usage_limit or per_customer_limit
entries.question: Among coupons that actually have a usage_limit or per_customer_limit configured, which ones have been redeemed beyond that stated cap?
entries.sql:
WITH redemptions AS (
  SELECT
    cr.coupon_id,
    cr.user_id,
    cr.discount_amount,
    cr.currency_code,
    cr.redeemed_at
  FROM coupon_redemptions cr
  WHERE cr.redeemed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND cr.redeemed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
coupon_stats AS (
  SELECT
    r.coupon_id,
    COUNT(*) AS times_redeemed,
    COUNT(DISTINCT r.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
    SUM(r.discount_amount / COALESCE(er.rate, 1)) AS total_discount_eur
  FROM redemptions r
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = r.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(r.redeemed_at AS date)
  GROUP BY r.coupon_id
),
per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    r.coupon_id,
    r.user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS redemption_count
  FROM redemptions r
  GROUP BY r.coupon_id, r.user_id
),
customer_stats AS (
  SELECT
    pc.coupon_id,
    MAX(pc.redemption_count) AS max_redemptions_by_customer,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.per_customer_limit IS NOT NULL AND pc.redemption_count > c.per_customer_limit) AS customers_exceeding
  FROM per_customer pc
  JOIN coupons c ON c.id = pc.coupon_id
  GROUP BY pc.coupon_id
)
SELECT
  c.code AS coupon_code,
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  c.status,
  c.usage_limit,
  c.per_customer_limit,
  COALESCE(cs.times_redeemed, 0) AS times_redeemed,
  CASE WHEN c.usage_limit IS NOT NULL
       THEN GREATEST(COALESCE(cs.times_redeemed, 0) - c.usage_limit, 0)
       ELSE 0 END AS redemptions_over_usage_limit,
  COALESCE(custs.max_redemptions_by_customer, 0) AS max_redemptions_by_customer,
  COALESCE(custs.customers_exceeding, 0) AS customers_exceeding_per_customer_limit,
  ROUND(COALESCE(cs.total_discount_eur, 0), 2) AS total_discount_redeemed_eur,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_matching_coupons
FROM coupons c
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN coupon_stats cs ON cs.coupon_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN customer_stats custs ON custs.coupon_id = c.id
WHERE (c.usage_limit IS NOT NULL OR c.per_customer_limit IS NOT NULL)
  AND (
    (c.usage_limit IS NOT NULL AND COALESCE(cs.times_redeemed, 0) > c.usage_limit)
    OR COALESCE(custs.customers_exceeding, 0) > 0
  )
ORDER BY redemptions_over_usage_limit DESC, customers_exceeding_per_customer_limit DESC, coupon_code ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Coupon redemption patterns: repeat use, limit breaches and post-expiry usage, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Used coupon_redemptions' own currency_code/redeemed_at for EUR conversion (both fields already live on that table), so the orders join mentioned in the request wasn't needed. Added a total_matching_coupons column (count of all coupons meeting the breach criteria before the 50-row cutoff) so you know if the list was truncated.

entries.title: Within-customer order value lift on top discount codes, 2025
entries.question: For our top discounts, do the same customers spend more per order when using the discount than they do on their own other, non-discounted orders — our best approximate read on incrementality?
entries.sql:
WITH discount_order_lines AS (
    SELECT
        t1.id AS order_discount_id,
        t1.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
        t1.order_id AS order_id,
        t1.discount_id AS discount_id,
        t1.code AS coupon_code,
        t1.amount AS discount_amount,
        t1.currency_code AS discount_currency_code,
        t2.user_id AS user_id,
        t2.placed_at AS placed_at,
        t2.currency_code AS order_currency_code,
        t2.grand_total AS order_grand_total,
        t3.name AS discount_name
    FROM order_discounts t1
    JOIN orders t2
        ON t2.id = t1.order_id
       AND t2.tenant_id = t1.tenant_id
    JOIN discounts t3
        ON t3.id = t1.discount_id
       AND t3.tenant_id = t1.tenant_id
    WHERE t2.status <> 'cancelled'
      AND t2.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND t2.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND t3.name <> 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)'
),
discount_order_lines_eur AS (
    SELECT
        t4.*,
        t4.discount_amount / NULLIF(t5.rate, 0) AS discount_amount_eur,
        t4.order_grand_total / NULLIF(t6.rate, 0) AS order_grand_total_eur
    FROM discount_order_lines t4
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates t5
        ON t5.base_code = 'EUR'
       AND t5.quote_code = t4.discount_currency_code
       AND t5.as_of = CAST(t4.placed_at AS DATE)
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates t6
        ON t6.base_code = 'EUR'
       AND t6.quote_code = t4.order_currency_code
       AND t6.as_of = CAST(t4.placed_at AS DATE)
),
discounted_orders_distinct AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        discount_id,
        discount_name,
        tenant_id,
        order_id,
        user_id,
        order_grand_total_eur
    FROM discount_order_lines_eur
),
discount_spend AS (
    SELECT
        discount_id,
        discount_name,
        SUM(discount_amount_eur) AS total_discount_spend_eur
    FROM discount_order_lines_eur
    GROUP BY discount_id, discount_name
),
top_discounts AS (
    SELECT discount_id, discount_name, total_discount_spend_eur
    FROM discount_spend
    ORDER BY total_discount_spend_eur DESC
    LIMIT 15
),
discount_order_count AS (
    SELECT discount_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count
    FROM discounted_orders_distinct
    GROUP BY discount_id
),
discount_customer_count AS (
    SELECT discount_id, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS distinct_customers
    FROM discounted_orders_distinct
    GROUP BY discount_id
),
discount_avg_value AS (
    SELECT discount_id, AVG(order_grand_total_eur) AS avg_discounted_order_value_eur
    FROM discounted_orders_distinct
    GROUP BY discount_id
),
discount_coupon_code AS (
    SELECT discount_id, MAX(coupon_code) AS coupon_code
    FROM discount_order_lines_eur
    GROUP BY discount_id
),
customer_discount_pairs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT discount_id, tenant_id, user_id
    FROM discounted_orders_distinct
    WHERE discount_id IN (SELECT discount_id FROM top_discounts)
),
non_discounted_orders AS (
    SELECT
        t7.id AS order_id,
        t7.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
        t7.user_id AS user_id,
        t7.placed_at AS placed_at,
        t7.currency_code AS currency_code,
        t7.grand_total AS grand_total
    FROM orders t7
    WHERE t7.status <> 'cancelled'
      AND t7.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND t7.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts t8
          WHERE t8.order_id = t7.id AND t8.tenant_id = t7.tenant_id
      )
),
non_discounted_orders_eur AS (
    SELECT
        t9.*,
        t9.grand_total / NULLIF(t10.rate, 0) AS grand_total_eur
    FROM non_discounted_orders t9
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates t10
        ON t10.base_code = 'EUR'
       AND t10.quote_code = t9.currency_code
       AND t10.as_of = CAST(t9.placed_at AS DATE)
),
comparison_orders AS (
    SELECT
        t11.discount_id AS discount_id,
        t11.user_id AS user_id,
        t12.order_id AS order_id,
        t12.grand_total_eur AS grand_total_eur
    FROM customer_discount_pairs t11
    JOIN non_discounted_orders_eur t12
        ON t12.tenant_id = t11.tenant_id
       AND t12.user_id = t11.user_id
),
discount_comparison_avg AS (
    SELECT discount_id, AVG(grand_total_eur) AS avg_other_order_value_eur
    FROM comparison_orders
    GROUP BY discount_id
),
discount_comparison_customers AS (
    SELECT discount_id, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customers_with_other_orders
    FROM comparison_orders
    GROUP BY discount_id
)
SELECT
    t0.discount_name AS discount_name,
    COALESCE(t13.coupon_code, 'automatic') AS coupon_code,
    COALESCE(t14.order_count, 0) AS discounted_order_count,
    COALESCE(t15.distinct_customers, 0) AS distinct_customers,
    ROUND(COALESCE(t16.avg_discounted_order_value_eur, 0), 2) AS avg_discounted_order_value_eur,
    ROUND(t17.avg_other_order_value_eur, 2) AS avg_other_order_value_eur,
    ROUND(COALESCE(t16.avg_discounted_order_value_eur, 0) - t17.avg_other_order_value_eur, 2) AS lift_eur,
    ROUND(
        (COALESCE(t16.avg_discounted_order_value_eur, 0) - t17.avg_other_order_value_eur)
        / NULLIF(t17.avg_other_order_value_eur, 0) * 100, 1
    ) AS lift_pct,
    ROUND(
        CAST(COALESCE(t18.customers_with_other_orders, 0) AS DECIMAL)
        / NULLIF(t15.distinct_customers, 0) * 100, 1
    ) AS pct_customers_with_other_nondiscounted_order
FROM top_discounts t0
LEFT JOIN discount_coupon_code t13 ON t13.discount_id = t0.discount_id
LEFT JOIN discount_order_count t14 ON t14.discount_id = t0.discount_id
LEFT JOIN discount_customer_count t15 ON t15.discount_id = t0.discount_id
LEFT JOIN discount_avg_value t16 ON t16.discount_id = t0.discount_id
LEFT JOIN discount_comparison_avg t17 ON t17.discount_id = t0.discount_id
LEFT JOIN discount_comparison_customers t18 ON t18.discount_id = t0.discount_id
ORDER BY lift_pct ASC NULLS LAST, discount_name ASC
builds_on: Discount cost vs. order volume/revenue by discount, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Restricted to the top 15 discounts (by 2025 discount_amount converted to EUR, excluding 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)'); coupon code is picked as MAX(code) seen on that discount's redemptions since a discount can in principle be tied to more than one code. Rows where a discount's customers had zero other non-discounted 2025 orders show NULL for avg/lift columns and 0% in the last column — watch for discounts with a low distinct_customers count or low pct_customers_with_other_nondiscounted_order, as the within-customer comparison is weak/unavailable there.

entries.title: Subscription-delivery discount orders with no overlapping active subscription
entries.question: Among the fully-comped 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)' orders, are the ones with no active subscription at the time concentrated in a few customers, or traceable to subscriptions that had just lapsed — or are they true unexplained giveaways?
entries.sql:
WITH discount_orders AS (
  select
    o.id as order_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.placed_at,
    od.amount as discount_amount,
    od.currency_code
  from order_discounts od
  join discounts d on d.id = od.discount_id and d.name = 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)'
  join orders o on o.id = od.order_id
  where o.placed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
    and o.placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
    and o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
orphan_flagged AS (
  select
    do_.*,
    case when exists (
      select 1 from subscriptions s
      where s.tenant_id = do_.tenant_id
        and s.user_id = do_.user_id
        and s.started_at <= do_.placed_at
        and (s.ended_at is null or s.ended_at >= do_.placed_at)
        and s.status in ('trialing','active','past_due')
    ) then false else true end as is_orphan
  from discount_orders do_
),
orphan_only AS (
  select * from orphan_flagged where is_orphan
),
customer_orphan AS (
  select tenant_id, user_id, max(placed_at) as last_order_at, count(*) as orphan_order_count
  from orphan_only
  group by tenant_id, user_id
),
subs_ranked AS (
  select
    s.tenant_id, s.user_id, s.status, s.ended_at, s.started_at,
    row_number() over (partition by s.tenant_id, s.user_id order by s.started_at desc, s.id desc) as rn
  from subscriptions s
),
most_recent_sub AS (
  select tenant_id, user_id, status, ended_at
  from subs_ranked
  where rn = 1
),
customer_classified AS (
  select
    co.tenant_id,
    co.user_id,
    co.orphan_order_count,
    case
      when mrs.user_id is null then 'no_sub'
      when mrs.status = 'canceled' and mrs.ended_at is not null
        and mrs.ended_at >= co.last_order_at - interval '30 days'
        and mrs.ended_at <= co.last_order_at
      then 'lapsed'
      else 'other'
    end as classification
  from customer_orphan co
  left join most_recent_sub mrs
    on mrs.tenant_id = co.tenant_id and mrs.user_id = co.user_id
),
orphan_eur AS (
  select
    oo.tenant_id,
    oo.order_id,
    oo.discount_amount / er.rate as discount_amount_eur
  from orphan_only oo
  join exchange_rates er
    on er.base_code = 'EUR'
    and er.quote_code = oo.currency_code
    and er.as_of = cast(oo.placed_at as date)
),
tenant_totals AS (
  select tenant_id, count(*) as total_discount_orders
  from discount_orders
  group by tenant_id
),
tenant_orphan AS (
  select
    tenant_id,
    count(*) as orphan_order_count,
    count(distinct user_id) as orphan_customers
  from orphan_only
  group by tenant_id
),
tenant_max_customer AS (
  select tenant_id, max(orphan_order_count) as max_orphan_per_customer
  from customer_orphan
  group by tenant_id
),
tenant_class AS (
  select
    tenant_id,
    count(*) as total_customers,
    sum(case when classification = 'lapsed' then 1 else 0 end) as lapsed_customers,
    sum(case when classification = 'no_sub' then 1 else 0 end) as no_sub_customers
  from customer_classified
  group by tenant_id
),
tenant_eur AS (
  select tenant_id, sum(discount_amount_eur) as total_discount_eur
  from orphan_eur
  group by tenant_id
)
select
  t.name as tenant_name,
  tor.orphan_order_count,
  round(100.0 * tor.orphan_order_count / tt.total_discount_orders, 1) as orphan_pct_of_discount_orders,
  tor.orphan_customers as distinct_orphan_customers,
  tmc.max_orphan_per_customer,
  round(100.0 * tc.lapsed_customers / nullif(tc.total_customers,0), 1) as pct_lapsed_subscriber,
  round(100.0 * tc.no_sub_customers / nullif(tc.total_customers,0), 1) as pct_no_subscription_record,
  round(te.total_discount_eur, 2) as total_discount_amount_eur
from tenant_orphan tor
join tenants t on t.id = tor.tenant_id
join tenant_totals tt on tt.tenant_id = tor.tenant_id
join tenant_max_customer tmc on tmc.tenant_id = tor.tenant_id
join tenant_class tc on tc.tenant_id = tor.tenant_id
join tenant_eur te on te.tenant_id = tor.tenant_id
order by tor.orphan_order_count desc, t.name asc
builds_on: Order economics behind the 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)' discount
entries.engineer_note: For the lapsed/no-subscription classification, each orphan customer's "most recent subscription" is taken as their single latest subscription record (by started_at) for that tenant, and the 30-day lapse window is measured against that customer's most recent orphan-order date (customers can have several orphan orders). Customers who are neither lapsed nor no-record fall into an implicit 'other' (true unexplained) bucket, recoverable as 100% minus the two reported percentages.

entries.title: Corrected incrementality read: pre-discount basket size on top marketing discounts, 2025
entries.question: Using basket size before the discount is applied (subtotal), do customers actually buy bigger baskets when using our top marketing discount codes, or was the earlier post-discount comparison just showing the mechanical effect of the discount itself?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  d.name AS discount_name,
  COALESCE(cc.coupon_code, 'automatic') AS coupon_code,
  disc.order_count AS discounted_order_count,
  disc.customer_count AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(disc.avg_subtotal_eur, 2) AS avg_discounted_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(cmp.avg_subtotal_eur, 2) AS avg_comparison_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(disc.avg_subtotal_eur - cmp.avg_subtotal_eur, 2) AS subtotal_lift_eur,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN cmp.avg_subtotal_eur IS NULL OR cmp.avg_subtotal_eur = 0 THEN NULL
             ELSE (disc.avg_subtotal_eur - cmp.avg_subtotal_eur) / cmp.avg_subtotal_eur * 100 END, 1) AS subtotal_lift_pct,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN disc.customer_count = 0 THEN NULL
             ELSE 100.0 * cmp.customers_with_comparison / disc.customer_count END, 1) AS pct_customers_with_comparison_order,
  (disc.customer_count - cmp.customers_with_comparison) AS customers_with_no_comparison_order
FROM discounts d
JOIN (
  SELECT dconv.discount_id,
         COUNT(*) AS order_count,
         COUNT(DISTINCT dconv.user_id) AS customer_count,
         AVG(dconv.subtotal_eur) AS avg_subtotal_eur
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT od.discount_id, o.id AS order_id, o.user_id,
           CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.subtotal ELSE o.subtotal / er.rate END AS subtotal_eur
    FROM order_discounts od
    JOIN orders o ON o.id = od.order_id AND o.tenant_id = od.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
           AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
           AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
    WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
      AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND od.discount_id IN (
        SELECT id FROM discounts
        WHERE name IN ('Welcome 10% off', 'Black Friday 2025', 'January Sale 2025', 'Summer Sale 2025')
      )
  ) dconv
  GROUP BY dconv.discount_id
) disc ON disc.discount_id = d.id
JOIN (
  SELECT dcust.discount_id,
         COUNT(cp.user_id) AS customers_with_comparison,
         SUM(cp.cmp_subtotal_sum) / NULLIF(SUM(cp.cmp_order_count), 0) AS avg_subtotal_eur
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT od.discount_id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id
    FROM order_discounts od
    JOIN orders o ON o.id = od.order_id AND o.tenant_id = od.tenant_id
    WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
      AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND od.discount_id IN (
        SELECT id FROM discounts
        WHERE name IN ('Welcome 10% off', 'Black Friday 2025', 'January Sale 2025', 'Summer Sale 2025')
      )
  ) dcust
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT o2.tenant_id, o2.user_id,
           COUNT(*) AS cmp_order_count,
           SUM(CASE WHEN o2.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o2.subtotal ELSE o2.subtotal / er2.rate END) AS cmp_subtotal_sum
    FROM orders o2
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2 ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
           AND er2.quote_code = o2.currency_code
           AND er2.as_of = CAST(o2.placed_at AS date)
    WHERE o2.status <> 'cancelled'
      AND o2.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND o2.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts od2 WHERE od2.order_id = o2.id
      )
    GROUP BY o2.tenant_id, o2.user_id
  ) cp ON cp.tenant_id = dcust.tenant_id AND cp.user_id = dcust.user_id
  GROUP BY dcust.discount_id
) cmp ON cmp.discount_id = d.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT discount_id, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT code, ', ') AS coupon_code
  FROM order_discounts
  WHERE code IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY discount_id
) cc ON cc.discount_id = d.id
WHERE d.name IN ('Welcome 10% off', 'Black Friday 2025', 'January Sale 2025', 'Summer Sale 2025')
ORDER BY subtotal_lift_pct ASC, discount_name ASC, d.id ASC
builds_on: Within-customer order value lift on top discount codes, 2025
entries.engineer_note: I could not re-derive the exact "top 15 by discount_amount_eur" list from the prior report (no data access in dry runs), so I selected discount rows by exact name match on the four named campaigns (discounts.name IN (...)), which naturally includes every tenant/coupon-variant row sharing those names and excludes Volume tier and Subscription delivery as requested. Added "customers_with_no_comparison_order" as an explicit count column so the analyst sees that figure directly rather than only in a note.

entries.title: Return and refund rates on discounted orders vs. baseline, 2025
entries.question: Do orders placed under our top discounts return or get refunded at a higher rate than normal, meaning the real cost is higher than the discount line alone suggests?
entries.sql:
WITH discount_eur AS (
  SELECT od.discount_id,
         SUM(od.amount / er.rate) AS discount_amount_eur
  FROM order_discounts od
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = od.order_id
  JOIN discounts d ON d.id = od.discount_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = od.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND d.name <> 'Subscription delivery'
  GROUP BY od.discount_id
),
top15 AS (
  SELECT discount_id, discount_amount_eur,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY discount_amount_eur DESC, discount_id ASC) AS rn
  FROM discount_eur
),
discounted_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT od.discount_id, o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id
  FROM order_discounts od
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = od.order_id
  WHERE od.discount_id IN (SELECT discount_id FROM top15 WHERE rn <= 15)
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
),
order_rma_flag AS (
  SELECT dco.discount_id, dco.order_id,
         EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns orr WHERE orr.order_id = dco.order_id) AS has_rma
  FROM discounted_orders dco
),
discount_summary AS (
  SELECT dco.discount_id,
         COUNT(DISTINCT dco.order_id) AS order_count,
         COUNT(DISTINCT dco.order_id) FILTER (WHERE f.has_rma) AS orders_with_rma
  FROM discounted_orders dco
  JOIN order_rma_flag f ON f.discount_id = dco.discount_id AND f.order_id = dco.order_id
  GROUP BY dco.discount_id
),
refunds AS (
  SELECT dco.discount_id,
         SUM(orr.refund_total / er.rate) AS refund_eur
  FROM discounted_orders dco
  JOIN order_returns orr ON orr.order_id = dco.order_id AND orr.status = 'refunded'
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = dco.order_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = orr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(orr.refunded_at, o.placed_at) AS date)
  GROUP BY dco.discount_id
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
         COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS baseline_order_count,
         COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) FILTER (
           WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns orr2 WHERE orr2.order_id = o.id)
         ) AS baseline_rma_count
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts od2 WHERE od2.order_id = o.id)
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  d.name AS discount_name,
  COALESCE(cc.code, 'automatic') AS coupon_code,
  ds.order_count,
  ds.orders_with_rma,
  ROUND(100.0 * ds.orders_with_rma / NULLIF(ds.order_count, 0), 2) AS return_rate_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.refund_eur, 0), 2) AS total_refunded_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(r.refund_eur, 0) / NULLIF(t.discount_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS refund_pct_of_discount_cost,
  ROUND(100.0 * b.baseline_rma_count / NULLIF(b.baseline_order_count, 0), 2) AS baseline_return_rate_pct,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * ds.orders_with_rma / NULLIF(ds.order_count, 0)
    - 100.0 * b.baseline_rma_count / NULLIF(b.baseline_order_count, 0), 2
  ) AS return_rate_lift_pp
FROM top15 t
JOIN discounts d ON d.id = t.discount_id
JOIN discount_summary ds ON ds.discount_id = t.discount_id
LEFT JOIN refunds r ON r.discount_id = t.discount_id
LEFT JOIN baseline b ON b.tenant_id = d.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT c.code FROM coupons c WHERE c.discount_id = d.id ORDER BY c.id LIMIT 1
) cc ON true
WHERE t.rn <= 15
ORDER BY return_rate_lift_pp DESC NULLS LAST, discount_name ASC
builds_on: Discount cost vs. order volume/revenue by discount, 2025
Within-customer order value lift on top discount codes, 2025
entries.engineer_note: I recomputed the top-15 discount set within this query (2025 discount_amount_eur from order_discounts, excluding discounts named 'Subscription delivery') since the prior night's exact ranking query wasn't available to me here; if that differs from the original lift-analysis set please flag it and I'll re-run against the exact 15 discount_ids. Coupon code is taken as the first coupon linked to the discount (or 'automatic' if none).

entries.title: Subscription status distribution behind orphan comped-delivery orders
entries.question: What subscription status do the 'orphan' Subscription-delivery-discount customers (no active subscription overlap found) actually have on record, since neither 'lapsed within 30 days' nor 'no subscription at all' explained them?
entries.sql:
WITH orphan_orders AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    o.user_id AS user_id,
    o.placed_at AS placed_at,
    od.amount AS discount_amount,
    od.currency_code AS discount_currency
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_discounts od
    ON od.order_id = o.id
   AND od.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN discounts d
    ON d.id = od.discount_id
   AND d.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE d.name = 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM subscriptions s
      WHERE s.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
        AND s.user_id = o.user_id
        AND s.status IN ('trialing','active','past_due')
        AND s.started_at <= o.placed_at
        AND (s.ended_at IS NULL OR s.ended_at >= o.placed_at)
    )
),
latest_subscription AS (
  SELECT
    s.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    s.user_id AS user_id,
    s.status AS status,
    s.ended_at AS ended_at,
    s.started_at AS started_at,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.tenant_id, s.user_id ORDER BY s.started_at DESC, s.id DESC) AS rn
  FROM subscriptions s
),
orphan_with_category AS (
  SELECT
    oo.order_id AS order_id,
    oo.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    oo.user_id AS user_id,
    oo.placed_at AS placed_at,
    oo.discount_amount AS discount_amount,
    oo.discount_currency AS discount_currency,
    COALESCE(ls.status, 'no_subscription_record') AS status_category,
    ls.ended_at AS sub_ended_at
  FROM orphan_orders oo
  LEFT JOIN latest_subscription ls
    ON ls.tenant_id = oo.tenant_id
   AND ls.user_id = oo.user_id
   AND ls.rn = 1
),
t0 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT status_category FROM orphan_with_category
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT status_category, COUNT(*) AS orphan_customer_count
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT status_category, tenant_id, user_id
    FROM orphan_with_category
  ) dc
  GROUP BY status_category
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT status_category, COUNT(*) AS orphan_order_count
  FROM orphan_with_category
  GROUP BY status_category
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orphan_orders FROM orphan_with_category
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT status_category,
         AVG(COALESCE(sub_ended_at::date, DATE '2026-01-05') - placed_at::date) AS avg_days_sub_end_to_order
  FROM orphan_with_category
  WHERE status_category <> 'no_subscription_record'
  GROUP BY status_category
),
t5 AS (
  SELECT ow.status_category,
         SUM(
           CASE WHEN ow.discount_currency = 'EUR' THEN ow.discount_amount
                ELSE ow.discount_amount / er.rate
           END
         ) AS total_discount_eur
  FROM orphan_with_category ow
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = ow.discount_currency
   AND er.as_of = ow.placed_at::date
  GROUP BY ow.status_category
)
SELECT
  t0.status_category AS status_category,
  COALESCE(t1.orphan_customer_count, 0) AS orphan_customer_count,
  COALESCE(t2.orphan_order_count, 0) AS orphan_order_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t2.orphan_order_count, 0) / NULLIF(t3.total_orphan_orders, 0), 2) AS pct_of_all_orphan_orders,
  ROUND(t4.avg_days_sub_end_to_order, 1) AS avg_days_sub_end_to_order,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t5.total_discount_eur, 0), 2) AS total_discount_amount_eur
FROM t0
LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.status_category = t0.status_category
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.status_category = t0.status_category
CROSS JOIN t3
LEFT JOIN t4 ON t4.status_category = t0.status_category
LEFT JOIN t5 ON t5.status_category = t0.status_category
ORDER BY COALESCE(t2.orphan_order_count, 0) DESC, t0.status_category ASC
builds_on: Subscription-delivery discount orders with no overlapping active subscription
entries.engineer_note: Rebuilt the orphan-order population per the stated definition (2025 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)' order_discounts, status != 'cancelled', no date-overlapping subscription in trialing/active/past_due for that tenant+user). For each orphan customer's most recent subscription (any status, latest by started_at), categorized orders/customers by that status or 'no_subscription_record'. Avg-days-to-ended_at uses the fixed reporting date 2026-01-05 for still-open subscriptions and is left null for the no_subscription_record category where it doesn't apply; discount amounts converted to EUR via same-day exchange_rates (base=EUR) divided into the discount currency.

entries.title: Aggregate within-customer basket-size lift by promotion family, 2025
entries.question: Across all tenants running each major marketing promotion, do customers buy bigger baskets (pre-discount subtotal) when using the code, stated as one clean weighted number per promotion family?
entries.sql:
WITH promo_names AS (
  SELECT name FROM (VALUES
    ('Welcome 10% off'),
    ('Black Friday 2025'),
    ('January Sale 2025'),
    ('Summer Sale 2025')
  ) AS v(name)
),
discounted AS (
  SELECT d.name AS promo_name,
         d.id AS discount_id,
         o.tenant_id,
         o.user_id,
         o.id AS order_id,
         o.subtotal / er.rate AS subtotal_eur
  FROM order_discounts od
  JOIN discounts d ON d.id = od.discount_id AND d.tenant_id = od.tenant_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = od.order_id AND o.tenant_id = od.tenant_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = DATE(o.placed_at)
  WHERE d.name IN (SELECT name FROM promo_names)
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
discounted_orders AS (
  SELECT promo_name, tenant_id, user_id, order_id, MAX(subtotal_eur) AS subtotal_eur
  FROM discounted
  GROUP BY promo_name, tenant_id, user_id, order_id
),
instance_customers AS (
  SELECT promo_name, discount_id, COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id || ':' || user_id) AS customers_in_instance
  FROM discounted
  GROUP BY promo_name, discount_id
),
discounted_agg AS (
  SELECT promo_name,
         COUNT(*) AS discounted_order_count,
         SUM(subtotal_eur) AS discounted_subtotal_sum
  FROM discounted_orders
  GROUP BY promo_name
),
instance_agg AS (
  SELECT promo_name,
         COUNT(DISTINCT discount_id) AS discount_instances,
         SUM(customers_in_instance) AS distinct_customers_summed
  FROM instance_customers
  GROUP BY promo_name
),
customer_set AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT promo_name, tenant_id, user_id FROM discounted_orders
),
customer_set_agg AS (
  SELECT promo_name, COUNT(*) AS customer_set_count FROM customer_set GROUP BY promo_name
),
comparison_orders AS (
  SELECT cs.promo_name, cs.tenant_id, cs.user_id, o.id AS order_id,
         o.subtotal / er.rate AS subtotal_eur
  FROM customer_set cs
  JOIN orders o ON o.tenant_id = cs.tenant_id AND o.user_id = cs.user_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = DATE(o.placed_at)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts od2
      WHERE od2.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND od2.order_id = o.id
    )
),
comparison_agg AS (
  SELECT promo_name,
         COUNT(*) AS comparison_order_count,
         SUM(subtotal_eur) AS comparison_subtotal_sum,
         COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id || ':' || user_id) AS customers_with_comparison
  FROM comparison_orders
  GROUP BY promo_name
)
SELECT
  pn.name AS promotion_name,
  COALESCE(ia.discount_instances, 0) AS discount_instances,
  COALESCE(da.discounted_order_count, 0) AS discounted_order_count,
  COALESCE(ia.distinct_customers_summed, 0) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(da.discounted_subtotal_sum / NULLIF(da.discounted_order_count,0), 2) AS avg_discounted_order_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(ca.comparison_subtotal_sum / NULLIF(ca.comparison_order_count,0), 2) AS avg_comparison_order_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(
    (da.discounted_subtotal_sum / NULLIF(da.discounted_order_count,0))
    - (ca.comparison_subtotal_sum / NULLIF(ca.comparison_order_count,0))
  , 2) AS subtotal_lift_eur,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * (
      (da.discounted_subtotal_sum / NULLIF(da.discounted_order_count,0))
      - (ca.comparison_subtotal_sum / NULLIF(ca.comparison_order_count,0))
    ) / NULLIF(ca.comparison_subtotal_sum / NULLIF(ca.comparison_order_count,0), 0)
  , 1) AS subtotal_lift_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(ca.customers_with_comparison,0) / NULLIF(cs.customer_set_count,0), 1) AS pct_customers_with_comparison_order
FROM promo_names pn
LEFT JOIN instance_agg ia ON ia.promo_name = pn.name
LEFT JOIN discounted_agg da ON da.promo_name = pn.name
LEFT JOIN customer_set_agg cs ON cs.promo_name = pn.name
LEFT JOIN comparison_agg ca ON ca.promo_name = pn.name
ORDER BY subtotal_lift_pct ASC NULLS LAST, pn.name
builds_on: Corrected incrementality read: pre-discount basket size on top marketing discounts, 2025
entries.engineer_note: "Distinct customers" is summed per discount instance (a customer appearing under two same-named discount rows in one tenant counts twice), while the comparison-order share uses a tenant-deduplicated customer set, per the request's distinct definitions for those two columns. Comparison orders exclude any order with any order_discounts row (not just this promotion), matching "no row in order_discounts".

entries.title: Concentration of refund cost on the two highest refund-to-discount-ratio instances
entries.question: For the two discount instances whose total refunds exceeded their own discount cost (Welcome 10% off with 260 orders, Volume tier 10+ with 104 orders, both from the prior return-rate report), is that refund cost driven by a handful of large refunds or spread broadly across many orders?
entries.sql:
WITH discount_orders AS (
  SELECT od.discount_id, d.name AS discount_name, o.id AS order_id, o.grand_total, o.currency_code
  FROM order_discounts od
  JOIN discounts d ON d.id = od.discount_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = od.order_id
  WHERE d.name IN ('Welcome 10% off', 'Volume tier 10+')
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
discount_counts AS (
  SELECT discount_id, discount_name, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM discount_orders
  GROUP BY discount_id, discount_name
),
target_discounts AS (
  SELECT discount_id, discount_name, order_count
  FROM discount_counts
  WHERE (discount_name = 'Welcome 10% off' AND order_count = 260)
     OR (discount_name = 'Volume tier 10+' AND order_count = 104)
),
target_orders AS (
  SELECT do2.discount_id, td.discount_name, td.order_count, do2.order_id, do2.grand_total, do2.currency_code
  FROM discount_orders do2
  JOIN target_discounts td ON td.discount_id = do2.discount_id
),
refunds AS (
  SELECT
    tord.discount_id,
    tord.discount_name,
    tord.order_count,
    tord.order_id,
    tord.grand_total,
    orr.id AS return_id,
    orr.refund_total,
    orr.refunded_at,
    (orr.refund_total / er.rate) AS refund_eur
  FROM target_orders tord
  JOIN order_returns orr ON orr.order_id = tord.order_id AND orr.status = 'refunded'
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = orr.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(orr.refunded_at AS date)
),
order_refund_totals AS (
  SELECT discount_id, discount_name, order_id, grand_total, SUM(refund_total) AS total_refund_native
  FROM refunds
  GROUP BY discount_id, discount_name, order_id, grand_total
),
ranked_refunds AS (
  SELECT
    discount_id,
    discount_name,
    refund_eur,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY discount_id ORDER BY refund_eur DESC) AS rn
  FROM refunds
),
discount_agg AS (
  SELECT
    discount_id,
    discount_name,
    COUNT(*) AS refund_count,
    SUM(refund_eur) AS total_refund_eur,
    MAX(refund_eur) AS max_refund_eur,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY refund_eur) AS median_refund_eur
  FROM refunds
  GROUP BY discount_id, discount_name
),
top3_agg AS (
  SELECT discount_id, SUM(refund_eur) AS top3_sum
  FROM ranked_refunds
  WHERE rn <= 3
  GROUP BY discount_id
),
full_refund_agg AS (
  SELECT discount_id, COUNT(*) AS full_refund_orders
  FROM order_refund_totals
  WHERE total_refund_native >= grand_total
  GROUP BY discount_id
)
SELECT
  td.discount_name AS discount_name,
  td.order_count AS order_count,
  ROUND(da.total_refund_eur, 2) AS total_refunded_eur,
  da.refund_count AS refund_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * t3.top3_sum / NULLIF(da.total_refund_eur,0), 1) AS top3_pct_of_total,
  ROUND(da.median_refund_eur, 2) AS median_refund_eur,
  ROUND(da.max_refund_eur, 2) AS max_refund_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(fr.full_refund_orders,0) / td.order_count, 1) AS pct_orders_fully_refunded
FROM target_discounts td
JOIN discount_agg da ON da.discount_id = td.discount_id
LEFT JOIN top3_agg t3 ON t3.discount_id = td.discount_id
LEFT JOIN full_refund_agg fr ON fr.discount_id = td.discount_id
ORDER BY td.discount_name ASC
builds_on: Return and refund rates on discounted orders vs. baseline, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Discount instances are re-identified by matching the exact 2025 non-cancelled order count (260 / 104) as specified. "Refunded in full" is evaluated by summing all refunded order_returns per order (in native currency) against the order's grand_total, since a single order can have multiple partial refunds; amounts are converted to EUR via exchange_rates as_of the refund date.

entries.title: Loyalty points and referral reward cost by month
entries.question: How much is the loyalty/referral programme costing the business each month - points value issued and redeemed, outstanding points liability, and referral rewards paid - and is that cost trending up or down?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
),
loyalty_tx AS (
  SELECT
    lt.id,
    lt.direction,
    lt.occurred_at,
    lp.currency_code,
    (CAST(lt.points AS numeric) / lp.points_per_currency) AS amount_in_currency
  FROM loyalty_transactions lt
  JOIN loyalty_accounts la ON la.id = lt.loyalty_account_id
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la.loyalty_program_id
  WHERE lt.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND lt.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
loyalty_tx_eur AS (
  SELECT
    lt.direction,
    lt.amount_in_currency / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN lt.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS amount_eur,
    date_trunc('month', lt.occurred_at)::date AS month_start
  FROM loyalty_tx lt
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = lt.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(lt.occurred_at AS date)
),
loyalty_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'earn' THEN ABS(amount_eur) ELSE 0 END) AS earned_value_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction <> 'earn' THEN ABS(amount_eur) ELSE 0 END) AS redeemed_value_eur
  FROM loyalty_tx_eur
  GROUP BY month_start
),
referral_tx AS (
  SELECT
    rr.redeemed_at,
    rr.reward_amount,
    rr.currency_code
  FROM referral_redemptions rr
  WHERE rr.redeemed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND rr.redeemed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND rr.reward_amount IS NOT NULL
),
referral_tx_eur AS (
  SELECT
    rt.reward_amount / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN rt.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS amount_eur,
    date_trunc('month', rt.redeemed_at)::date AS month_start
  FROM referral_tx rt
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = rt.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(rt.redeemed_at AS date)
),
referral_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    month_start,
    SUM(amount_eur) AS referral_rewards_paid_eur,
    COUNT(*) AS referral_redemptions_count
  FROM referral_tx_eur
  GROUP BY month_start
),
enrollments_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', enrolled_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS new_enrollments
  FROM loyalty_accounts
  WHERE enrolled_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND enrolled_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', enrolled_at)::date
),
combined AS (
  SELECT
    m.month_label,
    m.month_start,
    COALESCE(lm.earned_value_eur, 0) AS points_earned_value_eur,
    COALESCE(lm.redeemed_value_eur, 0) AS points_redeemed_value_eur,
    COALESCE(lm.earned_value_eur, 0) - COALESCE(lm.redeemed_value_eur, 0) AS net_points_liability_change_eur,
    COALESCE(rm.referral_rewards_paid_eur, 0) AS referral_rewards_paid_eur,
    COALESCE(rm.referral_redemptions_count, 0) AS referral_redemptions_count,
    COALESCE(em.new_enrollments, 0) AS new_loyalty_enrollments
  FROM months m
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_monthly lm ON lm.month_start = m.month_start
  LEFT JOIN referral_monthly rm ON rm.month_start = m.month_start
  LEFT JOIN enrollments_monthly em ON em.month_start = m.month_start
)
SELECT
  month_label AS month,
  ROUND(points_earned_value_eur, 2) AS points_earned_value_eur,
  ROUND(points_redeemed_value_eur, 2) AS points_redeemed_value_eur,
  ROUND(net_points_liability_change_eur, 2) AS net_points_liability_change_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(net_points_liability_change_eur) OVER (ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS cumulative_points_liability_eur,
  ROUND(referral_rewards_paid_eur, 2) AS referral_rewards_paid_eur,
  referral_redemptions_count,
  new_loyalty_enrollments
FROM combined
ORDER BY month_start
entries.engineer_note: Direction 'earn' is treated as issuance and any other direction value as redemption, per the request; magnitudes are taken as absolute point values. EUR conversion uses the exchange rate as of the transaction/redemption date, falling back to rate=1 only when the program/redemption currency is already EUR and no matching rate row exists. 36 monthly rows (2023-01 through 2025-12) are produced, all fitting on one page.

entries.title: Loyalty member vs non-member customer behavior
entries.question: Do enrolled loyalty members actually order more often, spend more, stick around longer, and return items less than non-member customers, as of today?
entries.sql:
WITH orders_base AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.status,
    o.currency_code,
    o.grand_total,
    COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at) AS order_date
  FROM orders o
  JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id AND u.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at) >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at) < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
orders_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    ob.*,
    CASE WHEN ob.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ob.grand_total
         ELSE ob.grand_total / er.rate END AS eur_amount,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = ob.order_id AND p.amount_refunded > 0) AS has_refund,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = ob.order_id) AS has_return
  FROM orders_base ob
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = ob.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(ob.order_date AS DATE)
),
customer_agg AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status <> 'cancelled') AS noncancelled_orders,
    SUM(eur_amount) FILTER (WHERE status <> 'cancelled') AS noncancelled_revenue,
    MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date,
    MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE has_refund OR has_return) AS refunded_orders
  FROM orders_enriched
  GROUP BY user_id
),
segmented AS (
  SELECT
    ca.*,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la WHERE la.user_id = ca.user_id)
         THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
  FROM customer_agg ca
)
SELECT
  segment,
  COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
  ROUND(AVG(total_orders)::numeric, 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND((SUM(noncancelled_revenue) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0))::numeric, 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND((SUM(noncancelled_revenue) / NULLIF(SUM(noncancelled_orders),0))::numeric, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND((AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (last_order_date - first_order_date)) / 86400.0))::numeric, 1) AS avg_tenure_days,
  ROUND((100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE total_orders >= 2) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0))::numeric, 1) AS repeat_purchase_rate_pct,
  ROUND((100.0 * SUM(refunded_orders) / NULLIF(SUM(total_orders),0))::numeric, 1) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM segmented
GROUP BY segment
ORDER BY CASE WHEN segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, segment
entries.engineer_note: Lifetime orders/repeat-rate/refund-rate denominators use all orders (any status) per the population definition; revenue and AOV use non-cancelled orders only, as specified. Tenure and revenue dates use COALESCE(placed_at, created_at); EUR conversion divides local amount by the EUR→currency exchange rate for that date.

entries.title: Referred vs non-referred customer early behavior
entries.question: Do customers acquired through a referral behave better in their first 90 days - more orders, more revenue, more likely to return, fewer refunds - than customers acquired another way?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  seg AS segment,
  COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
  ROUND(AVG(orders_90d)::numeric, 2) AS avg_orders_90d,
  ROUND(AVG(revenue_90d_eur)::numeric, 2) AS avg_revenue_90d_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN orders_90d >= 2 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END), 1) AS pct_2nd_order_within_90d,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN orders_90d < 2 AND has_order_90_180 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN orders_90d < 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 1) AS pct_2nd_order_90_180d,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(refunded_orders_90d) / NULLIF(SUM(orders_90d), 0), 1) AS refund_rate_90d_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    u.id AS user_id,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM referral_redemptions rr WHERE rr.referred_user_id = u.id) THEN 'referred' ELSE 'other' END AS seg,
    fo.day0,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL AND o.placed_at >= fo.day0 AND o.placed_at < fo.day0 + INTERVAL '90 days') AS orders_90d,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total ELSE o.grand_total / NULLIF(er.rate, 0) END), 0)
       FROM orders o
       LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
       WHERE o.user_id = u.id AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL AND o.placed_at >= fo.day0 AND o.placed_at < fo.day0 + INTERVAL '90 days'
    ) AS revenue_90d_eur,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL AND o.placed_at >= fo.day0 AND o.placed_at < fo.day0 + INTERVAL '90 days'
       AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
            OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id))
    ) AS refunded_orders_90d,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.user_id = u.id AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL AND o.placed_at >= fo.day0 + INTERVAL '90 days' AND o.placed_at < fo.day0 + INTERVAL '180 days') AS has_order_90_180
  FROM users u
  JOIN (SELECT user_id, MIN(placed_at) AS day0 FROM orders WHERE placed_at IS NOT NULL GROUP BY user_id) fo ON fo.user_id = u.id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND CAST(u.created_at AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-10-02'
) t
GROUP BY seg
ORDER BY CASE WHEN seg = 'referred' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, seg
entries.engineer_note: Day0 = first order with non-null placed_at per user; "2nd order within 90 days" is derived as orders_90d >= 2 (equivalent since day0 is the min placed_at, any additional order in the window is necessarily the chronological 2nd order). Refund flag uses payments.amount_refunded > 0 OR an order_returns row, per order, within the 90-day window. Revenue converted to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code=EUR, quote_code=order currency, as_of = order placed_at's date); EUR orders pass through unconverted.

entries.title: Loyalty member vs non-member behavior by account tenure
entries.question: Does the loyalty-member gap in orders, revenue, AOV and refunds from last night's report persist once we control for how long the customer has had an account, or is it just that members and non-members differ in account age?
entries.sql:
WITH population AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id,
         CASE
           WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(u.created_at AS DATE)) < 182 THEN 'under 6 months'
           WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(u.created_at AS DATE)) < 365 THEN '6 to 12 months'
           WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(u.created_at AS DATE)) < 730 THEN '12 to 24 months'
           ELSE 'over 24 months'
         END AS tenure_band,
         CASE WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la WHERE la.user_id = u.id
              ) THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
  FROM users u
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM orders o
      WHERE o.user_id = u.id
        AND COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at) >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01'
        AND COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at) < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    )
),
grain_keys AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenure_band, segment FROM population
),
t_customer_count AS (
  SELECT tenure_band, segment, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
  FROM population
  GROUP BY tenure_band, segment
),
t_lifetime_orders AS (
  SELECT p.tenure_band, p.segment, COUNT(o.id) AS total_orders
  FROM population p
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = p.user_id
  GROUP BY p.tenure_band, p.segment
),
t_refunded_orders AS (
  SELECT p.tenure_band, p.segment, COUNT(o.id) AS refunded_orders
  FROM population p
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = p.user_id
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments pay WHERE pay.order_id = o.id AND pay.amount_refunded > 0)
     OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)
  GROUP BY p.tenure_band, p.segment
),
t_revenue AS (
  SELECT p.tenure_band, p.segment,
         SUM(CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
                  ELSE o.grand_total / NULLIF(er.rate, 0) END) AS total_revenue_eur,
         COUNT(o.id) AS non_cancelled_orders
  FROM population p
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = p.user_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at) AS DATE)
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY p.tenure_band, p.segment
)
SELECT
  gk.tenure_band,
  gk.segment,
  COALESCE(cc.customer_count, 0) AS customer_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(lo.total_orders, 0)::numeric / NULLIF(cc.customer_count, 0), 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rev.total_revenue_eur, 0) / NULLIF(cc.customer_count, 0), 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rev.total_revenue_eur, 0) / NULLIF(rev.non_cancelled_orders, 0), 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(ro.refunded_orders, 0) / NULLIF(lo.total_orders, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM grain_keys gk
LEFT JOIN t_customer_count cc ON cc.tenure_band = gk.tenure_band AND cc.segment = gk.segment
LEFT JOIN t_lifetime_orders lo ON lo.tenure_band = gk.tenure_band AND lo.segment = gk.segment
LEFT JOIN t_refunded_orders ro ON ro.tenure_band = gk.tenure_band AND ro.segment = gk.segment
LEFT JOIN t_revenue rev ON rev.tenure_band = gk.tenure_band AND rev.segment = gk.segment
ORDER BY
  CASE gk.tenure_band
    WHEN 'under 6 months' THEN 1
    WHEN '6 to 12 months' THEN 2
    WHEN '12 to 24 months' THEN 3
    WHEN 'over 24 months' THEN 4
  END,
  CASE gk.segment WHEN 'loyalty member' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END
builds_on: Loyalty member vs non-member customer behavior
entries.engineer_note: Tenure bands are bucketed by whole days from users.created_at to 2025-12-31 (under 6mo = under 182 days, 6-12mo = 182-364 days, 12-24mo = 365-729 days, over 24mo = 730+ days) since the warehouse has no month-interval type; boundaries approximate calendar months. Refund_rate_pct and AOV are computed as aggregate totals within each tenure-band/segment cell (refunded orders ÷ all orders; revenue ÷ non-cancelled orders), not averaged per customer, consistent with a rate/AOV definition.

entries.title: Loyalty member order behavior before vs after enrollment
entries.question: For the same loyalty members, does their own order frequency, spend and refund rate actually change after they enroll, compared to their behavior before they joined - or is the elevated refund rate already present pre-enrollment?
entries.sql:
WITH lu AS (
  SELECT la.tenant_id AS tenant_id, la.user_id AS user_id, MIN(la.enrolled_at) AS enrolled_at
  FROM loyalty_accounts la
  GROUP BY la.tenant_id, la.user_id
),
lu2 AS (
  SELECT t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id, t0.user_id AS user_id, t0.enrolled_at AS enrolled_at, u0.created_at AS user_created_at
  FROM lu t0
  JOIN users u0 ON u0.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id AND u0.id = t0.user_id
),
ord AS (
  SELECT
    o0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    o0.user_id AS user_id,
    o0.id AS order_id,
