    o0.placed_at AS placed_at,
    o0.status AS status,
    o0.currency_code AS currency_code,
    o0.grand_total AS grand_total,
    CASE WHEN o0.placed_at < lu2.enrolled_at THEN 'pre-enrollment' ELSE 'post-enrollment' END AS period
  FROM orders o0
  JOIN lu2 ON lu2.tenant_id = o0.tenant_id AND lu2.user_id = o0.user_id
  WHERE o0.placed_at IS NOT NULL
),
ord_refund AS (
  SELECT
    ord.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    ord.order_id AS order_id,
    ord.period AS period,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM payments p0
            WHERE p0.tenant_id = ord.tenant_id AND p0.order_id = ord.order_id AND p0.amount_refunded > 0
          )
          OR EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r0
            WHERE r0.tenant_id = ord.tenant_id AND r0.order_id = ord.order_id
          )
     THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM ord
),
ord_eur AS (
  SELECT
    ord.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    ord.order_id AS order_id,
    ord.period AS period,
    CASE WHEN ord.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ord.grand_total
         ELSE ord.grand_total / NULLIF(er0.rate, 0)
    END AS eur_amount
  FROM ord
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er0.quote_code = ord.currency_code
   AND er0.as_of = CAST(ord.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE ord.status <> 'cancelled'
),
m_orders AS (
  SELECT ord.period AS period, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT ord.user_id) AS distinct_customers
  FROM ord
  GROUP BY ord.period
),
m_aov AS (
  SELECT ord_eur.period AS period, AVG(ord_eur.eur_amount) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM ord_eur
  GROUP BY ord_eur.period
),
m_refund AS (
  SELECT ord_refund.period AS period, 100.0 * SUM(ord_refund.is_refunded) / COUNT(*) AS refund_rate_pct
  FROM ord_refund
  GROUP BY ord_refund.period
),
cust_pre AS (
  SELECT ord.tenant_id AS tenant_id, ord.user_id AS user_id, MIN(ord.placed_at) AS first_pre_order_at
  FROM ord
  WHERE ord.period = 'pre-enrollment'
  GROUP BY ord.tenant_id, ord.user_id
),
cust_post AS (
  SELECT ord.tenant_id AS tenant_id, ord.user_id AS user_id, MAX(ord.placed_at) AS last_post_order_at
  FROM ord
  WHERE ord.period = 'post-enrollment'
  GROUP BY ord.tenant_id, ord.user_id
),
cust_exposure AS (
  SELECT
    lu2.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    lu2.user_id AS user_id,
    GREATEST(1, CAST(lu2.enrolled_at AS DATE) - CAST(COALESCE(cp0.first_pre_order_at, lu2.user_created_at) AS DATE)) AS pre_exposed_days,
    GREATEST(1, CAST(COALESCE(cpo0.last_post_order_at, DATE '2025-12-31') AS DATE) - CAST(lu2.enrolled_at AS DATE)) AS post_exposed_days
  FROM lu2
  LEFT JOIN cust_pre cp0 ON cp0.tenant_id = lu2.tenant_id AND cp0.user_id = lu2.user_id
  LEFT JOIN cust_post cpo0 ON cpo0.tenant_id = lu2.tenant_id AND cpo0.user_id = lu2.user_id
),
exposure_by_period AS (
  SELECT 'pre-enrollment' AS period, SUM(ce.pre_exposed_days) AS total_exposed_days FROM cust_exposure ce
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'post-enrollment' AS period, SUM(ce.post_exposed_days) AS total_exposed_days FROM cust_exposure ce
),
periods AS (
  SELECT 'pre-enrollment' AS period
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'post-enrollment' AS period
)
SELECT
  p0.period AS period,
  COALESCE(mo0.distinct_customers, 0) AS distinct_customers,
  COALESCE(mo0.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ma0.avg_order_value_eur, 0), 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(
    COALESCE(mo0.total_orders, 0) / NULLIF(COALESCE(ep0.total_exposed_days, 0) / 365.0, 0)
  , 2) AS orders_per_customer_per_year,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mr0.refund_rate_pct, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM periods p0
LEFT JOIN m_orders mo0 ON mo0.period = p0.period
LEFT JOIN m_aov ma0 ON ma0.period = p0.period
LEFT JOIN m_refund mr0 ON mr0.period = p0.period
LEFT JOIN exposure_by_period ep0 ON ep0.period = p0.period
ORDER BY CASE WHEN p0.period = 'pre-enrollment' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, p0.period
builds_on: Loyalty member vs non-member customer behavior
entries.engineer_note: For exposure days I used the customer's first order within the pre-period (vs users.created_at if none) as the pre-period start, and the customer's last order within the post-period (vs 2025-12-31 if none yet) as the post-period end, which is how I read the 'first/last order ... or X if ...' rule. Refund rate counts an order as refunded if any linked payment has amount_refunded>0 or it has any order_returns row, regardless of order status.

entries.title: Referral redemption concentration by referrer
entries.question: Is referral activity concentrated among a small number of referrers in a way that looks like gaming rather than broad-based word-of-mouth, and are the top referrers themselves genuine, active customers?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  ra.referrer_user_id,
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  ra.redemption_count,
  ra.distinct_referred_customers,
  ROUND(ra.total_reward_paid_eur, 2) AS total_reward_paid_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * ra.redemption_count / SUM(ra.redemption_count) OVER (), 2) AS share_of_all_redemptions_pct,
  COALESCE(oa.lifetime_order_count, 0) AS referrer_lifetime_order_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.lifetime_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS referrer_lifetime_revenue_eur
FROM (
    SELECT rr.tenant_id, ref.referrer_user_id,
           COUNT(*) AS redemption_count,
           COUNT(DISTINCT rr.referred_user_id) AS distinct_referred_customers,
           SUM(CASE WHEN rr.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN rr.reward_amount
                    ELSE rr.reward_amount / er.rate END) AS total_reward_paid_eur
    FROM referral_redemptions rr
    JOIN referrals ref ON ref.id = rr.referral_id
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
      ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
     AND er.quote_code = rr.currency_code
     AND er.as_of = CAST(rr.redeemed_at AS date)
    GROUP BY rr.tenant_id, ref.referrer_user_id
) ra
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ra.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT o.tenant_id, o.user_id,
           COUNT(*) AS lifetime_order_count,
           SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN
                    CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
                         ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate END
                    ELSE 0 END) AS lifetime_revenue_eur
    FROM orders o
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
      ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
     AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
     AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
    GROUP BY o.tenant_id, o.user_id
) oa ON oa.tenant_id = ra.tenant_id AND oa.user_id = ra.referrer_user_id
ORDER BY ra.redemption_count DESC, ra.referrer_user_id ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Referred vs non-referred customer early behavior
entries.engineer_note: Report caps at 50 rows as requested; since the query can't also return a separate "total rows/redemptions" summary within the 12-column single-grain report, please note in the memo that the true referrer count and overall redemption total can be read off by summing redemption_count across all returned+unreturned rows if needed as a follow-up query. referrer_lifetime_order_count/revenue are scoped to the same tenant as the referral (users belong to one tenant).

entries.title: Refund rate on points-redeeming orders vs other member orders
entries.question: Among loyalty members' own orders, do the ones where loyalty points were actually redeemed show a higher refund rate than their other orders - i.e. is the elevated member refund rate concentrated in reward-redeeming purchases, suggesting rewards are being used without real purchase intent?
entries.sql:
WITH loyalty_members AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id
  FROM loyalty_accounts
),
scoped_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.status, o.currency_code, o.grand_total, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN loyalty_members lm ON lm.user_id = o.user_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
redeem_agg AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(ABS(points)) AS points_redeemed, COUNT(*) AS redeem_tx_count
  FROM loyalty_transactions
  WHERE direction <> 'earn' AND order_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY order_id
),
refund_payment_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id
  FROM payments
  WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL AND amount_refunded > 0
),
refund_return_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id
  FROM order_returns
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    so.id,
    so.tenant_id,
    so.user_id,
    so.status,
    so.currency_code,
    so.grand_total,
    so.placed_at,
    CASE WHEN ra.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'points redeemed on this order' ELSE 'no points redeemed on this order' END AS order_type,
    COALESCE(ra.points_redeemed, 0) AS points_redeemed,
    CASE WHEN rpo.order_id IS NOT NULL OR rro.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM scoped_orders so
  LEFT JOIN redeem_agg ra ON ra.order_id = so.id
  LEFT JOIN refund_payment_orders rpo ON rpo.order_id = so.id
  LEFT JOIN refund_return_orders rro ON rro.order_id = so.id
),
valued AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    CASE WHEN c.status <> 'cancelled' THEN c.grand_total / er.rate ELSE NULL END AS grand_total_eur
  FROM classified c
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = c.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(c.placed_at AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  order_type,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(is_refunded) / COUNT(*), 2) AS refund_rate_pct,
  ROUND(AVG(grand_total_eur), 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(points_redeemed), 2) AS avg_points_redeemed_per_order
FROM valued
GROUP BY order_type
ORDER BY CASE WHEN order_type = 'points redeemed on this order' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, order_type
builds_on: Loyalty member order behavior before vs after enrollment
Loyalty member vs non-member behavior by account tenure
entries.engineer_note: Population is scoped to orders with a non-null placed_at in 2023-2025 (orders without a placed_at, e.g. still-pending carts-to-order, can't be dated and are excluded). avg_order_value_eur is averaged only over non-cancelled orders with a matching EUR exchange rate for their placed_at date; refund_rate_pct uses all orders in the group regardless of status, per the stated refund definition.

entries.title: Loyalty and referral programme participation rate over time
entries.question: What share of our active customer base is enrolled in loyalty or has ever used a referral code, and is that share growing, flat, or shrinking over time?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  q.quarter AS quarter,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id)
     FROM orders o
     JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id
    WHERE u.is_staff = false
      AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
      AND CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE) <= q.quarter_end) AS active_customers_cumulative,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT la.user_id)
     FROM loyalty_accounts la
     JOIN users u ON u.id = la.user_id
    WHERE u.is_staff = false
      AND CAST(la.enrolled_at AS DATE) <= q.quarter_end) AS loyalty_members_cumulative,
  ROUND(100.0 *
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT la.user_id)
       FROM loyalty_accounts la
       JOIN users u ON u.id = la.user_id
      WHERE u.is_staff = false
        AND CAST(la.enrolled_at AS DATE) <= q.quarter_end)
    / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id)
                FROM orders o
                JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id
               WHERE u.is_staff = false
                 AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
                 AND CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE) <= q.quarter_end), 0)
  , 2) AS pct_customers_loyalty_members,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rr.referred_user_id)
     FROM referral_redemptions rr
     JOIN users u ON u.id = rr.referred_user_id
    WHERE u.is_staff = false
      AND CAST(rr.redeemed_at AS DATE) <= q.quarter_end) AS referred_customers_cumulative,
  ROUND(100.0 *
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT rr.referred_user_id)
       FROM referral_redemptions rr
       JOIN users u ON u.id = rr.referred_user_id
      WHERE u.is_staff = false
        AND CAST(rr.redeemed_at AS DATE) <= q.quarter_end)
    / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id)
                FROM orders o
                JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id
               WHERE u.is_staff = false
                 AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
                 AND CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE) <= q.quarter_end), 0)
  , 2) AS pct_customers_referred
FROM (
  SELECT
    year_num,
    quarter_num,
    CONCAT(CAST(year_num AS VARCHAR), '-Q', CAST(quarter_num AS VARCHAR)) AS quarter,
    MAX(calendar_date) AS quarter_end
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE year_num BETWEEN 2023 AND 2025
  GROUP BY year_num, quarter_num
) q
ORDER BY q.year_num ASC, q.quarter_num ASC
builds_on: Loyalty points and referral reward cost by month
entries.engineer_note: Counts are aggregated across all tenants (global platform view) since the question is about overall customer base, not a specific merchant; percentages are rounded to 2 decimals and 0-base guarded with NULLIF.
warnings: 3 scalar subqueries in the select list (over a FROM, may be per-row values)

entries.title: B2B invoice payment behavior: loyalty-enrolled vs not
entries.question: Among our B2B wholesaler tenants (industrial supplies, office equipment), do customers enrolled in the loyalty programme settle invoices faster and carry fewer overdue balances than non-enrolled customers?
entries.sql:
WITH b2b_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name
  FROM tenants
  WHERE lower(coalesce(industry,'')) LIKE '%industrial%supplies%'
     OR lower(coalesce(industry,'')) LIKE '%office%equipment%'
     OR lower(coalesce(industry,'')) LIKE '%industrial%'
     OR lower(coalesce(industry,'')) LIKE '%wholesale%'
     OR lower(coalesce(name,''))     LIKE '%industrial%'
     OR lower(coalesce(name,''))     LIKE '%office%equipment%'
     OR lower(coalesce(slug,''))     LIKE '%industrial%'
     OR lower(coalesce(slug,''))     LIKE '%office-equipment%'
),
scoped_invoices AS (
  SELECT i.*
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN b2b_tenants t ON t.id = i.tenant_id
  WHERE i.issued_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND i.issued_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
),
loyalty_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id
  FROM loyalty_accounts
),
segmented AS (
  SELECT
    si.*,
    CASE WHEN lu.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
  FROM scoped_invoices si
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_users lu
    ON lu.tenant_id = si.tenant_id AND lu.user_id = si.user_id
),
eur_amounts AS (
  SELECT
    s.*,
    s.total / NULLIF(er.rate, 0) AS total_eur
  FROM segmented s
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(s.issued_at AS date)
)
SELECT
  segment,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customer_count,
  COUNT(*) AS invoice_count,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (paid_at - issued_at)) / 86400.0) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid'), 2) AS avg_days_to_pay,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid' AND paid_at > due_at)
    / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid'), 0), 2
  ) AS pct_invoices_paid_late,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE status = 'past_due'
         OR (status = 'open' AND due_at < DATE '2025-12-31' AND amount_due > 0)
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2
  ) AS pct_invoices_currently_overdue,
  ROUND(AVG(total_eur), 2) AS avg_invoice_amount_eur
FROM eur_amounts
GROUP BY segment
ORDER BY CASE WHEN segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, segment
entries.engineer_note: B2B wholesaler tenants were identified by matching tenants.industry/name/slug against 'industrial supplies', 'office equipment', 'industrial' and 'wholesale' (case-insensitive substring match) — since I can only dry-run queries (no data preview), I can't list the exact matched tenant names here; the analyst should pull the matched tenant.id/name list as a quick follow-up if the exact roster needs sign-off. A user is 'loyalty member' if they have any loyalty_accounts row for that tenant, regardless of program status; avg_invoice_amount_eur excludes invoices whose currency had no exchange_rates row for the issue date.

entries.title: Loyalty and referral programme reach by merchant vertical
entries.question: In which merchant verticals does the loyalty/referral programme even exist and get adopted - is B2B wholesale genuinely excluded, and is participation concentrated in a few verticals?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.industry AS industry,
  t0.tenant_count AS tenant_count,
  COALESCE(t1.tenants_with_any_loyalty_program, 0) AS tenants_with_any_loyalty_program,
  COALESCE(t2.active_customers, 0) AS active_customers,
  COALESCE(t3.loyalty_members, 0) AS loyalty_members,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t2.active_customers, 0) = 0 THEN 0
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t3.loyalty_members, 0) / t2.active_customers, 2)
  END AS pct_customers_enrolled,
  COALESCE(t4.referred_customers, 0) AS referred_customers,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(t2.active_customers, 0) = 0 THEN 0
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t4.referred_customers, 0) / t2.active_customers, 2)
  END AS pct_customers_referred
FROM (
  SELECT COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown') AS industry, COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) AS tenant_count
  FROM tenants t
  GROUP BY COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown')
) t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown') AS industry, COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) AS tenants_with_any_loyalty_program
  FROM tenants t
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.tenant_id = t.id
  GROUP BY COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown')
) t1 ON t1.industry = t0.industry
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown') AS industry, COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) AS active_customers
  FROM tenants t
  JOIN users u ON u.tenant_id = t.id AND u.is_staff = false
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id AND o.tenant_id = t.id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown')
) t2 ON t2.industry = t0.industry
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown') AS industry, COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) AS loyalty_members
  FROM tenants t
  JOIN users u ON u.tenant_id = t.id AND u.is_staff = false
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id AND o.tenant_id = t.id
  JOIN loyalty_accounts la ON la.user_id = u.id AND la.tenant_id = t.id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown')
) t3 ON t3.industry = t0.industry
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown') AS industry, COUNT(DISTINCT u.id) AS referred_customers
  FROM tenants t
  JOIN users u ON u.tenant_id = t.id AND u.is_staff = false
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id AND o.tenant_id = t.id
  JOIN referral_redemptions rr ON rr.referred_user_id = u.id AND rr.tenant_id = t.id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY COALESCE(t.industry, 'Unknown')
) t4 ON t4.industry = t0.industry
ORDER BY COALESCE(t2.active_customers, 0) DESC, t0.industry ASC
builds_on: B2B invoice payment behavior: loyalty-enrolled vs not
Loyalty and referral programme participation rate over time
entries.engineer_note: tenants.industry is nullable; any tenant without an industry value is grouped under 'Unknown' rather than dropped, so the vertical breakdown stays complete.

entries.title: Loyalty member refund rate by merchant vertical
entries.question: Is the elevated refund rate among loyalty members a broad pattern across verticals, or is it concentrated in one or two verticals that happen to have naturally high returns, such as apparel?
entries.sql:
WITH eligible_users AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        o.user_id,
        o.tenant_id,
        t.industry
    FROM orders o
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
    JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id AND u.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
      AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
      AND u.is_staff = false
),
loyalty_flags AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id
    FROM loyalty_accounts
),
user_segment AS (
    SELECT
        eu.tenant_id,
        eu.user_id,
        eu.industry,
        CASE WHEN lf.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
    FROM eligible_users eu
    LEFT JOIN loyalty_flags lf
        ON lf.tenant_id = eu.tenant_id AND lf.user_id = eu.user_id
),
all_orders_for_users AS (
    SELECT
        o.id AS order_id,
        o.tenant_id,
        o.user_id,
        o.status,
        o.placed_at,
        o.currency_code,
        o.grand_total
    FROM orders o
    JOIN user_segment us
        ON us.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND us.user_id = o.user_id
),
refund_flags AS (
    SELECT
        ao.order_id,
        CASE WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM payments p
                WHERE p.order_id = ao.order_id AND p.amount_refunded > 0
             )
             OR EXISTS (
                SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r
                WHERE r.order_id = ao.order_id
             )
        THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
    FROM all_orders_for_users ao
),
order_value_eur AS (
    SELECT
        ao.order_id,
        ao.tenant_id,
        ao.user_id,
        ao.grand_total / er.rate AS order_value_eur
    FROM all_orders_for_users ao
    LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = ao.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(ao.placed_at AS DATE)
    WHERE ao.status <> 'cancelled'
),
per_user_stats AS (
    SELECT
        us.tenant_id,
        us.user_id,
        us.industry,
        us.segment,
        COUNT(ao.order_id) AS lifetime_order_count
    FROM user_segment us
    LEFT JOIN all_orders_for_users ao
        ON ao.tenant_id = us.tenant_id AND ao.user_id = us.user_id
    GROUP BY us.tenant_id, us.user_id, us.industry, us.segment
),
industry_segment_counts AS (
    SELECT
        industry,
        segment,
        COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS customer_count,
        AVG(lifetime_order_count) AS avg_lifetime_orders
    FROM per_user_stats
    GROUP BY industry, segment
),
order_value_agg AS (
    SELECT
        us.industry,
        us.segment,
        AVG(ov.order_value_eur) AS avg_order_value_eur
    FROM order_value_eur ov
    JOIN user_segment us
        ON us.tenant_id = ov.tenant_id AND us.user_id = ov.user_id
    GROUP BY us.industry, us.segment
),
refund_agg AS (
    SELECT
        us.industry,
        us.segment,
        AVG(CAST(rf.is_refunded AS DECIMAL)) * 100 AS refund_rate_pct
    FROM refund_flags rf
    JOIN all_orders_for_users ao ON ao.order_id = rf.order_id
    JOIN user_segment us
        ON us.tenant_id = ao.tenant_id AND us.user_id = ao.user_id
    GROUP BY us.industry, us.segment
),
qualifying_industries AS (
    SELECT industry
    FROM industry_segment_counts
    GROUP BY industry
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT segment) = 2 AND MIN(customer_count) >= 20
)
SELECT
    isc.industry,
    isc.segment,
    isc.customer_count,
    ROUND(isc.avg_lifetime_orders, 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
    ROUND(ova.avg_order_value_eur, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
    ROUND(ra.refund_rate_pct, 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM industry_segment_counts isc
JOIN qualifying_industries qi ON qi.industry = isc.industry
LEFT JOIN order_value_agg ova ON ova.industry = isc.industry AND ova.segment = isc.segment
LEFT JOIN refund_agg ra ON ra.industry = isc.industry AND ra.segment = isc.segment
ORDER BY isc.industry, (CASE WHEN isc.segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)
builds_on: Loyalty member vs non-member behavior by account tenure
entries.engineer_note: Population, segment definition, and metric definitions mirror the earlier tenure report (orders 2023-01-01..2025-12-31, is_staff=false, loyalty membership = any loyalty_accounts row, EUR conversion via exchange_rates as-of placed_at, refund = amount_refunded>0 or any order_returns row). Industries where either segment has fewer than 20 customers are dropped entirely from the output rather than flagged with a count column, since adding a count would break the single industry×segment grain — any industry missing from the table was excluded for low volume.

entries.title: Loyalty programme unit economics: points cost vs revenue per customer
entries.question: Putting cost and revenue side by side: how does the points value we issue and redeem per loyalty member compare to the revenue those members actually generate, versus non-members?
entries.sql:
WITH population AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT u.id AS user_id, u.tenant_id
  FROM users u
  JOIN orders o
    ON o.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
   AND o.user_id = u.id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
),
segment_membership AS (
  SELECT
    p.user_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    CASE WHEN la.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
  FROM population p
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_accounts) la
    ON la.tenant_id = p.tenant_id AND la.user_id = p.user_id
),
revenue_detail AS (
  SELECT
    sm.segment,
    o.grand_total / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS revenue_eur
  FROM segment_membership sm
  JOIN orders o
    ON o.tenant_id = sm.tenant_id AND o.user_id = sm.user_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
),
loyalty_tx_detail AS (
  SELECT
    sm.segment,
    lt.direction,
    ABS(lt.points) / lp.points_per_currency
      / COALESCE(er.rate, CASE WHEN lp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS points_value_eur
  FROM segment_membership sm
  JOIN loyalty_accounts la
    ON la.tenant_id = sm.tenant_id AND la.user_id = sm.user_id
  JOIN loyalty_transactions lt
    ON lt.tenant_id = la.tenant_id AND lt.loyalty_account_id = la.id
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp
    ON lp.tenant_id = la.tenant_id AND lp.id = la.loyalty_program_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = lp.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(lt.occurred_at AS date)
),
customer_counts AS (
  SELECT segment, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
  FROM segment_membership
  GROUP BY segment
),
revenue_totals AS (
  SELECT segment, SUM(revenue_eur) AS total_revenue_eur
  FROM revenue_detail
  GROUP BY segment
),
redeemed_totals AS (
  SELECT segment, SUM(points_value_eur) AS total_redeemed_eur
  FROM loyalty_tx_detail
  WHERE direction <> 'earn'
  GROUP BY segment
),
earned_totals AS (
  SELECT segment, SUM(points_value_eur) AS total_earned_eur
  FROM loyalty_tx_detail
  WHERE direction = 'earn'
  GROUP BY segment
)
SELECT
  cc.segment,
  cc.customer_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rev.total_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS total_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rev.total_revenue_eur, 0) / cc.customer_count, 2) AS revenue_per_customer_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(red.total_redeemed_eur, 0), 2) AS total_points_redeemed_cost_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(red.total_redeemed_eur, 0) / cc.customer_count, 2) AS redeemed_cost_per_customer_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(earn.total_earned_eur, 0), 2) AS total_points_earned_liability_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(earn.total_earned_eur, 0) / cc.customer_count, 2) AS earned_liability_per_customer_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(red.total_redeemed_eur, 0) / NULLIF(COALESCE(rev.total_revenue_eur, 0), 0), 2) AS redeemed_cost_pct_of_revenue
FROM customer_counts cc
LEFT JOIN revenue_totals rev ON rev.segment = cc.segment
LEFT JOIN redeemed_totals red ON red.segment = cc.segment
LEFT JOIN earned_totals earn ON earn.segment = cc.segment
ORDER BY CASE WHEN cc.segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, cc.segment
builds_on: Loyalty points and referral reward cost by month
Loyalty member vs non-member customer behavior

entries.title: B2B Wholesale Pipeline: Opportunities by Merchant and Stage
entries.question: Across our B2B wholesale merchants, at which pipeline stage do the most opportunities get stuck or lost — i.e. which stage is the graveyard?
entries.sql:
WITH wholesale_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id, name AS merchant
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%'
),
stages AS (
  SELECT
    os.tenant_id,
    os.id AS stage_id,
    os.name AS stage_name,
    os.sort_position,
    os.win_probability,
    p.name AS pipeline_name
  FROM opportunity_stages os
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = os.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = os.tenant_id
  JOIN wholesale_tenants wt ON wt.tenant_id = os.tenant_id
),
opp_agg AS (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    o.stage_id,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_closed = false) AS open_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.is_won = true) AS won_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.is_won = false) AS lost_count,
    AVG(o.amount) AS avg_amount,
    MIN(o.currency_code) AS currency_code
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN wholesale_tenants wt ON wt.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id, o.stage_id
)
SELECT
  wt.merchant,
  s.pipeline_name,
  s.stage_name,
  s.sort_position AS stage_order,
  ROUND(s.win_probability, 4) AS default_win_probability,
  COALESCE(oa.open_count, 0) AS opportunities_open,
  COALESCE(oa.won_count, 0) AS opportunities_closed_won,
  COALESCE(oa.lost_count, 0) AS opportunities_closed_lost,
  ROUND(oa.avg_amount, 2) AS avg_opportunity_amount,
  oa.currency_code
FROM stages s
JOIN wholesale_tenants wt ON wt.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN opp_agg oa ON oa.tenant_id = s.tenant_id AND oa.stage_id = s.stage_id
ORDER BY wt.merchant, s.sort_position, s.stage_name
entries.engineer_note: Grain is tenant x stage as requested. avg_opportunity_amount/currency_code are computed per (tenant, stage) without FX conversion; if a tenant's opportunities span more than one currency, currency_code shows only the lexically-smallest code present and the average mixes currencies for that row (per the request's assumption of one currency per tenant, this should be rare/absent). Please have the analyst check row count and flag any wholesale tenant that returns zero stages or zero opportunity rows, as that would indicate the industry filter missed a merchant or that merchant doesn't use the CRM/pipeline module - I could not verify this without reading data.

entries.title: B2B Wholesale Deal Cycle Time Trend by Month
entries.question: From an opportunity being opened to it closing (won or lost), how long does that take for our B2B wholesale merchants, and is that cycle time getting longer or shorter over the last three years?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  cd.month_label AS month,
  count(*) AS opportunities_closed,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_won) AS closed_won,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT o.is_won) AS closed_lost,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE o.is_won) / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
  round(avg(DATE_PART('day', o.closed_at - o.created_at))::numeric, 1) AS avg_cycle_days,
  round(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY DATE_PART('day', o.closed_at - o.created_at))::numeric, 1) AS median_cycle_days
FROM opportunities o
JOIN accounts a ON a.id = o.account_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = a.tenant_id
JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(o.closed_at AS date)
WHERE (t.industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR t.industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR t.industry ILIKE '%wholesal%')
  AND o.is_closed = true
  AND o.closed_at IS NOT NULL
  AND o.closed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
  AND o.closed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY cd.month_label
ORDER BY month ASC
entries.engineer_note: Cycle time is approximated as closed_at - created_at on the opportunity itself, since opportunities carry no FK back to the originating lead (known limitation, as requested). Win rate, avg and median cycle days are rounded to 1 decimal; monthly grain uses calendar_days.month_label keyed off closed_at.

entries.title: B2B Wholesale Opportunities: Won vs Lost Characteristics
entries.question: Among closed B2B wholesale opportunities, what reliably differs between the ones we won and the ones we lost — deal size, touches/activities before close, days open, or how concentrated they are among accounts and reps?
entries.sql:
WITH b2b_tenants AS (
  SELECT id FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%'
),
closed_opps AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.tenant_id, o.account_id, o.owner_user_id, o.is_won, o.closed_at, o.created_at,
    o.amount,
    o.currency_code,
    CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
         ELSE o.amount / (
           SELECT er.rate FROM exchange_rates er
           WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
             AND er.as_of <= o.closed_at::date
           ORDER BY er.as_of DESC LIMIT 1
         )
    END AS amount_eur
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN b2b_tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.closed_at IS NOT NULL
),
activity_counts AS (
  SELECT co.id AS opportunity_id, COUNT(a.id) AS activity_count
  FROM closed_opps co
  LEFT JOIN activities a ON a.opportunity_id = co.id AND a.occurred_at <= co.closed_at
  GROUP BY co.id
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN co.is_won THEN 'won' ELSE 'lost' END AS outcome,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities,
  ROUND(AVG(co.amount_eur), 2) AS avg_amount_eur,
  ROUND(CAST(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY co.amount_eur) AS numeric), 2) AS median_amount_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(ac.activity_count), 2) AS avg_activities_before_close,
  ROUND(CAST(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (co.closed_at - co.created_at)) / 86400.0) AS numeric), 1) AS avg_days_open,
  COUNT(DISTINCT co.account_id) AS distinct_accounts,
  COUNT(DISTINCT co.owner_user_id) AS distinct_reps
FROM closed_opps co
JOIN activity_counts ac ON ac.opportunity_id = co.id
GROUP BY co.is_won
ORDER BY co.is_won DESC
entries.engineer_note: Amounts converted to EUR using the exchange rate as of the closed_at date, falling back to the most recent prior available rate (covers weekends/gaps) per house standards. Activities-before-close counts only activities linked directly to the opportunity via activities.opportunity_id with occurred_at <= closed_at.

entries.title: New Business Pipeline: Stage Where Lost Opportunities Were Last Seen
entries.question: Among B2B wholesale opportunities that were actually lost in new-customer acquisition (not renewals), which stage were they sitting in just before they were marked Closed Lost — i.e. where is the real graveyard?
entries.sql:
WITH lost_opps AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.tenant_id
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id
  WHERE p.name = 'New business'
    AND o.is_closed = true
    AND o.is_won = false
    AND (t.industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR t.industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR t.industry ILIKE '%wholesal%')
),
last_stage_change AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (ch.entity_id)
    ch.entity_id,
    ch.tenant_id,
    (ch.before_data->>'stage_id') AS before_stage_id
  FROM change_history ch
  JOIN lost_opps lo ON lo.id = ch.entity_id AND lo.tenant_id = ch.tenant_id
  WHERE ch.entity_table = 'opportunities'
    AND 'stage_id' = ANY(ch.changed_columns)
  ORDER BY ch.entity_id, ch.occurred_at DESC
),
opp_stage AS (
  SELECT
    lo.id AS opportunity_id,
    os.name AS stage_name,
    os.sort_position AS stage_order
  FROM lost_opps lo
  LEFT JOIN last_stage_change lsc ON lsc.entity_id = lo.id
  LEFT JOIN opportunity_stages os ON os.id = CAST(lsc.before_stage_id AS bigint)
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(stage_name, 'No stage transition recorded') AS stage_name,
  stage_order,
  COUNT(*) AS lost_opportunities_last_seen_here,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_total_lost_in_new_business,
  SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS total_lost_opportunities_new_business
FROM opp_stage
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY lost_opportunities_last_seen_here DESC, stage_name
builds_on: B2B Wholesale Pipeline: Opportunities by Merchant and Stage
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per New-business pipeline stage (plus a 'No stage transition recorded' bucket), scoped to lost opportunities at wholesale tenants as specified. Please check the row count/share for the 'No stage transition recorded' bucket in the printed report: if it holds most of the lost opportunities, the change_history audit trail doesn't have enough coverage to answer the graveyard-stage question and the result should be read as inconclusive rather than a real stage distribution.

entries.title: New Business Only: Won vs Lost Opportunity Characteristics
entries.question: Restricted to genuine new-customer acquisition deals (excluding renewals), what reliably differs between won and lost opportunities — deal size, activities before close, days open, or concentration among accounts and reps?
entries.sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%'
),
new_business_pipelines AS (
  SELECT id, tenant_id
  FROM pipelines
  WHERE name = 'New business'
),
base_opportunities AS (
  SELECT o.*
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN new_business_pipelines p
    ON o.pipeline_id = p.id
   AND o.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE o.tenant_id IN (SELECT id FROM target_tenants)
    AND o.is_closed = true
),
opp_with_rate AS (
  SELECT
    bo.*,
    (
      SELECT er.rate
      FROM exchange_rates er
      WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = bo.currency_code
        AND er.as_of <= date(bo.closed_at)
      ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS eur_rate
  FROM base_opportunities bo
),
activities_before_close AS (
  SELECT
    a.opportunity_id,
    count(*) AS activity_count
  FROM activities a
  JOIN base_opportunities bo
    ON a.opportunity_id = bo.id
   AND a.tenant_id = bo.tenant_id
  WHERE a.occurred_at <= bo.closed_at
  GROUP BY a.opportunity_id
),
opp_final AS (
  SELECT
    owr.id,
    owr.account_id,
    owr.owner_user_id,
    owr.is_won,
    owr.amount / owr.eur_rate AS amount_eur,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (owr.closed_at - owr.created_at)) / 86400.0 AS days_open,
    COALESCE(ac.activity_count, 0) AS activity_count
  FROM opp_with_rate owr
  LEFT JOIN activities_before_close ac
    ON ac.opportunity_id = owr.id
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN is_won THEN 'won' ELSE 'lost' END AS outcome,
  count(*) AS opportunities,
  round(avg(amount_eur)::numeric, 2) AS avg_amount_eur,
  round(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount_eur)::numeric, 2) AS median_amount_eur,
  round(avg(activity_count)::numeric, 2) AS avg_activities_before_close,
  round(avg(days_open)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_open,
  count(DISTINCT account_id) AS distinct_accounts,
  count(DISTINCT owner_user_id) AS distinct_reps
FROM opp_final
GROUP BY is_won
ORDER BY CASE WHEN is_won THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
builds_on: B2B Wholesale Opportunities: Won vs Lost Characteristics
entries.engineer_note: Restricted to pipelines named 'New business' (joined on pipelines.name) as requested, excluding Renewals; all other filters (tenant industry, is_closed) and conversions (EUR via nearest prior-day exchange rate) match the prior report's methodology.

entries.title: New Business Only: Deal Cycle Time Trend by Month
entries.question: Restricted to genuine new-customer acquisition deals (excluding renewals), how long does it take to close an opportunity, and is that cycle time trending up or down over the last three years?
entries.sql:
WITH tenant_scope AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry ILIKE '%industrial%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%office equipment%'
     OR industry ILIKE '%wholesal%'
),
new_business_pipelines AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, id AS pipeline_id
  FROM pipelines
  WHERE name = 'New business'
),
scoped_opportunities AS (
  SELECT
    o.id,
    o.is_won,
    o.created_at,
    o.closed_at
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN tenant_scope ts ON ts.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN new_business_pipelines nbp
    ON nbp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
   AND nbp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
    AND o.closed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o.closed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.closed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
opportunities_with_month AS (
  SELECT
    so.id,
    so.is_won,
    cd.month_label,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (so.closed_at - so.created_at)) / 86400.0 AS cycle_days
  FROM scoped_opportunities so
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(so.closed_at AS DATE)
),
monthly_stats AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_won) AS closed_won,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_won) AS closed_lost,
    AVG(cycle_days) AS avg_cycle_days_raw,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY cycle_days) AS median_cycle_days_raw
  FROM opportunities_with_month
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  month_label AS month,
  opportunities_closed,
  closed_won,
  closed_lost,
  ROUND(100.0 * closed_won / NULLIF(opportunities_closed, 0), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(avg_cycle_days_raw::numeric, 1) AS avg_cycle_days,
  ROUND(median_cycle_days_raw::numeric, 1) AS median_cycle_days
FROM monthly_stats
ORDER BY month ASC
builds_on: B2B Wholesale Deal Cycle Time Trend by Month
entries.engineer_note: Filtered to pipelines named exactly 'New business' per tenant, joined via tenant_id+pipeline_id; months with zero closed opportunities in scope won't appear as rows (no calendar spine requested). Cycle time computed as closed_at minus created_at in days (fractional).

entries.title: B2B Wholesale: Win Rate and Cycle Time by Merchant (New Business)
entries.question: Is the acquisition struggle spread evenly across our B2B wholesale merchants, or concentrated in a few accounts?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name AS merchant,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_won,
  SUM(CASE WHEN NOT o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_lost,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.closed_at - o.created_at)) / 86400.0), 1) AS avg_days_open,
  ROUND(AVG(o.amount / (SELECT er.rate
                         FROM exchange_rates er
                         WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
                           AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
                           AND er.as_of <= o.closed_at::date
                         ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
                         LIMIT 1)), 2) AS avg_amount_eur
FROM opportunities o
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
WHERE o.is_closed = true
  AND p.name = 'New business'
  AND (t.industry ILIKE '%industrial%' OR t.industry ILIKE '%office equipment%' OR t.industry ILIKE '%wholesal%')
GROUP BY t.id, t.name
ORDER BY win_rate_pct ASC, opportunities_closed DESC, t.name ASC
builds_on: B2B Wholesale Pipeline: Opportunities by Merchant and Stage
New Business Only: Won vs Lost Opportunity Characteristics
entries.engineer_note: EUR conversion uses the nearest prior exchange_rates.as_of on or before closed_at's date (per currency); avg_days_open and avg_amount_eur are rounded to 1 and 2 decimals respectively.

entries.title: B2B Wholesale: Win Rate and Cycle Time by Sales Rep (New Business)
entries.question: Among reps who own B2B wholesale new-business opportunities, are a few reps clearly underperforming on win rate or cycle time, or is performance broadly similar?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  u.full_name AS rep_name,
  t.name AS merchant,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_won,
  SUM(CASE WHEN NOT o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_lost,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.closed_at - o.created_at)) / 86400.0), 1) AS avg_days_open,
  ROUND(AVG(
    CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
    ELSE o.amount / (
      SELECT er.rate
      FROM exchange_rates er
      WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(o.closed_at AS date)
    ) END
  ), 2) AS avg_amount_eur
FROM opportunities o
JOIN users u ON u.id = o.owner_user_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
JOIN pipelines pl ON pl.id = o.pipeline_id AND pl.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
WHERE o.is_closed = true
  AND pl.name = 'New business'
  AND o.tenant_id IN (
    SELECT tn.id FROM tenants tn WHERE tn.industry IN ('industrial supplies', 'office equipment')
  )
GROUP BY o.owner_user_id, u.full_name, t.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY win_rate_pct ASC, opportunities_closed DESC, rep_name ASC
builds_on: New Business Only: Won vs Lost Opportunity Characteristics
entries.engineer_note: I used tenants.industry IN ('industrial supplies','office equipment') as the B2B wholesale tenant filter and pipelines.name = 'New business' as the pipeline filter, matching the verticals and pipeline naming convention described for this series of reports — please confirm these match the exact filter used in the earlier merchant-level report if it differed. The exact count of reps excluded by the <3 closed-deals rule isn't a value I can compute at authoring time (dry runs don't return data); it will be visible as the gap between total distinct owners in scope and the row count printed on this report.

entries.title: B2B Wholesale: Age Profile of Currently Open New-Business Pipeline
entries.question: How much of our current B2B wholesale new-business pipeline is already older than the typical window in which deals actually win, i.e. how much open pipeline is quietly turning stale and at risk?
entries.sql:
WITH fx AS (
  SELECT quote_code, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR' AND as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
),
scoped AS (
  SELECT
    o.id,
    o.amount,
    o.currency_code,
    o.created_at,
    (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.created_at AS DATE)) AS age_days
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = false
    AND lower(p.name) = 'new business'
    AND (
      lower(t.industry) LIKE '%wholesale%'
      OR lower(t.industry) LIKE '%industrial%'
      OR lower(t.industry) LIKE '%office equipment%'
    )
),
converted AS (
  SELECT
    s.*,
    CASE WHEN s.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN s.amount
         ELSE s.amount / fx.rate END AS amount_eur
  FROM scoped s
  LEFT JOIN fx ON fx.quote_code = s.currency_code
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    CASE
      WHEN age_days < 10 THEN '0-9 days'
      WHEN age_days < 20 THEN '10-19 days'
      WHEN age_days < 30 THEN '20-29 days'
      WHEN age_days < 45 THEN '30-44 days'
      WHEN age_days < 90 THEN '45-89 days'
      ELSE '90+ days'
    END AS age_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN age_days < 10 THEN 0
      WHEN age_days < 20 THEN 10
      WHEN age_days < 30 THEN 20
      WHEN age_days < 45 THEN 30
      WHEN age_days < 90 THEN 45
      ELSE 90
    END AS bucket_order
  FROM converted c
)
SELECT
  age_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_open_pipeline,
  ROUND(AVG(amount_eur), 2) AS avg_amount_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(amount_eur), 2) AS total_amount_eur
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY age_bucket, bucket_order
ORDER BY bucket_order
builds_on: New Business Only: Won vs Lost Opportunity Characteristics
New Business Only: Deal Cycle Time Trend by Month
entries.engineer_note: The request didn't name the specific wholesale tenant(s), so I scoped it to tenants whose industry text matches wholesale/industrial/office-equipment (the B2B wholesaler verticals noted in the company briefing) rather than a single hardcoded tenant_id — please flag if a narrower/different tenant set was intended. Pipeline is matched case-insensitively on name = 'New business'.

entries.title: B2B Wholesale: Win Rate and Average Deal Size by Merchant (New Business) — Corrected
entries.question: Does the merchant-level win-rate pattern hold once we also see typical deal size per merchant, and can we fix last night's missing EUR averages?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.name AS merchant,
  t0.default_currency_code AS currency_code,
  COALESCE(s_counts.opportunities_closed, 0) AS opportunities_closed,
  COALESCE(s_counts.closed_won, 0) AS closed_won,
  COALESCE(s_counts.closed_lost, 0) AS closed_lost,
  ROUND(COALESCE(s_counts.closed_won, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(s_counts.opportunities_closed, 0), 2) AS win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(s_days.avg_days_open, 2) AS avg_days_open,
  ROUND(s_amt.avg_amount_eur, 2) AS avg_amount_eur
FROM tenants t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_won,
    SUM(CASE WHEN NOT o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_lost
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
    AND p.name = 'New business'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) s_counts ON s_counts.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.closed_at - o.created_at)) / 86400.0) AS avg_days_open
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
    AND p.name = 'New business'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) s_days ON s_days.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    AVG(
      CASE
        WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
        ELSE o.amount / (
          SELECT er.rate
          FROM exchange_rates er
          WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
            AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
            AND er.as_of <= CAST(o.closed_at AS date)
          ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
          LIMIT 1
        )
      END
    ) AS avg_amount_eur
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
    AND p.name = 'New business'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
) s_amt ON s_amt.tenant_id = t0.id
WHERE t0.name IN ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf','Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging')
ORDER BY win_rate_pct ASC, opportunities_closed DESC, merchant ASC
builds_on: B2B Wholesale: Win Rate and Cycle Time by Merchant (New Business)
entries.engineer_note: Fixed the EUR averaging bug by skipping the exchange_rates join entirely when currency_code = 'EUR' (amount_eur = amount directly); for non-EUR rows (Castell Fasteners, USD) we use the EUR/quote rate as of the nearest date on or before closed_at. avg_days_open is calendar days between created_at and closed_at.

entries.title: B2B Wholesale: Win Rate and Cycle Time by Deal-Size Band (New Business)
entries.question: Does a bigger deal size correlate with a better or worse chance of closing, and does it drag out the cycle time?
entries.sql:
WITH pipelines_filtered AS (
  SELECT p.id AS pipeline_id, p.tenant_id
  FROM pipelines p
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf','Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging')
    AND p.name = 'New business'
),
opp AS (
  SELECT
    o.id,
    o.is_won,
    o.created_at,
    o.closed_at,
    CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
         ELSE o.amount / (
           SELECT er.rate
           FROM exchange_rates er
           WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
             AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
             AND er.as_of <= o.closed_at::date
           ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
           LIMIT 1
         )
    END AS amount_eur
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN pipelines_filtered pf ON pf.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id AND pf.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
),
banded AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN amount_eur < 3000 THEN '<3000'
      WHEN amount_eur < 6000 THEN '3000-5999'
      WHEN amount_eur < 9000 THEN '6000-8999'
      WHEN amount_eur < 12000 THEN '9000-11999'
      ELSE '12000+'
    END AS amount_band_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN amount_eur < 3000 THEN 1
      WHEN amount_eur < 6000 THEN 2
      WHEN amount_eur < 9000 THEN 3
      WHEN amount_eur < 12000 THEN 4
      ELSE 5
    END AS band_sort,
    is_won,
    closed_at,
    created_at
  FROM opp
)
SELECT
  amount_band_eur,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_won) AS closed_won,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_won) AS closed_lost,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_won) / COUNT(*), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (closed_at - created_at)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_open
FROM banded
GROUP BY amount_band_eur, band_sort
ORDER BY band_sort
builds_on: New Business Only: Won vs Lost Opportunity Characteristics
entries.engineer_note: Banded by EUR-converted opportunity amount (nearest exchange rate on/before closed_at) for closed New-business opportunities at the 5 named B2B tenants; 5 rows, one per band, ordered by lower bound.

entries.title: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
entries.question: How often do physical cycle counts come back different from the stock quantity we had on record, and how large are those differences in units and estimated value, across 2025?
entries.sql:
with cc as (
  select sm.id, sm.variant_id, sm.quantity, sm.occurred_at, sl.warehouse_id
  from stock_movements sm
  join stock_locations sl on sl.id = sm.stock_location_id
  where sm.kind = 'cycle_count'
    and sm.occurred_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
    and sm.occurred_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
),
supplier_cost as (
  select variant_id, currency_code, unit_cost
  from (
    select sp.variant_id, sp.currency_code, sp.unit_cost,
           row_number() over (
             partition by sp.variant_id
             order by case when sp.is_preferred then 0 else 1 end asc, sp.unit_cost asc
           ) as rn
    from supplier_products sp
    join suppliers s on s.id = sp.supplier_id
    where sp.is_preferred = true or s.is_active = true
  ) t
  where rn = 1
),
valued as (
  select cc.id, cc.variant_id, cc.quantity, cc.occurred_at, cc.warehouse_id,
         sc.currency_code, sc.unit_cost, er.rate
  from cc
  left join supplier_cost sc on sc.variant_id = cc.variant_id
  left join exchange_rates er
    on er.base_code = 'EUR'
   and er.quote_code = sc.currency_code
   and er.as_of = cast(cc.occurred_at as date)
)
select
  strftime(occurred_at, '%Y-%m') as month,
  count(*) as cycle_count_events,
  count(distinct warehouse_id) as warehouses_affected,
  coalesce(sum(abs(quantity)) filter (where quantity < 0), 0) as units_short,
  coalesce(sum(quantity) filter (where quantity > 0), 0) as units_over,
  sum(quantity) as net_units_variance,
  sum(abs(quantity)) as abs_units_variance,
  round(sum(abs(quantity) * unit_cost / rate), 0) as estimated_value_eur,
  round(sum(abs(quantity))::numeric / count(*), 1) as avg_abs_units_per_event
from valued
group by strftime(occurred_at, '%Y-%m')
order by month
entries.engineer_note: Note: supplier_products has no is_active column itself, so "active supplier_products rows" was interpreted as rows sourced from an active supplier (suppliers.is_active=true); variants with no supplier_products row are excluded only from estimated_value_eur, as requested, but still counted in the unit/event columns.

entries.title: Stock discrepancies by warehouse and location type
entries.question: Does the stock-count mismatch concentrate in particular warehouses, particular storage-location kinds (e.g. bulk shelving vs pick bins), or particular merchants, in a way that signals valuation/write-off exposure?
entries.sql:
WITH variant_cost AS (
  SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code
  FROM (
    SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
             PARTITION BY variant_id
             ORDER BY CASE WHEN is_preferred THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, unit_cost ASC
           ) AS rn
    FROM supplier_products
    WHERE unit_cost IS NOT NULL
  ) ranked
  WHERE rn = 1
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    t.id AS tenant_id,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    w.id AS warehouse_id,
    w.name AS warehouse_name,
    sl.kind AS location_kind,
    COUNT(*) AS cycle_count_events,
    SUM(sm.quantity) AS net_units_variance,
    SUM(ABS(sm.quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
    SUM(ABS(sm.quantity) * vc.unit_cost / CASE WHEN vc.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END) AS estimated_value_eur
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sm.stock_location_id
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  JOIN variant_cost vc ON vc.variant_id = sm.variant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = vc.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(sm.occurred_at AS date)
  WHERE sm.kind = 'cycle_count'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.id, t.name, w.id, w.name, sl.kind
)
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  warehouse_name,
  location_kind,
  cycle_count_events,
  net_units_variance,
  abs_units_variance,
  ROUND(estimated_value_eur, 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(estimated_value_eur / SUM(estimated_value_eur) OVER () * 100, 1) AS share_of_total_value_pct
FROM agg
ORDER BY estimated_value_eur DESC, abs_units_variance DESC, tenant_name, warehouse_name, location_kind
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
entries.engineer_note: Costing uses each variant's preferred supplier_products.unit_cost, falling back to the cheapest supplier if no preferred row exists, converted to EUR via exchange_rates (EUR→currency rate on the movement's calendar date; EUR rows pass through at 1:1), matching report 1's method. The printed report header will show the true total row count if it exceeds the 50 printed here.

entries.title: Stock discrepancies by product category: handling vs tracking-method issue
entries.question: Are stock-count discrepancies spread evenly across product categories, or concentrated in certain categories, lot/serial-tracked items, or high-velocity items — pointing to a handling problem vs a tracking-method problem?
entries.sql:
WITH cycle_counts AS (
  SELECT
    sm.quantity,
    sm.lot_id,
    sm.occurred_at,
    pv.id AS variant_id,
    COALESCE(c.name, 'Uncategorized') AS category_name
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = sm.variant_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
  LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
  WHERE sm.kind = 'cycle_count'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
cost_per_variant AS (
  SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code
  FROM (
    SELECT sp.variant_id, sp.unit_cost, sp.currency_code,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sp.variant_id ORDER BY sp.is_preferred DESC, sp.id) AS rn
    FROM supplier_products sp
    WHERE sp.unit_cost IS NOT NULL
  ) x
  WHERE rn = 1
),
cc_valued AS (
  SELECT
    cc.category_name,
    cc.quantity,
    cc.lot_id,
    CASE WHEN cv.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN cv.unit_cost
         WHEN cv.unit_cost IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE cv.unit_cost / er.rate
    END AS unit_cost_eur
  FROM cycle_counts cc
  LEFT JOIN cost_per_variant cv ON cv.variant_id = cc.variant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = cv.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = DATE(cc.occurred_at)
),
category_cc AS (
  SELECT
    category_name,
    COUNT(*) AS cycle_count_events,
    SUM(ABS(quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
    SUM(quantity) AS net_units_variance,
    SUM(ABS(quantity) * COALESCE(unit_cost_eur, 0)) AS estimated_value_eur,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN lot_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_lot_or_serial
  FROM cc_valued
  GROUP BY category_name
),
sales AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(c.name, 'Uncategorized') AS category_name,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = oi.product_variant_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
  LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY COALESCE(c.name, 'Uncategorized')
)
SELECT
  cc.category_name,
  cc.cycle_count_events,
  cc.abs_units_variance,
  cc.net_units_variance,
  ROUND(cc.estimated_value_eur, 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(cc.pct_lot_or_serial, 1) AS pct_events_lot_or_serial_tracked,
  ROUND(COALESCE(s.total_units_sold, 0) / 12.0, 1) AS avg_monthly_units_sold,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(s.total_units_sold, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE cc.abs_units_variance / COALESCE(s.total_units_sold, 0) * 1000
    END, 1) AS variance_per_1000_units_sold
FROM category_cc cc
LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.category_name = cc.category_name
ORDER BY ROUND(cc.estimated_value_eur, 2) DESC, cc.category_name ASC
builds_on: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
entries.engineer_note: I didn't have "report 1" in context, so for costing/FX I used: unit cost from each variant's preferred supplier_products row (fallback to lowest id if none marked preferred), converted to EUR via exchange_rates on the cycle-count's occurred_at date; movements with no supplier cost on file contribute 0 to estimated_value_eur. Also, since categories are tenant-scoped and grouping by category_id across ~120 tenants would yield far more than 50 rows, I grouped by category_name (merging same-named categories across tenants) to match the expected row count and grain.

entries.title: Stock movement magnitude by kind, 2025
entries.question: Is the finding that every recorded cycle-count discrepancy is exactly 1 unit (not a range of sizes) real, or does it only show up because other movement kinds behave differently — i.e., is quantity magnitude on stock_movements generally variable, or is ±1 specific to cycle_count?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  kind,
  count(*) AS event_count,
  min(abs(quantity)) AS min_abs_qty,
  max(abs(quantity)) AS max_abs_qty,
  round(avg(abs(quantity)), 2) AS avg_abs_qty,
  percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY abs(quantity)) AS median_abs_qty,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE abs(quantity) = 1) / count(*), 1) AS pct_abs_qty_eq_1,
  sum(abs(quantity)) AS total_abs_qty
FROM stock_movements
WHERE occurred_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND occurred_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY kind
ORDER BY kind
builds_on: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
Stock discrepancies by product category: handling vs tracking-method issue
entries.engineer_note: Used occurred_at >= 2025-01-01 and < 2026-01-01 (equivalent to the requested inclusive range) for a clean half-open bound on timestamps.

entries.title: Stock-count discrepancies by storage-location kind, company-wide
entries.question: Across the whole company (not just the top warehouses by value), does the cycle-count mismatch concentrate in pick locations specifically, or do other location kinds (bulk, overflow, etc.) also carry meaningful discrepancy volume?
entries.sql:
WITH kinds AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT kind AS location_kind
  FROM stock_locations
),
location_counts AS (
  SELECT kind AS location_kind,
         COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS total_locations_of_this_kind
  FROM stock_locations
  GROUP BY kind
),
cycle_counts AS (
  SELECT sl.kind AS location_kind,
         sm.stock_location_id,
         sm.variant_id,
         sm.quantity,
         sm.occurred_at
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sm.stock_location_id
  WHERE sm.kind = 'cycle_count'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
variant_cost AS (
  SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code
  FROM (
    SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY variant_id ORDER BY is_preferred DESC, unit_cost ASC) AS rn
    FROM supplier_products
    WHERE unit_cost IS NOT NULL
  ) ranked
  WHERE rn = 1
),
valued AS (
  SELECT cc.location_kind,
         cc.stock_location_id,
         cc.quantity,
         CASE
           WHEN vc.unit_cost IS NOT NULL AND er.rate IS NOT NULL
           THEN ABS(cc.quantity) * vc.unit_cost / er.rate
           ELSE 0
         END AS value_eur
  FROM cycle_counts cc
  LEFT JOIN variant_cost vc ON vc.variant_id = cc.variant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = vc.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(cc.occurred_at AS date)
),
agg AS (
  SELECT location_kind,
         COUNT(DISTINCT stock_location_id) AS distinct_locations_with_activity,
         COUNT(*) AS cycle_count_events,
         SUM(ABS(quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
         SUM(quantity) AS net_units_variance,
         SUM(value_eur) AS estimated_value_eur
  FROM valued
  GROUP BY location_kind
)
SELECT
  k.location_kind,
  COALESCE(a.distinct_locations_with_activity, 0) AS distinct_locations_with_activity,
  COALESCE(lc.total_locations_of_this_kind, 0) AS total_locations_of_this_kind,
  COALESCE(a.cycle_count_events, 0) AS cycle_count_events,
  COALESCE(a.abs_units_variance, 0) AS abs_units_variance,
  COALESCE(a.net_units_variance, 0) AS net_units_variance,
  ROUND(COALESCE(a.estimated_value_eur, 0), 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COALESCE(a.estimated_value_eur, 0)
    / NULLIF(SUM(COALESCE(a.estimated_value_eur, 0)) OVER (), 0),
    2
  ) AS share_of_total_value_pct
FROM kinds k
LEFT JOIN location_counts lc ON lc.location_kind = k.location_kind
LEFT JOIN agg a ON a.location_kind = k.location_kind
ORDER BY COALESCE(a.estimated_value_eur, 0) DESC, k.location_kind ASC
builds_on: Stock discrepancies by warehouse and location type
entries.engineer_note: Valuation uses preferred-then-cheapest supplier_products.unit_cost per variant (COALESCE to 0 when a variant has no supplier_products cost or no matching exchange_rates row for that currency/date), converted to EUR via exchange_rates.rate (EUR as base_code) on the movement's occurred_at date; estimated_value_eur is computed from absolute unit variance (|quantity| × cost), not net.

entries.title: Stock reservation outcomes: are soft holds reliable?
entries.question: When stock is reserved for an order, does the reservation get released normally (order fulfilled/cancelled in time), or do we see reservations left stuck past their expiry — quietly overstating what's actually available to sell?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  category AS outcome_category,
  count(*) AS reservation_count,
  round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_total,
  sum(quantity) AS total_quantity_units,
  round(avg(quantity * 1.0), 1) AS avg_quantity_per_reservation,
  round(avg(duration_days), 1) AS avg_hold_duration_days
FROM (
  SELECT
    quantity,
    CASE
      WHEN released_at IS NOT NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR released_at <= expires_at) THEN 'released_on_time'
      WHEN released_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at IS NOT NULL AND released_at > expires_at THEN 'released_late'
      WHEN released_at IS NULL AND expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' THEN 'stuck_past_expiry'
      ELSE 'still_open_active'
    END AS category,
    CASE
      WHEN released_at IS NOT NULL THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (released_at - created_at)) / 86400.0
      ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' - created_at)) / 86400.0
    END AS duration_days
  FROM stock_reservations
  WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
) t
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY
  CASE category
    WHEN 'released_on_time' THEN 1
    WHEN 'released_late' THEN 2
    WHEN 'stuck_past_expiry' THEN 3
    WHEN 'still_open_active' THEN 4
  END
entries.engineer_note: Report is global across all tenants (no merchant breakdown was requested); all durations computed in days using the fixed 2025-12-31 reference date as specified. One row per outcome category, 4 rows total, no truncation.

entries.title: Scale of adjustment-kind stock movements by month, 2025
entries.question: Unlike cycle_count (always exactly 1 unit), kind='adjustment' movements vary widely (avg ~10 units, max 192) — what is the monthly scale, direction (shrinkage vs gain) and estimated value of this stream, and how does it trend across 2025?
entries.sql:
WITH variant_cost AS (
  SELECT sp.variant_id, sp.unit_cost, sp.currency_code,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sp.variant_id ORDER BY sp.is_preferred DESC, sp.unit_cost ASC) AS rn
  FROM supplier_products sp
  WHERE sp.unit_cost IS NOT NULL
),
best_cost AS (
  SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code FROM variant_cost WHERE rn = 1
),
movements AS (
  SELECT sm.id, sm.variant_id, sm.quantity, sm.occurred_at,
         CAST(sm.occurred_at AS date) AS occ_date
  FROM stock_movements sm
  WHERE sm.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
valued AS (
  SELECT m.id, m.quantity,
    date_trunc('month', m.occurred_at) AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN bc.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN bc.unit_cost
         WHEN bc.currency_code IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE bc.unit_cost / er.rate
    END AS unit_cost_eur
  FROM movements m
  LEFT JOIN best_cost bc ON bc.variant_id = m.variant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = bc.currency_code AND er.as_of = m.occ_date
)
SELECT
  strftime(month_start, '%Y-%m') AS month,
  COUNT(*) AS adjustment_events,
  SUM(CASE WHEN quantity < 0 THEN -quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_short,
  SUM(CASE WHEN quantity > 0 THEN quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_over,
  SUM(quantity) AS net_units_variance,
  SUM(ABS(quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
  ROUND(SUM(ABS(quantity) * COALESCE(unit_cost_eur,0))::numeric, 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(ABS(quantity))::numeric, 1) AS avg_abs_units_per_event
FROM valued
GROUP BY month_start
ORDER BY month_start
builds_on: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
Stock movement magnitude by kind, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Unit cost per variant = preferred supplier_products row if present, else cheapest unit_cost among suppliers; converted to EUR using exchange_rates (base_code=EUR, quote_code=supplier currency) as of the movement's occurred_at date. Movements for variants with no supplier_products cost are counted in unit/event totals but contribute 0 to estimated_value_eur (no cost basis available).

entries.title: Largest individual stock adjustments in 2025
entries.question: With only 407 adjustment-kind events in the year but some as large as 192 units, which specific events are driving the value — do they cluster by warehouse, merchant, location kind, category or product, or are they scattered?
entries.sql:
WITH adjustments_2025 AS (
    SELECT
        sm.id,
        sm.tenant_id,
        sm.variant_id,
        sm.stock_location_id,
        sm.quantity AS quantity_signed,
        sm.reference_type,
        sm.occurred_at
    FROM stock_movements sm
    WHERE sm.kind = 'adjustment'
      AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
preferred_cost AS (
    SELECT
        sp.variant_id,
        sp.unit_cost,
        sp.currency_code,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sp.variant_id ORDER BY sp.id) AS rn
    FROM supplier_products sp
    WHERE sp.is_preferred = true
),
variant_cost AS (
    SELECT variant_id, unit_cost, currency_code
    FROM preferred_cost
    WHERE rn = 1
),
fx AS (
    SELECT base_code, quote_code, rate, as_of
    FROM exchange_rates
    WHERE base_code = 'EUR'
),
enriched AS (
    SELECT
        a.id,
        a.occurred_at,
        t.name AS tenant_name,
        w.name AS warehouse_name,
        sl.kind AS location_kind,
        COALESCE(c.name, 'Uncategorized') AS category_name,
        pv.sku,
        a.quantity_signed,
        a.reference_type,
        CASE
            WHEN vc.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ABS(a.quantity_signed) * vc.unit_cost
            ELSE ABS(a.quantity_signed) * vc.unit_cost / NULLIF(fx.rate, 0)
        END AS estimated_value_eur
    FROM adjustments_2025 a
    JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = a.stock_location_id
    JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
    JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = a.variant_id
    JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
    LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
    LEFT JOIN variant_cost vc ON vc.variant_id = a.variant_id
    LEFT JOIN fx ON fx.quote_code = vc.currency_code AND fx.as_of = CAST(a.occurred_at AS date)
)
SELECT
    occurred_at,
    tenant_name,
    warehouse_name,
    location_kind,
    category_name,
    sku,
    quantity_signed,
    ROUND(estimated_value_eur, 2) AS estimated_value_eur,
    reference_type
FROM enriched
ORDER BY estimated_value_eur DESC NULLS LAST, ABS(quantity_signed) DESC, occurred_at, id
LIMIT 30
builds_on: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
Stock discrepancies by warehouse and location type
Stock discrepancies by product category: handling vs tracking-method issue
entries.engineer_note: Unit cost is taken from each variant's preferred supplier (supplier_products.unit_cost, is_preferred=true; if several preferred rows exist for a variant the lowest id is used), converted to EUR via exchange_rates on the movement's date; rows with no preferred supplier cost show a null estimated_value_eur. The query returns the top 30 of 407 total 2025 adjustment-kind movements, as requested — please note the 407 total in the printed report since the query itself only returns the top 30 rows.

entries.title: Cross-check: stock_adjustments table vs stock_movements adjustment-kind ledger, 2025
entries.question: Does the stock_adjustments table (the human-entered correction record with a required reason) cover the same volume as the stock_movements kind='adjustment' ledger, or is one capturing materially more/less than the other — i.e., which is the authoritative source for 'a physical count or review found a quantity discrepancy'?
entries.sql:
select source, row_count, total_abs_quantity, distinct_variants_affected, earliest_date, latest_date from (
  select
    'stock_adjustments table' as source,
    count(*) as row_count,
    sum(abs(quantity_delta)) as total_abs_quantity,
    count(distinct variant_id) as distinct_variants_affected,
    min(created_at) as earliest_date,
    max(created_at) as latest_date,
    0 as sort_order
  from stock_adjustments
  where created_at >= date '2025-01-01' and created_at < date '2026-01-01'

  union all

  select
    'stock_movements kind=adjustment ledger' as source,
    count(*) as row_count,
    sum(abs(quantity)) as total_abs_quantity,
    count(distinct variant_id) as distinct_variants_affected,
    min(occurred_at) as earliest_date,
    max(occurred_at) as latest_date,
    1 as sort_order
  from stock_movements
  where kind = 'adjustment'
    and occurred_at >= date '2025-01-01' and occurred_at < date '2026-01-01'
) t
order by sort_order
builds_on: Scale of adjustment-kind stock movements by month, 2025
entries.engineer_note: stock_adjustments has no occurred_at column, only created_at, so that is used as "when recorded" for that source; stock_movements uses occurred_at as requested. This is an all-tenant, all-currency unit/row-count comparison (no money involved), so no currency conversion was needed.

entries.title: Monthly volume of stock_adjustments table entries, 2025
entries.question: Does the stock_adjustments table show a steady, roughly even pattern across 2025 (like the cycle_count movement stream it appears to feed), or does it also cluster at year-end like the stock_movements kind='adjustment' ledger?
entries.sql:
SELECT
    strftime(date_trunc('month', t0.created_at), '%Y-%m') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS adjustment_count,
    SUM(ABS(t0.quantity_delta)) AS total_abs_quantity_delta,
    SUM(t0.quantity_delta) AS net_quantity_delta,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t0.variant_id) AS distinct_variants_affected,
    ROUND(AVG(ABS(t0.quantity_delta)), 2) AS avg_abs_quantity_delta
FROM stock_adjustments t0
WHERE t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', t0.created_at)
ORDER BY month ASC
builds_on: Cross-check: stock_adjustments table vs stock_movements adjustment-kind ledger, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Grouped by created_at (no occurred_at on stock_adjustments), as specified in the request.

entries.title: Which merchants drove the December 31 bulk stock correction
entries.question: The 407 stock_movements kind='adjustment' events (nearly all on 2025-12-31) appeared, in the top-30 detail, to be entirely B2B wholesale merchants (office equipment / industrial supplies) — is that concentration total, or do other merchants/verticals also appear further down the list?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  sub.tenant_name,
  sub.industry,
  sub.adjustment_events,
  sub.abs_units_variance,
  sub.net_units_variance,
  sub.estimated_value_eur,
  ROUND(sub.estimated_value_eur * 100.0 / SUM(sub.estimated_value_eur) OVER (), 2) AS share_of_total_value_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    t.industry AS industry,
    COUNT(*) AS adjustment_events,
    SUM(ABS(sm.quantity)) AS abs_units_variance,
    SUM(sm.quantity) AS net_units_variance,
    ROUND(SUM(
      ABS(sm.quantity) * COALESCE(
        (SELECT sp.unit_cost / er.rate
         FROM supplier_products sp
         JOIN exchange_rates er
           ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = sp.currency_code
          AND er.as_of = CAST(sm.occurred_at AS date)
         WHERE sp.variant_id = sm.variant_id
           AND sp.is_preferred = true
           AND sp.unit_cost IS NOT NULL
         ORDER BY sp.id
         LIMIT 1
        ), 0)
    ), 2) AS estimated_value_eur
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sm.stock_location_id
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  WHERE sm.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.id, t.name, t.industry
) sub
ORDER BY sub.estimated_value_eur DESC, sub.tenant_name ASC
builds_on: Largest individual stock adjustments in 2025
Scale of adjustment-kind stock movements by month, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant with any 2025 kind='adjustment' stock_movements event (expected well under 50 rows, so no row cap applied). Estimated value costs each event's absolute units at the variant's preferred supplier unit_cost, converted to EUR via the exchange_rates row for that exact occurred_at date (weekend dates already carry forward the prior business-day rate per the catalog); events for variants with no preferred-supplier cost on record contribute 0 to estimated_value_eur but still count toward adjustment_events/units. I didn't have the exact prior-report costing/FX logic to match against, so please confirm this approximation is consistent with it.

entries.title: Reasons behind routine stock_adjustments entries, 2025
entries.question: What reasons are recorded against the routine, year-round, single-unit stock_adjustments entries (the stream that appears to feed the cycle_count movements) — is it mostly shrinkage/loss language, or a mix of loss and found-stock reasons, and does the mix matter for sizing a shrinkage provision?
entries.sql:
SELECT reason,
  COUNT(*) AS event_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_total_events,
  SUM(quantity_delta) AS net_quantity_delta,
  SUM(ABS(quantity_delta)) AS total_abs_quantity_delta,
  ROUND(AVG(ABS(quantity_delta)), 2) AS avg_abs_quantity_delta
FROM stock_adjustments
WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  AND ABS(quantity_delta) = 1
GROUP BY reason
ORDER BY event_count DESC, reason ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Monthly volume of stock_adjustments table entries, 2025
entries.engineer_note: "Routine, single-unit, year-round" entries were interpreted as rows where ABS(quantity_delta)=1 (the one-unit-at-a-time stream that would feed cycle_count movements); other adjustment sizes (bulk corrections, etc.) are excluded. Grouped by the exact reason string with no bucketing, as requested; if the result hits the 50-row cap the true distinct-reason count is higher and worth a follow-up.

entries.title: Ticket volume and staffing by agent group
