entries.question: How is ticket volume distributed across our agent groups, and does staffing (agent count) look balanced against that load?
entries.sql:
WITH group_names AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT name AS agent_group_name
  FROM agent_groups
),

ticket_window AS (
  SELECT
    t.id,
    t.agent_group_id,
    t.tenant_id,
    ag.name AS group_name,
    t.status,
    t.assignee_agent_id,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  LEFT JOIN agent_groups ag
    ON ag.id = t.agent_group_id AND ag.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),

ticket_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(group_name, 'Unassigned queue') AS agent_group_name,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status NOT IN ('solved','closed')) AS open_ticket_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE assignee_agent_id IS NULL) AS unassigned_ticket_count,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (first_response_at - created_at)) / 60.0)
      FILTER (WHERE first_response_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 60.0)
      FILTER (WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes
  FROM ticket_window
  GROUP BY COALESCE(group_name, 'Unassigned queue')
),

agent_counts AS (
  SELECT
    ag.name AS agent_group_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT agm.tenant_id::text || ':' || agm.support_agent_id::text) AS agent_count
  FROM agent_group_members agm
  JOIN agent_groups ag
    ON ag.id = agm.agent_group_id AND ag.tenant_id = agm.tenant_id
  GROUP BY ag.name
),

all_rows AS (
  SELECT agent_group_name FROM group_names
  UNION
  SELECT 'Unassigned queue'
)

SELECT
  r.agent_group_name,
  COALESCE(tm.ticket_count, 0) AS ticket_count,
  COALESCE(tm.open_ticket_count, 0) AS open_ticket_count,
  ac.agent_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(tm.ticket_count,0)::numeric / NULLIF(ac.agent_count,0), 1) AS tickets_per_agent,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(tm.unassigned_ticket_count,0) / NULLIF(tm.ticket_count,0), 1) AS pct_unassigned,
  ROUND(tm.avg_first_response_minutes::numeric) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(tm.avg_resolution_minutes::numeric) AS avg_resolution_minutes
FROM all_rows r
LEFT JOIN ticket_metrics tm ON tm.agent_group_name = r.agent_group_name
LEFT JOIN agent_counts ac ON ac.agent_group_name = r.agent_group_name
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN r.agent_group_name = 'Unassigned queue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
  COALESCE(tm.ticket_count,0) DESC,
  r.agent_group_name
entries.engineer_note: Agent groups are tenant-scoped, so this rolls up all tenants' groups by name (e.g. every merchant's 'Tier 1' group is combined into one row) since the request didn't scope to a particular merchant; ticket/agent counts and the Unassigned-queue footnote are totals across the whole platform for 2025.

entries.title: SLA breach rates by agent group
entries.question: Which agent groups miss first-response and resolution SLA targets most often, and by how much when they do?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.agent_group_id, COALESCE(ag.name, 'Unassigned queue') AS agent_group_name,
         t.created_at, t.first_response_at, t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  LEFT JOIN agent_groups ag ON ag.id = t.agent_group_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
),
ticket_stats AS (
  SELECT agent_group_id, agent_group_name,
         COUNT(*) AS ticket_count_with_sla,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (first_response_at - created_at))/60.0) FILTER (WHERE first_response_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
         AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at))/60.0) FILTER (WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes
  FROM base
  GROUP BY agent_group_id, agent_group_name
),
breach_join AS (
  SELECT base.agent_group_id, base.agent_group_name, sb.ticket_id, sb.breach_kind, sb.minutes_over
  FROM base
  JOIN sla_breaches sb ON sb.ticket_id = base.id
),
breach_stats AS (
  SELECT agent_group_id, agent_group_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE breach_kind = 'first_response') AS fr_breach_tickets,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE breach_kind = 'resolution') AS res_breach_tickets,
    AVG(minutes_over) FILTER (WHERE breach_kind = 'first_response') AS avg_minutes_over_first_response,
    AVG(minutes_over) FILTER (WHERE breach_kind = 'resolution') AS avg_minutes_over_resolution
  FROM breach_join
  GROUP BY agent_group_id, agent_group_name
)
SELECT
  ts.agent_group_name,
  ts.ticket_count_with_sla,
  ROUND(CAST(100.0 * COALESCE(bs.fr_breach_tickets, 0) / ts.ticket_count_with_sla AS numeric), 1) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  ROUND(CAST(100.0 * COALESCE(bs.res_breach_tickets, 0) / ts.ticket_count_with_sla AS numeric), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate,
  ROUND(CAST(bs.avg_minutes_over_first_response AS numeric), 0) AS avg_minutes_over_first_response,
  ROUND(CAST(bs.avg_minutes_over_resolution AS numeric), 0) AS avg_minutes_over_resolution,
  ROUND(CAST(ts.avg_first_response_minutes AS numeric), 0) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(CAST(ts.avg_resolution_minutes AS numeric), 0) AS avg_resolution_minutes
FROM ticket_stats ts
LEFT JOIN breach_stats bs ON bs.agent_group_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ts.agent_group_id
ORDER BY
  (ts.agent_group_name = 'Unassigned queue') ASC,
  resolution_breach_rate DESC NULLS LAST,
  ts.agent_group_name ASC
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per agent_group (grouped by the group's id across all tenants, since the request didn't restrict to a merchant); all tickets with a null agent_group_id are collapsed into a single 'Unassigned queue' row as requested. avg_first_response_minutes and avg_resolution_minutes are computed only over tickets that actually have a first_response_at/resolved_at timestamp (pending ones excluded from those two averages, though still counted in ticket_count_with_sla).

entries.title: SLA breach rates by priority, with overall headline rate
entries.question: What is our overall SLA breach rate for 2025, and which priority levels drive the misses?
entries.sql:
with base as (
  select t.id as ticket_id, t.priority,
         sp.first_response_target_minutes,
         sp.resolution_target_minutes
  from tickets t
  join sla_policies sp on sp.id = t.sla_policy_id
  where t.created_at >= date '2025-01-01'
    and t.created_at < date '2026-01-01'
    and t.sla_policy_id is not null
),
breach_fr as (
  select ticket_id, avg(minutes_over) as minutes_over
  from sla_breaches
  where breach_kind = 'first_response'
  group by ticket_id
),
breach_res as (
  select ticket_id, avg(minutes_over) as minutes_over
  from sla_breaches
  where breach_kind = 'resolution'
  group by ticket_id
),
per_priority as (
  select
    b.priority::text as priority,
    count(*) as ticket_count_with_sla,
    round(avg(b.first_response_target_minutes)) as typical_first_response_target_minutes,
    round(avg(b.resolution_target_minutes)) as typical_resolution_target_minutes,
    round(100.0 * count(fr.ticket_id) / count(*), 1) as first_response_breach_rate,
    round(100.0 * count(res.ticket_id) / count(*), 1) as resolution_breach_rate,
    round(avg(fr.minutes_over)) as avg_minutes_over_first_response,
    round(avg(res.minutes_over)) as avg_minutes_over_resolution
  from base b
  left join breach_fr fr on fr.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
  left join breach_res res on res.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
  group by b.priority
),
overall as (
  select
    'All priorities'::text as priority,
    count(*) as ticket_count_with_sla,
    null::numeric as typical_first_response_target_minutes,
    null::numeric as typical_resolution_target_minutes,
    round(100.0 * count(fr.ticket_id) / count(*), 1) as first_response_breach_rate,
    round(100.0 * count(res.ticket_id) / count(*), 1) as resolution_breach_rate,
    round(avg(fr.minutes_over)) as avg_minutes_over_first_response,
    round(avg(res.minutes_over)) as avg_minutes_over_resolution
  from base b
  left join breach_fr fr on fr.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
  left join breach_res res on res.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
),
combined as (
  select 0 as sort_rank, * from overall
  union all
  select 1 as sort_rank, * from per_priority
)
select
  priority,
  ticket_count_with_sla,
  typical_first_response_target_minutes,
  typical_resolution_target_minutes,
  first_response_breach_rate,
  resolution_breach_rate,
  avg_minutes_over_first_response,
  avg_minutes_over_resolution
from combined
order by sort_rank, resolution_breach_rate desc nulls last, priority
entries.engineer_note: Breach rate = share of in-scope tickets (created in 2025, sla_policy_id not null) with at least one sla_breaches row of that kind, across all tenants/currencies (rates and minute counts are currency-agnostic so no FX conversion needed). "Typical" target minutes per priority are averaged from the sla_policies rows actually attached to those tickets (ticket-weighted), not a flat lookup, since policies can vary by tenant.

entries.title: Ticket volume and SLA performance by merchant
entries.question: Is ticket volume and SLA breach pain concentrated in a handful of merchants, and do any merchants stand out as outliers?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  ticket_count,
  round(pct_of_total_tickets, 1) AS pct_of_total_tickets,
  round(sum(pct_of_total_tickets) OVER (ORDER BY ticket_count DESC, tenant_name), 1) AS cumulative_pct_of_total_tickets,
  round(first_response_breach_rate, 1) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  round(resolution_breach_rate, 1) AS resolution_breach_rate,
  round(avg_resolution_minutes, 1) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  agent_count,
  total_tenants_with_tickets
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    tk.tenant_id,
    tk.ticket_count,
    100.0 * tk.ticket_count / tot.total_tickets AS pct_of_total_tickets,
    100.0 * coalesce(frb.breach_count, 0) / nullif(tk.sla_ticket_count, 0) AS first_response_breach_rate,
    100.0 * coalesce(rb.breach_count, 0) / nullif(tk.sla_ticket_count, 0) AS resolution_breach_rate,
    tk.avg_resolution_minutes,
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT sa.id) FROM support_agents sa WHERE sa.tenant_id = tk.tenant_id) AS agent_count,
    tot.total_tickets,
    tnt.total_tenants_with_tickets
  FROM (
    SELECT
      tenant_id,
      count(*) AS ticket_count,
      count(*) FILTER (WHERE sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL) AS sla_ticket_count,
      avg(extract(epoch FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 60.0) FILTER (WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
  ) tk
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tk.tenant_id
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT count(*) AS total_tickets
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  ) tot
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS total_tenants_with_tickets
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  ) tnt
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT sb.tenant_id, count(*) AS breach_count
    FROM sla_breaches sb
    JOIN tickets tk2 ON tk2.id = sb.ticket_id
    WHERE sb.breach_kind = 'first_response'
      AND tk2.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND tk2.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
      AND tk2.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY sb.tenant_id
  ) frb ON frb.tenant_id = tk.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT sb.tenant_id, count(*) AS breach_count
    FROM sla_breaches sb
    JOIN tickets tk3 ON tk3.id = sb.ticket_id
    WHERE sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
      AND tk3.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND tk3.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
      AND tk3.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY sb.tenant_id
  ) rb ON rb.tenant_id = tk.tenant_id
) x
ORDER BY ticket_count DESC, tenant_name
LIMIT 30
builds_on: Ticket volume and staffing by agent group
SLA breach rates by agent group
entries.engineer_note: Printed to the top 30 tenants by 2025 ticket volume, ordered desc with cumulative share computed over all tenants before truncation. Added a `total_tenants_with_tickets` column (constant across rows) so the analyst has the total merchant count with ≥1 ticket in 2025 without a separate query; agent_count uses support_agents.tenant_id directly per the "simpler" option noted in the request.

entries.title: Highest-volume merchant + agent-group units
entries.question: At the real operational unit (one merchant's one agent group), where is ticket load heaviest, and does staffing (agent count) look right for that load?
entries.sql:
WITH ticket_agg AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, agent_group_id,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE assignee_agent_id IS NULL) AS unassigned_count,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (first_response_at - created_at))/60.0) FILTER (WHERE first_response_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at))/60.0) FILTER (WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes
  FROM tickets
  WHERE agent_group_id IS NOT NULL
    AND created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id, agent_group_id
),
breach_agg AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, t.agent_group_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT sb.ticket_id) AS resolution_breach_count
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN sla_breaches sb ON sb.ticket_id = t.id AND sb.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.agent_group_id IS NOT NULL
    AND t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id, t.agent_group_id
),
agent_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, agent_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT support_agent_id) AS agent_count
  FROM agent_group_members
  GROUP BY tenant_id, agent_group_id
)
SELECT
  ten.name AS tenant_name,
  ag.name AS agent_group_name,
  ta.ticket_count,
  COALESCE(ac.agent_count,0) AS agent_count,
  ROUND(ta.ticket_count::numeric / NULLIF(ac.agent_count,0), 1) AS tickets_per_agent,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.unassigned_count / NULLIF(ta.ticket_count,0), 1) AS pct_unassigned,
  ROUND(ta.avg_first_response_minutes::numeric, 1) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(ta.avg_resolution_minutes::numeric, 1) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(ba.resolution_breach_count,0) / NULLIF(ta.ticket_count,0), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM ticket_agg ta
JOIN tenants ten ON ten.id = ta.tenant_id
JOIN agent_groups ag ON ag.id = ta.agent_group_id
LEFT JOIN agent_counts ac ON ac.tenant_id = ta.tenant_id AND ac.agent_group_id = ta.agent_group_id
LEFT JOIN breach_agg ba ON ba.tenant_id = ta.tenant_id AND ba.agent_group_id = ta.agent_group_id
ORDER BY ta.ticket_count DESC, ten.name, ag.name
LIMIT 20
builds_on: Ticket volume and staffing by agent group
SLA breach rates by agent group
entries.engineer_note: Resolution-breach rate assumes sla_breaches.breach_kind uses the value 'resolution' (the catalog doesn't enumerate this free-text column's allowed values, so please confirm against a sample row). The report shows the top 20 (tenant, agent_group) rows by ticket_count; ask me for a quick count query if you need the total number of combinations in 2025 as a separate figure.

entries.title: SLA breach rates by day of week and time of day
entries.question: Is there a time-of-day or day-of-week pattern to when we breach first-response and resolution SLA targets?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    t.id AS ticket_id,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    cd.day_name,
    cd.iso_day_of_week,
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.created_at)::int AS hr
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(t.created_at AS date)
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    ticket_id,
    created_at,
    first_response_at,
    day_name,
    iso_day_of_week,
    CASE
      WHEN hr >= 0 AND hr < 6 THEN 'Night (00-06)'
      WHEN hr >= 6 AND hr < 12 THEN 'Morning (06-12)'
      WHEN hr >= 12 AND hr < 18 THEN 'Afternoon (12-18)'
      ELSE 'Evening (18-24)'
    END AS time_of_day_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN hr >= 0 AND hr < 6 THEN 1
      WHEN hr >= 6 AND hr < 12 THEN 2
      WHEN hr >= 12 AND hr < 18 THEN 3
      ELSE 4
    END AS bucket_order
  FROM base
),
breaches AS (
  SELECT
    ticket_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN breach_kind = 'first_response' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fr_breach,
    MAX(CASE WHEN breach_kind = 'resolution' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS res_breach
  FROM sla_breaches
  GROUP BY ticket_id
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    b.*,
    COALESCE(br.fr_breach, 0) AS fr_breach,
    COALESCE(br.res_breach, 0) AS res_breach
  FROM bucketed b
  LEFT JOIN breaches br ON br.ticket_id = b.ticket_id
)
SELECT
  day_name AS day_of_week,
  time_of_day_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(fr_breach) / COUNT(*), 1) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(res_breach) / COUNT(*), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN first_response_at IS NOT NULL
                 THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (first_response_at - created_at)) / 60.0
            END)) AS avg_first_response_minutes
FROM joined
GROUP BY day_name, iso_day_of_week, time_of_day_bucket, bucket_order
ORDER BY iso_day_of_week, bucket_order
builds_on: SLA breach rates by priority, with overall headline rate
entries.engineer_note: Breach rates are computed by matching sla_breaches.breach_kind against the literal values 'first_response' and 'resolution' (the catalog does not enumerate allowed codes for this column, so this assumes the naming matches tickets.first_response_at/resolved_at conventions); please flag if the warehouse uses different breach_kind labels so we can correct it.

entries.title: SLA breach_kind code audit and validation
entries.question: What values does sla_breaches.breach_kind actually take, and do our assumed codes ('first_response', 'resolution') account for all breach rows so last night's breach-rate numbers can be trusted?
entries.sql:
with sla_breaches_2025 as (
    select
        breach_kind,
        ticket_id,
        minutes_over,
        breached_at
    from sla_breaches
    where breached_at >= date '2025-01-01'
      and breached_at < date '2026-01-01'
),
breach_kind_summary as (
    select
        breach_kind,
        count(*) as row_count,
        count(distinct ticket_id) as distinct_tickets_affected,
        avg(minutes_over) as avg_minutes_over,
        min(minutes_over) as min_minutes_over,
        max(minutes_over) as max_minutes_over,
        min(breached_at) as earliest_breached_at,
        max(breached_at) as latest_breached_at
    from sla_breaches_2025
    group by breach_kind
)
select
    breach_kind,
    row_count,
    distinct_tickets_affected,
    round(avg_minutes_over, 1) as avg_minutes_over,
    min_minutes_over,
    max_minutes_over,
    earliest_breached_at,
    latest_breached_at
from breach_kind_summary
order by row_count desc, breach_kind asc
builds_on: SLA breach rates by agent group
SLA breach rates by priority, with overall headline rate
SLA breach rates by day of week and time of day
entries.engineer_note: Grouped directly by whatever breach_kind strings exist in sla_breaches, filtered on breached_at in 2025 (simpler than joining ticket creation dates, and breached_at is the natural event date for a breach). I did not add a row for breaches referencing non-2025-created tickets since sla_breaches has no direct tenant-independent way to detect that cheaply without a tickets join that risks dropping/duplicating rows; if you need that reconciliation, it should be its own report comparing ticket_id sets between sla_breaches and tickets.created_at. Please compare the printed breach_kind set and counts against the ~875/~471 assumption yourselves - if any third kind or materially different counts appear, that confirms the rate calc needs fixing.

entries.title: Ticket speed by channel and assignment status
entries.question: Does the channel a ticket comes in on, or whether it currently sits unassigned, separate fast-resolving tickets from slow ones?
entries.sql:
WITH ticket_window AS (
  SELECT
    t.id,
    t.tenant_id,
    t.channel,
    CASE WHEN t.assignee_agent_id IS NULL THEN 'Unassigned' ELSE 'Assigned' END AS assignment_status,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
ticket_breach_flags AS (
  SELECT
    tw.id AS ticket_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN sb.breach_kind = 'first_response' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS first_response_breached,
    MAX(CASE WHEN sb.breach_kind = 'resolution' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS resolution_breached
  FROM ticket_window tw
  LEFT JOIN sla_breaches sb
    ON sb.ticket_id = tw.id AND sb.tenant_id = tw.tenant_id
  GROUP BY tw.id
),
ticket_metrics AS (
  SELECT
    tw.id,
    tw.channel,
    tw.assignment_status,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tw.first_response_at - tw.created_at)) / 60.0 AS first_response_minutes,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tw.resolved_at - tw.created_at)) / 60.0 AS resolution_minutes,
    bf.first_response_breached,
    bf.resolution_breached
  FROM ticket_window tw
  JOIN ticket_breach_flags bf ON bf.ticket_id = tw.id
)
SELECT
  channel,
  assignment_status,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(AVG(first_response_minutes)::numeric, 0) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(AVG(resolution_minutes)::numeric, 0) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(first_response_breached)::numeric, 1) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(resolution_breached)::numeric, 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM ticket_metrics
GROUP BY channel, assignment_status
ORDER BY avg_resolution_minutes DESC, channel, assignment_status
builds_on: Ticket volume and staffing by agent group
SLA breach rates by agent group
entries.engineer_note: I did not receive the companion audit's confirmed breach_kind codes, so this uses 'first_response' and 'resolution' as the breach_kind values in sla_breaches; please swap in the corrected codes if the audit found different ones. Avg minutes are computed only over tickets that have a first_response_at/resolved_at timestamp (unanswered/unresolved tickets are excluded from those two averages but still count in ticket_count and breach rates).

entries.title: Macro usage overview
entries.question: How much do agents actually lean on canned-reply macros, and is usage concentrated in a few macros or spread across the library?
entries.sql:
WITH macro_totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_macro_count, SUM(usage_count) AS total_macro_usage_sum
  FROM macros
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
),
agent_reply_totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_agent_reply_messages_2025
  FROM ticket_messages
  WHERE is_public = true
    AND author_agent_id IS NOT NULL
    AND created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
)
SELECT
  m.title AS macro_title,
  m.is_shared,
  m.usage_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * m.usage_count / NULLIF(mt.total_macro_usage_sum, 0), 2) AS pct_of_total_macro_usage,
  mt.total_macro_count,
  mt.total_macro_usage_sum,
  art.total_agent_reply_messages_2025
FROM macros m
CROSS JOIN macro_totals mt
CROSS JOIN agent_reply_totals art
WHERE m.deleted_at IS NULL
ORDER BY m.usage_count DESC, m.title ASC
LIMIT 20
entries.engineer_note: Report is platform-wide (not tenant-filtered) since the question is about overall macro reliance across the library. usage_count is a lifetime counter with no date dimension, so pct_of_total_macro_usage and the constants are all-time, while total_agent_reply_messages_2025 is scoped to 2025 as a rough denominator only - the two are not directly comparable periods. total_macro_count reflects the full non-deleted library size so you can see concentration vs. the long tail beyond the top 20 shown.

entries.title: Knowledge base article effectiveness
entries.question: Which knowledge base articles get used, and are the ones we have actually rated as helpful by customers?
entries.sql:
WITH published AS (
  SELECT ka.id, ka.title, kc.name AS category_name, ka.view_count, ka.helpful_count, ka.not_helpful_count
  FROM knowledge_articles ka
  LEFT JOIN knowledge_categories kc ON kc.id = ka.knowledge_category_id
  WHERE ka.is_published = true AND ka.deleted_at IS NULL
),
agg AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_published_articles,
         SUM(helpful_count) AS total_helpful,
         SUM(helpful_count + not_helpful_count) AS total_votes
  FROM published
)
SELECT
  p.title,
  p.category_name AS knowledge_category_name,
  p.view_count,
  p.helpful_count,
  p.not_helpful_count,
  CASE WHEN (p.helpful_count + p.not_helpful_count) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(p.helpful_count::numeric / (p.helpful_count + p.not_helpful_count), 4)
  END AS helpful_rate,
  a.total_published_articles,
  ROUND(a.total_helpful::numeric / NULLIF(a.total_votes,0), 4) AS platform_avg_helpful_rate
FROM published p
CROSS JOIN agg a
ORDER BY p.view_count DESC, p.id ASC
LIMIT 20
entries.engineer_note: Report is platform-wide across all tenants (no tenant filter was specified, since the question is about KB effectiveness in general rather than a particular merchant); article titles are not guaranteed unique across tenants, so if the Support Ops Manager wants this scoped to a single merchant or needs tenant/merchant name shown, let me know and I'll re-run. helpful_rate and platform_avg_helpful_rate are rounded to 4 decimals; rows with zero feedback show helpful_rate as null as requested.

entries.title: Ticket volume and speed by topic tag
entries.question: Are certain ticket topics (support tags) driving a disproportionate share of volume or taking much longer to resolve than others?
entries.sql:
WITH tickets_2025 AS (
  SELECT id, tenant_id, created_at, first_response_at, resolved_at
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tagged AS (
  SELECT
    ttm.ticket_id,
    st.name AS tag_name,
    t.created_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    t.resolved_at
  FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
  JOIN support_tags st
    ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id AND st.tenant_id = ttm.tenant_id
  JOIN tickets_2025 t
    ON t.id = ttm.ticket_id
),
breaches_per_ticket AS (
  SELECT
    ticket_id,
    BOOL_OR(breach_kind = 'first_response') AS fr_breach,
    BOOL_OR(breach_kind = 'resolution') AS res_breach
  FROM sla_breaches
  WHERE breach_kind IN ('first_response', 'resolution')
  GROUP BY ticket_id
),
tag_stats AS (
  SELECT
    tagged.tag_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tagged.ticket_id) AS ticket_count,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tagged.first_response_at - tagged.created_at)) / 60.0)
      FILTER (WHERE tagged.first_response_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tagged.resolved_at - tagged.created_at)) / 60.0)
      FILTER (WHERE tagged.resolved_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tagged.ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE bpt.fr_breach) AS fr_breach_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tagged.ticket_id) FILTER (WHERE bpt.res_breach) AS res_breach_count
  FROM tagged
  LEFT JOIN breaches_per_ticket bpt ON bpt.ticket_id = tagged.ticket_id
  GROUP BY tagged.tag_name
),
totals AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets_2025) AS total_tickets_2025,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ttm.ticket_id)
       FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
       JOIN tickets_2025 t ON t.id = ttm.ticket_id) AS total_tagged_tickets_2025
)
SELECT
  tag_stats.tag_name,
  tag_stats.ticket_count,
  ROUND(tag_stats.avg_first_response_minutes, 1) AS avg_first_response_minutes,
  ROUND(tag_stats.avg_resolution_minutes, 1) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(tag_stats.fr_breach_count::numeric / NULLIF(tag_stats.ticket_count, 0), 4) AS first_response_breach_rate,
  ROUND(tag_stats.res_breach_count::numeric / NULLIF(tag_stats.ticket_count, 0), 4) AS resolution_breach_rate,
  totals.total_tagged_tickets_2025,
  totals.total_tickets_2025
FROM tag_stats
CROSS JOIN totals
ORDER BY tag_stats.ticket_count DESC, tag_stats.tag_name ASC
LIMIT 20
builds_on: Ticket speed by channel and assignment status
entries.engineer_note: Tags are matched by name across all tenants (support_tags is tenant-scoped, but the report grain is topic/tag name, not merchant), so a tag name used by several merchants is combined into one row. Breach rates are breached-ticket-count ÷ ticket_count for that tag (not restricted to tickets that actually had an SLA policy assigned), and avg response/resolution minutes only average over tickets that have a non-null first_response_at/resolved_at respectively. total_tagged_tickets_2025 and total_tickets_2025 are constants repeated on every row for easy comparison; the report doesn't separately list the total distinct-tag count, which would need its own single-value report if wanted.

entries.title: CSAT score by resolution speed bucket
entries.question: Does customer satisfaction after a resolved ticket track with how fast it was resolved and whether it breached SLA, or does something else seem to drive it?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  bucket AS resolution_time_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(AVG(score), 2) AS avg_csat_score,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN breached THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_resolution_sla_breached,
  ROUND(AVG(resolution_minutes)) AS avg_resolution_minutes
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.id AS ticket_id,
    c.score AS score,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 60.0 AS resolution_minutes,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM sla_breaches sb
      WHERE sb.ticket_id = t.id AND sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
    ) AS breached,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 4 THEN 'Under 4h'
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 24 THEN '4-24h'
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 72 THEN '1-3 days'
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.resolved_at - t.created_at)) / 3600.0 < 168 THEN '3-7 days'
      ELSE 'Over 7 days'
    END AS bucket
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN csat_responses c ON c.ticket_id = t.id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND t.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
) x
GROUP BY bucket
ORDER BY
  CASE bucket
    WHEN 'Under 4h' THEN 1
    WHEN '4-24h' THEN 2
    WHEN '1-3 days' THEN 3
    WHEN '3-7 days' THEN 4
    ELSE 5
  END
builds_on: SLA breach_kind code audit and validation
entries.engineer_note: Resolution time is computed as resolved_at - created_at across all tenants combined (no currency conversion needed since there's no money here); SLA breach share uses an EXISTS check against sla_breaches for breach_kind='resolution'. 5 bucket rows total, well within the 50-row limit.

entries.title: 2025 payout fee revenue and volume by currency
entries.question: Does our 2025 fee-revenue total hold up when broken down by currency, and which currencies carry our FX exposure?
entries.sql:
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT
    p.currency_code,
    COUNT(*) AS payout_count,
    SUM(p.gross_amount) AS total_gross_native,
    SUM(p.fee_amount) AS total_fee_native,
    SUM(p.gross_amount / er.rate) AS total_gross_eur,
    SUM(p.fee_amount / er.rate) AS total_fee_eur
  FROM payouts p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = date(p.paid_at)
  WHERE p.status = 'paid'
    AND p.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.currency_code
)
SELECT
  currency_code,
  payout_count,
  ROUND(total_gross_native, 2) AS total_gross_native,
  ROUND(total_fee_native, 2) AS total_fee_native,
  ROUND(total_gross_eur, 2) AS total_gross_eur,
  ROUND(total_fee_eur, 2) AS total_fee_eur,
  ROUND(total_fee_native / NULLIF(total_fee_eur,0), 4) AS implied_avg_rate_native_per_eur,
  ROUND(100 * total_fee_eur / SUM(total_fee_eur) OVER (), 2) AS share_of_total_fee_eur_pct
FROM agg
ORDER BY total_fee_eur DESC, currency_code ASC
builds_on: Payout status & date-field reconciliation
Revenue by vertical, trailing 12 months (corrected)
entries.engineer_note: Aggregated payouts (status='paid', paid_at in 2025) per currency before converting, joining exchange_rates 1:1 by (EUR, currency, as_of=date(paid_at)) — no fan-out joins, matching the validated methodology. The sum of total_fee_eur across all rows in this report is the comparable figure to Finance's €93,583; if it reconciles to ~€53,186 as before, nothing has changed, otherwise please flag back to us since the batch run will show the actual totals (dry runs can't read data).

entries.title: Merchant refund-rate spike check, Q4 2025 vs 2025 baseline
entries.question: Is the Q4 2025 refund-rate increase concentrated in a handful of merchants, or spread broadly across the merchant base?
entries.sql:
WITH t1 AS (
  SELECT
    t10.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(t10.amount / t11.rate) AS captured_eur_q4,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t10.order_id) AS order_count_q4
  FROM payments AS t10
  JOIN exchange_rates AS t11
    ON t11.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t11.quote_code = t10.currency_code
   AND t11.as_of = CAST(t10.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE t10.status IN ('captured', 'partially_refunded', 'refunded')
    AND t10.captured_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND t10.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t10.tenant_id
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    t20.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(t20.amount / t21.rate) AS captured_eur_baseline
  FROM payments AS t20
  JOIN exchange_rates AS t21
    ON t21.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t21.quote_code = t20.currency_code
   AND t21.as_of = CAST(t20.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE t20.status IN ('captured', 'partially_refunded', 'refunded')
    AND t20.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t20.captured_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY t20.tenant_id
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    t30.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(t30.amount / t31.rate) AS refund_eur_q4
  FROM payment_refunds AS t30
  JOIN exchange_rates AS t31
    ON t31.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t31.quote_code = t30.currency_code
   AND t31.as_of = CAST(t30.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE t30.status = 'succeeded'
    AND t30.processed_at >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND t30.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t30.tenant_id
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT
    t40.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(t40.amount / t41.rate) AS refund_eur_baseline
  FROM payment_refunds AS t40
  JOIN exchange_rates AS t41
    ON t41.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t41.quote_code = t40.currency_code
   AND t41.as_of = CAST(t40.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE t40.status = 'succeeded'
    AND t40.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t40.processed_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY t40.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t0.name AS merchant_name,
  t0.industry AS vertical,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t3.refund_eur_q4, 0) / NULLIF(t1.captured_eur_q4, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_q4_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t4.refund_eur_baseline, 0) / NULLIF(t2.captured_eur_baseline, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_baseline_pct,
  ROUND(
    (100.0 * COALESCE(t3.refund_eur_q4, 0) / NULLIF(t1.captured_eur_q4, 0))
    - (100.0 * COALESCE(t4.refund_eur_baseline, 0) / NULLIF(t2.captured_eur_baseline, 0))
  , 2) AS change_vs_baseline_pp,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t3.refund_eur_q4, 0), 2) AS refund_amount_q4_eur,
  t1.order_count_q4 AS order_count_q4
FROM tenants AS t0
JOIN t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN t4 ON t4.tenant_id = t0.id
WHERE t1.order_count_q4 >= 10
ORDER BY change_vs_baseline_pp DESC NULLS LAST, refund_amount_q4_eur DESC, t0.id ASC
entries.engineer_note: Used payments.tenant_id / payment_refunds.tenant_id directly (both carry tenant_id natively, no need to route through orders). Merchants with no captured volume in the Q1-Q3 baseline window show a blank baseline rate and change (division by zero avoided via NULLIF), sorted last. Order count = distinct orders with a qualifying captured payment in Q4 2025.

entries.title: Merchant risk signals snapshot: receivables, traffic and revenue trend
entries.question: Which merchants look at risk right now, based on unpaid invoices, traffic decline, and revenue trend — our 'accounts to watch' list?
entries.sql:
with latest_rates as (
  select distinct on (quote_code) quote_code, rate
  from exchange_rates
  where base_code = 'EUR' and as_of <= DATE '2025-12-31'
  order by quote_code, as_of desc
),
unpaid as (
  select i.tenant_id,
    sum(i.amount_due / case when i.currency_code = 'EUR' then 1 else lr.rate end) as unpaid_eur
  from invoices i
  left join latest_rates lr on lr.quote_code = i.currency_code
  where i.status in ('open','past_due')
  group by i.tenant_id
),
traffic as (
  select tenant_id,
    count(*) filter (where started_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01' and started_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01') as q3_sessions,
    count(*) filter (where started_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01' and started_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01') as q4_sessions
  from web_sessions
  group by tenant_id
),
payout_rates as (
  select p.id as payout_id, p.tenant_id, p.paid_at,
    p.fee_amount / case when p.currency_code = 'EUR' then 1 else er.rate end as fee_eur
  from payouts p
  left join exchange_rates er
    on er.base_code = 'EUR' and er.quote_code = p.currency_code and er.as_of = CAST(p.paid_at AS DATE)
  where p.status = 'paid'
),
revenue as (
  select tenant_id,
    sum(fee_eur) filter (where paid_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-07-01' and paid_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01') as q3_fee,
    sum(fee_eur) filter (where paid_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01' and paid_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01') as q4_fee
  from payout_rates
  group by tenant_id
),
last_order as (
  select tenant_id, max(placed_at) as last_placed_at
  from orders
  group by tenant_id
)
select
  t.name as merchant_name,
  t.industry as vertical,
  round(coalesce(u.unpaid_eur, 0), 2) as unpaid_invoice_balance_eur,
  round(case when tr.q3_sessions is null or tr.q3_sessions = 0 then null
             else 100.0 * (tr.q4_sessions - tr.q3_sessions) / tr.q3_sessions end, 1) as traffic_change_pct_q4_vs_q3,
  round(case when r.q3_fee is null or r.q3_fee = 0 then null
             else 100.0 * (r.q4_fee - r.q3_fee) / r.q3_fee end, 1) as fee_revenue_change_pct_q4_vs_q3,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lo.last_placed_at AS DATE)) as days_since_last_order,
  t.status as tenant_status
from tenants t
left join unpaid u on u.tenant_id = t.id
left join traffic tr on tr.tenant_id = t.id
left join revenue r on r.tenant_id = t.id
left join last_order lo on lo.tenant_id = t.id
where t.deleted_at is null
order by unpaid_invoice_balance_eur desc nulls last, traffic_change_pct_q4_vs_q3 asc nulls last, merchant_name
limit 50
entries.engineer_note: Used tenants.industry as "vertical" (no separate vertical field exists). Invoice balances use the latest EUR exchange rate on/before 2025-12-31 (a single snapshot rate per currency, as specified); payout fees are converted using each payout's own paid_at-date rate since the request implied a period trend rather than a point-in-time valuation. The requested "total merchant count with any non-zero unpaid balance or traffic/revenue decline" is a different, single-number aggregate outside this report's per-merchant grain and the 50-row cap, so it isn't included here — happy to run it as a separate one-row report if useful.

entries.title: Merchant refund-rate spike check, Q3 2025 vs H1 2025 baseline
entries.question: Does the refund spike Finance flagged for Q3 2025 (naming OfficeHub Nordic and Sports & Outdoor sellers) hold up at the merchant level, and is it the same story as Q4?
entries.sql:
WITH q3_refunds AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id,
         SUM(pr.amount / er.rate) AS refund_amount_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = pr.processed_at::date
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-07-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY pr.tenant_id
),
q3_payments AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         SUM(p.amount / er.rate) AS captured_amount_eur
  FROM payments p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = p.captured_at::date
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured','partially_refunded','refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-07-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
h1_refunds AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id,
         SUM(pr.amount / er.rate) AS refund_amount_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = pr.processed_at::date
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY pr.tenant_id
),
h1_payments AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         SUM(p.amount / er.rate) AS captured_amount_eur
  FROM payments p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = p.captured_at::date
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured','partially_refunded','refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2025-07-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
q3_orders AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-07-01'
    AND placed_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry AS vertical,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(qr.refund_amount_eur,0) / NULLIF(qp.captured_amount_eur,0), 2) AS refund_rate_q3_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(hr.refund_amount_eur,0) / NULLIF(hp.captured_amount_eur,0), 2) AS refund_rate_h1_baseline_pct,
  ROUND(
    (100.0 * COALESCE(qr.refund_amount_eur,0) / NULLIF(qp.captured_amount_eur,0))
    - (100.0 * COALESCE(hr.refund_amount_eur,0) / NULLIF(hp.captured_amount_eur,0))
  , 2) AS change_vs_baseline_pp,
  ROUND(COALESCE(qr.refund_amount_eur,0), 2) AS refund_amount_q3_eur,
  qo.order_count AS order_count_q3
FROM q3_orders qo
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = qo.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN q3_refunds qr ON qr.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN q3_payments qp ON qp.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN h1_refunds hr ON hr.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN h1_payments hp ON hp.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
WHERE qo.order_count >= 10
ORDER BY change_vs_baseline_pp DESC NULLS LAST, refund_amount_q3_eur DESC, merchant_name ASC
builds_on: Merchant refund-rate spike check, Q4 2025 vs 2025 baseline
entries.engineer_note: Vertical is taken from tenants.industry (closest match to "vertical" in the catalog). Order count is the count of orders with placed_at in Q3 2025, used both as the >=10 filter and the reported column; merchants with zero Q3 captured-payment volume show a null refund rate/change rather than divide-by-zero.

entries.title: Receivables aging: who owes us and for how long
entries.question: Which merchants are slowest to pay their invoices, how large and how overdue are the balances, and is this concentrated in B2B wholesale?
entries.sql:
SELECT t0.name AS merchant_name,
       COALESCE(t0.industry, 'Unknown') AS vertical,
       ROUND(COALESCE(m1.total_unpaid_eur,0),2) AS total_unpaid_balance_eur,
       COALESCE(m2.open_invoice_count,0) AS open_invoice_count,
       COALESCE(m3.days_overdue_oldest,0) AS days_overdue_oldest,
       ROUND(COALESCE(m4.largest_unpaid_eur,0),2) AS largest_unpaid_invoice_eur,
       m5.net_terms_days AS net_terms_days
FROM tenants t0
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT i0.tenant_id,
           SUM(i0.amount_due / CASE WHEN i0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx0.rate END) AS total_unpaid_eur
    FROM invoices i0
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT er0.quote_code AS currency_code, er0.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er0
        WHERE er0.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er0.as_of = (
              SELECT MAX(er1.as_of)
              FROM exchange_rates er1
              WHERE er1.base_code = 'EUR'
                AND er1.quote_code = er0.quote_code
                AND er1.as_of <= DATE '2025-12-31'
          )
    ) fx0 ON fx0.currency_code = i0.currency_code
    WHERE i0.status IN ('open','past_due') AND i0.amount_due > 0
    GROUP BY i0.tenant_id
) m1 ON m1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT i2.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS open_invoice_count
    FROM invoices i2
    WHERE i2.status IN ('open','past_due') AND i2.amount_due > 0
    GROUP BY i2.tenant_id
) m2 ON m2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT i3.tenant_id,
           GREATEST(0, CAST(DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(i3.due_at) AS DATE) AS INTEGER)) AS days_overdue_oldest
    FROM invoices i3
    WHERE i3.status IN ('open','past_due') AND i3.amount_due > 0
    GROUP BY i3.tenant_id
) m3 ON m3.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT i4.tenant_id,
           MAX(i4.amount_due / CASE WHEN i4.currency_code='EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx4.rate END) AS largest_unpaid_eur
    FROM invoices i4
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT er2.quote_code AS currency_code, er2.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er2
        WHERE er2.base_code='EUR'
          AND er2.as_of = (
              SELECT MAX(er3.as_of) FROM exchange_rates er3
              WHERE er3.base_code='EUR' AND er3.quote_code=er2.quote_code AND er3.as_of <= DATE '2025-12-31'
          )
    ) fx4 ON fx4.currency_code = i4.currency_code
    WHERE i4.status IN ('open','past_due') AND i4.amount_due > 0
    GROUP BY i4.tenant_id
) m4 ON m4.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT bp0.tenant_id, MAX(bp0.net_terms_days) AS net_terms_days
    FROM billing_profiles bp0
    WHERE bp0.is_default = true AND bp0.deleted_at IS NULL
    GROUP BY bp0.tenant_id
) m5 ON m5.tenant_id = t0.id
WHERE COALESCE(m1.total_unpaid_eur,0) <> 0
ORDER BY total_unpaid_balance_eur DESC, days_overdue_oldest DESC, t0.id ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Merchant risk signals snapshot: receivables, traffic and revenue trend
entries.engineer_note: EUR conversion uses the EUR-base exchange_rates row whose as_of date is the latest on/before 2025-12-31 for each currency (a single snapshot rate per currency, not a per-invoice historical rate). Net terms are taken from each tenant's default, non-deleted billing_profiles row; if a tenant somehow has more than one default profile the highest net_terms_days is shown. Report returns up to 50 merchants ranked by unpaid balance; the printed report will show the true total row count.

entries.title: Cost-driver volume inventory by merchant, 2025
entries.question: What operational cost-driver volumes do we actually have per merchant today, to serve as the measurable building blocks for a cost-to-serve model?
entries.sql:
WITH shipment_costs AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
         COUNT(*) AS shipment_count,
         SUM(s.shipping_cost / er.rate) AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
returns_counts AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS return_count
  FROM order_returns r
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = r.order_id
  WHERE r.requested_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND r.requested_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),
refund_amounts AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id,
         SUM(pr.amount / er.rate) AS refund_amount_eur
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY pr.tenant_id
),
ticket_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
failed_webhooks AS (
  SELECT w.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS failed_webhook_count
  FROM webhook_deliveries wd
  JOIN webhooks w ON w.id = wd.webhook_id
  WHERE wd.status = 'failed'
    AND wd.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND wd.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY w.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry AS vertical,
  COALESCE(sc.shipment_count, 0) AS shipment_count_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(sc.shipping_cost_eur, 0), 2) AS total_shipping_cost_eur_2025,
  COALESCE(rc.return_count, 0) AS return_count_2025,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ra.refund_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS refund_amount_eur_2025,
  COALESCE(tc.ticket_count, 0) AS ticket_count_2025,
  COALESCE(fw.failed_webhook_count, 0) AS failed_webhook_count_2025
FROM tenants t
LEFT JOIN shipment_costs sc ON sc.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN returns_counts rc ON rc.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN refund_amounts ra ON ra.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN ticket_counts tc ON tc.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN failed_webhooks fw ON fw.tenant_id = t.id
ORDER BY total_shipping_cost_eur_2025 DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Ordered by total shipping cost EUR descending (not merchant name) per your fallback instruction, to keep ordering deterministic without a secondary sort key conflicting with the requested limit; printed rows are capped at 50 but the query includes every tenant (all ~120 merchants) before the LIMIT, so if fewer than 50 tenants exist all are shown. Used tenants.industry as the "vertical" column since that is the closest attribute in the schema.

entries.title: Platform billing risk: merchants past_due, suspended or churned
entries.question: Which merchants are currently behind on paying us or already cut off, and how big/active are they — our clearest churn-risk signal?
entries.sql:
WITH tenant_base AS (
  SELECT t.id AS tenant_id, t.name AS merchant_name, t.industry AS vertical, t.status AS tenant_status, t.created_at
  FROM tenants t
  WHERE t.status IN ('past_due','suspended','churned') AND t.deleted_at IS NULL
),
last_order AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, MAX(placed_at) AS last_order_at
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
last_paid_payout AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, MAX(paid_at) AS last_paid_payout_at
  FROM payouts
  WHERE status = 'paid'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
fee_revenue_ttm AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN p.fee_amount ELSE p.fee_amount / er.rate END) AS fee_revenue_eur
  FROM payouts p
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(p.paid_at AS date)
  WHERE p.status = 'paid'
    AND p.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tb.merchant_name,
  tb.vertical,
  tb.tenant_status,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(tb.created_at AS date)) AS tenure_days,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lo.last_order_at AS date)) AS days_since_last_order,
  (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lp.last_paid_payout_at AS date)) AS days_since_last_paid_payout,
  ROUND(COALESCE(fr.fee_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS fee_revenue_ttm_eur
FROM tenant_base tb
LEFT JOIN last_order lo ON lo.tenant_id = tb.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN last_paid_payout lp ON lp.tenant_id = tb.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN fee_revenue_ttm fr ON fr.tenant_id = tb.tenant_id
ORDER BY
  CASE tb.tenant_status WHEN 'churned' THEN 1 WHEN 'suspended' THEN 2 WHEN 'past_due' THEN 3 END,
  fee_revenue_ttm_eur DESC,
  tb.merchant_name ASC
builds_on: Merchant status and payout activity, today
Receivables aging: who owes us and for how long
entries.engineer_note: Fee revenue is converted to EUR by dividing payout fee_amount by the EUR→currency exchange_rates.rate on the paid_at date (treated as 1:1 when currency_code is already EUR); recency/tenure columns are day counts as of 2026-01-05, null where a merchant has no orders or no paid payouts.

entries.title: Deskline Supplies shipping cost breakdown by carrier
entries.question: Is Deskline Supplies' unusually high average shipping cost (~€1,038/shipment vs. ~€4-30/shipment for comparable merchants) a real freight-cost pattern or a data outlier?
entries.sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT t1.id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants t1
  WHERE t1.name = 'Deskline Supplies'
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    s.carrier AS carrier,
    s.service_level AS service_level,
    s.shipping_cost AS shipping_cost,
    COALESCE(s.currency_code, tn.default_currency_code) AS ship_currency_code,
    s.shipped_at AS shipped_at
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  JOIN t0 ON t0.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
  JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = s.tenant_id
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT
    t2.carrier AS carrier,
    t2.service_level AS service_level,
    t2.shipping_cost AS shipping_cost,
    CASE
      WHEN t2.ship_currency_code = 'EUR' THEN t2.shipping_cost
      ELSE t2.shipping_cost / er.rate
    END AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM t2
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = t2.ship_currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(t2.shipped_at AS date)
)
SELECT
  t3.carrier AS carrier,
  t3.service_level AS service_level,
  COUNT(*) AS shipment_count_2025,
  ROUND(SUM(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS total_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS avg_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(MIN(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS min_shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(MAX(t3.shipping_cost_eur), 2) AS max_shipping_cost_eur
FROM t3
GROUP BY t3.carrier, t3.service_level
ORDER BY total_shipping_cost_eur DESC, t3.carrier ASC, t3.service_level ASC
builds_on: Cost-driver volume inventory by merchant, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Shipments joined via fulfillments->orders to filter to Deskline Supplies' tenant_id, limited to shipped_at in 2025, with shipping_cost converted to EUR using exchange_rates (EUR base, shipment's own currency_code, falling back to the tenant's default currency if the shipment row has none) at the as_of date matching shipped_at's calendar day. Min/max per carrier+service_level lane should make it easy to spot whether the high average is driven by a few outlier shipments or a broad pattern.

entries.title: Directional unit economics by vertical, 2025 (first pass)
entries.question: Using only the revenue and cost signals we currently trust, which verticals look directionally profitable to grow versus costly to serve?
entries.sql:
WITH t_industry AS (
  SELECT
    t0.id AS tenant_id,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(t0.industry), ''), 'Unspecified') AS vertical
  FROM tenants t0
),
d_vertical AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ti0.vertical AS vertical
  FROM t_industry ti0
),
m_merchants AS (
  SELECT
    ti1.vertical AS vertical,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ti1.tenant_id) AS merchant_count
  FROM t_industry ti1
  GROUP BY ti1.vertical
),
m_fee AS (
  SELECT
    ti2.vertical AS vertical,
    SUM(p0.fee_amount / COALESCE(er0.rate, CASE WHEN p0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0 END)) AS fee_revenue_eur
  FROM payouts p0
  JOIN t_industry ti2 ON ti2.tenant_id = p0.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er0.quote_code = p0.currency_code
    AND er0.as_of = CAST(p0.paid_at AS date)
  WHERE p0.status = 'paid'
    AND p0.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p0.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti2.vertical
),
m_shipping AS (
  SELECT
    ti3.vertical AS vertical,
    SUM(s0.shipping_cost / COALESCE(er1.rate, CASE WHEN s0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0 END)) AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM shipments s0
  JOIN t_industry ti3 ON ti3.tenant_id = s0.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er1.quote_code = s0.currency_code
    AND er1.as_of = CAST(s0.shipped_at AS date)
  WHERE s0.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s0.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND s0.shipping_cost IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ti3.vertical
),
m_refund AS (
  SELECT
    ti4.vertical AS vertical,
    SUM(r0.refund_total / COALESCE(er2.rate, CASE WHEN r0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0 END)) AS refund_amount_eur
  FROM order_returns r0
  JOIN t_industry ti4 ON ti4.tenant_id = r0.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er2.quote_code = r0.currency_code
    AND er2.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(r0.refunded_at, r0.requested_at) AS date)
  WHERE r0.status = 'refunded'
    AND COALESCE(r0.refunded_at, r0.requested_at) >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND COALESCE(r0.refunded_at, r0.requested_at) < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti4.vertical
),
m_tickets AS (
  SELECT
    ti5.vertical AS vertical,
    COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
  FROM tickets tk0
  JOIN t_industry ti5 ON ti5.tenant_id = tk0.tenant_id
  WHERE tk0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND tk0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti5.vertical
)
SELECT
  d0.vertical AS vertical,
  COALESCE(mm0.merchant_count, 0) AS merchant_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mf0.fee_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS fee_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(ms0.shipping_cost_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mr0.refund_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS refund_amount_eur,
  COALESCE(mt0.ticket_count, 0) AS support_ticket_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mf0.fee_revenue_eur, 0) - COALESCE(ms0.shipping_cost_eur, 0) - COALESCE(mr0.refund_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS rough_net_contribution_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(mf0.fee_revenue_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE 100.0 * (COALESCE(mf0.fee_revenue_eur, 0) - COALESCE(ms0.shipping_cost_eur, 0) - COALESCE(mr0.refund_amount_eur, 0)) / mf0.fee_revenue_eur
    END, 1
  ) AS net_contribution_pct_of_fee_revenue
FROM d_vertical d0
LEFT JOIN m_merchants mm0 ON mm0.vertical = d0.vertical
LEFT JOIN m_fee mf0 ON mf0.vertical = d0.vertical
LEFT JOIN m_shipping ms0 ON ms0.vertical = d0.vertical
LEFT JOIN m_refund mr0 ON mr0.vertical = d0.vertical
LEFT JOIN m_tickets mt0 ON mt0.vertical = d0.vertical
ORDER BY rough_net_contribution_eur DESC, d0.vertical ASC
builds_on: Revenue by vertical, trailing 12 months (corrected)
Cost-driver volume inventory by merchant, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Refund amount is sourced from order_returns.refund_total (status='refunded', dated by refunded_at, falling back to requested_at) since the schema has no direct FK linking payment_refunds to order_returns — this is the closest EUR-denominated, return-linked refund signal available. As requested, rough net contribution excludes support cost, carrier penalties, engineering cost and platform-plan revenue; it is directional only.

entries.title: Vertical unit economics, rate-based view, 2025
entries.question: Which verticals look efficient versus costly to serve, measured as comparable rates against gross payment volume rather than misleading absolute euros against our thin fee take?
entries.sql:
WITH tenant_industry AS (
    SELECT
        id AS tenant_id,
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(industry), ''), 'Unspecified') AS vertical
    FROM tenants
),

payout_totals AS (
    SELECT
        p.tenant_id,
        SUM(p.gross_amount / er.rate) AS gross_eur,
        SUM(p.fee_amount / er.rate) AS fee_eur
    FROM payouts p
    JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(p.paid_at AS date)
    WHERE p.status = 'paid'
        AND p.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND p.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),

refund_totals AS (
    SELECT
        r.tenant_id,
        SUM(r.refund_total / er.rate) AS refund_eur
    FROM order_returns r
    JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = r.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(r.refunded_at, r.requested_at) AS date)
    WHERE r.status = 'refunded'
        AND COALESCE(r.refunded_at, r.requested_at) >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND COALESCE(r.refunded_at, r.requested_at) < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY r.tenant_id
),

shipping_totals AS (
    SELECT
        o.tenant_id,
        SUM(s.shipping_cost / er.rate) AS shipping_eur
    FROM shipments s
    JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
    JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
    JOIN exchange_rates er
        ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)
    WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
        AND s.shipping_cost IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY o.tenant_id
),

order_counts AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM orders
    WHERE status IN ('paid', 'partially_fulfilled', 'fulfilled', 'refunded')
        AND placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
),

ticket_counts AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
),

merchant_counts AS (
    SELECT
        vertical,
        COUNT(*) AS merchant_count
    FROM tenant_industry
    GROUP BY vertical
),

tenant_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        ti.tenant_id,
        ti.vertical,
        COALESCE(pt.gross_eur, 0) AS gross_eur,
        COALESCE(pt.fee_eur, 0) AS fee_eur,
        COALESCE(rt.refund_eur, 0) AS refund_eur,
        COALESCE(st.shipping_eur, 0) AS shipping_eur,
        COALESCE(oc.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
        COALESCE(tc.ticket_count, 0) AS ticket_count
    FROM tenant_industry ti
    LEFT JOIN payout_totals pt ON pt.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN refund_totals rt ON rt.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN shipping_totals st ON st.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN order_counts oc ON oc.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
    LEFT JOIN ticket_counts tc ON tc.tenant_id = ti.tenant_id
),

vertical_agg AS (
    SELECT
        vertical,
        SUM(gross_eur) AS gross_eur,
        SUM(fee_eur) AS fee_eur,
        SUM(refund_eur) AS refund_eur,
        SUM(shipping_eur) AS shipping_eur,
        SUM(order_count) AS order_count,
        SUM(ticket_count) AS ticket_count
    FROM tenant_metrics
    GROUP BY vertical
)

SELECT
    va.vertical AS vertical,
    mc.merchant_count AS merchant_count,
    ROUND(va.gross_eur, 2) AS gross_payment_volume_eur,
    ROUND(va.fee_eur, 2) AS fee_revenue_eur,
    ROUND(CASE WHEN va.gross_eur = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 100.0 * va.fee_eur / va.gross_eur END, 2) AS take_rate_pct,
    ROUND(CASE WHEN va.gross_eur = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 100.0 * va.refund_eur / va.gross_eur END, 2) AS refund_rate_pct,
    ROUND(CASE WHEN va.gross_eur = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 100.0 * va.shipping_eur / va.gross_eur END, 2) AS shipping_cost_rate_pct,
    va.order_count AS order_count_2025,
    ROUND(CASE WHEN va.order_count = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 100.0 * va.ticket_count / va.order_count END, 2) AS tickets_per_100_orders
FROM vertical_agg va
JOIN merchant_counts mc ON mc.vertical = va.vertical
ORDER BY va.gross_eur DESC, va.vertical ASC
builds_on: Directional unit economics by vertical, 2025 (first pass)
Revenue by vertical, trailing 12 months (corrected)
entries.engineer_note: Merchant count reflects all tenants in each industry (not just those with 2025 payout activity), since the request asked for a vertical-level merchant count rather than an "active in 2025" count; tenants with no matching payouts/returns/shipments/orders/tickets in 2025 contribute zeros to the sums. Industry is grouped as 'Unspecified' when null or blank.

entries.title: Merchant unit economics, rate-based view: top 20 by volume, 2025
entries.question: Among our largest merchants, which look efficient versus costly to serve on a like-for-like rate basis?
entries.sql:
WITH payout_eur AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         SUM(p.gross_amount / er.rate) AS gross_eur,
         SUM(p.fee_amount / er.rate) AS fee_eur
  FROM payouts p
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code AND er.as_of = p.paid_at::date
  WHERE p.paid_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND p.paid_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
returns_eur AS (
  SELECT r.tenant_id,
         SUM(r.refund_total / er.rate) AS refund_eur
  FROM order_returns r
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = r.currency_code AND er.as_of = r.requested_at::date
  WHERE r.requested_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND r.requested_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY r.tenant_id
),
shipping_eur AS (
  SELECT s.tenant_id,
         SUM(s.shipping_cost / er.rate) AS shipping_eur
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code AND er.as_of = s.shipped_at::date
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01' AND s.shipping_cost IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY s.tenant_id
),
orders_cnt AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS orders_2025
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
tickets_cnt AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS tickets_2025
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT t.name AS merchant_name,
       t.industry AS vertical,
       ROUND(pe.gross_eur, 2) AS gross_payment_volume_eur,
       ROUND(pe.fee_eur, 2) AS fee_revenue_eur,
       ROUND(100 * pe.fee_eur / NULLIF(pe.gross_eur, 0), 2) AS take_rate_pct,
       ROUND(100 * COALESCE(re.refund_eur, 0) / NULLIF(pe.gross_eur, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_pct,
       ROUND(100 * COALESCE(se.shipping_eur, 0) / NULLIF(pe.gross_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_cost_rate_pct,
       ROUND(100 * COALESCE(tc.tickets_2025, 0) / NULLIF(oc.orders_2025, 0)::numeric, 2) AS tickets_per_100_orders
FROM payout_eur pe
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = pe.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN returns_eur re ON re.tenant_id = pe.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN shipping_eur se ON se.tenant_id = pe.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN orders_cnt oc ON oc.tenant_id = pe.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN tickets_cnt tc ON tc.tenant_id = pe.tenant_id
ORDER BY pe.gross_eur DESC, t.name
LIMIT 20
builds_on: Vertical unit economics, rate-based view, 2025
Merchant revenue concentration, trailing 12 months
entries.engineer_note: Methodology: gross volume/fee revenue from payouts.gross_amount/fee_amount (paid_at in 2025); refund rate from order_returns.refund_total (requested_at in 2025); shipping cost rate from shipments.shipping_cost (shipped_at in 2025); tickets per 100 orders uses tickets.created_at and orders.placed_at in 2025. All amounts converted to EUR via the daily EUR exchange rate on the respective transaction date. I did not have the exact prior vertical-level report to copy definitions from verbatim, so these are my best-match, like-for-like rate definitions against gross volume - flag if they differ from tonight's vertical report.

entries.title: Shipping cost recovery: customer-paid shipping vs. carrier cost, by vertical, 2025
entries.question: Is shipping actually a net cost exposure, or does what we collect from customers for shipping roughly cover what we pay carriers?
entries.sql:
WITH order_rev AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(NULLIF(t.industry, ''), 'Unspecified') AS vertical,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(o.shipping_total / er.rate) AS shipping_revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'partially_fulfilled', 'fulfilled', 'refunded')
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1
),
ship_cost AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(NULLIF(t.industry, ''), 'Unspecified') AS vertical,
    SUM(s.shipping_cost / er.rate) AS shipping_cost_eur
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = s.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)
  WHERE s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(r.vertical, c.vertical) AS vertical,
  COALESCE(r.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.shipping_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(c.shipping_cost_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_cost_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.shipping_revenue_eur, 0) - COALESCE(c.shipping_cost_eur, 0), 2) AS shipping_margin_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(r.shipping_revenue_eur, 0) <> 0
      THEN (COALESCE(r.shipping_revenue_eur, 0) - COALESCE(c.shipping_cost_eur, 0)) / r.shipping_revenue_eur * 100
      ELSE NULL
    END, 1
  ) AS shipping_margin_pct
FROM order_rev r
FULL OUTER JOIN ship_cost c ON r.vertical = c.vertical
ORDER BY shipping_margin_eur ASC, vertical ASC
builds_on: Cost-driver volume inventory by merchant, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Revenue side (orders) and cost side (shipments) are aggregated independently by vertical before joining, since they sit at different grains and a direct join would fan out; order_count reflects the orders-side filter only (shipments with no matching orders rows, if any, would show as a cost-only row with order_count 0). Orders/shipments missing a currency match in exchange_rates for their date would be silently excluded from that side's sum.

entries.title: Audit Sample: End-to-End Transaction Walkthrough, 2025
entries.question: For a representative sample of 2025 transactions, does the shopper payment amount, any refund, the resulting merchant payout (gross/fee/net), and the linked ledger entries all tie out consistently?
entries.sql:
WITH base_payments AS (
  SELECT
    p.id AS payment_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.order_id,
    p.currency_code,
    p.amount AS payment_amount,
    p.amount_refunded,
    p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND p.order_id IS NOT NULL
),
fx_rates AS (
  SELECT quote_code, as_of, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR'
),
payments_with_eur AS (
  SELECT
    bp.*,
    CASE WHEN bp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN bp.payment_amount
         ELSE bp.payment_amount / fx.rate END AS payment_amount_eur
  FROM base_payments bp
  LEFT JOIN fx_rates fx
    ON fx.quote_code = bp.currency_code
   AND fx.as_of = CAST(bp.captured_at AS date)
),
payout_agg AS (
  SELECT payment_id, amount AS payout_item_amount, fee_amount AS payout_item_fee_amount
  FROM payout_items
),
ledger_agg AS (
  SELECT
    payment_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'debit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS ledger_debit_total,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'credit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS ledger_credit_total
  FROM ledger_entries
  WHERE payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY payment_id
),
enriched AS (
  SELECT
    pwe.payment_id,
    pwe.tenant_id,
    pwe.order_id,
    pwe.currency_code,
    pwe.payment_amount,
    pwe.amount_refunded,
    pwe.payment_amount_eur,
    pa.payout_item_amount,
    pa.payout_item_fee_amount,
    la.ledger_debit_total,
    la.ledger_credit_total
  FROM payments_with_eur pwe
  LEFT JOIN payout_agg pa ON pa.payment_id = pwe.payment_id
  LEFT JOIN ledger_agg la ON la.payment_id = pwe.payment_id
),
tenant_top_payment AS (
  SELECT e.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.tenant_id ORDER BY e.payment_amount_eur DESC) AS tenant_rn
  FROM enriched e
),
largest_sample AS (
  SELECT
    payment_id, tenant_id, order_id, currency_code, payment_amount, amount_refunded,
    payment_amount_eur, payout_item_amount, payout_item_fee_amount,
    ledger_debit_total, ledger_credit_total, 'A_LARGEST' AS sample_category
  FROM tenant_top_payment
  WHERE tenant_rn = 1
  ORDER BY payment_amount_eur DESC
  LIMIT 8
),
refund_candidates AS (
  SELECT
    e.*,
    CASE WHEN e.amount_refunded = e.payment_amount THEN 'FULL' ELSE 'PARTIAL' END AS refund_kind
  FROM enriched e
  WHERE e.amount_refunded > 0
),
refund_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    rc.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rc.tenant_id, rc.refund_kind ORDER BY rc.amount_refunded DESC) AS tenant_refund_rn
  FROM refund_candidates rc
),
refund_sample AS (
  (SELECT payment_id, tenant_id, order_id, currency_code, payment_amount, amount_refunded,
          payment_amount_eur, payout_item_amount, payout_item_fee_amount,
          ledger_debit_total, ledger_credit_total, 'B_REFUND' AS sample_category
   FROM refund_ranked WHERE refund_kind = 'FULL' AND tenant_refund_rn = 1
   ORDER BY amount_refunded DESC LIMIT 4)
  UNION ALL
  (SELECT payment_id, tenant_id, order_id, currency_code, payment_amount, amount_refunded,
          payment_amount_eur, payout_item_amount, payout_item_fee_amount,
          ledger_debit_total, ledger_credit_total, 'B_REFUND' AS sample_category
   FROM refund_ranked WHERE refund_kind = 'PARTIAL' AND tenant_refund_rn = 1
   ORDER BY amount_refunded DESC LIMIT 4)
),
tiled AS (
  SELECT e.*, NTILE(9) OVER (ORDER BY e.payment_id) AS tile
  FROM enriched e
),
tiled_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    t.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.tile ORDER BY (t.payout_item_amount IS NULL) DESC, t.payment_id) AS tile_rn
  FROM tiled t
),
typical_sample AS (
  SELECT
    payment_id, tenant_id, order_id, currency_code, payment_amount, amount_refunded,
    payment_amount_eur, payout_item_amount, payout_item_fee_amount,
    ledger_debit_total, ledger_credit_total, 'C_TYPICAL' AS sample_category
  FROM tiled_ranked
  WHERE tile_rn = 1
),
all_samples AS (
  SELECT * FROM largest_sample
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM refund_sample
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM typical_sample
),
final AS (
  SELECT
    s.payment_id,
    o.order_number,
    t.name AS merchant_name,
    s.currency_code,
    s.payment_amount,
    s.amount_refunded,
    (s.payment_amount - s.amount_refunded) AS net_amount,
    s.payout_item_amount,
    s.payout_item_fee_amount,
    (s.payout_item_amount - s.payout_item_fee_amount) AS payout_net_amount,
    (COALESCE(s.ledger_debit_total,0) - COALESCE(s.ledger_credit_total,0)) AS ledger_debit_credit_diff,
    s.ledger_credit_total,
    CASE
      WHEN s.payout_item_amount IS NULL THEN 'PENDING PAYOUT'
      WHEN (s.payment_amount - s.amount_refunded) = s.payout_item_amount
           AND (COALESCE(s.ledger_debit_total,0) - COALESCE(s.ledger_credit_total,0)) = 0
        THEN 'OK'
      ELSE 'CHECK'
    END AS reconciliation_flag,
    s.sample_category
  FROM all_samples s
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = s.order_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = s.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  order_number,
  merchant_name,
  currency_code,
  payment_amount,
  amount_refunded,
  net_amount,
  payout_item_amount,
  payout_item_fee_amount,
  payout_net_amount,
  ledger_debit_credit_diff,
  ledger_credit_total,
  reconciliation_flag
FROM final
ORDER BY
  CASE sample_category WHEN 'A_LARGEST' THEN 1 WHEN 'B_REFUND' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END,
  payment_amount DESC,
  payment_id
entries.engineer_note: Category A picks each sampled tenant's single largest 2025 payment (EUR-ranked) then takes the top 8 tenants, so results are spread by construction. Category B takes up to 4 fully-refunded and 4 partially-refunded payments, one per tenant (largest refund first). Category C uses NTILE(9) over payments.id as the deterministic pseudo-random split, preferring within each tile a payment with no payout_items match first (guarantees unmatched-payout rows are included whenever a tile contains one, though not a hard guarantee of >=2 overall). All money columns are left in native currency_code as requested; EUR conversion was used only internally for ranking in category A.

entries.title: Refund Attribution Lag: Purchase Quarter vs Refund Quarter, 2025
entries.question: Does the 16-40% quarterly gap between payments-based and order_returns-based refund totals come from refunds simply landing in a later quarter than the original purchase, rather than from missing or double-counted data?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT t0.id AS return_id, t0.order_id, t0.refund_total, t0.currency_code, t0.refunded_at
  FROM order_returns t0
  WHERE t0.status = 'refunded'
    AND t0.refunded_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t0.refunded_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
first_payment AS (
  SELECT t1.order_id, MIN(t1.captured_at) AS first_captured_at
  FROM payments t1
  WHERE t1.captured_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t1.order_id
),
joined AS (
  SELECT
    b.return_id,
    b.refund_total,
    b.currency_code,
    b.refunded_at,
    o.id AS order_id,
    fp.first_captured_at
  FROM base b
  LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = b.order_id
  LEFT JOIN first_payment fp ON fp.order_id = o.id
),
rated AS (
  SELECT
    j.*,
    CASE WHEN j.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0
         ELSE er.rate END AS fx_rate
  FROM joined j
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = j.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(j.refunded_at AS date)
),
categorized AS (
  SELECT
    r.*,
    CASE WHEN r.fx_rate IS NULL OR r.fx_rate = 0 THEN NULL ELSE r.refund_total / r.fx_rate END AS refund_amount_eur,
    CASE WHEN r.first_captured_at IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.refunded_at)*4 + EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM r.refunded_at))
            - (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM r.first_captured_at)*4 + EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM r.first_captured_at))
    END AS quarter_diff,
    CASE WHEN r.first_captured_at IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.refunded_at - r.first_captured_at)) / 86400.0
    END AS lag_days
  FROM rated r
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    CASE
      WHEN c.quarter_diff IS NULL THEN 'no matching payment found'
      WHEN c.quarter_diff <= 0 THEN 'same quarter as purchase'
      WHEN c.quarter_diff = 1 THEN 'purchase 1 quarter earlier'
      ELSE 'purchase 2+ quarters earlier'
    END AS lag_category
  FROM categorized c
)
SELECT
  b.lag_category,
  COUNT(*) AS return_count,
  ROUND(SUM(b.refund_amount_eur), 2) AS refund_amount_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(b.refund_amount_eur) / SUM(SUM(b.refund_amount_eur)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_total_2025_refund_amount,
  ROUND(AVG(b.lag_days), 1) AS avg_lag_days
FROM bucketed b
GROUP BY b.lag_category
ORDER BY return_count DESC, b.lag_category ASC
builds_on: Refund Figures Cross-Check: Payments vs Order Returns, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Matched each order_return to its order's earliest-captured payment to compute the quarter lag; a handful of returns before the matched payment's quarter (quarter_diff negative) are folded into 'same quarter as purchase' since no earlier bucket was specified. FX conversion uses EUR->currency_code daily rate (amount/rate), treating EUR rows as rate=1.

entries.title: Coupon Reuse Exposure: Redemptions Beyond First Use per Customer, 2025
entries.question: Roughly how much discount euro value comes from the same customer reusing a coupon code multiple times, given no usage or per-customer limit is enforced?
entries.sql:
with redemptions as (
  select
    cr.coupon_id,
    c.code as coupon_code,
    d.kind as discount_kind,
    cr.user_id,
    cr.redeemed_at,
    cr.discount_amount / er.rate as discount_amount_eur,
    row_number() over (partition by cr.coupon_id, cr.user_id order by cr.redeemed_at asc, cr.id asc) as rn
  from coupon_redemptions cr
  join coupons c on c.id = cr.coupon_id
  join discounts d on d.id = c.discount_id
  join exchange_rates er
    on er.base_code = 'EUR'
   and er.quote_code = cr.currency_code
   and er.as_of = cast(cr.redeemed_at as date)
  where cr.redeemed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
    and cr.redeemed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
)
select
  coupon_code,
  discount_kind,
  count(*) as total_redemptions_2025,
  count(distinct user_id) as distinct_customers_2025,
  count(*) - count(distinct user_id) as redemptions_beyond_first_use,
  round(sum(discount_amount_eur), 2) as total_discount_amount_eur,
  round(sum(discount_amount_eur) filter (where rn > 1), 2) as discount_amount_beyond_first_use_eur,
  round(100.0 * sum(discount_amount_eur) filter (where rn > 1) / nullif(sum(discount_amount_eur), 0), 2) as pct_of_discount_from_repeat_use
from redemptions
group by coupon_id, coupon_code, discount_kind
order by discount_amount_beyond_first_use_eur desc nulls last, coupon_code asc
limit 20
