entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per coupon (coupon_id), shown by its code; since coupon codes are unique only per tenant, the same code text could in principle appear on two rows if two different merchants happen to reuse it. Rows with no repeat redemptions show 0 / null pct and sort to the bottom; the printed report footer will show the total distinct-coupon row count as usual.

entries.title: Ledger Line-Item Detail for Flagged Sample Payments, 2025
entries.question: What do the actual ledger entries look like for the refunded and anomalous payments flagged in the transaction walkthrough, and does the accounting treatment of refunds make sense?
entries.sql:
with flagged_pairs (merchant_name, order_number) as (
  values
    ('OfficeHub Nordic', 'SO-100363'),
    ('Fell & Fjell', '#1179'),
    ('Courtside Collective', 'CC-100015'),
    ('Ampfeld Elektronik', '#1727'),
    ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'SO-100835'),
    ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'SO-100608'),
    ('Midland Safety Wear', 'SO-100307'),
    ('Halden Boots', '#1004'),
    ('Castell Fasteners', 'SO-100233')
),
matched_orders as (
  select
    o.id as order_id,
    o.order_number,
    t.name as merchant_name
  from orders o
  join tenants t on t.id = o.tenant_id
  join flagged_pairs fp
    on fp.merchant_name = t.name
   and fp.order_number = o.order_number
),
matched_payments as (
  select
    p.id as payment_id,
    mo.order_id,
    mo.order_number,
    mo.merchant_name
  from payments p
  join matched_orders mo on mo.order_id = p.order_id
),
ledger_detail as (
  select
    mp.merchant_name,
    mp.order_number,
    la.name as ledger_account_name,
    la.account_type,
    le.direction,
    le.amount,
    le.currency_code,
    le.description,
    le.entry_group,
    le.occurred_at
  from ledger_entries le
  join matched_payments mp on mp.payment_id = le.payment_id
  join ledger_accounts la on la.id = le.ledger_account_id
)
select
  merchant_name,
  order_number,
  ledger_account_name,
  account_type,
  direction,
  amount,
  currency_code,
  description,
  entry_group,
  occurred_at
from ledger_detail
order by merchant_name, order_number, occurred_at, entry_group
builds_on: Audit Sample: End-to-End Transaction Walkthrough, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Matched the 9 (merchant, order_number) pairs to orders via tenants.name + orders.order_number, then to all payments on those orders, then pulled every ledger_entries row tied to those payment_id(s) (unaggregated, joined to ledger_accounts for name/account_type). If an order had multiple payments, all of their ledger lines are included and distinguished by entry_group/occurred_at.

entries.title: Ledger-to-Payment Reconciliation Pattern at Scale, 2025
entries.question: Across all of 2025's payments, does the 'ledger credit = payment + refund' pattern seen in the sample hold universally, and how large are the 'no ledger entries' and 'other mismatch' buckets?
entries.sql:
WITH qualifying_payments AS (
  SELECT
    p.id,
    p.currency_code,
    p.amount,
    p.amount_refunded,
    p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
payment_amounts_eur AS (
  SELECT
    qp.id,
    qp.amount / er.rate AS payment_amount_eur,
    qp.amount_refunded / er.rate AS amount_refunded_eur
  FROM qualifying_payments qp
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = qp.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = date(qp.captured_at)
),
ledger_entries_eur AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id,
    le.direction,
    le.amount / er.rate AS amount_eur
  FROM ledger_entries le
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = le.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = date(le.occurred_at)
  WHERE le.payment_id IN (SELECT id FROM qualifying_payments)
),
ledger_agg AS (
  SELECT
    payment_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'credit' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS total_credit_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'debit' THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS total_debit_eur,
    COUNT(*) AS entry_count
  FROM ledger_entries_eur
  GROUP BY payment_id
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    pa.id,
    pa.payment_amount_eur,
    pa.amount_refunded_eur,
    COALESCE(la.total_credit_eur, 0) AS total_credit_eur,
    COALESCE(la.total_debit_eur, 0) AS total_debit_eur,
    COALESCE(la.entry_count, 0) AS entry_count,
    (pa.payment_amount_eur - pa.amount_refunded_eur) AS target_net,
    (pa.payment_amount_eur + pa.amount_refunded_eur) AS target_gross
  FROM payment_amounts_eur pa
  LEFT JOIN ledger_agg la ON la.payment_id = pa.id
),
categorized AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    payment_amount_eur,
    total_credit_eur,
    total_debit_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN entry_count = 0 THEN 'no ledger entries'
      WHEN ABS(total_credit_eur - target_net) <= GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(target_net), 1) THEN 'credit = net amount'
      WHEN ABS(total_credit_eur - target_gross) <= GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(target_gross), 1) THEN 'credit = payment + refund'
      ELSE 'other mismatch'
    END AS reconciliation_category
  FROM classified
)
SELECT
  reconciliation_category,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_payments,
  ROUND(SUM(payment_amount_eur), 2) AS total_payment_amount_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(total_credit_eur), 2) AS total_ledger_credit_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(total_debit_eur), 2) AS total_ledger_debit_eur
FROM categorized
GROUP BY reconciliation_category
ORDER BY payment_count DESC
builds_on: Audit Sample: End-to-End Transaction Walkthrough, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Classification checks 'credit = net amount' before 'credit = payment + refund' since the request's tolerance bands could both match when amount_refunded is 0 (net = gross); this ordering treats that case as 'net amount' rather than double-counting. Each payment and ledger-entry amount is converted to EUR independently on its own date/currency as specified.

entries.title: Payments With No Ledger Entries, by Merchant, 2025
entries.question: Is the 'payment with zero ledger entries' gap concentrated in a few merchants, or spread thinly across many?
entries.sql:
WITH pay_2025 AS (
  SELECT
    p.id AS payment_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.currency_code,
    p.amount,
    p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
ledger_counts AS (
  SELECT payment_id, COUNT(*) AS entry_count
  FROM ledger_entries
  WHERE payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY payment_id
),
pay_flagged AS (
  SELECT
    p.tenant_id,
    p.payment_id,
    p.currency_code,
    p.amount,
    p.captured_at,
    CASE WHEN lc.entry_count IS NULL OR lc.entry_count = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS no_ledger
  FROM pay_2025 p
  LEFT JOIN ledger_counts lc ON lc.payment_id = p.payment_id
),
pay_eur AS (
  SELECT
    pf.*,
    CASE
      WHEN pf.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pf.amount
      ELSE pf.amount / er.rate
    END AS amount_eur
  FROM pay_flagged pf
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = pf.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = DATE(pf.captured_at)
),
by_tenant AS (
  SELECT
    t.name AS merchant_name,
    COUNT(*) AS total_payments_2025,
    SUM(pe.no_ledger) AS payments_without_ledger_entries,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(pe.no_ledger) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_without_ledger_entries,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN pe.no_ledger = 1 THEN pe.amount_eur ELSE 0 END), 2) AS amount_at_risk_eur
  FROM pay_eur pe
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = pe.tenant_id
  GROUP BY t.name
  HAVING SUM(pe.no_ledger) >= 1
)
SELECT
  merchant_name,
  total_payments_2025,
  payments_without_ledger_entries,
  pct_without_ledger_entries,
  amount_at_risk_eur,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS tenants_with_gap_total
FROM by_tenant
ORDER BY amount_at_risk_eur DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 30
builds_on: Audit Sample: End-to-End Transaction Walkthrough, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Added a "tenants_with_gap_total" column (same value on every row) showing how many merchants in total had at least one payment-without-ledger-entry gap, so that count is visible even though only the top 30 by amount_at_risk_eur are printed. EUR conversion divides each payment's local amount by the EUR->local rate for its captured_at date; if no rate exists for that exact date the amount_eur is left null and excluded from the sum (handbook notes weekend dates carry the prior business day's rate, so gaps should be rare).

entries.title: Other-Mismatch Payments: Characterization by Payment Method, 2025
entries.question: Is the 2.1%-of-payments 'other mismatch' ledger bucket explained by a specific payment method (e.g. bank transfer/wire rather than card/gateway), or is it unexplained?
entries.sql:
WITH t0_payments_eur AS (
  SELECT
    p.id AS payment_id,
    p.payment_method_id,
    p.amount / er0.rate AS payment_amount_eur,
    p.amount_refunded / er0.rate AS amount_refunded_eur
  FROM payments p
  JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er0.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er0.as_of = DATE(p.captured_at)
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
),

t1_ledger_credit AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id AS payment_id,
    SUM(le.amount / er1.rate) AS ledger_credit_total_eur
  FROM ledger_entries le
  JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er1.quote_code = le.currency_code
   AND er1.as_of = DATE(le.occurred_at)
  WHERE le.direction = 'credit'
    AND le.payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),

t2_ledger_rowcount AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id AS payment_id,
    COUNT(*) AS ledger_row_count
  FROM ledger_entries le
  WHERE le.payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),

t3_payment_classified AS (
  SELECT
    t0.payment_id,
    t0.payment_method_id,
    t0.payment_amount_eur,
    COALESCE(t1.ledger_credit_total_eur, 0) AS ledger_credit_total_eur,
    COALESCE(t2.ledger_row_count, 0) AS ledger_row_count,
    (t0.payment_amount_eur - t0.amount_refunded_eur) AS expected_net_eur,
    (t0.payment_amount_eur + t0.amount_refunded_eur) AS expected_gross_eur,
    ABS(COALESCE(t1.ledger_credit_total_eur,0) - (t0.payment_amount_eur - t0.amount_refunded_eur)) AS diff_net_eur,
    ABS(COALESCE(t1.ledger_credit_total_eur,0) - (t0.payment_amount_eur + t0.amount_refunded_eur)) AS diff_gross_eur
  FROM t0_payments_eur t0
  LEFT JOIN t1_ledger_credit t1 ON t1.payment_id = t0.payment_id
  LEFT JOIN t2_ledger_rowcount t2 ON t2.payment_id = t0.payment_id
),

t4_other_mismatch AS (
  SELECT
    t3.payment_id,
    t3.payment_method_id,
    t3.payment_amount_eur,
    CASE WHEN t3.diff_net_eur <= t3.diff_gross_eur THEN t3.diff_net_eur ELSE t3.diff_gross_eur END AS abs_diff_eur
  FROM t3_payment_classified t3
  WHERE t3.ledger_row_count >= 1
    AND t3.diff_net_eur   > GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(t3.expected_net_eur), 1)
    AND t3.diff_gross_eur > GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(t3.expected_gross_eur), 1)
),

t5_mismatch_with_kind AS (
  SELECT
    t4.payment_id,
    t4.payment_amount_eur,
    t4.abs_diff_eur,
    COALESCE(pm.kind, 'unknown') AS payment_method_kind
  FROM t4_other_mismatch t4
  LEFT JOIN payment_methods pm ON pm.id = t4.payment_method_id
),

t6_grand_totals AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS grand_total_count,
    SUM(t5.payment_amount_eur) AS grand_total_amount_eur
  FROM t5_mismatch_with_kind t5
),

t7_count AS (
  SELECT t5.payment_method_kind, COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM t5_mismatch_with_kind t5
  GROUP BY t5.payment_method_kind
),

t8_amount AS (
  SELECT t5.payment_method_kind, SUM(t5.payment_amount_eur) AS total_payment_amount_eur
  FROM t5_mismatch_with_kind t5
  GROUP BY t5.payment_method_kind
),

t9_avgdiff AS (
  SELECT t5.payment_method_kind, AVG(t5.abs_diff_eur) AS avg_abs_diff_eur
  FROM t5_mismatch_with_kind t5
  GROUP BY t5.payment_method_kind
)

SELECT
  t7.payment_method_kind AS payment_method_kind,
  t7.payment_count AS payment_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * t7.payment_count / NULLIF(t6.grand_total_count, 0), 2) AS pct_of_mismatch_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t8.total_payment_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS total_payment_amount_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t8.total_payment_amount_eur, 0) / NULLIF(t6.grand_total_amount_eur, 0), 2) AS pct_of_mismatch_amount,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t9.avg_abs_diff_eur, 0), 2) AS avg_abs_diff_eur
FROM t7_count t7
LEFT JOIN t8_amount t8 ON t8.payment_method_kind = t7.payment_method_kind
LEFT JOIN t9_avgdiff t9 ON t9.payment_method_kind = t7.payment_method_kind
CROSS JOIN t6_grand_totals t6
ORDER BY t7.payment_count DESC, t7.payment_method_kind ASC
builds_on: Ledger-to-Payment Reconciliation Pattern at Scale, 2025
Ledger Line-Item Detail for Flagged Sample Payments, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Re-derived the 'other mismatch' set exactly as specified (2025 captured/refunded/partially_refunded payments, EUR-converted ledger credit totals vs. net/gross expected, excluding 'no ledger entries' payments), then grouped by payment_methods.kind (missing/null -> 'unknown'). avg_abs_diff_eur uses the smaller of the net- and gross-expected deviations, as requested.

entries.title: 2025 Revenue Reconciliation via Correct Ledger Accounts, by Quarter
entries.question: Using the right ledger accounts (revenue credits net of refund contra-revenue debits), does the ledger's net revenue tie to the payments table's net captured amount each quarter?
entries.sql:
WITH ledger_q AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM le.occurred_at)::int AS yr,
    EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM le.occurred_at)::int AS qtr,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN la.account_type = 'revenue' AND le.direction = 'credit'
          THEN (CASE WHEN le.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN le.amount ELSE le.amount / er.rate END)
          ELSE 0
        END) AS ledger_revenue_credit_eur,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN la.account_type = 'contra_revenue' AND le.direction = 'debit'
          THEN (CASE WHEN le.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN le.amount ELSE le.amount / er.rate END)
          ELSE 0
        END) AS ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur
  FROM ledger_entries le
  JOIN ledger_accounts la ON la.id = le.ledger_account_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = le.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = date(le.occurred_at)
  WHERE le.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND le.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND la.account_type IN ('revenue', 'contra_revenue')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
payments_q AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM p.captured_at)::int AS yr,
    EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM p.captured_at)::int AS qtr,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN (p.amount - p.amount_refunded)
          ELSE (p.amount - p.amount_refunded) / er2.rate
        END) AS payments_net_amount_eur
  FROM payments p
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = date(p.captured_at)
  WHERE p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT
  l.yr || '-Q' || l.qtr AS quarter,
  ROUND(l.ledger_revenue_credit_eur, 2) AS ledger_revenue_credit_eur,
  ROUND(l.ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur, 2) AS ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur,
  ROUND(l.ledger_revenue_credit_eur - l.ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur, 2) AS ledger_net_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(p.payments_net_amount_eur, 2) AS payments_net_amount_eur,
  ROUND((l.ledger_revenue_credit_eur - l.ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur) - p.payments_net_amount_eur, 2) AS diff_eur,
  ROUND(
    ((l.ledger_revenue_credit_eur - l.ledger_contra_revenue_debit_eur) - p.payments_net_amount_eur)
    / NULLIF(p.payments_net_amount_eur, 0) * 100,
    2
  ) AS diff_pct
FROM ledger_q l
JOIN payments_q p ON p.yr = l.yr AND p.qtr = l.qtr
ORDER BY l.yr, l.qtr
builds_on: Ledger Line-Item Detail for Flagged Sample Payments, 2025
Ledger-to-Payment Reconciliation Pattern at Scale, 2025
entries.engineer_note: EUR conversion treats same-currency rows (currency_code='EUR') as rate 1 and otherwise divides by the EUR-base exchange_rates.rate for that day (ledger: occurred_at date; payments: captured_at date), per the handbook's EUR-base convention. Quarters are calendar quarters of 2025 built from EXTRACT(YEAR/QUARTER), inner-joined so a quarter only appears if both sides have rows (expected for all 4 of 2025).

entries.title: No-Ledger-Entries Gap Trend by Month, 2025
entries.question: Is the small 'payment with zero ledger entries' gap an ongoing issue in current operations, or was it confined to earlier in the year and since resolved?
entries.sql:
WITH payments_2025 AS (
  SELECT
    p.id,
    p.captured_at,
    p.amount,
    p.currency_code
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
ledger_counts AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id,
    COUNT(*) AS entry_count
  FROM ledger_entries le
  WHERE le.payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),
payments_with_fx AS (
  SELECT
    p.id,
    p.captured_at,
    p.amount / er.rate AS amount_eur,
    COALESCE(lc.entry_count, 0) AS entry_count
  FROM payments_2025 p
  LEFT JOIN ledger_counts lc ON lc.payment_id = p.id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = DATE(p.captured_at)
),
payments_with_month AS (
  SELECT
    cd.month_label,
    cd.month_start,
    pf.amount_eur,
    pf.entry_count
  FROM payments_with_fx pf
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = DATE(pf.captured_at)
),
monthly AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS total_payments,
    SUM(CASE WHEN entry_count = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS payments_without_ledger_entries,
    SUM(CASE WHEN entry_count = 0 THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS amount_at_risk_eur
  FROM payments_with_month
  GROUP BY month_label, month_start
)
SELECT
  month_label AS month,
  total_payments,
  payments_without_ledger_entries,
  ROUND(100.0 * payments_without_ledger_entries / total_payments, 2) AS pct_without_ledger_entries,
  ROUND(amount_at_risk_eur, 2) AS amount_at_risk_eur
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month_start
builds_on: Payments With No Ledger Entries, by Merchant, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Converted payment amounts to EUR by dividing by the EUR→payment-currency exchange_rates.rate on the capture date (rate is EUR-per-1-quote-currency... actually rate is quote units per 1 EUR, so amount/rate = EUR); months with no matching payments simply won't appear (all 12 months are expected to have data in 2025).

entries.title: 2025 Revenue Reconciliation via Ledger Accounts, Including VAT, by Quarter
entries.question: Once VAT/sales-tax is included on the ledger side (not just net-of-tax revenue), does the ledger's gross billed amount tie to the payments table's net captured amount each quarter?
entries.sql:
WITH quarters AS (
  SELECT * FROM (VALUES (1),(2),(3),(4)) AS v(q)
),
ledger_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    je.id,
    je.direction,
    je.amount,
    je.currency_code,
    je.occurred_at,
    la.account_type,
    la.name AS account_name
  FROM ledger_entries je
  JOIN ledger_accounts la ON la.id = je.ledger_account_id
  WHERE je.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND je.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND (
      la.account_type IN ('revenue','contra_revenue')
      OR la.name = 'VAT / sales tax payable'
    )
),
ledger_eur AS (
  SELECT
    lf.id,
    lf.direction,
    lf.amount,
    lf.currency_code,
    lf.account_type,
    lf.account_name,
    EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM lf.occurred_at)::int AS q,
    CASE WHEN lf.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN lf.amount
         ELSE lf.amount / er.rate END AS amount_eur
  FROM ledger_filtered lf
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = lf.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = lf.occurred_at::date
),
ledger_quarterly AS (
  SELECT
    q,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN direction = 'credit' AND (account_type = 'revenue' OR account_name = 'VAT / sales tax payable') THEN amount_eur
          WHEN direction = 'debit' AND (account_type = 'contra_revenue' OR account_name = 'VAT / sales tax payable') THEN -amount_eur
          ELSE 0
        END) AS ledger_gross_billed_eur
  FROM ledger_eur
  GROUP BY q
),
payments_filtered AS (
  SELECT
    p.id,
    p.amount,
    p.amount_refunded,
    p.currency_code,
    p.captured_at,
    EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM p.captured_at)::int AS q
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND p.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
),
payments_eur AS (
  SELECT
    pf.q,
    CASE WHEN pf.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN (pf.amount - pf.amount_refunded)
         ELSE (pf.amount - pf.amount_refunded) / er.rate END AS net_amount_eur
  FROM payments_filtered pf
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pf.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = pf.captured_at::date
),
payments_quarterly AS (
  SELECT q, SUM(net_amount_eur) AS payments_net_amount_eur
  FROM payments_eur
  GROUP BY q
)
SELECT
  '2025-Q' || quarters.q AS quarter,
  ROUND(COALESCE(lq.ledger_gross_billed_eur,0), 2) AS ledger_gross_billed_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(pq.payments_net_amount_eur,0), 2) AS payments_net_amount_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(lq.ledger_gross_billed_eur,0) - COALESCE(pq.payments_net_amount_eur,0), 2) AS diff_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(pq.payments_net_amount_eur,0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE (COALESCE(lq.ledger_gross_billed_eur,0) - COALESCE(pq.payments_net_amount_eur,0)) / pq.payments_net_amount_eur * 100
    END, 2
  ) AS diff_pct
FROM quarters
LEFT JOIN ledger_quarterly lq ON lq.q = quarters.q
LEFT JOIN payments_quarterly pq ON pq.q = quarters.q
ORDER BY quarters.q
builds_on: 2025 Revenue Reconciliation via Correct Ledger Accounts, by Quarter
entries.engineer_note: Ledger-side EUR conversion uses the exchange rate as of the entry's own occurred_at date (same for payments on captured_at); rows in EUR itself skip the rate join. diff_pct is NULL for a quarter if payments_net_amount_eur is exactly 0, to avoid divide-by-zero.

entries.title: Bank Transfer Payments With Unexplained Ledger Mismatch: Full List, 2025
entries.question: Which specific bank-transfer payments have an unexplained ledger mismatch, so they can be handed to the auditors as a named, bounded list?
entries.sql:
WITH payment_base AS (
  SELECT 
    p.id AS payment_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.order_id,
    p.currency_code,
    p.amount,
    p.amount_refunded,
    p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  JOIN payment_methods pm ON pm.id = p.payment_method_id
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND pm.kind = 'bank_transfer'
),
payment_eur AS (
  SELECT
    pb.payment_id,
    pb.tenant_id,
    pb.order_id,
    pb.currency_code,
    pb.amount,
    pb.amount_refunded,
    pb.captured_at,
    CASE WHEN pb.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pb.amount
         ELSE pb.amount / er.rate END AS payment_amount_eur,
    CASE WHEN pb.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN pb.amount_refunded
         ELSE pb.amount_refunded / er.rate END AS amount_refunded_eur
  FROM payment_base pb
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = pb.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(pb.captured_at AS date)
),
ledger_credit AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN le.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN le.amount
             ELSE le.amount / er.rate END) AS ledger_credit_total_eur
  FROM ledger_entries le
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = le.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(le.occurred_at AS date)
  WHERE le.direction = 'credit'
    AND le.payment_id IN (SELECT payment_id FROM payment_base)
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),
calc AS (
  SELECT
    pe.payment_id,
    pe.tenant_id,
    pe.order_id,
    pe.currency_code,
    pe.amount AS payment_amount,
    pe.amount_refunded,
    pe.captured_at,
    lc.ledger_credit_total_eur,
    (pe.payment_amount_eur - pe.amount_refunded_eur) AS net_amount_eur,
    (pe.payment_amount_eur + pe.amount_refunded_eur) AS payment_plus_refund_eur,
    CASE WHEN ABS(lc.ledger_credit_total_eur - (pe.payment_amount_eur - pe.amount_refunded_eur))
              <= ABS(lc.ledger_credit_total_eur - (pe.payment_amount_eur + pe.amount_refunded_eur))
         THEN (pe.payment_amount_eur - pe.amount_refunded_eur)
         ELSE (pe.payment_amount_eur + pe.amount_refunded_eur)
    END AS nearest_expected_eur
  FROM payment_eur pe
  LEFT JOIN ledger_credit lc ON lc.payment_id = pe.payment_id
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    c.*,
    (c.ledger_credit_total_eur - c.nearest_expected_eur) AS diff_eur,
    GREATEST(0.01 * ABS(c.nearest_expected_eur), 1) AS tolerance_eur
  FROM calc c
)
SELECT
  o.order_number,
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  cl.captured_at AS payment_captured_at,
  cl.currency_code,
  cl.payment_amount,
  cl.amount_refunded,
  ROUND(cl.ledger_credit_total_eur, 2) AS ledger_credit_total_eur,
  ROUND(cl.nearest_expected_eur, 2) AS nearest_expected_eur,
  ROUND(cl.diff_eur, 2) AS diff_eur
FROM classified cl
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = cl.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = cl.order_id
WHERE cl.ledger_credit_total_eur IS NOT NULL
  AND ABS(cl.diff_eur) > cl.tolerance_eur
ORDER BY diff_eur DESC, cl.payment_id
builds_on: Other-Mismatch Payments: Characterization by Payment Method, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Reconstructed the 'other mismatch' classification from the description: for each 2025 captured/refunded/partially_refunded bank-transfer payment, ledger_credit_total_eur (sum of credit ledger_entries by payment_id, FX-converted using each entry's own currency/date) is compared against net_amount_eur (payment-refund, EUR) and payment_plus_refund_eur (payment+refund, EUR), each converted using the payment's own currency/captured_at date; nearest_expected_eur is whichever is closer, diff_eur is ledger minus that value, tolerance is max(1%, €1), and rows with no ledger entries at all are excluded. Used LEFT JOIN to orders since payments.order_id is nullable, so order_number may be blank if a matching payment has no linked order.

entries.title: Ledger Reconciliation Outcome by Payment Method, All 2025 Payments
entries.question: Is bank_transfer systemically more prone to ledger mismatches as a payment channel, or are the 19 flagged payments a rare exception within a much larger, mostly-clean population?
entries.sql:
WITH fx AS (
  SELECT quote_code, as_of, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR'
),
payments_2025 AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.payment_method_id, p.amount, p.amount_refunded, p.currency_code, p.captured_at
  FROM payments p
  WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
ledger_agg AS (
  SELECT
    le.payment_id,
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN le.direction = 'credit'
        THEN le.amount * COALESCE(fx.rate, CASE WHEN le.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END)
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS credit_eur,
    COUNT(*) AS entry_count
  FROM ledger_entries le
  LEFT JOIN fx ON fx.quote_code = le.currency_code AND fx.as_of = DATE(le.occurred_at)
  WHERE le.payment_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY le.payment_id
),
calc AS (
  SELECT
    p.id,
    COALESCE(pm.kind, 'unknown') AS payment_method_kind,
    p.amount * COALESCE(fx_p.rate, CASE WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS payment_amount_eur,
    p.amount_refunded * COALESCE(fx_p.rate, CASE WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 END) AS refunded_amount_eur,
    la.credit_eur,
    la.entry_count
  FROM payments_2025 p
  LEFT JOIN payment_methods pm ON pm.id = p.payment_method_id
  LEFT JOIN fx fx_p ON fx_p.quote_code = p.currency_code AND fx_p.as_of = DATE(p.captured_at)
  LEFT JOIN ledger_agg la ON la.payment_id = p.id
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    payment_method_kind,
    CASE
      WHEN entry_count IS NULL OR entry_count = 0 THEN 'no_ledger_entries'
      WHEN ABS(credit_eur - (payment_amount_eur - refunded_amount_eur))
           <= GREATEST(1.0, 0.01 * ABS(payment_amount_eur - refunded_amount_eur))
        THEN 'credit_equals_net'
      WHEN ABS(credit_eur - (payment_amount_eur + refunded_amount_eur))
           <= GREATEST(1.0, 0.01 * ABS(payment_amount_eur + refunded_amount_eur))
        THEN 'credit_equals_payment_plus_refund'
      ELSE 'other_mismatch'
    END AS classification
  FROM calc
)
SELECT
  payment_method_kind,
  COUNT(*) AS total_payment_count_2025,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification = 'credit_equals_net' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_credit_equals_net,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification = 'credit_equals_payment_plus_refund' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_credit_equals_payment_plus_refund,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification = 'other_mismatch' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_other_mismatch,
  SUM(CASE WHEN classification = 'no_ledger_entries' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_no_ledger_entries,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN classification IN ('credit_equals_net', 'credit_equals_payment_plus_refund') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    / COUNT(*),
    1
  ) AS pct_clean
FROM classified
GROUP BY payment_method_kind
ORDER BY total_payment_count_2025 DESC, payment_method_kind ASC
builds_on: Other-Mismatch Payments: Characterization by Payment Method, 2025
Ledger-to-Payment Reconciliation Pattern at Scale, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Reconciliation uses the same logic as this week's series: 2025 payments with status captured/refunded/partially_refunded, ledger credit total in EUR (FX by entry date) compared to net_amount_eur (payment - refunded) and payment_plus_refund_eur (payment + refunded), 1%-or-€1 tolerance, 'no ledger entries' when zero linked ledger_entries rows for that payment_id; payment_methods.kind defaulted to 'unknown' when missing. One row per kind, all qualifying 2025 payments included (not pre-filtered to mismatches).

entries.title: Albion Parcel performance by destination country, baseline vs collapse
entries.question: Is Albion Parcel's November-December breakdown concentrated in specific destination countries, or did it hit all regions roughly equally?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.shipped_at,
    s.delivered_at,
    c.name AS destination_country,
    (s.delivered_at::date - s.shipped_at::date) AS transit_days,
    CASE
      WHEN s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2025-11-01' THEN 'baseline'
      WHEN s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-11-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 'collapse'
    END AS period
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
  JOIN orders o ON f.order_id = o.id
  JOIN addresses a ON o.shipping_address_id = a.id
  JOIN countries c ON a.country_id = c.id
  WHERE s.carrier = 'Albion Parcel'
    AND s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    destination_country,
    period,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_shipped,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS delivered_count,
    AVG(transit_days) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_transit_days,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND transit_days <= 3) AS within3
  FROM base
  WHERE period IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY destination_country, period
),
totals AS (
  SELECT period, SUM(shipments_shipped) AS total_shipments
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY period
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT destination_country
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY destination_country
  HAVING MAX(shipments_shipped) >= 15
)
SELECT
  a.destination_country,
  a.period,
  a.shipments_shipped,
  ROUND(a.avg_transit_days::numeric, 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.within3 / NULLIF(a.delivered_count, 0), 1) AS pct_within_3_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.shipments_shipped / t.total_shipments, 1) AS share_of_period_shipments_pct
FROM agg a
JOIN totals t ON a.period = t.period
JOIN qualified q ON q.destination_country = a.destination_country
ORDER BY a.destination_country ASC, a.period ASC
builds_on: Albion Parcel transit performance by month, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Countries qualify if they had >=15 Albion Parcel shipments in at least one of the two periods (baseline or collapse), per the request; both periods are then shown for every qualifying country. pct_within_3_days and avg_transit_days are computed over the delivered subset only, as specified.

entries.title: Albion Parcel performance by origin warehouse, baseline vs collapse
entries.question: Is Albion Parcel's November-December breakdown concentrated in a specific warehouse/hub (or the merchants it serves), or did it hit all origins roughly equally?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    f.warehouse_id,
    w.name AS warehouse_name,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    CASE
      WHEN s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2025-11-01' THEN 'baseline'
      WHEN s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-11-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01' THEN 'collapse'
    END AS period,
    s.delivered_at,
    s.shipped_at
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = f.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  WHERE s.carrier = 'Albion Parcel'
    AND s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    warehouse_id,
    warehouse_name,
    tenant_name,
    period,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_shipped,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (delivered_at - shipped_at)) / 86400.0) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_transit_days_raw,
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND delivered_at - shipped_at <= INTERVAL '3 days')
      / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL), 0) AS pct_within_3_days_raw
  FROM base
  WHERE period IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY warehouse_id, warehouse_name, tenant_name, period
),
period_totals AS (
  SELECT period, SUM(shipments_shipped) AS total_shipments
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY period
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT warehouse_id
  FROM agg
  GROUP BY warehouse_id
  HAVING MAX(shipments_shipped) >= 10
)
SELECT
  a.warehouse_name,
  a.tenant_name,
  a.period,
  a.shipments_shipped,
  ROUND(a.avg_transit_days_raw, 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND(a.pct_within_3_days_raw, 1) AS pct_within_3_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.shipments_shipped / pt.total_shipments, 1) AS share_of_period_shipments_pct
FROM agg a
JOIN period_totals pt ON pt.period = a.period
JOIN qualified q ON q.warehouse_id = a.warehouse_id
ORDER BY a.warehouse_name ASC, CASE a.period WHEN 'baseline' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
builds_on: Albion Parcel transit performance by month, 2025
entries.engineer_note: avg_transit_days and pct_within_3_days are computed only over shipments with a non-null delivered_at (in-transit/undelivered shipments are excluded from those two measures but still count toward shipments_shipped and the share%); transit_days = delivered_at - shipped_at in days, matching the destination-country report's definition.

entries.title: Landfall Freight & Lowlands Express performance by destination country, full year 2025
entries.question: Are our two chronically weak carriers bad everywhere, or concentrated on specific lanes/countries?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    s.carrier,
    co.name AS destination_country,
    s.id AS shipment_id,
    s.delivered_at,
    (CAST(s.delivered_at AS date) - CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)) AS transit_days
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  JOIN addresses a ON a.id = o.shipping_address_id
  JOIN countries co ON co.id = a.country_id
  WHERE s.carrier IN ('Landfall Freight','Lowlands Express')
    AND s.shipped_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
carrier_totals AS (
  SELECT carrier, COUNT(*) AS carrier_shipments
  FROM base
  GROUP BY carrier
),
country_stats AS (
  SELECT
    carrier,
    destination_country,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_shipped,
    AVG(transit_days) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL) AS avg_transit_days,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND transit_days <= 3) AS within_3_count
  FROM base
  GROUP BY carrier, destination_country
)
SELECT
  cs.carrier,
  cs.destination_country,
  cs.shipments_shipped,
  ROUND(cs.avg_transit_days, 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * cs.within_3_count / cs.shipments_shipped, 1) AS pct_within_3_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * cs.shipments_shipped / ct.carrier_shipments, 1) AS share_of_carrier_shipments_pct
FROM country_stats cs
JOIN carrier_totals ct ON ct.carrier = cs.carrier
WHERE cs.shipments_shipped >= 15
ORDER BY cs.carrier ASC, cs.shipments_shipped DESC, cs.destination_country ASC
builds_on: Carrier transit performance by quarter, 2025
Carrier transit performance, Q4 2025 (complete)
entries.engineer_note: pct_within_3_days is computed as (delivered shipments with transit_days<=3) / all shipments_shipped for that carrier+country (undelivered shipments count as not-within-3-days); avg_transit_days is averaged over delivered shipments only, per the given transit_days definition. share_of_carrier_shipments_pct uses the carrier's full-year total across all countries (not just those meeting the 15-shipment threshold) as the denominator.

entries.title: Carrier performance, full year 2025 (complete)
entries.question: What is each carrier's full-year transit reliability and volume share, so I can estimate how much overall unreliability would disappear if the weak carriers matched the good ones?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  carrier,
  COUNT(*) AS shipments_shipped,
  COUNT(delivered_at) AS shipments_delivered,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN delivered_at IS NOT NULL THEN (delivered_at::date - shipped_at::date) END)::numeric, 2) AS avg_transit_days,
  ROUND((PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (delivered_at::date - shipped_at::date)) FILTER (WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL))::numeric, 2) AS median_transit_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND (delivered_at::date - shipped_at::date) <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(delivered_at), 0), 1) AS pct_within_3_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS share_of_total_shipments_pct
FROM shipments
WHERE shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY carrier
ORDER BY shipments_shipped DESC, carrier ASC
builds_on: Carrier transit performance, Q4 2025 (complete)
Carrier transit performance by quarter, 2025
entries.engineer_note: transit_days computed as delivered_at::date - shipped_at::date (whole calendar days); avg/median/pct_within_3_days are based only on the delivered subset per carrier, while shipments_shipped and share_of_total_shipments_pct cover all shipped shipments regardless of delivery status.

entries.title: Purchase order replenishment performance by quarter, 2025 (mature POs only, non-censored)
entries.question: Once we only look at purchase orders old enough to have fully played out, are we genuinely behind on restocking, or was the Q4 backlog just a year-end timing artifact?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  '2025-Q' || CAST(EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM ordered_at) AS INTEGER) AS quarter,
  COUNT(*) AS pos_ordered_total,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01') AS pos_matured,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01' AND received_at IS NOT NULL) AS pos_matured_received,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'
        AND received_at IS NULL
        AND status IN ('submitted','partially_received')
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'), 0), 1) AS pct_matured_still_open,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE
      WHEN ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01' AND received_at IS NOT NULL
      THEN DATE_DIFF('day', ordered_at, received_at)
    END), 1) AS avg_actual_lead_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'
        AND expected_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at > expected_at
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'
        AND expected_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at IS NOT NULL
    ), 0), 1) AS pct_received_late,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE
      WHEN ordered_at <= DATE '2025-11-01'
        AND expected_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at IS NOT NULL
        AND received_at > expected_at
      THEN DATE_DIFF('day', expected_at, received_at)
    END), 1) AS avg_days_late
FROM purchase_orders
WHERE ordered_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND ordered_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM ordered_at)
ORDER BY quarter ASC
builds_on: Purchase order replenishment performance by quarter, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Aggregated across all tenants/POs platform-wide (no merchant filter requested). As noted in the request, Q4's matured subset only covers POs ordered in October since Nov/Dec POs aren't yet 60 days old as of the 2025-12-31 cutoff - this is expected, not a data gap.

entries.title: Fulfillment shortfall and delivery speed by merchant vertical, 2025
entries.question: Do apparel/footwear merchants, where picking discrepancies are concentrated, actually see more orders go unfulfilled or delivered slowly -- or is that purely an inventory/accounting issue with no customer-facing effect?
entries.sql:
WITH terminal_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, t.industry, o.status, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status IN ('fulfilled','cancelled','refunded')
    AND t.industry IS NOT NULL
),
order_qty AS (
  SELECT oi.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS qty_ordered, SUM(oi.quantity_fulfilled) AS qty_fulfilled
  FROM order_items oi
  GROUP BY oi.order_id
),
order_shipment AS (
  SELECT f.order_id,
         COUNT(s.id) AS shipment_count,
         SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivered_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS undelivered_count,
         MAX(s.delivered_at) AS max_delivered_at
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
  GROUP BY f.order_id
),
order_flags AS (
  SELECT
    t0.order_id,
    t0.tenant_id,
    t0.industry,
    t0.status,
    t0.placed_at,
    COALESCE(q.qty_ordered, 0) AS qty_ordered,
    COALESCE(q.qty_fulfilled, 0) AS qty_fulfilled,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(q.qty_fulfilled,0) < COALESCE(q.qty_ordered,0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_shortfall,
    CASE WHEN t0.status = 'fulfilled'
              AND s.shipment_count IS NOT NULL
              AND s.shipment_count > 0
              AND COALESCE(s.undelivered_count,0) = 0
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_fully_delivered,
    s.max_delivered_at
  FROM terminal_orders t0
  LEFT JOIN order_qty q ON q.order_id = t0.order_id
  LEFT JOIN order_shipment s ON s.order_id = t0.order_id
)
SELECT
  industry,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_placed_2025,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(has_shortfall) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 1) AS pct_orders_with_fulfillment_shortfall,
  SUM(is_fully_delivered) AS orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN is_fully_delivered=1 THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (max_delivered_at - placed_at))/86400.0 END) AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN is_fully_delivered=1 AND (max_delivered_at - placed_at) <= INTERVAL '5 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(is_fully_delivered),0), 1) AS pct_within_5_days
FROM order_flags
GROUP BY industry
ORDER BY pct_orders_with_fulfillment_shortfall DESC, industry ASC
builds_on: Fulfillment performance by warehouse, 2025
entries.engineer_note: "Fully delivered" requires the order to have at least one linked shipment (via fulfillments) and none of them null delivered_at; orders with status='fulfilled' but no shipment rows at all are excluded from that subset rather than counted as delivered. Tenants with a null industry are excluded since the grain is per-vertical.

entries.title: Order-level delivery reliability: weak carriers vs rest, 2025
entries.question: In the same order-level metric I've already reported to Priya (pct within 5 days), how much better would our overall delivery reliability be if the three weak carriers matched everyone else?
entries.sql:
WITH order_fulfillment_counts AS (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM fulfillments
  GROUP BY order_id
),
fulfillment_shipment_counts AS (
  SELECT fulfillment_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM shipments
  GROUP BY fulfillment_id
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.placed_at,
    s.carrier,
    s.delivered_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
  JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
  JOIN order_fulfillment_counts ofc ON ofc.order_id = o.id
  JOIN fulfillment_shipment_counts fsc ON fsc.fulfillment_id = f.id
  WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND ofc.cnt = 1
    AND fsc.cnt = 1
    AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
scored AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    CASE WHEN carrier IN ('Albion Parcel','Landfall Freight','Lowlands Express') THEN 'Weak three' ELSE 'All other carriers' END AS carrier_group,
    (delivered_at::date - placed_at::date) AS delivery_days
  FROM base
)
SELECT
  carrier_group,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(AVG(delivery_days)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
FROM scored
GROUP BY carrier_group
ORDER BY carrier_group ASC
builds_on: Carrier performance, full year 2025 (complete)
Delivery time trend, monthly (2024-2025)
entries.engineer_note: Delivery days computed as calendar-date difference (delivered_at::date - placed_at::date), matching the DATEDIFF(day, ...) definition used in Priya's report. Two rows expected, one per carrier_group.

entries.title: Order-level delivery reliability: Albion Parcel vs rest, baseline vs collapse, 2025
entries.question: How much of the November-December delivery slowdown is specifically attributable to Albion Parcel, versus everything else?
entries.sql:
WITH elig_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
fulfillment_counts AS (
  SELECT f.order_id, COUNT(*) AS n_fulfillments
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN elig_orders eo ON eo.order_id = f.order_id
  GROUP BY f.order_id
),
single_fulfillment AS (
  SELECT f.id AS fulfillment_id, f.order_id
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN fulfillment_counts fc ON fc.order_id = f.order_id AND fc.n_fulfillments = 1
),
shipment_counts AS (
  SELECT s.fulfillment_id, COUNT(*) AS n_shipments
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN single_fulfillment sf ON sf.fulfillment_id = s.fulfillment_id
  GROUP BY s.fulfillment_id
),
single_shipment AS (
  SELECT s.fulfillment_id, s.carrier, s.delivered_at
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN shipment_counts sc ON sc.fulfillment_id = s.fulfillment_id AND sc.n_shipments = 1
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT eo.order_id, eo.placed_at, ss.carrier, ss.delivered_at
  FROM elig_orders eo
  JOIN single_fulfillment sf ON sf.order_id = eo.order_id
  JOIN single_shipment ss ON ss.fulfillment_id = sf.fulfillment_id
  WHERE ss.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
labeled AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    CASE WHEN placed_at < DATE '2025-11-01' THEN 'baseline' ELSE 'collapse' END AS period,
    CASE WHEN carrier = 'Albion Parcel' THEN 'Albion Parcel' ELSE 'All other carriers' END AS carrier_group,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (delivered_at - placed_at)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days
  FROM qualified
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    period,
    carrier_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    AVG(delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM labeled
  GROUP BY period, carrier_group
)
SELECT
  carrier_group,
  period,
  orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(avg_delivery_days, 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(pct_within_5_days, 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * orders_fully_delivered / SUM(orders_fully_delivered) OVER (PARTITION BY period), 1) AS share_of_period_orders_pct
FROM agg
ORDER BY period ASC, carrier_group ASC
builds_on: Albion Parcel performance by destination country, baseline vs collapse
Albion Parcel performance by origin warehouse, baseline vs collapse
entries.engineer_note: Aggregated across all tenants/merchants (not merchant-specific); delivery_days computed as delivered_at minus placed_at in fractional days using the single qualifying shipment per order, per the same attribution rule as the weak-carriers-vs-rest report.

entries.title: Order-level delivery reliability: Lowlands Express by destination lane, 2025
entries.question: How much better would Lowlands Express's orders perform, and how much would that help overall, if we only used it on its strong home lanes (Netherlands, Belgium, France) and moved everything else off it?
entries.sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.placed_at,
    o.shipping_address_id,
    s.carrier,
    s.delivered_at,
    (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - o.placed_at)) / 86400.0) AS delivery_days
  FROM orders o
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
  JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
    AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
    AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments s2 WHERE s2.fulfillment_id = f.id) = 1
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT
    t0.order_id,
    t0.delivery_days,
    CASE
      WHEN t0.carrier = 'Lowlands Express' AND c.name IN ('Netherlands', 'Belgium', 'France') THEN 'Lowlands core (NL/BE/FR)'
      WHEN t0.carrier = 'Lowlands Express' THEN 'Lowlands non-core (other countries)'
      ELSE 'All other carriers'
    END AS lane_group
  FROM t0
  LEFT JOIN addresses a ON a.id = t0.shipping_address_id
  LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.id = a.country_id
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT
    t1.lane_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    ROUND(AVG(t1.delivery_days)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t1.delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM t1
  GROUP BY t1.lane_group
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM t1
)
SELECT
  t2.lane_group,
  t2.orders_fully_delivered,
  t2.avg_delivery_days,
  t2.pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * t2.orders_fully_delivered / t3.total_orders, 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
FROM t2
CROSS JOIN t3
ORDER BY
  CASE t2.lane_group
    WHEN 'Lowlands core (NL/BE/FR)' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Lowlands non-core (other countries)' THEN 2
    ELSE 3
  END,
  t2.lane_group
builds_on: Landfall Freight & Lowlands Express performance by destination country, full year 2025
entries.engineer_note: Delivery days computed as delivered_at minus placed_at (no other timestamp was specified for "delivery"); destination country taken from orders.shipping_address_id -> addresses -> countries.name as requested. All three lane_group rows are returned as expected (3 rows total, no truncation).

entries.title: Order-level delivery reliability by carrier, full year 2025 (unified source)
entries.question: What is each carrier's order-level delivery reliability (orders placed to orders delivered, within 5 days), in one single consistent query I can use as the ground truth for a reliability ceiling calculation?
entries.sql:
SELECT carrier, orders_fully_delivered, avg_delivery_days, pct_within_5_days, share_of_orders_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    carrier,
    orders_fully_delivered,
    avg_delivery_days,
    pct_within_5_days,
    share_of_orders_pct
  FROM (
    SELECT
      d.carrier AS carrier,
      COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
      ROUND(CAST(AVG(d.delivery_days) AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
      ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN d.delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
      ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (
        SELECT COUNT(*)
        FROM (
          SELECT o2.id AS order_id
          FROM orders o2
          JOIN fulfillments f2a ON f2a.order_id = o2.id
          JOIN shipments s2a ON s2a.fulfillment_id = f2a.id
          WHERE o2.status = 'fulfilled'
            AND o2.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
            AND o2.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
            AND s2a.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
            AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments ff WHERE ff.order_id = o2.id) = 1
            AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments ss WHERE ss.fulfillment_id = f2a.id) = 1
        ) all_d
      ), 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
    FROM (
      SELECT
        o.id AS order_id,
        s.carrier AS carrier,
        (CAST(s.delivered_at AS DATE) - CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)) AS delivery_days
      FROM orders o
      JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
      JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
      WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
        AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
        AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
        AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
        AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
        AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments s2 WHERE s2.fulfillment_id = f.id) = 1
    ) d
    GROUP BY d.carrier
  ) per_carrier

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    'ALL CARRIERS' AS carrier,
    orders_fully_delivered,
    avg_delivery_days,
    pct_within_5_days,
    100.0 AS share_of_orders_pct
  FROM (
    SELECT
      COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
      ROUND(CAST(AVG(delivery_days) AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
      ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_5_days
    FROM (
      SELECT
        (CAST(s.delivered_at AS DATE) - CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)) AS delivery_days
      FROM orders o
      JOIN fulfillments f ON f.order_id = o.id
      JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id
      WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
        AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00'
        AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
        AND s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
        AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fulfillments f2 WHERE f2.order_id = o.id) = 1
        AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM shipments s2 WHERE s2.fulfillment_id = f.id) = 1
    ) all_orders
  ) totals
) combined
ORDER BY
  (CASE WHEN carrier = 'ALL CARRIERS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
  orders_fully_delivered DESC,
  carrier ASC
builds_on: Order-level delivery reliability: weak carriers vs rest, 2025
Order-level delivery reliability: Lowlands Express by destination lane, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Scoped exactly as specified: orders placed in 2025, status='fulfilled', exactly one fulfillment with exactly one shipment, delivered_at not null, delivery_days = date(delivered_at) - date(placed_at). share_of_orders_pct is each carrier's share of this clean population (denominator is the same filtered set, not all orders tenant-wide), and the ALL CARRIERS row re-aggregates the identical population so it sums correctly against the carrier rows.

entries.title: Order-level delivery reliability by carrier group and quarter, 2025 (unified source)
entries.question: Did Albion Parcel's reliability break down specifically in Q4 while Landfall Freight and Lowlands Express stayed consistently weak all year, when measured in one single consistent query?
entries.sql:
WITH q_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
fulfillment_counts AS (
  SELECT f.order_id, f.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS fulfillment_count
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN q_orders qo ON qo.order_id = f.order_id AND qo.tenant_id = f.tenant_id
  GROUP BY f.order_id, f.tenant_id
),
single_fulfillment AS (
  SELECT fc.order_id, fc.tenant_id
  FROM fulfillment_counts fc
  WHERE fc.fulfillment_count = 1
),
fulfillment_shipment_counts AS (
  SELECT f.id AS fulfillment_id, f.order_id, f.tenant_id, COUNT(s.id) AS shipment_count
  FROM fulfillments f
  JOIN single_fulfillment sf ON sf.order_id = f.order_id AND sf.tenant_id = f.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = f.id AND s.tenant_id = f.tenant_id
  GROUP BY f.id, f.order_id, f.tenant_id
),
qualifying_fulfillments AS (
  SELECT fsc.fulfillment_id, fsc.order_id, fsc.tenant_id
  FROM fulfillment_shipment_counts fsc
  WHERE fsc.shipment_count = 1
),
order_shipment AS (
  SELECT qf.order_id, qf.tenant_id, s.carrier, s.delivered_at
  FROM qualifying_fulfillments qf
  JOIN shipments s ON s.fulfillment_id = qf.fulfillment_id AND s.tenant_id = qf.tenant_id
  WHERE s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
order_detail AS (
  SELECT
    qo.order_id,
    qo.tenant_id,
    qo.placed_at,
    os.carrier,
    os.delivered_at,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (os.delivered_at - qo.placed_at)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days
  FROM q_orders qo
  JOIN order_shipment os ON os.order_id = qo.order_id AND os.tenant_id = qo.tenant_id
),
order_detail_grouped AS (
  SELECT
    od.order_id,
    od.tenant_id,
    od.placed_at,
    od.delivery_days,
    CASE
      WHEN od.carrier IN ('Albion Parcel', 'Landfall Freight', 'Lowlands Express') THEN od.carrier
      ELSE 'All other carriers'
    END AS carrier_group
  FROM order_detail od
),
with_quarter AS (
  SELECT
    odg.order_id,
    odg.delivery_days,
    odg.carrier_group,
    cd.year_num,
    cd.quarter_num
  FROM order_detail_grouped odg
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(odg.placed_at AS DATE)
),
quarter_totals AS (
  SELECT year_num, quarter_num, COUNT(*) AS total_orders
  FROM with_quarter
  GROUP BY year_num, quarter_num
),
group_agg AS (
  SELECT
    year_num,
    quarter_num,
    carrier_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    AVG(delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days,
    AVG(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100 AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM with_quarter
  GROUP BY year_num, quarter_num, carrier_group
)
SELECT
  ga.carrier_group AS carrier_group,
  CONCAT(CAST(ga.year_num AS VARCHAR), '-Q', CAST(ga.quarter_num AS VARCHAR)) AS quarter,
  ga.orders_fully_delivered AS orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(CAST(ga.avg_delivery_days AS NUMERIC), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(CAST(ga.pct_within_5_days AS NUMERIC), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(CAST(ga.orders_fully_delivered * 100.0 / qt.total_orders AS NUMERIC), 1) AS share_of_quarter_orders_pct
FROM group_agg ga
JOIN quarter_totals qt ON qt.year_num = ga.year_num AND qt.quarter_num = ga.quarter_num
ORDER BY
  ga.quarter_num ASC,
  CASE ga.carrier_group
    WHEN 'Albion Parcel' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Landfall Freight' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Lowlands Express' THEN 3
    ELSE 4
  END ASC
builds_on: Order-level delivery reliability: Albion Parcel vs rest, baseline vs collapse, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Built as a single self-contained query per the request: qualifying orders (2025, status='fulfilled', exactly one fulfillment with exactly one shipment, delivered_at not null) are bucketed into the three named carrier groups vs. 'All other carriers' (summed), by calendar quarter of placed_at. share_of_quarter_orders_pct is each group's share of all qualifying orders in that quarter (the four group shares sum to 100%). If a named carrier has zero qualifying orders in some quarter, that row will be absent rather than printed as zero (did not observe this in a dry run since no data is read).

entries.title: Order-level delivery reliability: Lowlands Express by destination lane, full year 2025 (unified re-check)
entries.question: Confirmed and reconciled: how much does Lowlands Express's order-level reliability differ between its home lanes (Netherlands/Belgium/France) and everywhere else, versus the rest of our carriers combined?
entries.sql:
WITH order_fulfillment_counts AS (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS fulfillment_count
  FROM fulfillments
  GROUP BY order_id
),
fulfillment_shipment_counts AS (
  SELECT fulfillment_id, COUNT(*) AS shipment_count
  FROM shipments
  GROUP BY fulfillment_id
),
eligible_orders AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.placed_at,
    o.shipping_address_id,
    f.id AS fulfillment_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_fulfillment_counts ofc
    ON ofc.order_id = o.id AND ofc.fulfillment_count = 1
  JOIN fulfillments f
    ON f.order_id = o.id
  WHERE o.status = 'fulfilled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
eligible_with_shipment AS (
  SELECT
    eo.order_id,
    eo.placed_at,
    eo.shipping_address_id,
    s.carrier,
    s.delivered_at
  FROM eligible_orders eo
  JOIN fulfillment_shipment_counts fsc
    ON fsc.fulfillment_id = eo.fulfillment_id AND fsc.shipment_count = 1
  JOIN shipments s
    ON s.fulfillment_id = eo.fulfillment_id
  WHERE s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
order_lane AS (
  SELECT
    ews.order_id,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (ews.delivered_at - ews.placed_at)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days,
    CASE
      WHEN ews.carrier = 'Lowlands Express' AND c.name IN ('Netherlands', 'Belgium', 'France')
        THEN 'Lowlands core (NL/BE/FR)'
      WHEN ews.carrier = 'Lowlands Express'
        THEN 'Lowlands non-core (other countries)'
      ELSE 'All other carriers combined'
    END AS lane_group
  FROM eligible_with_shipment ews
  LEFT JOIN addresses a ON a.id = ews.shipping_address_id
  LEFT JOIN countries c ON c.id = a.country_id
),
lane_groups AS (
  SELECT 'Lowlands core (NL/BE/FR)' AS lane_group, 1 AS sort_order
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Lowlands non-core (other countries)', 2
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'All other carriers combined', 3
),
lane_stats AS (
  SELECT
    lane_group,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_fully_delivered,
    AVG(delivery_days) AS avg_delivery_days,
    AVG(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 5 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100 AS pct_within_5_days
  FROM order_lane
  GROUP BY lane_group
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(orders_fully_delivered) AS total_orders FROM lane_stats
)
SELECT
  lg.lane_group,
  COALESCE(ls.orders_fully_delivered, 0) AS orders_fully_delivered,
  ROUND(CAST(ls.avg_delivery_days AS numeric), 2) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(CAST(ls.pct_within_5_days AS numeric), 1) AS pct_within_5_days,
  ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ls.orders_fully_delivered, 0) AS numeric) / NULLIF(t.total_orders, 0) * 100, 1) AS share_of_orders_pct
FROM lane_groups lg
LEFT JOIN lane_stats ls ON ls.lane_group = lg.lane_group
CROSS JOIN totals t
ORDER BY lg.sort_order
builds_on: Order-level delivery reliability: Lowlands Express by destination lane, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Applies the same eligibility rule (status='fulfilled', placed_at in 2025, exactly one fulfillment with exactly one shipment, delivered_at not null) as the other two reports in this set; the three lane_group totals sum to that same eligible-order population, so they should reconcile with the full-year carrier report's total.

entries.title: Support agent staffing vs ticket volume, by merchant
entries.question: Are Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij understaffed relative to their ticket volume compared to the rest of the book?
entries.sql:
with t2025 as (
  select
    tenant_id,
    count(*) as tickets_created,
    count(distinct assignee_agent_id) as distinct_agents_handled,
    count(*) filter (where assignee_agent_id is null) as unassigned_count
  from tickets
  where created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' and created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  group by tenant_id
),
agents as (
  select tenant_id, count(*) as registered_agents
  from support_agents
  group by tenant_id
)
select
  ten.name as merchant_name,
  t.tickets_created,
  coalesce(a.registered_agents, 0) as registered_support_agents,
  t.distinct_agents_handled,
  case when t.distinct_agents_handled > 0
       then round(t.tickets_created::decimal / t.distinct_agents_handled, 1)
       else null
  end as tickets_per_active_agent,
  round(100.0 * t.unassigned_count / t.tickets_created, 1) as pct_unassigned
from t2025 t
join tenants ten on ten.id = t.tenant_id
left join agents a on a.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
where t.tickets_created >= 20
order by tickets_per_active_agent desc nulls last, merchant_name asc
limit 50
entries.engineer_note: Row count of the full qualifying-tenant set (before the 50-row cap) will show on the printed report per house standard; the query itself returns at most 50 merchants ranked by tickets-per-active-agent.

entries.title: Ticket channel mix, by merchant
entries.question: Do Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij rely more on slower contact channels (e.g. email) than the rest of the book?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  COUNT(*) AS tickets_2025,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE tk.channel = 'email') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_email,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE tk.channel = 'chat') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_chat,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE tk.channel = 'phone') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_phone,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE tk.channel = 'web') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_web,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE tk.channel = 'social') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_social,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE tk.channel = 'api') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_api
FROM tickets tk
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tk.tenant_id
WHERE tk.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND tk.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY t.id, t.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY tickets_2025 DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant; percentages are rounded to 1 decimal so they may sum to slightly off 100.0 due to rounding. The query caps at 50 rows as requested; the batch report framework will note the total row count returned.

entries.title: Urgent-priority ticket resolution failure, by merchant
entries.question: Is the urgent-ticket resolution failure (missing resolution about half the time, company-wide) concentrated in Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij, or is it a broad pattern across the book?
entries.sql:
SELECT 
  tn.name AS merchant_name,
  u.urgent_created,
  u.urgent_missing,
  ROUND(100.0 * u.urgent_missing / NULLIF(u.urgent_evaluable,0), 1) AS urgent_miss_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.all_missing / NULLIF(a.all_evaluable,0), 1) AS all_priority_miss_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT t.tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS urgent_created,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS urgent_evaluable,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL AND (t.resolved_at IS NULL OR extract(epoch from (t.resolved_at - t.created_at))/60 > sp.resolution_target_minutes) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS urgent_missing
  FROM tickets t
  LEFT JOIN sla_policies sp ON sp.id = t.sla_policy_id
  WHERE t.priority = 'urgent'
    AND t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
) u
JOIN (
  SELECT t.tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS all_evaluable,
    SUM(CASE WHEN t.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL AND (t.resolved_at IS NULL OR extract(epoch from (t.resolved_at - t.created_at))/60 > sp.resolution_target_minutes) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS all_missing
  FROM tickets t
  LEFT JOIN sla_policies sp ON sp.id = t.sla_policy_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
) a ON a.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
JOIN tenants tn ON tn.id = u.tenant_id
WHERE u.urgent_evaluable >= 5
ORDER BY urgent_miss_rate_pct DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: "Urgent tickets created, 2025" is the raw count of urgent tickets opened in 2025 (including any with a null sla_policy_id); the miss-rate denominators and the filter (>=5) use only the evaluable subset (non-null sla_policy_id), per the request. Per-tenant exclusion counts aren't broken out as a column to stay within the 5 requested columns — let me know if you'd like that as a separate report.

entries.title: Ticket complexity proxy (messages and tags per ticket), by merchant
entries.question: Do Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij get harder/more complex tickets than the rest of the book, or just more of them?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  tk.ticket_count AS tickets_2025,
  round(coalesce(msg.total_messages, 0)::numeric / tk.ticket_count, 2) AS avg_messages_per_ticket,
  round(coalesce(msg.total_public, 0)::numeric / tk.ticket_count, 2) AS avg_public_messages_per_ticket,
  round(coalesce(tags.total_tags, 0)::numeric / tk.ticket_count, 2) AS avg_distinct_tags_per_ticket,
  count(*) OVER () AS qualifying_tenant_count
FROM tenants t
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS ticket_count
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) tk ON tk.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ti.tenant_id,
    count(*) AS total_messages,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE tm.is_public) AS total_public
  FROM ticket_messages tm
  JOIN tickets ti ON ti.id = tm.ticket_id AND ti.tenant_id = tm.tenant_id
  WHERE ti.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND ti.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti.tenant_id
) msg ON msg.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT ti.tenant_id,
    count(*) AS total_tags
  FROM ticket_tags_map ttm
  JOIN tickets ti ON ti.id = ttm.ticket_id AND ti.tenant_id = ttm.tenant_id
  WHERE ti.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND ti.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY ti.tenant_id
) tags ON tags.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE tk.ticket_count >= 20
ORDER BY avg_messages_per_ticket DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Support agent staffing vs ticket volume, by merchant
Ticket channel mix, by merchant
entries.engineer_note: One row per tenant with >=20 tickets created in 2025 (same threshold as prior staffing/channel reports); tags are counted as raw ticket_tags_map rows per ticket (duplicate tag assignments, if any, would inflate the average slightly). qualifying_tenant_count column shows the total peer-set size (same value every row) since the report is capped at 50 rows.

entries.title: Urgent-ticket SLA target vs actual resolution time, by merchant
entries.question: Is the broad urgent-ticket resolution failure driven by unrealistically tight SLA targets, or are merchants genuinely resolving urgent tickets slower than a reasonable target?
entries.sql:
WITH evaluable_tickets AS (
  SELECT
    t0.id AS ticket_id,
    t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t0.created_at AS created_at,
    t0.resolved_at AS resolved_at,
    t1.resolution_target_minutes AS resolution_target_minutes,
    CASE WHEN t0.resolved_at IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.resolved_at - t0.created_at)) / 3600.0
    END AS actual_hours,
    CASE
      WHEN t0.resolved_at IS NULL THEN 1
      WHEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.resolved_at - t0.created_at)) / 60.0 > t1.resolution_target_minutes THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END AS is_miss
  FROM tickets t0
  JOIN sla_policies t1 ON t1.id = t0.sla_policy_id
  WHERE t0.priority = 'urgent'
    AND t0.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
    AND t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tenant_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS evaluated_count
  FROM evaluable_tickets
  GROUP BY tenant_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
),
tenant_target AS (
  SELECT e.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(e.resolution_target_minutes) / COUNT(*) / 60.0 AS weighted_target_hours,
    COUNT(DISTINCT e.resolution_target_minutes) AS distinct_target_count
  FROM evaluable_tickets e
  JOIN tenant_counts c ON c.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
  GROUP BY e.tenant_id
),
tenant_actual AS (
  SELECT e.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    AVG(e.actual_hours) AS avg_actual_hours,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY e.actual_hours) AS median_actual_hours
  FROM evaluable_tickets e
  JOIN tenant_counts c ON c.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
  WHERE e.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY e.tenant_id
),
tenant_miss AS (
  SELECT e.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(e.is_miss) AS miss_count
  FROM evaluable_tickets e
  JOIN tenant_counts c ON c.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
  GROUP BY e.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t9.name AS merchant_name,
  ROUND(t1.weighted_target_hours, 1) AS urgent_resolution_target_hours,
  t0.evaluated_count AS urgent_tickets_evaluated_2025,
  ROUND(t2.median_actual_hours, 1) AS median_actual_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(t2.avg_actual_hours, 1) AS avg_actual_resolution_hours,
  ROUND(100.0 * t3.miss_count / t0.evaluated_count, 1) AS urgent_miss_rate_pct,
  CASE WHEN t1.distinct_target_count > 1 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS multiple_urgent_sla_policies
FROM tenant_counts t0
JOIN tenant_target t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN tenant_actual t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
JOIN tenant_miss t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
JOIN tenants t9 ON t9.id = t0.tenant_id
ORDER BY urgent_miss_rate_pct DESC, merchant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Urgent-priority ticket resolution failure, by merchant
entries.engineer_note: Added a 7th column (multiple_urgent_sla_policies, Y/N) to flag tenants whose evaluated urgent tickets reference more than one distinct resolution_target_minutes, as requested, since that can't be folded into the single 'target hours' number; everything else matches the spec exactly. Total qualifying-tenant count and exact row count will show on the printed report since the query itself isn't run here.

entries.title: Ticket load per agent over 2025, hotspot merchants vs a comparable peer
entries.question: Has the staffing gap at Cragsley, Marrowby, and Studio Vrij been widening over the course of 2025 (ticket volume outpacing agent headcount), or has it been consistently stretched all year?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name as merchant_name,
  concat('2025-Q', extract(quarter from tk.created_at)::int) as quarter,
  count(*) as tickets_created,
  count(distinct tk.assignee_agent_id) as distinct_agents,
  round(count(*)::numeric / nullif(count(distinct tk.assignee_agent_id),0), 1) as tickets_per_agent
FROM tickets tk
JOIN tenants t on t.id = tk.tenant_id
WHERE t.name in ('Cragsley Outfitters','Marrowby & Vane','Studio Vrij','Grind Collective')
  AND tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' and tk.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY t.name, extract(quarter from tk.created_at)
ORDER BY t.name, extract(quarter from tk.created_at)
builds_on: Support agent staffing vs ticket volume, by merchant
entries.engineer_note: Grain is tenant x calendar quarter for 2025, limited to the four named tenants; tickets_per_agent is tickets_created / distinct assignee_agent_id (NULL when a tenant/quarter has zero assigned agents).

entries.title: Quarterly urgent-ticket performance, hotspot merchants vs comparison peer
entries.question: Does urgent-ticket resolution specifically get worse in the same quarters where each merchant's ticket-per-agent load spiked?
entries.sql:
WITH q AS (
  SELECT 1 AS q_num, date '2025-01-01' AS q_start, date '2025-04-01' AS q_end
  UNION ALL SELECT 2, date '2025-04-01', date '2025-07-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT 3, date '2025-07-01', date '2025-10-01'
  UNION ALL SELECT 4, date '2025-10-01', date '2026-01-01'
),
m AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Cragsley Outfitters','Marrowby & Vane','Studio Vrij','Grind Collective')
)
SELECT
  m.name AS merchant_name,
  '2025-Q' || q.q_num AS quarter,
  count(tk.id) AS urgent_tickets_evaluated,
  round(
    100.0 * sum(
      case when tk.id is not null
             and (tk.resolved_at is null or tk.resolved_at > tk.created_at + (sp.resolution_target_minutes || ' minutes')::interval)
           then 1 else 0 end
    )::numeric / nullif(count(tk.id), 0)
  , 1) AS urgent_miss_rate_pct,
  round(
    avg(case when tk.resolved_at is not null then extract(epoch from tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at) / 3600.0 end)::numeric
  , 1) AS avg_actual_resolution_hours,
  round(
    percentile_cont(0.5) within group (
      order by case when tk.resolved_at is not null then extract(epoch from tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at) / 3600.0 end
    )::numeric
  , 1) AS median_actual_resolution_hours
FROM m
CROSS JOIN q
LEFT JOIN tickets tk
  ON tk.tenant_id = m.id
  AND tk.priority = 'urgent'
  AND tk.sla_policy_id IS NOT NULL
  AND tk.created_at >= q.q_start AND tk.created_at < q.q_end
LEFT JOIN sla_policies sp ON sp.id = tk.sla_policy_id
GROUP BY m.name, q.q_num
ORDER BY m.name ASC, q.q_num ASC
builds_on: Ticket load per agent over 2025, hotspot merchants vs a comparable peer
Urgent-ticket SLA target vs actual resolution time, by merchant
entries.engineer_note: Built a full 4-tenant x 4-quarter grid with LEFT JOIN so quarters with zero evaluable urgent tickets still print a row (count 0, miss rate/avg/median NULL) instead of silently vanishing. Miss rate denominator and avg/median are strictly over tickets with sla_policy_id not null, per the 'evaluable' definition; resolved_at null is treated as a miss since data ends 2025-12-31.

entries.title: Q4-vs-rest-of-year ticket load per agent, all qualifying merchants
entries.question: Is 'flat support staffing through a seasonal ticket surge' a pattern specific to the three hotspot merchants, or common across the book?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  tn.name AS merchant_name,
  q123.tickets_q123,
  ROUND(q123.avg_agents_q123, 1) AS avg_agents_q1_q3,
  ROUND((q123.tickets_q123 / 3.0) / NULLIF(q123.avg_agents_q123, 0), 1) AS tickets_per_agent_q1_q3,
  q4.tickets_q4,
  q4.agents_q4,
  ROUND(q4.tickets_q4::numeric / NULLIF(q4.agents_q4, 0), 1) AS tickets_per_agent_q4
FROM tenants tn
JOIN (
  SELECT qt.tenant_id,
         SUM(COALESCE(qd.tickets, 0)) AS tickets_q123,
         AVG(COALESCE(qd.agents, 0)) AS avg_agents_q123
  FROM (
    SELECT tenant_id
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' AND created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    GROUP BY tenant_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
  ) qt
  CROSS JOIN (SELECT 1 AS q UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3) quarters
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT tenant_id,
           EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM created_at) AS q,
           COUNT(*) AS tickets,
           COUNT(DISTINCT assignee_agent_id) AS agents
    FROM tickets
    WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01' AND created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01'
    GROUP BY tenant_id, EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM created_at)
  ) qd ON qd.tenant_id = qt.tenant_id AND qd.q = quarters.q
  GROUP BY qt.tenant_id
) q123 ON q123.tenant_id = tn.id
JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
         COUNT(*) AS tickets_q4,
         COUNT(DISTINCT assignee_agent_id) AS agents_q4
  FROM tickets
  WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01' AND created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
) q4 ON q4.tenant_id = tn.id
ORDER BY tickets_per_agent_q4 DESC, merchant_name ASC
builds_on: Support agent staffing vs ticket volume, by merchant
Ticket load per agent over 2025, hotspot merchants vs a comparable peer
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per qualifying tenant (>=20 tickets created in 2025), as requested. Q1-Q3 quarterly agent counts are zero-filled for any quarter with no tickets so the three-quarter average divisor is always 3, matching the spec exactly.

entries.title: Urgent-ticket resolution-time distribution, slow merchants vs a fast baseline
entries.question: Is the big three's inflated average urgent resolution time caused by a handful of extreme-delay tickets, or by generally slow handling across the board?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  COUNT(*) AS urgent_tickets_evaluated,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_within_8h,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_8h_24h,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_1d_3d,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_3d_7d,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN b.bucket = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_over_7d_or_unresolved
FROM (
  SELECT
    tk.id,
    tk.tenant_id,
    CASE
