  group by tenant_id
),
ranked_days as (
  select tenant_id, day_count,
    row_number() over (partition by tenant_id order by day_count desc) as rn
  from day_counts
),
top3_days as (
  select tenant_id, sum(day_count) as top3_sum
  from ranked_days
  where rn <= 3
  group by tenant_id
)
select
  tt.tenant_name,
  du.distinct_user_agents,
  round(100.0 * tu.top_ua_count / tt.total_failed, 1) as top_user_agent_share_pct,
  dd.distinct_calendar_days_with_failures,
  md.max_failed_attempts_single_day,
  round(100.0 * t3.top3_sum / tt.total_failed, 1) as pct_failed_attempts_in_top_3_days
from tenant_totals tt
join distinct_ua du on du.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
join top_ua tu on tu.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
join distinct_days dd on dd.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
join max_day md on md.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
join top3_days t3 on t3.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
order by tt.tenant_name
builds_on: February 2025 failed login concentration by merchant
entries.engineer_note: One row per tenant as requested, computed solely from login_attempts (succeeded=false, Feb 2025) for the three named tenants; distinct_calendar_days_with_failures is a raw count of days with at least one failure (out of the 28 in February), not a percentage.

entries.title: Quarterly failed-login rate history for the 3 Feb-2025-affected merchants
entries.question: For the 3 merchants behind the February 2025 spike, was that an isolated one-quarter event, or do they show a recurring pattern of elevated login failures over the full history?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT t.id AS tenant_id, t.name AS tenant_name, c.year_num, c.quarter_num
  FROM tenants t
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT year_num, quarter_num
    FROM calendar_days
    WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
  ) c
  WHERE t.name IN ('Cragsley Outfitters', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij')
)
SELECT
  b.tenant_name AS tenant_name,
  b.year_num || '-Q' || b.quarter_num AS quarter,
  COALESCE(ta.total_attempts, 0) AS total_attempts,
  COALESCE(fa.failed_attempts, 0) AS failed_attempts,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ta.total_attempts, 0) = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(fa.failed_attempts, 0) / ta.total_attempts, 2)
  END AS pct_failed
FROM base b
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT la.tenant_id, cd.year_num, cd.quarter_num, COUNT(*) AS total_attempts
  FROM login_attempts la
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(la.occurred_at AS DATE)
  GROUP BY la.tenant_id, cd.year_num, cd.quarter_num
) ta ON ta.tenant_id = b.tenant_id AND ta.year_num = b.year_num AND ta.quarter_num = b.quarter_num
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT la.tenant_id, cd.year_num, cd.quarter_num, COUNT(*) AS failed_attempts
  FROM login_attempts la
  JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(la.occurred_at AS DATE)
  WHERE la.succeeded = false
  GROUP BY la.tenant_id, cd.year_num, cd.quarter_num
) fa ON fa.tenant_id = b.tenant_id AND fa.year_num = b.year_num AND fa.quarter_num = b.quarter_num
ORDER BY b.tenant_name, b.year_num, b.quarter_num
builds_on: February 2025 failed login concentration by merchant
entries.engineer_note: Grain is tenant x quarter as requested (36 rows, 2023-Q1..2025-Q4), with zero-activity quarters shown as 0 rather than omitted; pct_failed is set to 0 (not null) when total_attempts is 0.

entries.title: Pre-2023 data subject requests: status and completion check
entries.question: Do the 12 data_subject_requests rows with received_at before 2023-01-01 represent any hidden backlog or unresolved risk, outside the window we've otherwise been reporting on?
entries.sql:
select
  status,
  count(*) as count,
  count(completed_at) as count_with_completed_at,
  min(received_at) as min_received_at,
  max(received_at) as max_received_at
from data_subject_requests
where received_at < date '2023-01-01'
group by status

builds_on: Row counts by year for tables with pre-2023 timestamps
entries.engineer_note: One row per status among the 12 pre-2023 data_subject_requests rows, with counts, how many have a completed_at set, and the received_at range per status, as requested.

entries.title: Daily failed-login and access-denied alignment for the 3 merchants in February 2025
entries.question: Did the February 2025 failure spike hit the same calendar days across all three affected merchants (pointing to one shared platform cause), and was access-denied logging silent specifically on those spike days?
entries.sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name
  FROM tenants
  WHERE name ILIKE '%cragsley%' OR name ILIKE '%marrowby%' OR name ILIKE '%studio vrij%'
),
days AS (
  SELECT calendar_date
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2025-02-01' AND calendar_date <= DATE '2025-02-28'
),
failed_logins AS (
  SELECT
    la.tenant_id,
    DATE(la.occurred_at) AS login_date,
    COUNT(*) AS failed_count
  FROM login_attempts la
  JOIN target_tenants tt ON tt.id = la.tenant_id
  WHERE la.succeeded = false
    AND la.occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01'
    AND la.occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01'
  GROUP BY la.tenant_id, DATE(la.occurred_at)
),
access_denied_all AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log
  WHERE action = 'access_denied'
    AND occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01'
    AND occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT tenant_id, occurred_at
  FROM audit_log_archive
  WHERE action = 'access_denied'
    AND occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01'
    AND occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01'
),
access_denied_daily AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(ad.occurred_at) AS event_date,
    COUNT(*) AS access_denied_count
  FROM access_denied_all ad
  JOIN target_tenants tt ON tt.id = ad.tenant_id
  GROUP BY DATE(ad.occurred_at)
)
SELECT
  d.calendar_date AS date,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN tt.name ILIKE '%cragsley%' THEN fl.failed_count END), 0) AS cragsley_failed_logins,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN tt.name ILIKE '%marrowby%' THEN fl.failed_count END), 0) AS marrowby_vane_failed_logins,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN tt.name ILIKE '%studio vrij%' THEN fl.failed_count END), 0) AS studio_vrij_failed_logins,
  COALESCE(SUM(fl.failed_count), 0) AS total_failed_logins_3_merchants,
  COALESCE(MAX(adn.access_denied_count), 0) AS access_denied_events_3_merchants
FROM days d
LEFT JOIN failed_logins fl ON fl.login_date = d.calendar_date
LEFT JOIN target_tenants tt ON tt.id = fl.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN access_denied_daily adn ON adn.event_date = d.calendar_date
GROUP BY d.calendar_date
ORDER BY d.calendar_date ASC
builds_on: February 2025 failed login concentration by merchant
February 2025 failed-login pattern diagnostics for the 3 affected merchants
Audit log volume and actor identification by month
entries.engineer_note: Tenants are matched by name via ILIKE ('%cragsley%', '%marrowby%', '%studio vrij%') since no tenant IDs were supplied; please confirm these resolve to exactly the intended 3 tenants with no unintended matches.

entries.title: Cart contents: stalled vs. fast-converting carts, 2025
entries.question: Does basket size, price point, or discount usage differ between carts that convert quickly and carts that stall for hours or days?
entries.sql:
WITH tenant_filter AS (
  SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
cart_base AS (
  SELECT c.id, c.tenant_id, c.status, c.item_count, c.subtotal, c.currency_code, c.created_at,
         coalesce(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) AS resolved_at,
         er.rate AS eur_rate
  FROM carts c
  JOIN tenant_filter tf ON tf.id = c.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code='EUR' AND er.quote_code = c.currency_code AND er.as_of = c.created_at::date
  WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
cart_calc AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE WHEN currency_code='EUR' THEN subtotal ELSE subtotal / NULLIF(eur_rate,0) END AS subtotal_eur,
    CASE WHEN resolved_at IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at))/3600.0 END AS resolution_hours
  FROM cart_base
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE
      WHEN resolution_hours IS NULL THEN 'unresolved/still active'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 1 THEN '<1 hour'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 24 THEN '1-24 hours'
      WHEN resolution_hours < 168 THEN '1-7 days'
      ELSE '>7 days'
    END AS duration_bucket
  FROM cart_calc
),
order_discount_flag AS (
  SELECT o.cart_id, CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts od WHERE od.order_id = o.id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_discount
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.cart_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  b.duration_bucket AS duration_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
  ROUND(AVG(b.item_count)::numeric, 2) AS avg_item_count,
  ROUND(AVG(b.subtotal_eur)::numeric, 2) AS avg_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY b.subtotal_eur)::numeric, 2) AS median_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.status='converted') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_converted,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.status='converted' AND odf.has_discount=1) / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.status='converted'),0), 1) AS pct_converted_with_discount
FROM bucketed b
LEFT JOIN order_discount_flag odf ON odf.cart_id = b.id
GROUP BY b.duration_bucket
ORDER BY CASE b.duration_bucket
  WHEN '<1 hour' THEN 1
  WHEN '1-24 hours' THEN 2
  WHEN '1-7 days' THEN 3
  WHEN '>7 days' THEN 4
  WHEN 'unresolved/still active' THEN 5
END
builds_on: Cart abandonment timing by tenant, Q4 2025 (retail merchants)
entries.engineer_note: One row per duration bucket as specified, 5 rows total. Carts in EUR are passed through subtotal unchanged; other currencies divided by the matching exchange_rates.rate (EUR->currency) for the cart's creation date.

entries.title: Cart bleed trend by month, 2025
entries.question: Is the cart-stage drop-off getting better, worse, or staying flat over the past year?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  cd.month_label AS month,
  COUNT(*) AS carts_created,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.status = 'converted') / COUNT(*), 1) AS overall_conversion_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at <= INTERVAL '1 hour') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_resolved_within_1_hour,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at > INTERVAL '1 hour' AND COALESCE(c.converted_at, c.abandoned_at, c.expires_at) - c.created_at <= INTERVAL '7 days') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_resolved_1_7_days,
  ROUND(CAST(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (c.converted_at - c.created_at))/86400.0) FILTER (WHERE c.status = 'converted') AS numeric), 1) AS median_days_to_convert
FROM carts c
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(c.created_at AS date)
WHERE t.name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
  AND c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY cd.month_label
ORDER BY cd.month_label
builds_on: Cart abandonment timing by tenant, Q4 2025 (retail merchants)
Cart abandonment: cliff or slow bleed, Q4 2025 (non-subscription merchants)
entries.engineer_note: pct_resolved_within_1_hour and pct_resolved_1_7_days are both computed as a share of all carts created in the month (same denominator as overall conversion), using resolution_time = coalesce(converted_at, abandoned_at, expires_at) - created_at; carts with none of those timestamps set (still open/no expiry recorded) fall outside both buckets. 12 rows expected, one per month of 2025.

entries.title: Subscription merchants: do customers browse before vs. after their first order?
entries.question: Is the near-zero web-session count for subscription merchants a tracking blind spot, or does it reflect real behavior — customers browsing once to sign up and then never browsing again?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
  COUNT(*) AS customers,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cust.before_cnt > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_with_session_before,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN cust.after_cnt > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_with_session_after,
  ROUND(AVG(cust.after_cnt), 2) AS avg_sessions_after_first_order_per_customer
FROM (
  SELECT fo.tenant_id, fo.user_id, fo.first_order_at,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM web_sessions ws WHERE ws.tenant_id = fo.tenant_id AND ws.user_id = fo.user_id AND ws.started_at <= fo.first_order_at) AS before_cnt,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM web_sessions ws WHERE ws.tenant_id = fo.tenant_id AND ws.user_id = fo.user_id AND ws.started_at > fo.first_order_at) AS after_cnt
  FROM (
    SELECT tenant_id, user_id, MIN(placed_at) AS first_order_at
    FROM orders
    WHERE tenant_id IN (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Brennquell Kaffee','Spice Route Box','Grind Collective','Honeycomb Larder'))
    GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
  ) fo
) cust
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = cust.tenant_id
GROUP BY t.name
ORDER BY t.name
builds_on: Session-tracking coverage vs order volume for top merchants, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Customers are distinct (tenant_id,user_id) pairs from orders (any status) per tenant; web_sessions are matched by tenant_id+user_id (anonymous pre-login sessions without a user_id are not linked to a customer and so can't be counted as 'before' browsing for them). All 4 named subscription tenants are included by name match against tenants.

entries.title: Cart conversion by week at Cragsley Outfitters around the Nov 24 reminder-email outage
entries.question: Did cart conversion dip during the week cart-reminder emails broke (week of Nov 24, 2025), suggesting those reminders meaningfully nudge stalled carts toward purchase?
entries.sql:
with tenant as (
  select id as tenant_id
  from tenants
  where name = 'Cragsley Outfitters'
),
cart_weeks as (
  select
    c.id,
    c.status,
    c.created_at,
    c.converted_at,
    cd.week_start
  from carts c
  join tenant t on c.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  join calendar_days cd on cd.calendar_date = c.created_at::date
  where cd.week_start >= date '2025-10-06'
    and cd.week_start <= date '2025-12-22'
)
select
  week_start,
  count(*) as carts_created,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when status = 'converted' then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as overall_conversion_pct,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when status = 'converted' and converted_at is not null
            and extract(epoch from (converted_at - created_at)) / 3600.0 <= 1
            then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_converted_within_1_hour,
  round(100.0 * sum(case when status = 'converted' and converted_at is not null
            and extract(epoch from (converted_at - created_at)) / 3600.0 >= 24
            and extract(epoch from (converted_at - created_at)) / 3600.0 <= 168
            then 1 else 0 end) / count(*), 1) as pct_converted_1_to_7_days
from cart_weeks
group by week_start
order by week_start asc
builds_on: Cart bleed trend by month, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Resolution-time buckets: "within 1 hour" = <=1h since created_at; "1-7 days" = 24h-168h inclusive (converted_at - created_at). Carts converting between 1h and 24h aren't shown in either bucket, consistent with prior cart-timing report definitions.

entries.title: Cart value tier vs. conversion speed, 2025
entries.question: Is checkout hesitation concentrated in higher-priced carts specifically (not just low-item-count carts), i.e. does price point on its own predict stalling?
entries.sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
cart_population AS (
  SELECT c.id, c.tenant_id, c.currency_code, c.subtotal, c.item_count, c.status, c.created_at, c.converted_at
  FROM carts c
  JOIN target_tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND c.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
cart_with_eur AS (
  SELECT cp.*,
    CASE WHEN cp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN cp.subtotal
         ELSE cp.subtotal / er.rate END AS subtotal_eur
  FROM cart_population cp
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = cp.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(cp.created_at AS DATE)
),
tiered_carts AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE
      WHEN subtotal_eur < 50 THEN '<€50'
      WHEN subtotal_eur < 100 THEN '€50-100'
      WHEN subtotal_eur < 200 THEN '€100-200'
      ELSE '€200+'
    END AS price_tier,
    CASE WHEN status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_converted,
    CASE WHEN status = 'converted' AND converted_at <= created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS resolved_1h,
    CASE WHEN status = 'converted' AND converted_at > created_at + INTERVAL '1 day' AND converted_at <= created_at + INTERVAL '7 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS resolved_1_7d
  FROM cart_with_eur
),
tier_totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_carts FROM tiered_carts
),
tier_aggregates AS (
  SELECT
    price_tier,
    COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
    AVG(item_count) AS avg_item_count,
    SUM(is_converted) AS converted_count,
    SUM(resolved_1h) AS resolved_1h_count,
    SUM(resolved_1_7d) AS resolved_1_7d_count
  FROM tiered_carts
  GROUP BY price_tier
)
SELECT
  ta.price_tier AS price_tier,
  ta.cart_count AS cart_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.cart_count / tt.total_carts, 2) AS pct_of_total_carts,
  ROUND(ta.avg_item_count, 2) AS avg_item_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.converted_count / ta.cart_count, 2) AS overall_conversion_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.resolved_1h_count / ta.cart_count, 2) AS pct_resolved_within_1_hour,
  ROUND(100.0 * ta.resolved_1_7d_count / ta.cart_count, 2) AS pct_resolved_in_1_7_days
FROM tier_aggregates ta
CROSS JOIN tier_totals tt
ORDER BY
  CASE ta.price_tier
    WHEN '<€50' THEN 1
    WHEN '€50-100' THEN 2
    WHEN '€100-200' THEN 3
    WHEN '€200+' THEN 4
  END
builds_on: Cart contents: stalled vs. fast-converting carts, 2025
entries.engineer_note: I did not have the exact wording of the "prior cart-timing reports," so I defined conversion/resolution the standard way: overall_conversion_pct = share of carts with status='converted'; pct_resolved_within_1_hour = share converted within 1 hour of created_at; pct_resolved_in_1_7_days = share converted strictly between 1 and 7 days after created_at (carts converted in the 1-hour-to-1-day gap are not double-counted in either bucket). Please flag if the prior reports used different cutoffs.

entries.title: Do stalled carts that receive an email convert more often?
entries.question: Among carts that don't convert within the first hour, is there already an organic recovery nudge happening (an email reaching the shopper), and does it correlate with eventually converting?
entries.sql:
WITH six_tenants AS (
  SELECT id FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
population AS (
  SELECT c.id, c.tenant_id, c.user_id, c.status, c.converted_at, c.created_at
  FROM carts c
  JOIN six_tenants st ON st.id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c.created_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
    AND NOT (c.status = 'converted' AND c.converted_at IS NOT NULL AND c.converted_at <= c.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour')
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT p.*,
    CASE WHEN p.user_id IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM email_log e
      WHERE e.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
        AND e.user_id = p.user_id
        AND e.sent_at > p.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour'
        AND e.sent_at <= p.created_at + INTERVAL '48 hour'
    ) THEN 'received_email' ELSE 'no_email' END AS grp
  FROM population p
),
agg AS (
  SELECT grp,
    COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE user_id IS NULL) AS guest_cart_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'converted') AS converted_count
  FROM grouped
  GROUP BY grp
),
medians AS (
  SELECT grp,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (converted_at - created_at))/86400.0) AS median_days_to_convert
  FROM grouped
  WHERE status = 'converted'
  GROUP BY grp
)
SELECT
  a.grp AS group_name,
  a.cart_count,
  a.guest_cart_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.converted_count / a.cart_count, 1) AS pct_eventually_converted,
  ROUND(m.median_days_to_convert::numeric, 1) AS median_days_to_convert
FROM agg a
LEFT JOIN medians m ON m.grp = a.grp
ORDER BY CASE WHEN a.grp = 'received_email' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, a.grp
builds_on: Cart abandonment timing by tenant, Q4 2025 (retail merchants)
entries.engineer_note: Added a guest_cart_count column (carts with null user_id, always bucketed into 'no_email') alongside the requested 4 metrics so the report itself shows what share of 'no_email' is guest traffic without a possible recovery email, per your flag-in-notes request — this didn't warrant a separate report since it's a supporting breakdown of the same no_email group, not a new question.

entries.title: Email nudge effect on stalled carts, controlling for guest vs. logged-in customers
entries.question: Once we separate carts that could never receive an email (guests) from logged-in customers who simply weren't emailed, does receiving an email still look like it drives recovery?
entries.sql:
WITH base_carts AS (
  SELECT c.tenant_id, c.user_id, c.status, c.created_at, c.converted_at,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM email_log e
      WHERE e.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
        AND e.user_id = c.user_id
        AND e.sent_at >= c.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour'
        AND e.sent_at <= c.created_at + INTERVAL '48 hour'
    ) AS has_email
  FROM carts c
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Kibblewick','Studio Vrij','Petalcourt Beauty','Marrowby & Vane','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik')
    AND c.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c.created_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
    AND NOT (c.status = 'converted' AND c.converted_at IS NOT NULL AND c.converted_at <= c.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour')
),
grouped AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN user_id IS NULL THEN 'guest'
      WHEN has_email THEN 'received_email'
      ELSE 'logged_in_no_email'
    END AS group_name,
    status,
    converted_at,
    created_at
  FROM base_carts
)
SELECT
  group_name AS "group",
  COUNT(*) AS cart_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'converted') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_eventually_converted,
  ROUND(
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (
      ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (converted_at - created_at)) / 86400.0
    ) FILTER (WHERE status = 'converted')
  , 1) AS median_days_to_convert
FROM grouped
GROUP BY group_name
ORDER BY CASE group_name WHEN 'received_email' THEN 1 WHEN 'logged_in_no_email' THEN 2 WHEN 'guest' THEN 3 END
builds_on: Do stalled carts that receive an email convert more often?
entries.engineer_note: Used the same cart population/exclusion and 'eventually converted' (cart.status='converted', any time) and median-days-to-convert (converted_at - created_at) definitions as the prior stalled-carts report; 'received_email' requires a matching email_log row (same tenant_id/user_id) with sent_at in (created_at+1h, created_at+48h).

entries.title: Daily cart conversion at Cragsley Outfitters, Nov 17 – Dec 1 2025
entries.question: Is there a visible conversion dip in the first few days after cart-reminder emails broke (Nov 24), before Black Friday/Cyber Monday demand likely swamps the signal?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  c.created_at::date AS cart_date,
  COUNT(*) AS carts_created,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS overall_conversion_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.status = 'converted' AND c.converted_at IS NOT NULL AND c.converted_at <= c.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_converted_within_1_hour
FROM carts c
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
WHERE t.name = 'Cragsley Outfitters'
  AND c.created_at >= DATE '2025-11-17'
  AND c.created_at < DATE '2025-12-02'
GROUP BY c.created_at::date
ORDER BY cart_date ASC
builds_on: Cart conversion by week at Cragsley Outfitters around the Nov 24 reminder-email outage
entries.engineer_note: Conversion = cart status 'converted'; within-1-hour = converted_at minus created_at <= 1 hour, matching the standard cart-conversion definitions used in prior weekly reports. 15 rows expected (Nov 17 - Dec 1 2025), one per day, no truncation.

entries.title: Single-item vs. multi-item cart conversion, by tenant
entries.question: Does the pattern 'small, single-item carts convert worse than multi-item carts' hold consistently across all 6 retail merchants, or is it driven by one or two of them?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.name AS tenant_name,
  COALESCE(t1.single_count, 0) AS single_item_cart_count,
  COALESCE(t2.single_conv_pct, 0) AS single_item_conversion_pct,
  COALESCE(t3.multi_count, 0) AS multi_item_cart_count,
  COALESCE(t4.multi_conv_pct, 0) AS multi_item_conversion_pct,
  COALESCE(t4.multi_conv_pct, 0) - COALESCE(t2.single_conv_pct, 0) AS gap_in_points
FROM tenants t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT c0.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS single_count
  FROM carts c0
  WHERE c0.item_count = 1
    AND c0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY c0.tenant_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT c1.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c1.status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS single_conv_pct
  FROM carts c1
  WHERE c1.item_count = 1
    AND c1.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c1.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY c1.tenant_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT c2.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS multi_count
  FROM carts c2
  WHERE c2.item_count >= 2
    AND c2.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c2.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY c2.tenant_id
) t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT c3.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c3.status = 'converted' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS multi_conv_pct
  FROM carts c3
  WHERE c3.item_count >= 2
    AND c3.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c3.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY c3.tenant_id
) t4 ON t4.tenant_id = t0.id
WHERE t0.name IN ('Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik')
ORDER BY gap_in_points DESC, tenant_name ASC
builds_on: Cart contents: stalled vs. fast-converting carts, 2025
Cart value tier vs. conversion speed, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Conversion pct is computed directly from carts.status = 'converted' per item-count group, as specified; carts with item_count = 0 (if any exist) are excluded from both groups since they match neither = 1 nor >= 2.

entries.title: Single-item vs. multi-item conversion, controlling for guest vs. logged-in status
entries.question: Does the 'single-item carts convert worse' pattern hold once we separate out guest (never logged in) carts, or is it mostly just another expression of the guest-vs-logged-in gap?
entries.sql:
with target_tenants as (
    select id, name
    from tenants
    where name in ('Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty', 'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik')
),
scoped_carts as (
    select
        c.id,
        c.status,
        case when c.user_id is null then 'guest' else 'logged_in' end as user_status,
        case when c.item_count = 1 then 'single-item' else 'multi-item' end as item_count_group
    from carts c
    join target_tenants t on t.id = c.tenant_id
    where c.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
      and c.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
      and c.item_count >= 1
),
grouped as (
    select
        user_status,
        item_count_group,
        count(*) as cart_count,
        sum(case when status = 'converted' then 1 else 0 end) as converted_count
    from scoped_carts
    group by user_status, item_count_group
)
select
    user_status,
    item_count_group,
    cart_count,
    round(100.0 * converted_count / cart_count, 1) as conversion_pct
from grouped
order by
    case
        when user_status = 'logged_in' and item_count_group = 'multi-item' then 1
        when user_status = 'logged_in' and item_count_group = 'single-item' then 2
        when user_status = 'guest' and item_count_group = 'multi-item' then 3
        when user_status = 'guest' and item_count_group = 'single-item' then 4
    end
builds_on: Single-item vs. multi-item cart conversion, by tenant
Email nudge effect on stalled carts, controlling for guest vs. logged-in customers
entries.engineer_note: Excluded carts with item_count = 0 per the request's note (if any exist); all other filters applied as specified. 4 rows, one per user-status x item-count-group cell.

entries.title: What kind of email reaches shoppers who recover a stalled cart?
entries.question: Is the email that correlates with cart recovery a deliberate cart-reminder/recovery mechanism, or just general marketing/engagement email that happens to land in that window?
entries.sql:
WITH t0 AS ( -- stalled carts: created in window, not converted within first hour
  SELECT
    c0.id AS cart_id,
    c0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    c0.user_id AS user_id,
    c0.created_at AS created_at
  FROM carts c0
  JOIN tenants t0t ON t0t.id = c0.tenant_id
  WHERE t0t.name IN (
      'Kibblewick', 'Studio Vrij', 'Petalcourt Beauty',
      'Marrowby & Vane', 'Cragsley Outfitters', 'Ampfeld Elektronik'
    )
    AND c0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND c0.created_at < DATE '2025-12-01'
    AND NOT (
      c0.status = 'converted'
      AND c0.converted_at IS NOT NULL
      AND c0.converted_at <= c0.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour'
    )
),
t1 AS ( -- distinct matched email_log rows per stalled cart owner, in the recovery window
  SELECT DISTINCT
    e1.id AS email_log_id,
    e1.template_id AS template_id
  FROM email_log e1
  JOIN t0 ON t0.tenant_id = e1.tenant_id
         AND t0.user_id = e1.user_id
         AND e1.sent_at >= t0.created_at + INTERVAL '1 hour'
         AND e1.sent_at <= t0.created_at + INTERVAL '48 hour'
),
t2 AS ( -- email counts per template (NULL template_id rows collapse into one 'ad hoc' group)
  SELECT
    t1.template_id AS template_id,
    COUNT(*) AS email_count
  FROM t1
  GROUP BY t1.template_id
),
t3 AS ( -- grand total of matched emails, for pct calc
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_matched
  FROM t1
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(nt.code, 'no template / ad hoc') AS template_code,
  COALESCE(nt.name, 'no template / ad hoc') AS template_name,
  COALESCE(nt.channel, 'n/a') AS channel,
  t2.email_count AS email_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * t2.email_count / NULLIF(t3.total_matched, 0), 2) AS pct_of_matched_emails
FROM t2
CROSS JOIN t3
LEFT JOIN notification_templates nt ON nt.id = t2.template_id
ORDER BY t2.email_count DESC, template_code
builds_on: Do stalled carts that receive an email convert more often?
Email nudge effect on stalled carts, controlling for guest vs. logged-in customers
entries.engineer_note: Each matched email_log row is counted once even if it fell inside the recovery window of more than one stalled cart for the same user (DISTINCT on email_log.id), to keep email_count from double-counting. 'Stalled' is operationalized as: cart created in range and not (status='converted' with converted_at within 1h of created_at) — carts lacking any converted_at are treated as stalled.

entries.title: Weekday-matched cart conversion baseline for Cragsley Outfitters, Sep 29 – Nov 25 2025
entries.question: Were Nov 24-25 (the start of the reminder-email outage) unusually low for their day of week, or within normal week-to-week variation?
entries.sql:
select
  cd.calendar_date as date,
  cd.day_name as day_of_week,
  count(*) as carts_created,
  round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where c.status = 'converted') / count(*), 1) as overall_conversion_pct
from carts c
join tenants t on t.id = c.tenant_id
join calendar_days cd on cd.calendar_date = date(c.created_at)
where t.name = 'Cragsley Outfitters'
  and cd.calendar_date between date '2025-09-29' and date '2025-11-25'
  and cd.iso_day_of_week in (1, 2)
group by cd.calendar_date, cd.day_name
order by cd.calendar_date asc
builds_on: Daily cart conversion at Cragsley Outfitters, Nov 17 – Dec 1 2025
entries.engineer_note: One row per date for every Monday/Tuesday from 2025-09-29 to 2025-11-25 (18 rows), carts_created and overall_conversion_pct computed over all carts created that date regardless of status lifecycle timing, matching the prior Cragsley daily report definition.

entries.title: Order-to-payment match rate by order age
entries.question: At the portfolio level, how much of the gap between order value and money collected is just timing (recent orders not yet settled) versus a permanent shortfall that age doesn't fix?
entries.sql:
WITH order_base AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.grand_total,
    o.currency_code,
    o.placed_at,
    (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) AS age_days,
    CASE
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 3 THEN '0-3 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 7 THEN '4-7 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 14 THEN '8-14 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 30 THEN '15-30 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 60 THEN '31-60 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 90 THEN '61-90 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 180 THEN '91-180 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(o.placed_at AS date)) <= 365 THEN '181-365 days'
      ELSE '366+ days'
    END AS age_bucket
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
order_count_agg AS (
  SELECT t0.age_bucket, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM order_base t0
  GROUP BY t0.age_bucket
),
grand_total_agg AS (
  SELECT t1.age_bucket, SUM(t1.grand_total / t2.rate) AS orders_grand_total_eur
  FROM order_base t1
  JOIN exchange_rates t2
    ON t2.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND t2.quote_code = t1.currency_code
    AND t2.as_of = CAST(t1.placed_at AS date)
  GROUP BY t1.age_bucket
),
payment_agg AS (
  SELECT t3.age_bucket, SUM(t4.amount / t5.rate) AS matched_money_collected_eur
  FROM order_base t3
  JOIN payments t4
    ON t4.order_id = t3.order_id
    AND t4.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
  JOIN exchange_rates t5
    ON t5.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND t5.quote_code = t4.currency_code
    AND t5.as_of = CAST(t4.captured_at AS date)
  GROUP BY t3.age_bucket
)
SELECT
  t6.age_bucket,
  t6.order_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t7.orders_grand_total_eur, 0), 2) AS orders_grand_total_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t8.matched_money_collected_eur, 0), 2) AS matched_money_collected_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t8.matched_money_collected_eur, 0) / NULLIF(t7.orders_grand_total_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS match_rate_pct
FROM order_count_agg t6
LEFT JOIN grand_total_agg t7 ON t7.age_bucket = t6.age_bucket
LEFT JOIN payment_agg t8 ON t8.age_bucket = t6.age_bucket
ORDER BY
  CASE t6.age_bucket
    WHEN '0-3 days' THEN 1
    WHEN '4-7 days' THEN 2
    WHEN '8-14 days' THEN 3
    WHEN '15-30 days' THEN 4
    WHEN '31-60 days' THEN 5
    WHEN '61-90 days' THEN 6
    WHEN '91-180 days' THEN 7
    WHEN '181-365 days' THEN 8
    ELSE 9
  END
builds_on: Order-to-payment gap re-measured with refund-inclusive payment status
entries.engineer_note: Built exactly as specified: age bucketed from 2025-12-31 minus placed_at, grand_total and matched payments (captured/refunded/partially_refunded) each converted to EUR via same-day exchange_rates, match_rate_pct = matched/grand_total*100 rounded to 1dp. Buckets with zero grand_total (none expected) would show a null match rate.

entries.title: Late-refund concentration and trend by merchant
entries.question: Is the refund-after-payout-settled problem concentrated in a handful of merchants, and did it get bigger or smaller in the second half of 2025 versus the first?
entries.sql:
WITH late_refunds AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id, pr.processed_at, pr.amount, pr.currency_code
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN payout_items pi ON pi.payment_id = pr.payment_id
  JOIN payouts po ON po.id = pi.payout_id
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at > po.paid_at
),
converted AS (
  SELECT
    lr.tenant_id,
    lr.processed_at,
    CASE WHEN lr.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN lr.amount
         ELSE lr.amount / er.rate END AS eur_amount
  FROM late_refunds lr
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = lr.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(lr.processed_at AS date)
),
tenant_totals AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    SUM(eur_amount) FILTER (WHERE processed_at < DATE '2025-07-01') AS h1_2025_late_refund_eur,
    SUM(eur_amount) FILTER (WHERE processed_at >= DATE '2025-07-01') AS h2_2025_late_refund_eur
  FROM converted
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
totals AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    COALESCE(h1_2025_late_refund_eur,0) + COALESCE(h2_2025_late_refund_eur,0) AS total_2025_late_refund_eur,
    h1_2025_late_refund_eur, h2_2025_late_refund_eur
  FROM tenant_totals
),
grand_total AS (
  SELECT SUM(total_2025_late_refund_eur) AS grand_total_eur FROM totals
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  ROUND(tot.h1_2025_late_refund_eur, 2) AS h1_2025_late_refund_eur,
  ROUND(tot.h2_2025_late_refund_eur, 2) AS h2_2025_late_refund_eur,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(tot.h1_2025_late_refund_eur,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND((tot.h2_2025_late_refund_eur - tot.h1_2025_late_refund_eur) / tot.h1_2025_late_refund_eur * 100, 1)
  END AS change_pct,
  ROUND(tot.total_2025_late_refund_eur, 2) AS total_2025_late_refund_eur,
  ROUND(tot.total_2025_late_refund_eur / gt.grand_total_eur * 100, 1) AS pct_of_all_late_refunds_2025
FROM totals tot
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tot.tenant_id
CROSS JOIN grand_total gt
ORDER BY tot.total_2025_late_refund_eur DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 20
builds_on: Refund timing relative to payout settlement
entries.engineer_note: pct_of_all_late_refunds_2025 is computed against the grand total across every tenant with late refunds in 2025, not just the top 20 shown, as requested. EUR conversion uses the exchange_rates row for the refund's own processed_at date (amount divided by the EUR->currency rate; EUR amounts passed through unconverted).

entries.title: 2025 revenue share by industry vertical
entries.question: How big a slice of our 2025 collected revenue comes from B2B wholesale merchants (industrial supplies, office equipment) versus every other vertical, so we know whether omitting their receivables line from the board pack is material?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  coalesce(t.industry, '(none)') as industry,
  count(distinct p.tenant_id) as tenant_count,
  sum(p.amount / er.rate) as total_2025_money_collected_eur,
  round(
    sum(p.amount / er.rate) * 100.0 / sum(sum(p.amount / er.rate)) over (),
    1
  ) as pct_of_total_revenue
FROM payments p
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id
JOIN exchange_rates er
  ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
  AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
  AND er.as_of = date(p.captured_at)
WHERE p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
  AND p.captured_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
  AND p.captured_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY coalesce(t.industry, '(none)')
ORDER BY total_2025_money_collected_eur DESC, industry
builds_on: 2025 revenue share by industry vertical
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per distinct tenants.industry value as stored (nulls bucketed as '(none)'), per the request; no re-bucketing into B2B vs. other was applied so the analyst can identify the wholesale rows (industrial supplies, office equipment) directly in the output.

entries.title: B2B wholesale tenants identified by CRM deal activity, with revenue and receivables
entries.question: Which tenants are actually operating as B2B wholesalers (by using the deals/CRM module, not just by industry label), how much 2025 revenue do they represent, and what does their receivables picture look like on the corrected tenant list?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  tenant_agg.tenant_name,
  tenant_agg.industry,
  tenant_agg.deal_count,
  ROUND(tenant_agg.total_contract_value_eur, 2) AS total_contract_value_eur,
  ROUND(tenant_agg.total_2025_revenue_eur, 2) AS total_2025_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(tenant_agg.total_2025_revenue_eur / NULLIF(company_total.total, 0) * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_2025_revenue,
  ROUND(tenant_agg.open_amount_due_eur, 2) AS open_amount_due_eur,
  tenant_agg.pct_amount_due_overdue
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.id,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    t.industry,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deals d WHERE d.tenant_id = t.id) AS deal_count,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(d.contract_value / er.rate), 0)
       FROM deals d
       JOIN exchange_rates er
         ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = d.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = COALESCE(d.signed_at, CAST(d.created_at AS date))
      WHERE d.tenant_id = t.id
    ) AS total_contract_value_eur,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(p.amount / er.rate), 0)
       FROM payments p
       JOIN exchange_rates er
         ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
      WHERE p.tenant_id = t.id
        AND p.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
        AND p.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
        AND p.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    ) AS total_2025_revenue_eur,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(i.amount_due / er.rate), 0)
       FROM invoices i
       JOIN exchange_rates er
         ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
      WHERE i.tenant_id = t.id
        AND i.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
        AND i.amount_due > 0
    ) AS open_amount_due_eur,
    (SELECT CASE
              WHEN SUM(i.amount_due / er.rate) = 0 THEN NULL
              ELSE ROUND(
                     SUM(CASE WHEN i.due_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' THEN i.amount_due / er.rate ELSE 0 END)
                     / SUM(i.amount_due / er.rate) * 100, 1)
            END
       FROM invoices i
       JOIN exchange_rates er
         ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = i.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
      WHERE i.tenant_id = t.id
        AND i.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
        AND i.amount_due > 0
    ) AS pct_amount_due_overdue
  FROM tenants t
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deals d WHERE d.tenant_id = t.id)
) AS tenant_agg
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(p2.amount / er2.rate), 0) AS total
  FROM payments p2
  JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = p2.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = CAST(p2.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p2.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p2.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p2.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
) AS company_total
ORDER BY tenant_agg.total_2025_revenue_eur DESC, tenant_agg.tenant_name
builds_on: 2025 revenue share by industry vertical
B2B wholesaler receivables aging
entries.engineer_note: Population is every tenant with at least one deals row (deals holds only closed-won B2B contracts per the catalog, so all rows qualify). pct_amount_due_overdue is left NULL for tenants with zero open_amount_due_eur, since the ratio is undefined; all monetary sums are EUR-converted using the exchange rate for the specified date as instructed.

entries.title: Existing customer/audience definitions already in use
entries.question: Do any marketing segments or analytics cohorts already encode a definition like 'customers who purchased recently' or 'all customers', so we can certify a customer count the business already uses rather than inventing a new one?
entries.sql:
SELECT
    'segment' AS source,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    s.name AS name,
    s.is_dynamic AS is_dynamic,
    s.member_count AS member_count,
    substring(cast(s.rules AS varchar), 1, 500) AS rules_definition,
    s.last_refreshed_at AS last_updated
FROM segments s
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = s.tenant_id
UNION ALL
SELECT
    'cohort' AS source,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    c.name AS name,
    c.is_dynamic AS is_dynamic,
    c.member_count AS member_count,
    substring(cast(c.definition AS varchar), 1, 500) AS rules_definition,
    c.computed_at AS last_updated
FROM cohorts c
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
ORDER BY member_count DESC, tenant_name ASC, name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Customer headcount by definition
entries.engineer_note: Top 50 named audience definitions (segments + cohorts) across all tenants by member_count, with rules/definition JSON truncated to 500 chars for display. Note: deleted_at is not filtered on either table, so soft-deleted segments/cohorts are included if present.

entries.title: Payment capture lag by payment method
entries.question: Does the 8-14 day dip in order-to-payment match rate trace to a specific payment method with inherently slower capture (e.g. bank transfer or wire), supporting the 'it's timing, not a hole' explanation?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.kind AS kind,
  COALESCE(t1.payment_count, 0) AS payment_count,
  t2.avg_days_order_to_capture AS avg_days_order_to_capture,
  t3.pct_captured_within_7_days AS pct_captured_within_7_days,
  t4.pct_captured_within_14_days AS pct_captured_within_14_days
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT pm0.kind AS kind FROM payment_methods pm0) t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT pm1.kind AS kind, COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payments p1
  JOIN payment_methods pm1 ON p1.payment_method_id = pm1.id
  JOIN orders o1 ON p1.order_id = o1.id
  WHERE p1.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p1.order_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pm1.kind
) t1 ON t1.kind = t0.kind
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT pm2.kind AS kind,
         ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (p2.captured_at - o2.placed_at)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_order_to_capture
  FROM payments p2
  JOIN payment_methods pm2 ON p2.payment_method_id = pm2.id
  JOIN orders o2 ON p2.order_id = o2.id
  WHERE p2.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p2.order_id IS NOT NULL
    AND p2.captured_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o2.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pm2.kind
) t2 ON t2.kind = t0.kind
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT pm3.kind AS kind,
         ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN (p3.captured_at - o3.placed_at) <= INTERVAL '7 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_captured_within_7_days
  FROM payments p3
  JOIN payment_methods pm3 ON p3.payment_method_id = pm3.id
  JOIN orders o3 ON p3.order_id = o3.id
  WHERE p3.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p3.order_id IS NOT NULL
    AND p3.captured_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o3.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pm3.kind
) t3 ON t3.kind = t0.kind
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT pm4.kind AS kind,
         ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN (p4.captured_at - o4.placed_at) <= INTERVAL '14 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_captured_within_14_days
  FROM payments p4
  JOIN payment_methods pm4 ON p4.payment_method_id = pm4.id
  JOIN orders o4 ON p4.order_id = o4.id
  WHERE p4.status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND p4.order_id IS NOT NULL
    AND p4.captured_at IS NOT NULL
    AND o4.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY pm4.kind
) t4 ON t4.kind = t0.kind
WHERE COALESCE(t1.payment_count, 0) > 0
ORDER BY t2.avg_days_order_to_capture DESC NULLS LAST, t0.kind ASC
builds_on: Order-to-payment match rate by order age
entries.engineer_note: Payment_count reflects the exact population described (status + order join); the three timing measures additionally require non-null captured_at/placed_at since the day-gap can't be computed otherwise, which in practice is the same rows (captured/refunded statuses always have captured_at set).

entries.title: Diagnose zero-value B2B deal tenants in native currency
entries.question: Are the 6 B2B-CRM tenants showing exactly 0.0 revenue/contract value/receivables genuinely inactive, or is this a currency-conversion or join artifact hiding real activity?
entries.sql:
WITH deal_tenants AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id FROM deals
),
deal_summary AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    string_agg(DISTINCT currency_code, ',') AS deal_currency_codes,
    count(*) AS deal_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE contract_value > 0) AS deals_with_positive_value_count,
    sum(contract_value) AS raw_contract_value_total
  FROM deals
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
line_items_summary AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    sum(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct)) AS raw_deal_line_items_total
  FROM deal_line_items
  WHERE tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM deal_tenants)
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
orders_summary AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS orders_count_2025
  FROM orders
  WHERE placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM deal_tenants)
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
payments_summary AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS payments_captured_count_2025
  FROM payments
  WHERE status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM deal_tenants)
  GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  t.default_currency_code AS tenant_default_currency_code,
  ds.deal_currency_codes,
  ds.deal_count,
  ds.deals_with_positive_value_count,
  ds.raw_contract_value_total,
  li.raw_deal_line_items_total,
  COALESCE(os.orders_count_2025, 0) AS orders_count_2025,
  COALESCE(ps.payments_captured_count_2025, 0) AS payments_captured_count_2025
FROM deal_summary ds
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ds.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN line_items_summary li ON li.tenant_id = ds.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN orders_summary os ON os.tenant_id = ds.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN payments_summary ps ON ps.tenant_id = ds.tenant_id
ORDER BY ds.deal_count DESC, t.name
builds_on: B2B wholesale tenants identified by CRM deal activity, with revenue and receivables
entries.engineer_note: Population is all 9 tenants with at least one deals row, as requested. raw_contract_value_total and raw_deal_line_items_total are unconverted native-currency sums (noted per the request that multi-currency tenants would mix units); deal_currency_codes lets the analyst spot those cases directly in the output.

entries.title: Castell Fasteners open invoices in detail
entries.question: What are Castell Fasteners' actual open invoices, so we can reconcile my €14,481 open-receivables figure against Merchant Success's reported €5,080 and present one consistent number to the board?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.invoice_number AS invoice_number,
  t0.status AS status,
  t0.currency_code AS currency_code,
  t0.total AS total,
  t0.amount_due AS amount_due,
  t0.issued_at AS issued_at,
  t0.due_at AS due_at,
  CASE
    WHEN t0.due_at IS NULL THEN 0
    ELSE GREATEST(CAST(DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(t0.due_at AS date) AS integer), 0)
  END AS days_overdue
FROM invoices t0
JOIN tenants t1 ON t1.id = t0.tenant_id
WHERE t1.name = 'Castell Fasteners'
  AND t0.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
  AND t0.amount_due > 0
ORDER BY t0.amount_due DESC, t0.invoice_number ASC
builds_on: B2B wholesale tenants identified by CRM deal activity, with revenue and receivables
entries.engineer_note: Joined invoices directly to tenants on tenant_id (name = 'Castell Fasteners'); billing_profiles was not needed since invoices carries tenant_id. Amounts are shown as stored in the invoice's native currency_code, no FX conversion applied, per request.

entries.title: Late-refund share as a percentage of each merchant's own refund volume
entries.question: Is Cragsley Outfitters' outsized share of company-wide late refunds just proportional to how big it is, or does it refund late at a higher rate than other large merchants?
entries.sql:
WITH refund_eur AS (
  SELECT pr.tenant_id,
         pr.amount / er.rate AS eur_amount,
         CASE WHEN po.paid_at IS NOT NULL AND pr.processed_at > po.paid_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_late
  FROM payment_refunds pr
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = pr.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(pr.processed_at AS date)
  LEFT JOIN payout_items pi ON pi.payment_id = pr.payment_id
  LEFT JOIN payouts po ON po.id = pi.payout_id
  WHERE pr.status = 'succeeded'
    AND pr.processed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND pr.processed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tenant_agg AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
         SUM(eur_amount) AS total_refunds_2025_eur,
         SUM(CASE WHEN is_late = 1 THEN eur_amount ELSE 0 END) AS late_refunds_2025_eur
  FROM refund_eur
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
company_agg AS (
  SELECT SUM(eur_amount) AS total_eur,
         SUM(CASE WHEN is_late = 1 THEN eur_amount ELSE 0 END) AS late_eur
  FROM refund_eur
)
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
       ta.total_refunds_2025_eur,
       ta.late_refunds_2025_eur,
       ROUND(ta.late_refunds_2025_eur / NULLIF(ta.total_refunds_2025_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS pct_of_own_refunds_late,
       ROUND(ca.late_eur / NULLIF(ca.total_eur, 0) * 100, 1) AS company_avg_pct_late_2025
FROM tenant_agg ta
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ta.tenant_id
CROSS JOIN company_agg ca
ORDER BY ta.total_refunds_2025_eur DESC, t.name ASC
LIMIT 15
builds_on: Late-refund concentration and trend by merchant
entries.engineer_note: Late is defined as payment_refunds.processed_at strictly after the settling payout's paid_at; refunds whose payment never appears in payout_items are excluded from the late bucket (per spec) but still count in total_refunds. company_avg_pct_late_2025 is computed company-wide (all tenants, not just the top 15) and repeated on every row.

entries.title: Corrected 2025 revenue and receivables by B2B tenant
entries.question: What is the real 2025 revenue and open receivables for all 9 verified B2B wholesale tenants, now that the EUR-conversion bug that zeroed out 6 of them is fixed?
entries.sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT t0.id AS tenant_id, t0.name AS tenant_name, t0.default_currency_code AS currency_code
  FROM tenants t0
  WHERE t0.name IN (
    'Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'Kontor24 Burobedarf', 'OfficeHub Nordic',
    'Midland Safety Wear', 'Castell Fasteners', 'Hanse Industriebedarf',
    'Polder Packaging', 'Deskline Supplies', 'Papeterie Grossiste'
  )
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deals d0 WHERE d0.tenant_id = t0.id)
),
revenue_tenant AS (
  SELECT p0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN p0.amount
             ELSE p0.amount / er0.rate END) AS total_2025_revenue_eur
  FROM payments p0
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er0
    ON er0.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er0.quote_code = p0.currency_code
   AND er0.as_of = CAST(p0.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p0.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p0.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p0.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY p0.tenant_id
),
revenue_all AS (
  SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN p1.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN p1.amount
                  ELSE p1.amount / er1.rate END) AS total_revenue_eur_all
  FROM payments p1
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er1
    ON er1.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er1.quote_code = p1.currency_code
   AND er1.as_of = CAST(p1.captured_at AS date)
  WHERE p1.status IN ('captured', 'refunded', 'partially_refunded')
    AND p1.captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND p1.captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
open_invoices_tenant AS (
  SELECT i0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN i0.amount_due
             ELSE i0.amount_due / er2.rate END) AS open_amount_due_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN i0.due_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00'
             THEN (CASE WHEN i0.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN i0.amount_due
                        ELSE i0.amount_due / er2.rate END)
             ELSE 0 END) AS overdue_amount_due_eur
  FROM invoices i0
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2
    ON er2.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er2.quote_code = i0.currency_code
   AND er2.as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
  WHERE i0.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
    AND i0.amount_due > 0
  GROUP BY i0.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tt0.tenant_name AS tenant_name,
  tt0.currency_code AS currency_code,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rt0.total_2025_revenue_eur, 0), 2) AS total_2025_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rt0.total_2025_revenue_eur, 0) / NULLIF(ra0.total_revenue_eur_all, 0) * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_2025_revenue,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oi0.open_amount_due_eur, 0), 2) AS open_amount_due_eur,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(oi0.open_amount_due_eur, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE oi0.overdue_amount_due_eur / oi0.open_amount_due_eur * 100 END
  , 1) AS pct_amount_due_overdue
FROM target_tenants tt0
LEFT JOIN revenue_tenant rt0 ON rt0.tenant_id = tt0.tenant_id
CROSS JOIN revenue_all ra0
LEFT JOIN open_invoices_tenant oi0 ON oi0.tenant_id = tt0.tenant_id
ORDER BY total_2025_revenue_eur DESC, tt0.tenant_name
builds_on: B2B wholesale tenants identified by CRM deal activity, with revenue and receivables
Diagnose zero-value B2B deal tenants in native currency
entries.engineer_note: Built exactly as specified: EUR amounts pass through at 1.0 (no self-join to exchange_rates for quote_code='EUR'), non-EUR amounts divide by the EUR-base daily rate; pct_of_total_2025_revenue is each tenant's share of company-wide 2025 captured/refunded/partially_refunded payment revenue (all tenants, same conversion rule); open receivables and overdue share use the 2025-12-31 snapshot rate per invoice currency.

entries.title: Scope of the EUR exchange-rate join bug on 2025 revenue
entries.question: If a query naively joins exchange_rates for EUR the same way it does for every other currency, how much revenue silently vanishes, and is EUR the only currency affected?
entries.sql:
WITH pop AS (
  SELECT currency_code, amount, captured_at
  FROM payments
  WHERE status IN ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded')
    AND captured_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND captured_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
naive AS (
  SELECT p.currency_code, SUM(p.amount / er.rate) AS naive_eur
  FROM pop p
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
  GROUP BY p.currency_code
),
correct AS (
  SELECT p.currency_code,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN p.amount ELSE p.amount / er.rate END) AS correct_eur
  FROM pop p
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = p.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(p.captured_at AS date)
  GROUP BY p.currency_code
)
SELECT
  c.currency_code,
  COALESCE(n.naive_eur, 0) AS total_2025_revenue_naive_eur,
  c.correct_eur AS total_2025_revenue_correct_eur,
  c.correct_eur - COALESCE(n.naive_eur, 0) AS shortfall_eur,
  ROUND((c.correct_eur - COALESCE(n.naive_eur, 0)) / c.correct_eur * 100, 1) AS shortfall_pct
FROM correct c
LEFT JOIN naive n ON n.currency_code = c.currency_code
ORDER BY c.correct_eur DESC, c.currency_code
builds_on: Corrected 2025 revenue and receivables by B2B tenant
entries.engineer_note: Assumes exchange_rates has no base_code='EUR', quote_code='EUR' rows (which is why the naive inner join drops EUR entirely); for non-EUR currencies the correct-sum also uses a LEFT JOIN to exchange_rates, so if any non-EUR currency/day is missing a rate row, both naive and correct sums would silently omit that slice equally (no shortfall shown for that gap) rather than erroring.

entries.title: Final B2B wholesale receivables aging (corrected)
entries.question: With the full, verified 9-tenant B2B wholesale list and EUR handled correctly, what does the receivables aging actually look like for the board pack?
entries.sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name
  FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN (
    'Ballycorran Industrial Supply',
    'Kontor24 Burobedarf',
    'OfficeHub Nordic',
    'Midland Safety Wear',
    'Castell Fasteners',
    'Hanse Industriebedarf',
    'Polder Packaging',
    'Deskline Supplies',
    'Papeterie Grossiste'
  )
),
rates AS (
  SELECT quote_code, rate
  FROM exchange_rates
  WHERE base_code = 'EUR' AND as_of = DATE '2025-12-31'
),
inv AS (
  SELECT
    i.id,
    i.amount_due,
    i.currency_code,
    i.due_at,
    CASE
      WHEN i.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN i.amount_due
      ELSE i.amount_due / r.rate
    END AS amount_due_eur,
    CASE
      WHEN i.due_at IS NULL OR i.due_at >= DATE '2025-12-31' THEN 'Not yet due'
      WHEN DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(i.due_at AS date) BETWEEN 1 AND 30 THEN '1-30 days overdue'
      WHEN DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(i.due_at AS date) BETWEEN 31 AND 60 THEN '31-60 days overdue'
      WHEN DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(i.due_at AS date) BETWEEN 61 AND 90 THEN '61-90 days overdue'
      ELSE '90+ days overdue'
    END AS aging_bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN i.due_at IS NULL OR i.due_at >= DATE '2025-12-31' THEN 0
      ELSE DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(i.due_at AS date)
    END AS days_past_due
  FROM invoices i
  JOIN target_tenants t ON t.id = i.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN rates r ON r.quote_code = i.currency_code
  WHERE i.status IN ('open', 'past_due')
    AND i.amount_due > 0
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    aging_bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS invoice_count,
    SUM(amount_due_eur) AS amount_due_eur,
    AVG(days_past_due) AS avg_days_past_due
  FROM inv
  GROUP BY aging_bucket
)
SELECT
  aging_bucket,
  invoice_count,
  ROUND(amount_due_eur, 2) AS amount_due_eur,
  ROUND(amount_due_eur / SUM(amount_due_eur) OVER () * 100, 1) AS pct_of_total_amount_due,
  ROUND(avg_days_past_due, 1) AS avg_days_past_due
FROM agg
ORDER BY amount_due_eur DESC, aging_bucket ASC
builds_on: B2B wholesaler receivables aging
Corrected 2025 revenue and receivables by B2B tenant
entries.engineer_note: Tenants matched by exact name against the 9 verified B2B wholesale merchants listed in the request; EUR invoices pass through at rate 1.0 and all other currencies are converted via exchange_rates (EUR base, as_of 2025-12-31).

entries.title: Full census of audit-trail deletion coverage, all soft-deletable tables
entries.question: Is the missing deletion audit trail we found for products a narrow, one-table problem, or does it extend across most of the tables that support soft-deletion?
entries.sql:
WITH soft_deleted AS (
  SELECT 'brands' AS entity_table, COUNT(*) AS total_soft_deleted, COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS tenant_count FROM brands WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'categories', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM categories WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'products', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM products WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'product_variants', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM product_variants WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'collections', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM collections WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'users', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM users WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'billing_profiles', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM billing_profiles WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'plans', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM plans WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'price_lists', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM price_lists WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'discounts', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM discounts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'coupons', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM coupons WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'promotions', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM promotions WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'campaigns', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM campaigns WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'email_templates', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM email_templates WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'segments', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM segments WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'landing_pages', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM landing_pages WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'referrals', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM referrals WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'loyalty_programs', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM loyalty_programs WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ab_tests', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM ab_tests WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'experiments', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM experiments WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'cohorts', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM cohorts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'funnels', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM funnels WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'contacts', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM contacts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'accounts', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM accounts WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'knowledge_articles', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM knowledge_articles WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'macros', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM macros WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'files', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM files WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'utm_links', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM utm_links WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'suppliers', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM suppliers WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL SELECT 'warehouses', COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM warehouses WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
),
audit_counts AS (
  SELECT entity_table, COUNT(*) AS deleted_audit_rows
  FROM audit_log
  WHERE action = 'delete'
  GROUP BY entity_table
)
SELECT
  sd.entity_table,
  sd.total_soft_deleted,
  COALESCE(ac.deleted_audit_rows, 0) AS matching_audit_rows,
  CASE WHEN sd.total_soft_deleted = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(ac.deleted_audit_rows, 0) / sd.total_soft_deleted, 1)
  END AS coverage_rate_pct,
  sd.tenant_count AS tenants_with_soft_deleted
FROM soft_deleted sd
LEFT JOIN audit_counts ac ON ac.entity_table = sd.entity_table
ORDER BY sd.total_soft_deleted DESC, sd.entity_table ASC
builds_on: Audit-trail coverage of actual soft-deletions, by entity table
entries.engineer_note: The requested list actually enumerates 30 distinct tables (not 29 as labeled) — all 30 are included, all confirmed to have a deleted_at column in the catalog. Audit matching is by entity_table name only (entity_schema ignored), as specified.

entries.title: Audit traceability of order cancellations and invoice voids
entries.question: For the two 'deletion-like' events on our financial documents that don't use soft-delete — a cancelled order, a voided invoice — is there any audit_log record at all tying back to that specific row?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  'order cancellations' AS entity_type,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (
    WHERE EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
      WHERE al.entity_table = 'orders'
        AND al.entity_id = o.id
        AND al.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
    )
  ) AS events_with_match,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
        WHERE al.entity_table = 'orders'
          AND al.entity_id = o.id
          AND al.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
      )
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1
  ) AS coverage_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM orders o
WHERE o.status = 'cancelled'
  AND o.cancelled_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
  AND o.cancelled_at < DATE '2026-01-01'

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'invoice voids' AS entity_type,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (
    WHERE EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
      WHERE al.entity_table = 'invoices'
        AND al.entity_id = i.id
        AND al.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
    )
  ) AS events_with_match,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM audit_log al
        WHERE al.entity_table = 'invoices'
          AND al.entity_id = i.id
          AND al.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
      )
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1
  ) AS coverage_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM invoices i
WHERE i.status = 'void'
  AND i.voided_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
  AND i.voided_at < DATE '2026-01-01'

ORDER BY entity_type
builds_on: Audit-trail coverage of actual soft-deletions, by entity table
entries.engineer_note: Events are scoped to 2023-01-01..2025-12-31 using orders.cancelled_at / invoices.voided_at (the rows where that timestamp is null despite the terminal status are excluded from the count, since there's no other way to date them). Match test is an EXISTS on audit_log by (entity_table, entity_id, tenant_id) with any action — as requested, this only proves some audit trail exists for the row, not that the cancellation/void itself was the logged event; even 100% coverage would not confirm that.

entries.title: Access still open on churned tenants, by surface
entries.question: Beyond Owner/Administrator accounts, how much other access (ordinary staff logins, open sessions, active API keys, active webhooks) is still live on tenants that have already churned?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users u WHERE u.tenant_id = t.id AND u.deleted_at IS NULL) AS total_users,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users u WHERE u.tenant_id = t.id AND u.deleted_at IS NULL AND u.status = 'active') AS active_users,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions s WHERE s.tenant_id = t.id AND s.revoked_at IS NULL) AS open_sessions,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM api_keys ak WHERE ak.tenant_id = t.id AND ak.status = 'active') AS active_api_keys,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM webhooks w WHERE w.tenant_id = t.id AND w.is_active = true) AS active_webhooks,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_accounts sa WHERE sa.tenant_id = t.id) AS service_accounts
FROM tenants t
WHERE t.status = 'churned'
ORDER BY active_users DESC, tenant_name ASC
builds_on: Dormant users holding Owner or Administrator access
entries.engineer_note: Per the request's explicit Details (users/sessions/api_keys/webhooks/service_accounts, no role join specified), this counts all users of any role — it does not separately exclude Owner/Administrator accounts, since no roles/user_roles join was given in the spec. If you want Owner/Admin excluded from the user counts specifically, that needs a follow-up report joining user_roles/roles.
warnings: 6 scalar subqueries in the select list (over a FROM, may be per-row values)

entries.title: Order status history coverage for cancelled orders
entries.question: Generic audit_log barely covers order cancellations (0.2%) — but does the purpose-built order_status_history table actually capture who cancelled each order and when?
entries.sql:
WITH cancelled_orders AS (
    SELECT
        id AS order_id,
        tenant_id
    FROM orders
    WHERE status = 'cancelled'
),
joined AS (
    SELECT
        co.tenant_id,
        co.order_id,
        h.id AS history_id,
        h.changed_by_user_id
    FROM cancelled_orders co
    LEFT JOIN order_status_history h
        ON h.order_id = co.order_id
        AND h.to_status = 'cancelled'
        AND h.tenant_id = co.tenant_id
),
per_tenant AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS cancelled_orders,
        COUNT(history_id) AS matching_history_rows,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN history_id IS NOT NULL THEN order_id END) AS orders_with_match,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN changed_by_user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) AS matching_rows_with_actor
    FROM joined
    GROUP BY tenant_id
)
SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    pt.cancelled_orders,
    pt.matching_history_rows,
    ROUND(100.0 * pt.orders_with_match / pt.cancelled_orders, 1) AS coverage_rate_pct,
    pt.matching_rows_with_actor
FROM per_tenant pt
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = pt.tenant_id
ORDER BY
    coverage_rate_pct ASC,
    pt.cancelled_orders DESC,
    tenant_name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Audit traceability of order cancellations and invoice voids
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per tenant with ≥1 cancelled order, worst coverage first; capped at 50 rows as instructed, and the warehouse's row-count note will show the true tenant total (expected ~90) since computing it would need a second metered query.

entries.title: Invoice void and uncollectible traceability, with timestamp completeness check
entries.question: Has any invoice actually been voided or marked uncollectible on the platform, and if so, is the event dated and traceable in audit_log — or was last night's zero result just because voided_at is missing?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  i.status AS invoice_status,
  COUNT(*) AS total_invoices,
  COUNT(i.voided_at) AS voided_at_populated,
  SUM(CASE WHEN i.voided_at IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS voided_at_null,
  SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log a
      WHERE a.entity_table = 'invoices'
        AND a.entity_id = i.id
        AND a.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matching_audit_log_rows,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM audit_log a
      WHERE a.entity_table = 'invoices'
        AND a.entity_id = i.id
        AND a.tenant_id = i.tenant_id
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)
  , 1) AS coverage_rate_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM invoices i
WHERE i.status IN ('void', 'uncollectible')
GROUP BY i.status
ORDER BY total_invoices DESC, invoice_status
builds_on: Audit traceability of order cancellations and invoice voids
entries.engineer_note: Counts all invoices with status in ('void','uncollectible') regardless of voided_at, splits them into voided_at populated vs null, and separately counts how many of those invoices have at least one matching audit_log row (entity_table='invoices', entity_id=invoices.id, same tenant_id) via EXISTS, which is also the basis for the coverage rate.

entries.title: Validity of never-revoked sessions on churned tenants
entries.question: The 9 churned tenants show 46-300 sessions per tenant that were never explicitly revoked — but are those sessions actually still usable today (expiry in the future), or did they just naturally expire without anyone bothering to revoke them?
entries.sql:
select
  t.name as tenant_name,
  count(*) as never_revoked_sessions,
  count(*) filter (where s.expires_at > timestamp '2026-01-05 00:00:00') as still_within_expiry,
  count(*) filter (where s.expires_at <= timestamp '2026-01-05 00:00:00') as already_expired,
  max(s.expires_at) as latest_expires_at,
  max(s.last_seen_at) as latest_last_seen_at
from sessions s
join tenants t on t.id = s.tenant_id
where t.status = 'churned'
  and s.revoked_at is null
group by t.name
order by still_within_expiry desc, tenant_name asc
builds_on: Access still open on churned tenants, by surface
entries.engineer_note: One row per churned tenant, counting never-revoked sessions split into still-valid (expires_at > 2026-01-05) vs naturally expired, plus the latest expiry and latest real use (last_seen_at) among them.

entries.title: Actor attribution in order_status_history, across all transition types
entries.question: Is the missing 'who changed this' actor specific to order cancellations, or does order_status_history never record an actor for any status transition?
entries.sql:
select
  to_status,
  count(*) as total_transitions,
  count(*) filter (where changed_by_user_id is not null) as transitions_with_actor,
  round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where changed_by_user_id is not null) / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) as share_with_actor_pct,
  count(distinct tenant_id) as distinct_tenants
from order_status_history
where created_at >= date '2023-01-01' and created_at < date '2026-01-01'
group by to_status
order by total_transitions desc, to_status
builds_on: Order status history coverage for cancelled orders
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per to_status, covering all transitions from 2023-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (created_at < 2026-01-01). Expect 7 rows, one per order status.

entries.title: Shopper authentication method mix: OAuth-linked vs password-only
entries.question: Since shopper accounts have 0% MFA, what actually stands in for a second factor today — are most shoppers authenticating through an OAuth provider (Google/Apple/etc., which carries its own security), or are they overwhelmingly raw password-only accounts with no backup at all?
entries.sql:
with shoppers as (
    select id, tenant_id, email
    from users
    where is_staff = false
      and deleted_at is null
),
oauth_linked_users as (
    select distinct user_id
    from oauth_accounts
),
confirmed_mfa_users as (
    select distinct user_id
    from mfa_devices
    where confirmed_at is not null
),
recent_login_users as (
    select distinct s.id as user_id
    from shoppers s
    join login_attempts la
      on la.tenant_id = s.tenant_id
     and (la.user_id = s.id or la.email = s.email)
    where la.occurred_at >= timestamp '2025-10-05'
      and la.occurred_at <  timestamp '2026-01-01'
),
classified_shoppers as (
    select
        s.id,
        case when o.user_id is not null then 'OAuth-linked' else 'password-only' end as method_category
    from shoppers s
    left join oauth_linked_users o on o.user_id = s.id
),
total_shoppers as (
    select count(*) as total_count from shoppers
)
select
    cs.method_category,
    count(*) as shopper_user_count,
    round(100.0 * count(*) / t.total_count, 1) as share_of_shoppers_pct,
    count(mfa.user_id) as confirmed_mfa_count,
    count(rl.user_id) as recently_active_count
from classified_shoppers cs
cross join total_shoppers t
left join confirmed_mfa_users mfa on mfa.user_id = cs.id
left join recent_login_users rl on rl.user_id = cs.id
group by cs.method_category, t.total_count
order by shopper_user_count desc, cs.method_category
builds_on: Platform-wide MFA adoption trend by month, staff vs. shoppers
entries.engineer_note: Recently-active match joins login_attempts to shoppers on tenant_id plus (user_id match OR email match), since login_attempts.email is not itself scoped by a global key; this follows the request's "matched by email or user_id" instruction as closely as the schema allows.

entries.title: Detail list of the oldest active API keys (4+ years), by tenant
entries.question: Henrik wants to know if the oldest, longest-unrotated API keys are concentrated among a few tenants/integrations and whether any show signs of broad/elevated access rather than narrow, routine use — here's the actual list.
entries.sql:
SELECT
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    t.status AS tenant_status,
    ak.name AS key_name,
    (DATE '2026-01-05' - ak.created_at::date) AS age_days,
    ak.last_used_at,
    CASE WHEN ak.last_used_at IS NULL THEN NULL
         ELSE (DATE '2026-01-05' - ak.last_used_at::date)
    END AS days_since_last_use,
    rl.limit_scope,
    rl.max_requests,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ak.id) OVER () AS total_matching_keys
FROM api_keys ak
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = ak.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN rate_limits rl ON rl.api_key_id = ak.id
WHERE ak.status = 'active'
  AND ak.created_at < DATE '2022-01-05'
ORDER BY age_days DESC, tenant_name ASC, key_name ASC, rl.id ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Active API key age distribution (rotation hygiene)
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per api_key, except keys with multiple rate_limits rows produce one extra row per scope (left join), as requested. The "total_matching_keys" column gives the full count of qualifying active 4+-year-old keys (pre-cap) distinct by key id, since the 50-row cap only limits printed rows; rate_limits rows with a null api_key_id (tenant-wide defaults) are excluded as they aren't tied to a specific key.

entries.title: Scope tally across all 76 long-lived (4+ year) active API keys
