entries.question: Of all 76 active API keys that are 4+ years old, how many actually carry the broad 'admin_api' rate-limit scope versus no scope recorded at all — the full count, not just the 50 printed last night?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(rl.limit_scope, 'no scope recorded') AS scope_category,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ak.id) AS distinct_key_count,
  ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT ak.id) * 100.0 / 76, 1) AS share_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ak.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM (
  SELECT id, tenant_id
  FROM api_keys
  WHERE status = 'active'
    AND created_at < DATE '2022-01-05'
) ak
LEFT JOIN rate_limits rl ON rl.api_key_id = ak.id
GROUP BY COALESCE(rl.limit_scope, 'no scope recorded')
ORDER BY distinct_key_count DESC, scope_category ASC
builds_on: Detail list of the oldest active API keys (4+ years), by tenant
entries.engineer_note: Population matches last night's 76-key cohort (active, created_at before 2022-01-05, i.e. 4+ years before the 2026-01-05 reporting date). Share % is computed against the fixed denominator of 76 as requested.

entries.title: Is admin_api scope concentrated in old keys, or standard across all ages?
entries.question: Are broadly-scoped (admin_api) keys specifically a feature of our oldest, longest-unrotated keys, or is that scope just how every integration key is set up regardless of age — i.e. is 'old + broad' a rotation failure or simply the norm?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  bucket AS age_bucket,
  COUNT(DISTINCT ak_id) AS total_active_keys,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN has_admin_api THEN ak_id END) AS admin_api_scoped_keys,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN has_admin_api THEN ak_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ak_id), 0), 1) AS admin_api_share_pct,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN no_scope_recorded THEN ak_id END) AS no_scope_recorded_keys,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
FROM (
  SELECT
    ak.id AS ak_id,
    ak.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    CASE
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 90 THEN 'Under 90 days'
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 365 THEN '90 days-1 year'
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 730 THEN '1-2 years'
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 1460 THEN '2-4 years'
      ELSE '4+ years'
    END AS bucket,
    CASE
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 90 THEN 1
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 365 THEN 2
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 730 THEN 3
      WHEN (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(ak.created_at AS DATE)) < 1460 THEN 4
      ELSE 5
    END AS bucket_order,
    CASE WHEN rl.has_admin_api = 1 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_admin_api,
    CASE WHEN rl.api_key_id IS NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS no_scope_recorded
  FROM api_keys ak
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT api_key_id, MAX(CASE WHEN limit_scope = 'admin_api' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_admin_api
    FROM rate_limits
    WHERE api_key_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY api_key_id
  ) rl ON rl.api_key_id = ak.id
  WHERE ak.status = 'active'
) sub
GROUP BY bucket, bucket_order
ORDER BY bucket_order
builds_on: Active API key age distribution (rotation hygiene)
Scope tally across all 76 long-lived (4+ year) active API keys
entries.engineer_note: "No scope recorded" means the active key has zero rate_limits rows at all (not merely a non-admin_api scope); admin_api_scoped_keys counts keys with at least one rate_limits row where limit_scope='admin_api'. Age buckets use the fixed 2026-01-05 reference date and the same 5 ranges as the earlier age-distribution report.

entries.title: Active API keys on churned tenants: scope and recent use
entries.question: The 2 churned tenants found earlier with a still-active API key (Dewdrop Studio, Aurum & Ash) — do those specific keys carry elevated (admin_api) scope, and how recently were they actually used?
entries.sql:
select
  t.name as tenant_name,
  ak.name as key_name,
  (date '2026-01-05' - cast(ak.created_at as date)) as age_days,
  ak.last_used_at,
  (date '2026-01-05' - cast(ak.last_used_at as date)) as days_since_last_use,
  rl.limit_scope,
  rl.max_requests
from api_keys ak
join tenants t on t.id = ak.tenant_id and t.status = 'churned'
left join rate_limits rl on rl.api_key_id = ak.id
where ak.status = 'active'
order by tenant_name, key_name, ak.id, rl.limit_scope
builds_on: Access still open on churned tenants, by surface
Detail list of the oldest active API keys (4+ years), by tenant
entries.engineer_note: days_since_last_use is null if last_used_at is null (key never used); rate_limits is scoped by api_key_id so a key with no matching rate limit row shows null scope/max_requests, and a key with more than one rate-limit row would appear on multiple lines (not expected given the small result set).

entries.title: Privacy request volume reconciliation: counts by type and status
entries.question: What is the defensible, auditable count of privacy (DSAR) requests by type and status, so we can reconcile against the ~48 figure quoted elsewhere and the 60 we found last week before briefing the regulator?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  request_type,
  status,
  count(*) AS request_count,
  min(received_at)::date AS earliest_received_at,
  max(received_at)::date AS latest_received_at,
  round(
    percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (
      ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM (completed_at - received_at)) / 86400.0
    ) FILTER (WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL),
    1
  ) AS median_days_to_close
FROM data_subject_requests
GROUP BY request_type, status
ORDER BY request_type, status
builds_on: Data subject request status audit: does completed_at reflect true closure?
entries.engineer_note: Full history, all tenants, request_type/status left exactly as stored (no casing normalization) per request, so any oddball strings will surface as their own rows. Median days-to-close is blank (NULL) for type/status combinations with no completed_at values.

entries.title: Portability requests: formal DSAR count vs. unlinked data exports
entries.question: Is 'zero portability requests in 3 years' a real zero, or are shopper data exports being fulfilled outside the formal DSAR process (a logging blind spot)?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN dsr.id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS linked_to_dsar,
  COUNT(*) AS export_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT de.subject_user_id) AS distinct_subject_users,
  MIN(CAST(de.requested_at AS date)) AS earliest_requested_at,
  MAX(CAST(de.requested_at AS date)) AS latest_requested_at,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE de.status = 'completed') AS completed_export_count,
  ROUND(AVG(de.row_count) FILTER (WHERE de.row_count IS NOT NULL), 1) AS avg_row_count
FROM data_exports de
LEFT JOIN data_subject_requests dsr ON dsr.data_export_id = de.id
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY linked_to_dsar DESC
builds_on: Data subject requests: monthly volume, closure time, and overdue backlog
entries.engineer_note: Completed export count uses status = 'completed' since data_exports.status has no documented fixed code list in the catalog; please confirm this is the correct 'finished' value if the warehouse uses a different code (e.g. 'done'/'success').

entries.title: Retention reality check beyond email: events, job_runs, page_views, system_health_checks
entries.question: Beyond the confirmed email_log failure, how much data in the other four policy-covered tables is currently sitting past its stated retention window?
entries.sql:
WITH policy AS (
  SELECT entity_table, MIN(retention_days) AS retention_days, MIN(action_on_expiry) AS action_on_expiry
  FROM retention_policies
  WHERE entity_table IN ('events','job_runs','page_views','system_health_checks')
  GROUP BY entity_table
),
events_stats AS (
  SELECT 'events' AS entity_table,
         COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
         (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(t0.occurred_at) AS DATE)) AS oldest_age_days,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t0.occurred_at < (DATE '2026-01-05' - (SELECT retention_days FROM policy WHERE policy.entity_table = 'events'))) AS exceeding_rows
  FROM events t0
),
job_runs_stats AS (
  SELECT 'job_runs' AS entity_table,
         COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
         (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(t0.queued_at) AS DATE)) AS oldest_age_days,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t0.queued_at < (DATE '2026-01-05' - (SELECT retention_days FROM policy WHERE policy.entity_table = 'job_runs'))) AS exceeding_rows
  FROM job_runs t0
),
page_views_stats AS (
  SELECT 'page_views' AS entity_table,
         COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
         (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(t0.viewed_at) AS DATE)) AS oldest_age_days,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t0.viewed_at < (DATE '2026-01-05' - (SELECT retention_days FROM policy WHERE policy.entity_table = 'page_views'))) AS exceeding_rows
  FROM page_views t0
),
system_health_checks_stats AS (
  SELECT 'system_health_checks' AS entity_table,
         COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
         (DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(MIN(t0.checked_at) AS DATE)) AS oldest_age_days,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t0.checked_at < (DATE '2026-01-05' - (SELECT retention_days FROM policy WHERE policy.entity_table = 'system_health_checks'))) AS exceeding_rows
  FROM system_health_checks t0
),
all_stats AS (
  SELECT * FROM events_stats
  UNION ALL SELECT * FROM job_runs_stats
  UNION ALL SELECT * FROM page_views_stats
  UNION ALL SELECT * FROM system_health_checks_stats
)
SELECT
  a.entity_table AS entity_table,
  COALESCE(p.retention_days, 0) AS stated_retention_days,
  COALESCE(p.action_on_expiry, 'unknown') AS action_on_expiry,
  a.total_rows AS total_rows,
  a.oldest_age_days AS oldest_row_age_days,
  a.exceeding_rows AS rows_exceeding_retention,
  ROUND(100.0 * a.exceeding_rows / NULLIF(a.total_rows, 0), 2) AS pct_exceeding_retention
FROM all_stats a
LEFT JOIN policy p ON p.entity_table = a.entity_table
ORDER BY pct_exceeding_retention DESC, a.entity_table ASC
builds_on: Retention policy landscape: distinct rules by entity table
email_log actual retention vs. the stated 730-day delete policy
audit_log actual archiving vs. the stated 730-day archive policy
entries.engineer_note: Retention_days and action_on_expiry are taken via MIN() per entity_table from retention_policies, relying on the analyst's confirmation that these are uniform across all 120 tenants (so MIN picks the single shared value); the query is platform-wide (not per-tenant) as requested.

entries.title: Pre-2023 data subject requests: backfill or data quality issue?
entries.question: Are the data subject requests received before 2023-01-01 legitimate historical/backfilled compliance records, or a data quality artifact?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.public_id AS public_id,
  t1.name AS tenant_name,
  t0.request_type AS request_type,
  t0.status AS status,
  t0.received_at AS received_at,
  t0.completed_at AS completed_at,
  t0.created_at AS created_at,
  ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t0.created_at - t0.received_at)) / 86400.0, 1) AS days_received_to_created,
  LEFT(COALESCE(t0.notes, ''), 200) AS notes
FROM data_subject_requests t0
JOIN tenants t1 ON t1.id = t0.tenant_id
WHERE t0.received_at < DATE '2023-01-01'
ORDER BY t0.received_at ASC, t0.public_id ASC
builds_on: Privacy request volume reconciliation: counts by type and status
entries.engineer_note: Returns full history of data_subject_requests rows with received_at before 2023-01-01, one row each, with the received_at-to-created_at gap (in days) as the key diagnostic column; if this exceeds 50 rows only the first 50 by received_at will print, and the report should note the true row count.

entries.title: Data export fulfillment audit: are access/portability exports actually completing?
entries.question: Is 'zero completed data exports' real, or is 'completed' simply the wrong status string for this table — and are shoppers who filed access requests actually receiving their data?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  status,
  COUNT(*) AS export_count,
  MIN(requested_at) AS earliest_requested_at,
  MAX(requested_at) AS latest_requested_at,
  COUNT(completed_at) AS count_with_completed_at,
  COUNT(file_url) AS count_with_file_url,
  ROUND(AVG(row_count) FILTER (WHERE row_count IS NOT NULL), 2) AS avg_row_count
FROM data_exports
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY export_count DESC, status ASC
builds_on: Portability requests: formal DSAR count vs. unlinked data exports
entries.engineer_note: Grouped by the raw status string exactly as stored in data_exports, platform-wide (no tenant filter), so the report will show whichever status values actually exist (e.g. 'completed' vs. 'succeeded' etc.) alongside completed_at/file_url fill rates to tell whether exports are genuinely finishing.

entries.title: Evidence check on the 3 legal-hold-linked chargeback disputes
entries.question: For the 3 accounts under a payment-dispute legal hold, what internal evidence (payment status, support ticket activity) suggests whether the underlying dispute is still active or has gone stale?
entries.sql:
WITH holds AS (
  SELECT lh.id AS legal_hold_id, lh.tenant_id, lh.subject_user_id, lh.placed_at, t.name AS tenant_name
  FROM legal_holds lh
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = lh.tenant_id
  WHERE lh.is_active = true
    AND t.name IN ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Rue Lafayette Studio', 'Cragsley Outfitters')
),
latest_payment AS (
  SELECT h.legal_hold_id, p.status, p.updated_at, p.amount, p.currency_code,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY h.legal_hold_id ORDER BY p.updated_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM holds h
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = h.subject_user_id AND o.tenant_id = h.tenant_id
  JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id
),
latest_payment_top AS (
  SELECT * FROM latest_payment WHERE rn = 1
),
open_tickets AS (
  SELECT h.legal_hold_id, COUNT(*) AS open_ticket_count
  FROM holds h
  JOIN tickets tk ON tk.requester_user_id = h.subject_user_id AND tk.tenant_id = h.tenant_id
  WHERE tk.status NOT IN ('solved','closed')
  GROUP BY h.legal_hold_id
),
latest_ticket AS (
  SELECT h.legal_hold_id, tk.last_message_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY h.legal_hold_id ORDER BY tk.last_message_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM holds h
  JOIN tickets tk ON tk.requester_user_id = h.subject_user_id AND tk.tenant_id = h.tenant_id
),
latest_ticket_top AS (
  SELECT * FROM latest_ticket WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
  h.tenant_name,
  h.subject_user_id,
  CAST(h.placed_at AS date) AS hold_placed_date,
  DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(h.placed_at AS date) AS days_since_placed,
  lp.status AS latest_payment_status,
  CAST(lp.updated_at AS date) AS latest_payment_updated_date,
  lp.amount AS latest_payment_amount,
  lp.currency_code AS latest_payment_currency,
  COALESCE(ot.open_ticket_count, 0) AS open_ticket_count,
  CAST(lt.last_message_at AS date) AS latest_ticket_activity_date,
  DATE '2026-01-05' - CAST(lt.last_message_at AS date) AS days_since_ticket_activity
FROM holds h
LEFT JOIN latest_payment_top lp ON lp.legal_hold_id = h.legal_hold_id
LEFT JOIN open_tickets ot ON ot.legal_hold_id = h.legal_hold_id
LEFT JOIN latest_ticket_top lt ON lt.legal_hold_id = h.legal_hold_id
ORDER BY days_since_placed DESC, h.tenant_name
builds_on: Legal holds: active scope, coverage, and staleness
Linking rejected erasure requests to active legal holds
entries.engineer_note: Legal holds for these 3 tenants have no entity_schema/entity_table/entity_id populated, so there is no direct link to a specific disputed payment or ticket; as instructed, the report approximates evidence using the subject user's most recent payment (via orders) and most recent/open support tickets as indirect signals of whether the dispute is still live.

entries.title: Consent purpose audit: full history and the analytics_cookies anomaly
entries.question: Across the full history, how many consent purposes do we actually track, and is the analytics_cookies 'always 100% opted in, zero withdrawals' pattern unique or does it appear elsewhere?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  cr.purpose,
  COUNT(*) AS total_records,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cr.user_id) AS distinct_users,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.status = 'granted') AS granted_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.status = 'withdrawn') AS withdrawn_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cr.status = 'expired') AS expired_count,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * (
      SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sub.user_id)
      FROM consent_records sub
      WHERE sub.purpose = cr.purpose
        AND sub.status IN ('withdrawn', 'expired')
    ) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT cr.user_id), 0)
  , 2) AS pct_users_ever_withdrawn_or_expired,
  MIN(cr.occurred_at) AS earliest_occurred_at,
  MAX(cr.occurred_at) AS latest_occurred_at
FROM consent_records cr
GROUP BY cr.purpose
ORDER BY total_records DESC, cr.purpose
builds_on: Consent trend by purpose and month: grants, withdrawals, and net opt-in rate
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide, full history, no date filter, one row per distinct purpose value as requested; this will surface every purpose actually present in consent_records (not just analytics_cookies) and show withdrawn/expired patterns across all of them.

entries.title: Post-erasure data footprint: what remains in sessions, logins, and access log
entries.question: After a data subject's erasure request is completed, what login/session and access-log history still remains, and for how long?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.public_id AS dsar_public_id,
  t0.tenant_name,
  t0.subject_user_id,
  t0.completed_at_date,
  DATE '2026-01-05' - t0.completed_at_date AS days_since_completed,
  COALESCE(t1.sessions_remaining, 0) AS sessions_remaining,
  t1.most_recent_session_started_at,
  COALESCE(t2.login_attempts_remaining, 0) AS login_attempts_remaining,
  t2.most_recent_login_attempt_at,
  COALESCE(t3.access_log_rows_remaining, 0) AS access_log_rows_remaining,
  t3.most_recent_access_log_at
FROM (
  SELECT
    d0.id AS request_id,
    d0.public_id,
    d0.tenant_id,
    tn0.name AS tenant_name,
    d0.subject_user_id,
    CAST(d0.completed_at AS date) AS completed_at_date
  FROM data_subject_requests d0
  JOIN tenants tn0 ON tn0.id = d0.tenant_id
  WHERE d0.request_type = 'erasure'
    AND d0.status = 'completed'
    AND d0.subject_user_id IS NOT NULL
) t0
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    s0.tenant_id,
    s0.user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS sessions_remaining,
    MAX(s0.started_at) AS most_recent_session_started_at
  FROM sessions s0
  GROUP BY s0.tenant_id, s0.user_id
) t1 ON t1.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id AND t1.user_id = t0.subject_user_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    la0.tenant_id,
    la0.user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS login_attempts_remaining,
    MAX(la0.occurred_at) AS most_recent_login_attempt_at
  FROM login_attempts la0
  WHERE la0.user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY la0.tenant_id, la0.user_id
) t2 ON t2.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id AND t2.user_id = t0.subject_user_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    al0.tenant_id,
    al0.actor_user_id AS user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS access_log_rows_remaining,
    MAX(al0.occurred_at) AS most_recent_access_log_at
  FROM access_log al0
  WHERE al0.actor_user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY al0.tenant_id, al0.actor_user_id
) t3 ON t3.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id AND t3.user_id = t0.subject_user_id
ORDER BY t0.completed_at_date ASC, t0.request_id ASC
builds_on: Pre-2023 data subject requests: backfill or data quality issue?
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per completed erasure DSAR with subject_user_id populated (rows lacking a linked subject_user_id, if any, can't be matched to sessions/login_attempts/access_log and are excluded); joins to the three history tables are scoped by tenant_id + user_id for correctness in the multi-tenant schema. "Days since completed" is computed against the fixed reporting date 2026-01-05.

entries.title: Post-withdrawal marketing suppression check
entries.question: When a shopper withdraws marketing_email consent, do we actually stop sending them marketing campaign emails, or does sending continue after withdrawal?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.user_key) AS withdrawn_users,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cm.id IS NOT NULL THEN w.user_key END) AS contacted_after_withdrawal_users,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cm.id IS NOT NULL THEN w.user_key END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT w.user_key), 0), 2) AS pct_contacted_after_withdrawal,
  COUNT(cm.id) AS total_post_withdrawal_sends,
  MAX(COALESCE(cm.sent_at, cm.created_at)::date - w.withdrawn_at::date) AS max_days_withdrawal_to_send,
  MAX(COALESCE(cm.sent_at, cm.created_at)) AS most_recent_post_withdrawal_send
FROM (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    user_id,
    occurred_at AS withdrawn_at,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY tenant_id, user_id) AS user_key
  FROM (
    SELECT
      tenant_id,
      user_id,
      status,
      occurred_at,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id, user_id ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, id DESC) AS rn
    FROM consent_records
    WHERE purpose = 'marketing_email'
  ) ranked
  WHERE rn = 1 AND status = 'withdrawn'
) w
LEFT JOIN campaign_messages cm
  ON cm.tenant_id = w.tenant_id
  AND cm.user_id = w.user_id
  AND COALESCE(cm.sent_at, cm.created_at) > w.withdrawn_at
ORDER BY withdrawn_users
builds_on: Marketing-email consent opt-in trend, full history
entries.engineer_note: Single aggregate row as requested: withdrawn-user population defined by each (tenant_id,user_id)'s latest marketing_email consent_records row being 'withdrawn' (platform-wide, full history through 2025-12-31). A send counts as post-withdrawal when COALESCE(sent_at, created_at) is strictly after the withdrawal's occurred_at; max-days and most-recent-send are computed only over users/sends that actually have a post-withdrawal match.

entries.title: Post-erasure login and session activity: timing and success
entries.question: After an erasure is marked completed, do login attempts and sessions actually stop, or does activity continue afterward — and if attempts occur, do any of them succeed?
entries.sql:
WITH erasures AS (
  SELECT dsr.id, dsr.public_id, dsr.tenant_id, t.name AS tenant_name, dsr.subject_user_id, dsr.completed_at
  FROM data_subject_requests dsr
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = dsr.tenant_id
  WHERE dsr.request_type = 'erasure' AND dsr.status = 'completed'
),
la AS (
  SELECT e.id AS erasure_id,
    count(*) AS login_attempts_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE la.succeeded) AS succeeded_count,
    min(la.occurred_at) AS earliest_attempt,
    max(la.occurred_at) AS latest_attempt
  FROM erasures e
  JOIN login_attempts la
    ON la.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
   AND la.user_id = e.subject_user_id
   AND la.occurred_at > e.completed_at
  GROUP BY e.id
),
se AS (
  SELECT e.id AS erasure_id,
    count(*) AS sessions_count,
    max(s.started_at) AS latest_session_start
  FROM erasures e
  JOIN sessions s
    ON s.tenant_id = e.tenant_id
   AND s.user_id = e.subject_user_id
   AND s.started_at > e.completed_at
  GROUP BY e.id
)
SELECT
  e.public_id AS dsar_public_id,
  e.tenant_name,
  e.subject_user_id,
  CAST(e.completed_at AS date) AS completed_at,
  COALESCE(la.login_attempts_count, 0) AS login_attempts_after,
  COALESCE(la.succeeded_count, 0) AS succeeded_attempts_after,
  la.earliest_attempt AS earliest_login_attempt_after,
  la.latest_attempt AS latest_login_attempt_after,
  COALESCE(se.sessions_count, 0) AS sessions_after,
  se.latest_session_start AS latest_session_start_after
FROM erasures e
LEFT JOIN la ON la.erasure_id = e.id
LEFT JOIN se ON se.erasure_id = e.id
ORDER BY e.completed_at ASC, e.id ASC
builds_on: Post-erasure data footprint: what remains in sessions, logins, and access log
entries.engineer_note: One row per completed erasure DSAR (same 39 rows), with login_attempts and sessions aggregated separately (via per-request subqueries) before joining back, so the strictly-after-completed_at filter does not fan out or double count across the two activity types.

entries.title: Does completed erasure actually deactivate the core user record?
entries.question: When an erasure request is marked completed, is the underlying users row actually deactivated or anonymized, or does the account remain fully active?
entries.sql:
select
  dsr.public_id as dsar_public_id,
  t.name as tenant_name,
  dsr.subject_user_id,
  cast(dsr.completed_at as date) as completed_at,
  u.status as user_status,
  cast(u.deleted_at as date) as user_deleted_at,
  u.updated_at as user_updated_at,
  cast(u.last_login_at as date) as user_last_login_at
from data_subject_requests dsr
join tenants t on t.id = dsr.tenant_id
join users u on u.tenant_id = dsr.tenant_id and u.id = dsr.subject_user_id
where dsr.request_type = 'erasure'
  and dsr.status = 'completed'
order by dsr.completed_at asc, dsr.public_id asc
builds_on: Post-erasure data footprint: what remains in sessions, logins, and access log
entries.engineer_note: One row per completed erasure DSAR joined to its subject user; no PII beyond status/deleted_at/updated_at/last_login_at pulled, as requested.

entries.title: Is users.deleted_at used anywhere on the platform?
entries.question: Is deleted_at a field that's actually populated for any users platform-wide, or is account deactivation simply not wired up at all (context for the erasure finding)?
entries.sql:
with user_status_stats as (
    select
        status,
        count(*) as total_users,
        count(deleted_at) as users_with_deleted_at,
        max(deleted_at) as most_recent_deleted_at
    from users
    group by status
)
select
    status,
    total_users,
    users_with_deleted_at as count_with_deleted_at_not_null,
    round(100.0 * users_with_deleted_at / nullif(total_users, 0), 2) as pct_with_deleted_at_set,
    most_recent_deleted_at
from user_status_stats
order by total_users desc, status asc
builds_on: Does completed erasure actually deactivate the core user record?
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide, all tenants, full history, one row per users.status as requested.

entries.title: Merchants Affected by the Sync-Webhook Stuck-Retry Pattern and Their Size
entries.question: How many merchants have ERP/WMS/Accounting sync webhooks stuck in retry, and is this concentrated in our biggest accounts or spread across the long tail?
entries.sql:
WITH sync_webhooks AS (
  SELECT id, tenant_id
  FROM webhooks
  WHERE lower(name) LIKE '%erp%sync%'
     OR lower(name) LIKE '%wms%sync%'
     OR lower(name) LIKE '%accounting%sync%'
),
distinct_sync_tenants AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id FROM sync_webhooks
),
sync_deliveries_2025 AS (
  SELECT wd.tenant_id, wd.status
  FROM webhook_deliveries wd
  JOIN sync_webhooks sw ON sw.id = wd.webhook_id
  WHERE wd.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND wd.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
delivery_stats AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_sync_deliveries_2025,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS success_rate_pct,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status IN ('pending','retrying') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pending_or_retrying_rate_pct
  FROM sync_deliveries_2025
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
order_eur_amounts AS (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    o.id AS order_id,
    CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
         ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate END AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tenant_revenue_all AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders_2025,
    ROUND(SUM(revenue_eur), 2) AS total_revenue_eur_2025
  FROM order_eur_amounts
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
revenue_ranked AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    total_orders_2025,
    total_revenue_eur_2025,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_revenue_eur_2025 DESC) AS revenue_rank
  FROM tenant_revenue_all
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  COALESCE(ds.total_sync_deliveries_2025, 0) AS total_sync_deliveries_2025,
  ds.success_rate_pct,
  ds.pending_or_retrying_rate_pct,
  COALESCE(rr.total_orders_2025, 0) AS total_orders_2025,
  rr.total_revenue_eur_2025,
  rr.revenue_rank
FROM distinct_sync_tenants dst
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = dst.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN delivery_stats ds ON ds.tenant_id = dst.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN revenue_ranked rr ON rr.tenant_id = dst.tenant_id
ORDER BY ds.pending_or_retrying_rate_pct DESC NULLS LAST, t.name ASC
builds_on: 2025 Webhook Delivery Reliability by Endpoint
Webhook Delivery Reliability: Carts.remind-Affected Tenants vs Others, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Dry runs never expose data, so I could not inspect the exact distinct webhooks.name values; I matched any webhook whose name contains 'erp'+'sync', 'wms'+'sync', or 'accounting'+'sync' (case-insensitive) to capture the three sync types and close variants. Tenants with a qualifying webhook but no 2025 deliveries, orders, or EUR rate match show 0/NULL rather than being dropped; revenue_rank is NULL if the tenant had no 2025 orders. No row limit was applied since the analyst asked for all qualifying tenants.

entries.title: 2025 Monthly Stuck-Retry Rate for Sync Webhooks (ERP/WMS/Accounting)
entries.question: Has the ~15% stuck-in-retry rate on sync webhooks been happening all year, or did it start/worsen recently?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t0.month_start AS month,
  t0.total_sync_deliveries,
  ROUND(100.0 * t0.success_count / NULLIF(t0.total_sync_deliveries,0), 2) AS success_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * t0.failed_count / NULLIF(t0.total_sync_deliveries,0), 2) AS failed_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * t0.pending_retrying_count / NULLIF(t0.total_sync_deliveries,0), 2) AS pending_or_retrying_rate_pct
FROM (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', wd.created_at) AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS total_sync_deliveries,
    SUM(CASE WHEN wd.status = 'success' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS success_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN wd.status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN wd.status IN ('pending','retrying') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pending_retrying_count
  FROM webhook_deliveries wd
  JOIN webhooks wh ON wh.id = wd.webhook_id
  WHERE wh.name IN ('ERP sync','WMS sync','ACCOUNTING sync')
    AND wd.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND wd.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY date_trunc('month', wd.created_at)
) t0
ORDER BY t0.month_start ASC
builds_on: 2025 Webhook Delivery Reliability Trend
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide monthly rates for webhooks named 'ERP sync', 'WMS sync', 'ACCOUNTING sync' across all tenants, using webhook_deliveries.created_at for 2025. "Pending or retrying" combines the pending and retrying status codes (the only non-success/non-failed states in this table).

entries.title: Carts.remind Failure Root Cause: Error Messages
entries.question: Did the 20 carts.remind failures in Nov 2025 share a common root cause (pointing to one shared bug/config issue) or look like scattered, tenant-specific problems (pointing to load/capacity)?
entries.sql:
select
  t.name as tenant_name,
  jr.queued_at,
  jr.started_at,
  jr.finished_at,
  jr.error_message,
  jr.attempt
from job_runs jr
join jobs j on j.id = jr.job_id
join tenants t on t.id = jr.tenant_id
where j.handler = 'carts.remind'
  and jr.status = 'failed'
  and jr.queued_at >= date '2025-11-01'
  and jr.queued_at < date '2025-12-01'
order by jr.queued_at asc, t.name asc
builds_on: 2025 Job Failures by Job Type (Handler)
entries.engineer_note: One row per failed carts.remind job run in Nov 2025, with tenant, timing and error_message/attempt to spot shared vs. scattered root causes; expect 20 rows.

entries.title: 2025 Monthly Sync-Webhook Stuck Rate for the 4 Highest-Impact Tenants
entries.question: For the 4 tenants that account for ~91% of all stuck sync-webhook deliveries (Brennquell Kaffee, Cragsley Outfitters, Ampfeld Elektronik, Marrowby & Vane), has their stuck rate been stable all year or is it new/worsening?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
       CAST(date_trunc('month', wd.created_at) AS date) AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS total_sync_deliveries,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE wd.status IN ('pending','retrying')) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pending_or_retrying_rate_pct
FROM webhook_deliveries wd
JOIN webhooks w ON w.id = wd.webhook_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = wd.tenant_id
WHERE t.name IN ('Brennquell Kaffee','Cragsley Outfitters','Ampfeld Elektronik','Marrowby & Vane')
  AND wd.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND wd.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  AND (w.name ILIKE '%ERP%sync%' OR w.name ILIKE '%WMS%sync%' OR w.name ILIKE '%ACCOUNTING%sync%')
GROUP BY t.name, date_trunc('month', wd.created_at)
ORDER BY t.name ASC, date_trunc('month', wd.created_at) ASC
builds_on: Merchants Affected by the Sync-Webhook Stuck-Retry Pattern and Their Size
2025 Monthly Stuck-Retry Rate for Sync Webhooks (ERP/WMS/Accounting)
entries.engineer_note: Month is printed as the first calendar day of that month (date type) since TO_CHAR isn't available in this engine; sync-webhook matching uses ILIKE '%ERP%sync%'/'%WMS%sync%'/'%ACCOUNTING%sync%' on webhooks.name to catch close name variants, consistent with the prior sync-webhook report's approach.

entries.title: Internal Health Check Signal Around the Nov 28 2025 Storefront API Outage
entries.question: Did our internal health checks detect a problem around the two carts.remind failure windows (2025-11-28, roughly 14:40 and 15:40 UTC)?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  date_trunc('hour', checked_at) AS hour,
  component,
  count(*) AS total_checks,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_healthy = false) AS unhealthy_checks,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_healthy = false) / count(*), 2) AS unhealthy_rate_pct,
  round(avg(latency_ms)) AS avg_latency_ms
FROM system_health_checks
WHERE checked_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-28 12:00:00'
  AND checked_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-11-28 18:00:00'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY hour ASC, component ASC
builds_on: Carts.remind Failure Root Cause: Error Messages
2025 Q4 Weekly Job Failures vs Health Check Alerts
entries.engineer_note: system_health_checks is not tenant-scoped in this report (it tracks internal platform components, not merchant data), so results are aggregated across all tenants per hour/component as requested.

entries.title: Ticket Subject Lines from Affected Merchants Before the Nov 24 Failures
entries.question: In the weeks before the carts.remind failures showed up in our logs, did the 10 affected merchants' shoppers raise tickets that look related to carts, reminders, or duplicate/missing emails?
entries.sql:
SELECT
    t2.name AS tenant_name,
    t0.created_at AS created_at,
    t0.subject AS subject,
    t0.status AS status,
    t0.priority AS priority
FROM tickets t0
JOIN users t1 ON t1.id = t0.requester_user_id
JOIN tenants t2 ON t2.id = t1.tenant_id
WHERE t2.name IN (
    'Ampfeld Elektronik',
    'Brennquell Kaffee',
    'Cinder Peak Sports Co.',
    'Cragsley Outfitters',
    'Fennel & Flint',
    'Gratlinie Outdoor',
    'Kibblewick',
    'Marrowby & Vane',
    'Petalcourt Beauty',
    'Studio Vrij'
)
AND t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-10-27'
AND t0.created_at < DATE '2025-11-24'
AND (
    lower(t0.subject) LIKE '%cart%'
    OR lower(t0.subject) LIKE '%remind%'
    OR lower(t0.subject) LIKE '%duplicate%'
    OR lower(t0.subject) LIKE '%missing%'
    OR lower(t0.subject) LIKE '%email%'
)
ORDER BY t0.created_at ASC, t0.id ASC
builds_on: Support Ticket Volume Around the Nov 2025 Carts.remind Incident
Support Tickets: Affected vs Other Tenants, Baseline vs Incident Period
entries.engineer_note: Query returns every matching ticket ordered by created_at (no row cap applied here); if the batch run returns more than 50 rows, only the first 50 will print per house rules and the analyst should check the total row count noted on the report.

entries.title: Checkout/Storefront Outage Timeline, Nov 28 2025
entries.question: Exactly when did the checkout/storefront outage start and end on Nov 28 2025?
entries.sql:
SELECT 
  date_trunc('hour', checked_at) + (floor(extract(minute from checked_at)/30)::int * interval '30 minute') AS interval_start,
  component,
  count(*) AS total_checks,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_healthy = false) AS unhealthy_checks,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_healthy = false) / count(*), 2) AS unhealthy_rate_pct,
  round(avg(latency_ms)) AS avg_latency_ms
FROM system_health_checks
WHERE checked_at >= timestamp '2025-11-28 13:00:00' AND checked_at < timestamp '2025-11-28 17:00:00'
  AND component IN ('checkout','storefront')
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY interval_start ASC, component ASC
builds_on: Internal Health Check Signal Around the Nov 28 2025 Storefront API Outage
entries.engineer_note: system_health_checks has no tenant filter requested, so this aggregates health checks across all tenants for the checkout/storefront components in the given window, as specified.

entries.title: Order Volume by Hour on Black Friday 2025 (Nov 28)
entries.question: Did order placement actually drop during the checkout outage window on Nov 28 2025, compared to the rest of that same (peak traffic) day?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM o.placed_at)::int AS hour,
  COUNT(*) AS total_orders_placed,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants_with_orders,
  ROUND(SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate)) AS total_revenue_eur
FROM orders o
JOIN exchange_rates er
  ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
  AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
  AND er.as_of = DATE '2025-11-28'
WHERE o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-11-28 00:00:00'
  AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-11-29 00:00:00'
GROUP BY EXTRACT(HOUR FROM o.placed_at)
ORDER BY hour ASC
builds_on: Checkout/Storefront Outage Timeline, Nov 28 2025
entries.engineer_note: Converted each order's grand_total to EUR by dividing by the EUR→order-currency exchange_rates.rate on 2025-11-28 (since rate is quoted as currency units per 1 EUR), then summed and rounded per hour. Hours with zero orders (if any) will not appear as rows since this is a GROUP BY over actual order placements.

entries.title: Black Friday 2025 Sales vs Surrounding Fridays and Black Friday 2024
entries.question: Despite the checkout outage, how did total Black Friday 2025 sales compare to the Fridays immediately before/after it and to Black Friday 2024 - was the day's performance meaningfully dented?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  v.calendar_date AS date,
  v.label AS label,
  count(o.id) AS total_orders,
  round(sum(o.grand_total / COALESCE(er.rate, 1))) AS total_revenue_eur
FROM (VALUES
    (date '2025-11-21', 'Prior Friday'),
    (date '2025-11-28', 'Black Friday 2025'),
    (date '2025-12-05', 'Following Friday'),
    (date '2024-11-29', 'Black Friday 2024')
  ) AS v(calendar_date, label)
LEFT JOIN orders o
  ON date(o.placed_at) = v.calendar_date
LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
  ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
  AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
  AND er.as_of = v.calendar_date
  AND o.currency_code <> 'EUR'
GROUP BY v.calendar_date, v.label
ORDER BY v.calendar_date ASC
builds_on: Order Volume by Hour on Black Friday 2025 (Nov 28)
entries.engineer_note: Revenue is sum of grand_total across all orders placed that UTC day, converted to EUR via exchange_rates (orders already in EUR use rate=1 since exchange_rates may not carry an EUR/EUR row). No order-status filter was applied since the request said "total orders/sales" without specifying a status; all orders placed that day are counted, including cancelled ones if any.

entries.title: Orders in the 14:00-16:00 UTC Window: Nov 28 vs Baseline Days
entries.question: How many orders (and how much revenue) were actually lost in the 14:00-16:00 UTC outage window on Black Friday, compared to the same window on comparable days?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  d.ref_date AS date,
  d.label AS label,
  COALESCE(w.orders_cnt, 0) AS orders_14_to_16_utc,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.revenue_eur, 0), 0) AS revenue_eur_14_to_16_utc,
  COALESCE(f.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders_full_day,
  ROUND(COALESCE(w.orders_cnt, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(f.total_orders, 0), 1) AS pct_of_day_in_window
FROM (VALUES
  (DATE '2025-11-21', 'Prior Friday'),
  (DATE '2025-11-28', 'Black Friday 2025'),
  (DATE '2025-12-05', 'Following Friday'),
  (DATE '2024-11-29', 'Black Friday 2024')
) AS d(ref_date, label)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    CAST(o.placed_at AS date) AS d,
    COUNT(*) AS orders_cnt,
    SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE CAST(o.placed_at AS date) IN (DATE '2025-11-21', DATE '2025-11-28', DATE '2025-12-05', DATE '2024-11-29')
    AND CAST(o.placed_at AS time) >= TIME '14:00:00'
    AND CAST(o.placed_at AS time) < TIME '16:00:00'
  GROUP BY CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
) AS w
  ON w.d = d.ref_date
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    CAST(o.placed_at AS date) AS d,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders
  FROM orders o
  WHERE CAST(o.placed_at AS date) IN (DATE '2025-11-21', DATE '2025-11-28', DATE '2025-12-05', DATE '2024-11-29')
  GROUP BY CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
) AS f
  ON f.d = d.ref_date
ORDER BY d.ref_date ASC
builds_on: Order Volume by Hour on Black Friday 2025 (Nov 28)
Black Friday 2025 Sales vs Surrounding Fridays and Black Friday 2024
entries.engineer_note: This aggregates across all tenants/merchants combined (no tenant filter was specified); revenue is converted to EUR per-order using that order's own currency and the exchange rate as_of its placed date. If the VP wants this broken out per merchant or filtered to specific tenants, let me know and I'll rerun.

entries.title: Checkout/Storefront Severe Outages, Nov-Dec 2025
entries.question: Was the Nov 28 checkout/storefront outage a one-off, or did similarly severe (>=50% unhealthy) readings happen at other times in the window we have data for?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  date_trunc('hour', checked_at) AS checked_hour,
  component,
  count(*) AS total_checks,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_healthy = false) AS unhealthy_checks,
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_healthy = false) / count(*), 2) AS unhealthy_rate_pct,
  round(avg(latency_ms)) AS avg_latency_ms
FROM system_health_checks
WHERE checked_at >= DATE '2025-11-01'
  AND checked_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  AND component IN ('checkout', 'storefront')
GROUP BY date_trunc('hour', checked_at), component
HAVING 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_healthy = false) / count(*) >= 50
ORDER BY checked_hour ASC, component ASC
builds_on: Checkout/Storefront Outage Timeline, Nov 28 2025
entries.engineer_note: system_health_checks carries tenant_id, but the request did not ask for a per-tenant breakdown, so checks are aggregated across all tenants per hour/component as specified. If this table is tenant-scoped and Nov 28 outage was specific to one or few tenants, a tenant-level cut may be worth a follow-up report.

entries.title: Payment Attempts During the Nov 28 2025 Outage Window
entries.question: Did payment processing itself fail or stall during the same 14:00-16:00 UTC window, confirming a full checkout-path outage rather than just the reminder-email job?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pa.attempted_at) AS hour,
  COUNT(*) AS total_payment_attempts,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE pa.status IN ('authorized', 'captured')) AS captured_or_authorized_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE pa.status = 'failed') AS failed_count,
  ROUND(
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE pa.status = 'failed')::decimal / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) * 100,
    2
  ) AS failure_rate_pct
FROM payment_attempts pa
WHERE pa.attempted_at >= DATE '2025-11-28'
  AND pa.attempted_at < DATE '2025-11-29'
GROUP BY EXTRACT(HOUR FROM pa.attempted_at)
ORDER BY hour ASC
builds_on: Order Volume by Hour on Black Friday 2025 (Nov 28)
entries.engineer_note: Query is platform-wide (all tenants) since the outage question is about the checkout path generally, not one merchant; hours with zero attempts will simply be absent from the 24-row output, as the request anticipated.

entries.title: Cragsley Outfitters: Poor Ratings by Product Category
entries.question: Within Cragsley Outfitters, is the poor-rating problem concentrated in particular kinds of products, or spread evenly across the catalog?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  c.name AS category_name,
  pc.product_count AS product_count,
  COALESCE(pr.products_5plus, 0) AS products_with_5plus_reviews,
  COALESCE(pr.poor_rated_count, 0) AS poor_rated_product_count,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(pr.products_5plus,0) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(pr.poor_rated_count::numeric / pr.products_5plus * 100, 1)
  END AS pct_poor_rated_products,
  ROUND(pr.avg_rating, 2) AS avg_rating_of_reviewed_products,
  COALESCE(rv.units_sold, 0) AS units_sold_last_12mo,
  ROUND(COALESCE(rv.revenue_eur, 0), 0) AS revenue_eur_last_12mo
FROM categories c
JOIN (
  SELECT p.primary_category_id, COUNT(*) AS product_count
  FROM products p
  WHERE p.tenant_id = (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Cragsley Outfitters')
    AND p.primary_category_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY p.primary_category_id
) pc ON pc.primary_category_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT p.primary_category_id,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE rc.review_count >= 5) AS products_5plus,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE rc.review_count >= 5 AND rc.avg_rating < 3.0) AS poor_rated_count,
    AVG(rc.avg_rating) FILTER (WHERE rc.review_count >= 5) AS avg_rating
  FROM products p
  JOIN (
    SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS review_count, AVG(rating) AS avg_rating
    FROM product_reviews
    WHERE is_approved = true
    GROUP BY product_id
  ) rc ON rc.product_id = p.id
  WHERE p.tenant_id = (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Cragsley Outfitters')
  GROUP BY p.primary_category_id
) pr ON pr.primary_category_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT p.primary_category_id,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold,
    SUM(CASE WHEN oi.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN oi.line_total ELSE oi.line_total / er.rate END) AS revenue_eur
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = oi.product_variant_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = oi.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.tenant_id = (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Cragsley Outfitters')
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND p.status = 'active'
  GROUP BY p.primary_category_id
) rv ON rv.primary_category_id = c.id
WHERE c.tenant_id = (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Cragsley Outfitters')
ORDER BY poor_rated_product_count DESC, pct_poor_rated_products DESC NULLS LAST, category_name
builds_on: Poorly-Rated Product Concentration by Merchant
entries.engineer_note: product_count and the review-based metrics include products of any status, while units_sold/revenue are restricted to currently active products per the request wording; revenue uses order_items.line_total (post-discount, pre/post-tax as stored) converted to EUR via same-day exchange_rates.

entries.title: Cragsley Outfitters: Rating Trend Over Time
entries.question: Has Cragsley Outfitters' rating problem been building over time, or has it always looked this way?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start AS month
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
),
tenant AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Cragsley Outfitters'
),
reviews AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', pr.created_at)::date AS month,
         count(*) AS review_count,
         avg(pr.rating) AS avg_rating,
         100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE pr.rating <= 2) / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS pct_1_2_star
  FROM product_reviews pr
  JOIN tenant t ON pr.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE pr.is_approved = true
  GROUP BY 1
),
orders_agg AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', o.placed_at)::date AS month,
         count(*) AS orders_count,
         sum(
           CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
                ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate
           END
         ) AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenant t ON o.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  strftime(m.month, '%Y-%m') AS month,
  COALESCE(r.review_count, 0) AS review_count,
  ROUND(r.avg_rating::numeric, 2) AS avg_rating,
  ROUND(r.pct_1_2_star::numeric, 1) AS pct_1_2_star,
  COALESCE(oa.orders_count, 0) AS orders_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(oa.revenue_eur, 0)::numeric, 0) AS revenue_eur
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN reviews r ON r.month = m.month
LEFT JOIN orders_agg oa ON oa.month = m.month
ORDER BY m.month ASC
builds_on: Poorly-Rated Product Concentration by Merchant
Monthly Review Volume and Rating Trend
entries.engineer_note: avg_rating and pct_1_2_star are NULL for months with zero approved reviews (no reviews to average); review_count and orders_count show 0 as requested. EUR-currency orders are passed through at face value, others converted via exchange_rates as of placed_at date.

entries.title: Cragsley Outfitters: Sales Trajectory of Poor-Rated vs Other Products
entries.question: For Cragsley's already-identified poor-rated products, is demand starting to slow down to match the bad reviews, or is it still growing despite them?
entries.sql:
WITH tenant_cte AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Cragsley Outfitters'
),
poor_tier AS (
  SELECT pr.product_id
  FROM product_reviews pr
  JOIN tenant_cte t ON pr.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE pr.is_approved = true
  GROUP BY pr.product_id
  HAVING count(*) >= 5 AND avg(pr.rating) < 3.0
),
other_tier AS (
  SELECT p.id AS product_id
  FROM products p
  JOIN tenant_cte t ON p.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE p.status = 'active'
    AND p.id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM poor_tier)
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start AS month
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-01'
),
line_items AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', o.placed_at)::date AS month,
    pv.product_id AS product_id,
    oi.quantity AS quantity,
    oi.line_total AS line_total,
    oi.currency_code AS currency_code,
    o.placed_at::date AS placed_date
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON oi.product_variant_id = pv.id
  JOIN tenant_cte t ON o.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
converted AS (
  SELECT
    li.month,
    li.product_id,
    li.quantity,
    CASE WHEN li.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN li.line_total
         ELSE li.line_total / er.rate END AS revenue_eur
  FROM line_items li
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = li.currency_code AND er.as_of = li.placed_date
),
tiered AS (
  SELECT c.month,
    CASE WHEN c.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM poor_tier) THEN 'poor'
         WHEN c.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM other_tier) THEN 'other'
         ELSE NULL END AS tier,
    c.quantity,
    c.revenue_eur
  FROM converted c
)
SELECT
  m.month,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.tier='poor' THEN t.quantity END),0) AS poor_tier_units_sold,
  ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.tier='poor' THEN t.revenue_eur END),0)) AS poor_tier_revenue_eur,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.tier='other' THEN t.quantity END),0) AS other_tier_units_sold,
  ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.tier='other' THEN t.revenue_eur END),0)) AS other_tier_revenue_eur
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN tiered t ON t.month = m.month
GROUP BY m.month
ORDER BY m.month
builds_on: Poorly-Rated Product Concentration by Merchant
entries.engineer_note: Poor tier is recomputed from the stated rule (>=5 approved reviews, all-time avg rating <3.0) rather than reusing the prior report's product list directly, since that list isn't materialized in the warehouse; it should match the 23 products if the same rule was used. Revenue uses order_items.line_total (post-discount, pre-tax) converted to EUR via same-day exchange_rates, rounded to whole EUR; products in neither tier (inactive, non-poor) are excluded from both columns.

entries.title: Fennel & Flint and Wiesgrund Wohnen: Review Sentiment vs Delivery Performance, Monthly
entries.question: Did delivery delays coincide with the rating dip at the two Home & Living merchants flagged last week, consistent with the platform-wide carrier breakdown?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start, month_label FROM calendar_days WHERE month_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-07-01' AND DATE '2025-12-01'
),
tenants_filtered AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id, name AS merchant_name FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Fennel & Flint','Wiesgrund Wohnen')
),
base AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, t.merchant_name, m.month_start, m.month_label
  FROM tenants_filtered t CROSS JOIN months m
),
reviews AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS review_count,
    AVG(rating) AS avg_rating,
    SUM(CASE WHEN rating IN (1,2) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_low
  FROM product_reviews
  WHERE is_approved = true
    AND tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM tenants_filtered)
    AND created_at >= DATE '2025-07-01' AND created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY tenant_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)::date
),
ship AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', s.shipped_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS shipments_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at <= INTERVAL '5 days' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_within_5,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_known,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.carrier = 'Albion Parcel' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS albion_count
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
  WHERE o.tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM tenants_filtered)
    AND s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-07-01' AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', s.shipped_at)::date
)
SELECT
  b.merchant_name,
  b.month_label AS month,
  COALESCE(r.review_count,0) AS review_count,
  ROUND(r.avg_rating::numeric,2) AS avg_rating,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN r.review_count > 0 THEN r.cnt_low::numeric / r.review_count * 100 ELSE NULL END,1) AS pct_1_2_star,
  COALESCE(sh.shipments_count,0) AS shipments_count,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN sh.delivered_known > 0 THEN sh.delivered_within_5::numeric / sh.delivered_known * 100 ELSE NULL END,1) AS pct_delivered_within_5_days,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN sh.shipments_count > 0 THEN sh.albion_count::numeric / sh.shipments_count * 100 ELSE NULL END,1) AS pct_shipped_via_albion_parcel
FROM base b
LEFT JOIN reviews r ON r.tenant_id = b.tenant_id AND r.month_start = b.month_start
LEFT JOIN ship sh ON sh.tenant_id = b.tenant_id AND sh.month_start = b.month_start
ORDER BY b.merchant_name, b.month_start
builds_on: Home & Living December 2025 Rating Dip: Merchant Breakdown
entries.engineer_note: pct_delivered_within_5_days excludes shipments with a null delivered_at from both numerator and denominator per the request; the count of such excluded shipments isn't shown as a column since it wasn't in the requested grain, but it equals shipments_count minus the implied delivered_known count for each row if you need to inspect it separately.

entries.title: Image-Count Buckets: Product Age, Status, and Vertical Mix
entries.question: Are zero-image product listings systematically different from one-plus-image listings (older, more likely draft/archived, or concentrated in certain verticals), rather than the image count itself being the driver?
entries.sql:
WITH product_base AS (
  SELECT
    t0.id AS product_id,
    t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t0.status AS status,
    t0.created_at AS created_at,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(t1.image_count, 0) = 0 THEN '0'
      WHEN COALESCE(t1.image_count, 0) = 1 THEN '1'
      WHEN COALESCE(t1.image_count, 0) BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN '2-3'
      WHEN COALESCE(t1.image_count, 0) BETWEEN 4 AND 6 THEN '4-6'
      ELSE '7+'
    END AS image_count_bucket
  FROM products t0
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      t1a.product_id AS product_id,
      COUNT(*) AS image_count
    FROM product_media t1a
    WHERE t1a.kind = 'image'
    GROUP BY t1a.product_id
  ) t1 ON t1.product_id = t0.id
),
dim_bucket AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t2.image_count_bucket AS image_count_bucket
  FROM product_base t2
),
m_count AS (
  SELECT
    t3.image_count_bucket AS image_count_bucket,
    COUNT(*) AS product_count
  FROM product_base t3
  GROUP BY t3.image_count_bucket
),
m_age AS (
  SELECT
    t4.image_count_bucket AS image_count_bucket,
    AVG(CAST(DATE '2025-12-31' - CAST(t4.created_at AS date) AS numeric)) AS avg_days_since_created
  FROM product_base t4
  GROUP BY t4.image_count_bucket
),
m_status AS (
  SELECT
    t5.image_count_bucket AS image_count_bucket,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t5.status = 'draft' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_status_draft,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t5.status = 'archived' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_status_archived,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t5.status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_status_active
  FROM product_base t5
  GROUP BY t5.image_count_bucket
),
m_industry AS (
  SELECT
    t6.image_count_bucket AS image_count_bucket,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(t7.industry) LIKE '%apparel%' OR LOWER(t7.industry) LIKE '%footwear%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_apparel_footwear_industry,
    100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(t7.industry) LIKE '%office%' OR LOWER(t7.industry) LIKE '%industrial%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS pct_b2b_industry
  FROM product_base t6
  JOIN tenants t7 ON t7.id = t6.tenant_id
  GROUP BY t6.image_count_bucket
),
m_variants AS (
  SELECT
    t8.image_count_bucket AS image_count_bucket,
    AVG(COALESCE(t9.variant_count, 0)) AS avg_variants_per_product
  FROM product_base t8
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      t9a.product_id AS product_id,
      COUNT(*) AS variant_count
    FROM product_variants t9a
    GROUP BY t9a.product_id
  ) t9 ON t9.product_id = t8.product_id
  GROUP BY t8.image_count_bucket
)
SELECT
  t10.image_count_bucket AS image_count_bucket,
  COALESCE(t11.product_count, 0) AS product_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t12.avg_days_since_created, 0), 1) AS avg_days_since_created,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t13.pct_status_draft, 0), 1) AS pct_status_draft,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t13.pct_status_archived, 0), 1) AS pct_status_archived,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t13.pct_status_active, 0), 1) AS pct_status_active,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t14.pct_apparel_footwear_industry, 0), 1) AS pct_apparel_footwear_industry,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t14.pct_b2b_industry, 0), 1) AS pct_b2b_industry,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t15.avg_variants_per_product, 0), 1) AS avg_variants_per_product
FROM dim_bucket t10
LEFT JOIN m_count t11 ON t11.image_count_bucket = t10.image_count_bucket
LEFT JOIN m_age t12 ON t12.image_count_bucket = t10.image_count_bucket
LEFT JOIN m_status t13 ON t13.image_count_bucket = t10.image_count_bucket
LEFT JOIN m_industry t14 ON t14.image_count_bucket = t10.image_count_bucket
LEFT JOIN m_variants t15 ON t15.image_count_bucket = t10.image_count_bucket
ORDER BY
  CASE t10.image_count_bucket
    WHEN '0' THEN 1
    WHEN '1' THEN 2
    WHEN '2-3' THEN 3
    WHEN '4-6' THEN 4
    WHEN '7+' THEN 5
  END
builds_on: Catalog Richness vs Sales Performance by Image Count Bucket
Image-Richness vs Sales Within Apparel & Footwear
entries.engineer_note: tenants.industry is free text, not a fixed enum, so apparel/footwear and B2B (office+industrial) shares are matched via case-insensitive substring matching on keywords ('apparel'/'footwear', 'office'/'industrial') rather than exact category codes; this could miss or over-match if the stored labels differ from expectations.

entries.title: Merchants Using Bundles: Raw Profile
entries.question: Among the handful of merchants that actually use product bundles, is there anything descriptively distinctive about them compared to the typical merchant?
entries.sql:
WITH bundle_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS active_bundle_count
  FROM product_bundles
  WHERE is_active = true
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
product_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS active_product_count
  FROM products
  WHERE status = 'active'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
variant_counts AS (
  SELECT p.tenant_id,
         COUNT(pv.id)::decimal / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.id), 0) AS avg_variants_per_product
  FROM products p
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.product_id = p.id AND pv.is_active = true
  WHERE p.status = 'active'
  GROUP BY p.tenant_id
),
bundled_products AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT p.tenant_id, p.id AS product_id
  FROM product_bundles pb
  JOIN bundle_items bi ON bi.bundle_id = pb.id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = bi.variant_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
  WHERE pb.is_active = true AND p.status = 'active'
),
bundled_product_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS bundled_product_count
  FROM bundled_products
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
order_stats AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id,
         SUM(o.grand_total / er.rate) AS revenue_eur,
         COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders o
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS date)
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  t.name AS merchant_name,
  t.industry,
  bc.active_bundle_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(bpc.bundled_product_count, 0) / NULLIF(pc.active_product_count, 0), 1) AS pct_active_products_in_a_bundle,
  pc.active_product_count,
  ROUND(vc.avg_variants_per_product, 2) AS avg_variants_per_product,
  ROUND(os.revenue_eur, 2) AS revenue_eur_last_12mo,
  ROUND(os.revenue_eur / NULLIF(os.order_count, 0), 2) AS avg_order_value_eur_last_12mo
FROM bundle_counts bc
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = bc.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN product_counts pc ON pc.tenant_id = bc.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN variant_counts vc ON vc.tenant_id = bc.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN bundled_product_counts bpc ON bpc.tenant_id = bc.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN order_stats os ON os.tenant_id = bc.tenant_id
ORDER BY pct_active_products_in_a_bundle DESC NULLS LAST, revenue_eur_last_12mo DESC NULLS LAST, t.id ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Collections and Bundles Adoption by Merchant
entries.engineer_note: Assumed definitions consistent with the named earlier reports: active_product_count/avg_variants_per_product scoped to status='active' products (variants with is_active=true); "in a bundle" means the product's variant appears as a component (bundle_items.variant_id) of an active bundle; revenue and AOV use orders placed 2025-01-01..2025-12-31, status<>'cancelled', converted to EUR via exchange_rates(EUR->currency, same day). If those earlier reports used different scoping, figures may need reconciling.

entries.title: Wiesgrund Wohnen December 2025: Product-Level Review Breakdown
entries.question: Since delivery performance doesn't explain Wiesgrund Wohnen's December dip, which specific products drove it?
entries.sql:
SELECT p.name as product_name,
       c.name as category_name,
       r.review_count,
       r.avg_rating,
       r.pct_1_2_star,
       (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity),0)
        FROM order_items oi
        JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
        WHERE o.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
          AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
          AND o.placed_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
          AND oi.product_variant_id IN (SELECT pv.id FROM product_variants pv WHERE pv.product_id = p.id)
       ) AS units_sold_last_12mo
FROM products p
JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
JOIN (
   SELECT pr.product_id,
          COUNT(*) AS review_count,
          ROUND(AVG(pr.rating),2) AS avg_rating,
          ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN pr.rating IN (1,2) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_1_2_star
   FROM product_reviews pr
   WHERE pr.is_approved = true
     AND pr.created_at >= timestamp '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
     AND pr.tenant_id = (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Wiesgrund Wohnen')
   GROUP BY pr.product_id
) r ON r.product_id = p.id
WHERE p.tenant_id = (SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE name = 'Wiesgrund Wohnen')
ORDER BY r.review_count DESC, r.avg_rating ASC, p.name ASC
builds_on: Fennel & Flint and Wiesgrund Wohnen: Review Sentiment vs Delivery Performance, Monthly
entries.engineer_note: units_sold_last_12mo uses orders.placed_at in 2025-01-01..2025-12-31 and excludes only 'cancelled' status (other non-fulfilled statuses like pending/refunded are still counted as sold units, per the request's wording "placed ... with status not cancelled").

entries.title: Fennel & Flint and Wiesgrund Wohnen: Historical December Pattern, 2023-2025
entries.question: Is the December rating dip a recurring yearly pattern for these two merchants (like we found at Cragsley), or something new and specific to 2025?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.name AS merchant_name, y.year,
  COALESCE(r.dec_review_count,0) AS dec_review_count,
  r.dec_avg_rating,
  r.dec_pct_1_2_star,
  COALESCE(o.dec_orders_count,0) AS dec_orders_count
FROM tenants t
CROSS JOIN (VALUES (2023),(2024),(2025)) AS y(year)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_at)::int AS yr,
    COUNT(*) AS dec_review_count,
    ROUND(AVG(rating)::numeric,2) AS dec_avg_rating,
    ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN rating<=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) AS dec_pct_1_2_star
  FROM product_reviews
  WHERE is_approved = true AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM created_at) = 12
  GROUP BY tenant_id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_at)
) r ON r.tenant_id = t.id AND r.yr = y.year
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM placed_at)::int AS yr,
    COUNT(*) AS dec_orders_count
  FROM orders
  WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM placed_at) = 12
  GROUP BY tenant_id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM placed_at)
) o ON o.tenant_id = t.id AND o.yr = y.year
WHERE t.name IN ('Fennel & Flint','Wiesgrund Wohnen')
ORDER BY t.name, y.year
builds_on: Fennel & Flint and Wiesgrund Wohnen: Review Sentiment vs Delivery Performance, Monthly
Cragsley Outfitters: Rating Trend Over Time
entries.engineer_note: Grain is merchant x year (Dec only, 2023-2025), one row per combination even if no reviews/orders occurred that December (counts show as 0, rating/pct as null). Review metrics use is_approved=true and created_at in December; orders use placed_at in December excluding cancelled status.

entries.title: Bundle Adoption Rate by Vertical
entries.question: Is bundle adoption really concentrated in specific verticals, and how strong is that pattern across the whole merchant base, not just the list of bundle-users?
entries.sql:
WITH active_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id, industry
  FROM tenants
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
),
bundle_using_tenants AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id
  FROM product_bundles
  WHERE is_active = true
),
active_products AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, id AS product_id
  FROM products
  WHERE status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL
),
bundled_product_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT pv.tenant_id, pv.product_id
  FROM bundle_items bi
  JOIN product_bundles pb
    ON pb.id = bi.bundle_id AND pb.tenant_id = bi.tenant_id
  JOIN product_variants pv
    ON pv.id = bi.variant_id AND pv.tenant_id = bi.tenant_id
  WHERE pb.is_active = true
),
tenant_bundle_counts AS (
  SELECT
    ap.tenant_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ap.product_id) AS active_product_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT bp.product_id) AS bundled_active_product_count
  FROM active_products ap
  LEFT JOIN bundled_product_ids bp
    ON bp.tenant_id = ap.tenant_id AND bp.product_id = ap.product_id
  GROUP BY ap.tenant_id
),
tenant_pct AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    CASE WHEN active_product_count > 0
      THEN bundled_active_product_count::decimal / active_product_count * 100
      ELSE NULL END AS pct_active_products_in_a_bundle
  FROM tenant_bundle_counts
),
tenant_summary AS (
  SELECT
    ten.tenant_id,
    COALESCE(ten.industry, 'Unknown') AS industry,
    CASE WHEN bu.tenant_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS uses_bundles,
    tp.pct_active_products_in_a_bundle
  FROM active_tenants ten
  LEFT JOIN bundle_using_tenants bu ON bu.tenant_id = ten.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN tenant_pct tp ON tp.tenant_id = ten.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  industry,
  COUNT(*) AS merchant_count,
  SUM(uses_bundles) AS merchants_using_bundles,
  ROUND(SUM(uses_bundles)::decimal / COUNT(*) * 100, 1) AS pct_merchants_using_bundles,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN uses_bundles = 1 THEN pct_active_products_in_a_bundle END), 1) AS avg_pct_products_bundled_among_users
FROM tenant_summary
GROUP BY industry
ORDER BY pct_merchants_using_bundles DESC, industry ASC
builds_on: Merchants Using Bundles: Raw Profile
Collections and Bundles Adoption by Merchant
entries.engineer_note: I didn't have the exact prior report text defining "pct_active_products_in_a_bundle," so I defined it per tenant as: (distinct active products whose variants appear as a component in at least one active bundle) / (distinct active, non-deleted products) * 100 — i.e. how much of the live catalog participates in bundling as a component. Tenants with no active products get a null pct, excluded from the average. Industry is blank-coalesced to 'Unknown' so every non-deleted tenant is represented.

entries.title: Bundle Creation Timing: Seeded in a Batch or Built Up Organically?
entries.question: Does the suspiciously clean 100%/0% bundle adoption split by vertical look like genuine, ongoing merchant activity, or does it look like a one-time data-seeding event?
entries.sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE month_start >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND month_start <= DATE '2025-12-01'
),
bundles AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at)::date AS month_start,
    COUNT(*) AS bundles_created_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants_creating_a_bundle
  FROM product_bundles
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  STRFTIME(m.month_start, '%Y-%m') AS month,
  COALESCE(b.bundles_created_count, 0) AS bundles_created_count,
  COALESCE(b.distinct_tenants_creating_a_bundle, 0) AS distinct_tenants_creating_a_bundle
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN bundles b ON b.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start
builds_on: Bundle Adoption Rate by Vertical
entries.engineer_note: One row per calendar month 2023-01 through 2025-12, built off the full calendar so zero-activity months still appear; counts are based on product_bundles.created_at regardless of tenant vertical (verticals live on tenants, not requested as a column per the grain given).

entries.title: Return and Damage Rates for Fragile vs Other Home & Living Categories
entries.question: Do fragile homeware categories (cookware, glassware, tableware, decor) see more damage-related returns than other Home & Living categories, supporting the in-transit-breakage theory for the December dip?
entries.sql:
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT
    c.name AS category_name,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = oi.product_variant_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
  JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE t.industry = 'Home & Living'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY c.name
),
returns AS (
  SELECT
    c.name AS category_name,
    COUNT(*) AS return_count,
    SUM(CASE
          WHEN LOWER(orr.reason) LIKE '%damage%'
            OR LOWER(orr.reason) LIKE '%broken%'
            OR LOWER(orr.reason) LIKE '%crack%'
            OR LOWER(orr.reason) LIKE '%chip%'
            OR LOWER(orr.reason) LIKE '%shattered%'
          THEN 1 ELSE 0
        END) AS damage_count
  FROM return_items ri
  JOIN order_returns orr ON orr.id = ri.return_id
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.id = ri.order_item_id
  JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = oi.product_variant_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
  JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE t.industry = 'Home & Living'
    AND orr.requested_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND orr.requested_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY c.name
)
SELECT
  s.category_name,
  s.units_sold AS units_sold_last_12mo,
  COALESCE(r.return_count, 0) AS return_count,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.return_count, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(s.units_sold, 0), 1) AS return_rate_pct,
  ROUND(COALESCE(r.damage_count, 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(r.return_count, 0), 1) AS pct_returns_damage_related
FROM sales s
LEFT JOIN returns r ON r.category_name = s.category_name
ORDER BY return_rate_pct DESC NULLS LAST, s.category_name ASC
builds_on: Wiesgrund Wohnen December 2025: Product-Level Review Breakdown
entries.engineer_note: Grain is by category name, rolled up across all Home & Living tenants that sold units in the product's primary category during 2025 (categories with zero units sold in the window are excluded since return rate would be undefined); damage-related share is computed only among the category's own returns, so it's null when return_count is 0.

entries.title: Fennel & Flint December 2025: Product-Level Review Breakdown
entries.question: Is Fennel & Flint's declining rating trend concentrated in specific products, or spread broadly across its catalog, in parallel to what we found at Wiesgrund Wohnen?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  p.name AS product_name,
  c.name AS category_name,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM product_reviews pr
     WHERE pr.product_id = p.id AND pr.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
       AND pr.is_approved = true
       AND pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  ) AS review_count,
  (SELECT ROUND(AVG(pr.rating)::numeric, 2) FROM product_reviews pr
     WHERE pr.product_id = p.id AND pr.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
       AND pr.is_approved = true
       AND pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  ) AS avg_rating,
  (SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN pr.rating <= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) FROM product_reviews pr
     WHERE pr.product_id = p.id AND pr.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
       AND pr.is_approved = true
       AND pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  ) AS pct_1_2_star,
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0)
     FROM order_items oi
     JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
     WHERE oi.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
       AND o.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
       AND o.status != 'cancelled'
       AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
       AND oi.product_variant_id IN (SELECT pv.id FROM product_variants pv WHERE pv.product_id = p.id)
  ) AS units_sold_last_12mo
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.primary_category_id
WHERE p.tenant_id = (SELECT t.id FROM tenants t WHERE t.name = 'Fennel & Flint')
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM product_reviews pr
    WHERE pr.product_id = p.id AND pr.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
      AND pr.is_approved = true
      AND pr.created_at >= DATE '2025-12-01' AND pr.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  )
ORDER BY review_count DESC, avg_rating ASC
builds_on: Wiesgrund Wohnen December 2025: Product-Level Review Breakdown
Fennel & Flint and Wiesgrund Wohnen: Historical December Pattern, 2023-2025
entries.engineer_note: units_sold_last_12mo is defined per the Wiesgrund report's spec as calendar-year 2025 order_items (not a true trailing-12-month window from report date), to match "same definitions" as requested.
warnings: 4 scalar subqueries in the select list (over a FROM, may be per-row values)

entries.title: Is the 'active' 18% of orphan subscription-delivery orders a categorization artifact or a real gap?
entries.question: For the ~291 orphan free-delivery orders where the customer's most-recent subscription record shows status 'active', did that order actually fall in a gap between an earlier (now-superseded) subscription and the current one, which would mean it belongs with the confirmed 'canceled' leakage group rather than being a separate unexplained case?
entries.sql:
WITH orphan_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.placed_at, od.amount AS discount_amount, od.currency_code AS discount_currency_code
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_discounts od ON od.order_id = o.id AND od.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN discounts d ON d.id = od.discount_id AND d.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE d.name = 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions s0
      WHERE s0.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
        AND s0.user_id = o.user_id
        AND s0.status IN ('trialing','active','past_due')
        AND s0.started_at <= o.placed_at
        AND (s0.ended_at IS NULL OR s0.ended_at >= o.placed_at)
    )
),
most_recent_sub AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.tenant_id, s.user_id)
    s.tenant_id, s.user_id, s.id AS sub_id, s.status
  FROM subscriptions s
  ORDER BY s.tenant_id, s.user_id, s.started_at DESC, s.id DESC
),
active_bucket_orders AS (
  SELECT oo.order_id, oo.tenant_id, oo.user_id, oo.placed_at,
         oo.discount_amount, oo.discount_currency_code,
         mrs.sub_id AS most_recent_sub_id
  FROM orphan_orders oo
  JOIN most_recent_sub mrs
    ON mrs.tenant_id = oo.tenant_id AND mrs.user_id = oo.user_id
  WHERE mrs.status = 'active'
),
older_sub_candidates AS (
  SELECT abo.order_id, s.id AS older_sub_id, s.started_at AS older_started_at, s.ended_at AS older_ended_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY abo.order_id ORDER BY s.started_at DESC, s.id DESC) AS rn
  FROM active_bucket_orders abo
  JOIN subscriptions s
    ON s.tenant_id = abo.tenant_id
   AND s.user_id = abo.user_id
   AND s.id <> abo.most_recent_sub_id
   AND s.started_at <= abo.placed_at
),
older_sub_pick AS (
  SELECT order_id, older_sub_id, older_started_at, older_ended_at
  FROM older_sub_candidates
  WHERE rn = 1
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    abo.order_id,
    abo.tenant_id,
    abo.user_id,
    abo.placed_at,
    abo.discount_amount,
    abo.discount_currency_code,
    CASE
      WHEN osp.older_sub_id IS NULL THEN 'order preceded customer''s first-ever subscription'
      WHEN osp.older_ended_at < abo.placed_at THEN 'order fell between two subscription stints (an older subscription record exists with started_at <= order date)'
      ELSE 'unexplained - active subscription dates should already have overlapped'
    END AS category
  FROM active_bucket_orders abo
  LEFT JOIN older_sub_pick osp ON osp.order_id = abo.order_id
),
with_eur AS (
  SELECT
    c.order_id, c.tenant_id, c.user_id, c.category,
    c.discount_amount / er.rate AS discount_amount_eur
  FROM classified c
  JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = c.discount_currency_code
   AND er.as_of = DATE(c.placed_at)
),
total AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM active_bucket_orders
)
SELECT
  w.category,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / t.total_orders, 1) AS pct_of_291_bucket,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(SUM(w.discount_amount_eur), 2) AS total_discount_eur
FROM with_eur w
CROSS JOIN total t
GROUP BY w.category, t.total_orders
ORDER BY order_count DESC, w.category
builds_on: Subscription status distribution behind orphan comped-delivery orders
entries.engineer_note: For each order in the active-bucket, I located the customer's most-recent subscription (by started_at) separately from any 'other' older subscription (started_at <= placed_at, picking the one with the latest started_at if several exist) and classified by whether that older subscription's started_at/ended_at window covered placed_at. The denominator used for the percentage is the actual count of active-bucket orphan orders found by the query (expected ~291) rather than a hardcoded 291, so it will self-check against last week's figure.

entries.title: Monthly trend of confirmed lapsed-subscriber free-delivery leakage, 2023-2025
