entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide snapshot across all tenants and currencies (no monetary amounts involved, so no FX conversion needed); 3 rows, one per status, as requested.

entries.title: Reconciled 2025 orphan population by tenant and subscription status (single pass)
entries.question: In one single query, does the 2025 orphan subscription-delivery population split by tenant reproduce last week's known-good totals (Grind Collective 167, Honeycomb Larder 127, Kibblewick 100, Feather & Fin 49, Saffron & Sage 17, The Balm Room 1 — 461 orders, €22,318.18 total), and how does each tenant's orphan pool split by the customer's most-recent subscription status?
entries.sql:
WITH base_orders AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.placed_at,
    o.currency_code
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status != 'cancelled'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM order_discounts od
      JOIN discounts d ON d.id = od.discount_id
      WHERE od.order_id = o.id
        AND d.name = 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)'
    )
),
row_per_order AS (
  SELECT
    bo.order_id,
    bo.tenant_id,
    bo.user_id,
    bo.placed_at,
    bo.currency_code,
    (
      SELECT SUM(od.amount)
      FROM order_discounts od
      JOIN discounts d ON d.id = od.discount_id
      WHERE od.order_id = bo.order_id
        AND d.name = 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)'
    ) AS discount_amount,
    NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM subscriptions s
      WHERE s.tenant_id = bo.tenant_id
        AND s.user_id = bo.user_id
        AND s.status IN ('trialing', 'active', 'past_due')
        AND s.started_at <= bo.placed_at
        AND (s.ended_at IS NULL OR s.ended_at >= bo.placed_at)
    ) AS is_orphan,
    (
      SELECT s2.status
      FROM subscriptions s2
      WHERE s2.tenant_id = bo.tenant_id
        AND s2.user_id = bo.user_id
      ORDER BY s2.started_at DESC, s2.id DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS most_recent_status,
    (
      SELECT er.rate
      FROM exchange_rates er
      WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = bo.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(bo.placed_at AS DATE)
    ) AS fx_rate
  FROM base_orders bo
),
categorized AS (
  SELECT
    r.*,
    CASE
      WHEN r.most_recent_status = 'canceled' THEN 'canceled'
      WHEN r.most_recent_status = 'active' THEN 'active'
      ELSE 'other-or-no-subscription-record'
    END AS status_category,
    CASE
      WHEN r.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN r.discount_amount
      ELSE r.discount_amount / NULLIF(r.fx_rate, 0)
    END AS eur_amount
  FROM row_per_order r
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  c.status_category,
  COUNT(*) AS orphan_order_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(SUM(c.eur_amount), 2) AS total_discount_amount_eur
FROM categorized c
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = c.tenant_id
WHERE c.is_orphan
GROUP BY t.name, c.status_category
ORDER BY t.name, c.status_category
builds_on: Subscription-delivery discount orders with no overlapping active subscription
Tenant-level breakdown of the lapsed-subscriber leakage trend, by half-year
entries.engineer_note: Built as one pass: base_orders filters 2025 non-cancelled orders carrying a 'Subscription delivery (prepaid)' discount; row_per_order computes, per order_id via correlated scalar subqueries (no duplicating joins), the summed discount amount, an orphan flag (no subscriptions row with status in trialing/active/past_due whose started_at/ended_at window covers placed_at), and the most-recent subscription status by started_at; categorized maps that status to canceled/active/other-or-no-subscription-record and converts the discount to EUR via exchange_rates(EUR->currency_code, as_of=placed_at date), dividing by the rate (EUR rows pass through unconverted). The final aggregation groups orphan-only rows by tenant and status category. Note: I cannot execute this against real data myself (dry_run only validates against an empty schema, and I have no other read access), so I could not pre-check the per-tenant totals against last week's reference figures (167/127/100/49/17/1, 461 orders, €22,318.18) — please have the batch run confirm reconciliation; if a tenant's summed orphan count across its status rows doesn't match its reference figure, the likely causes are either multiple order_discounts rows per order for other discount names being miscounted (unlikely, since we filter by exact discount name) or orders whose user_id had no rows in `subscriptions` at all previously being excluded/included differently than last week's method.

entries.title: Reconciled full-history (2023-2025) orphan population by tenant and subscription status (single pass)
entries.question: Using the same single-pass, fan-out-safe construction, does the full-history orphan population by tenant and status reproduce the monthly trend's cumulative canceled-bucket total (~€57,658.66, roughly 1,188 orders by hand-summing last week's monthly report)?
entries.sql:
WITH order_sub AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.discount_total,
    o.currency_code,
    o.placed_at,
    (
      SELECT s.status
      FROM invoices i
      JOIN subscriptions s ON s.id = i.subscription_id
      WHERE i.order_id = o.id
      ORDER BY i.issued_at DESC NULLS LAST, i.id DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS subscription_status
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.discount_total > 0
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM order_discounts od WHERE od.order_id = o.id
    )
),
rated AS (
  SELECT
    os.tenant_id,
    os.user_id,
    os.order_id,
    CASE
      WHEN os.subscription_status = 'canceled' THEN 'canceled'
      WHEN os.subscription_status = 'active' THEN 'active'
      ELSE 'other-or-no-subscription-record'
    END AS status_category,
    CASE
      WHEN os.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN os.discount_total
      ELSE os.discount_total / er.rate
    END AS discount_eur
  FROM order_sub os
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = os.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = os.placed_at::date
)
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  r.status_category,
  COUNT(*) AS orphan_order_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(SUM(r.discount_eur), 2) AS total_discount_eur
FROM rated r
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
GROUP BY t.name, r.status_category
ORDER BY t.name, r.status_category
builds_on: Monthly trend of confirmed lapsed-subscriber free-delivery leakage, 2023-2025
Reconciled 2025 orphan population by tenant and subscription status (single pass)
entries.engineer_note: Two caveats: (1) I don't have the text of the earlier "2025-only" request in this session, so I had to reconstruct the "orphan" definition from context: an order with a non-zero discount_total but no matching row in order_discounts (a one-row-per-order_id subquery using NOT EXISTS, so no fan-out), bucketed by the status of the most recent subscription linked via invoices (canceled / active / other-or-no-subscription-record), discounts converted to EUR via exchange_rates. If the prior report used a different orphan definition, this won't reconcile and should be re-aligned. (2) As the data engineer I only submit the query to the overnight batch and never see its output (dry_run runs against an empty schema), so I cannot personally confirm the ~1,188 orders / ~€57,658.66 canceled-bucket figures or state the grand totals - please have the analyst read those off the printed report and flag back if it diverges, e.g. due to a different orphan definition, FX edge cases, or EUR-currency orders being excluded by the exchange_rates join.

entries.title: Fan-out-safe date classification of the 2025 active-bucket orphan orders
entries.question: Rebuilt carefully so the category counts and the discount total come from the same population: of the 2025 orphan orders whose customer's most-recent subscription is 'active', how many had that subscription start after the order, how many show active status despite an already-past end date, and how many have dates that should have overlapped (a bug)?
entries.sql:
WITH orphan_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.placed_at, o.discount_total, o.currency_code
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions s
      WHERE s.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND s.user_id = o.user_id
        AND s.started_at <= o.placed_at
        AND (s.ended_at IS NULL OR s.ended_at >= o.placed_at)
    )
),
most_recent_sub AS (
  SELECT oo.order_id, oo.tenant_id, oo.user_id, oo.placed_at, oo.discount_total, oo.currency_code,
         s.id AS sub_id, s.started_at AS sub_started_at, s.ended_at AS sub_ended_at, s.status AS sub_status,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY oo.order_id ORDER BY s.started_at DESC, s.id DESC) AS rn
  FROM orphan_orders oo
  JOIN subscriptions s ON s.tenant_id = oo.tenant_id AND s.user_id = oo.user_id
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    mrs.order_id, mrs.tenant_id, mrs.user_id, mrs.placed_at, mrs.discount_total, mrs.currency_code,
    mrs.sub_started_at, mrs.sub_ended_at, mrs.sub_status,
    CASE
      WHEN mrs.sub_started_at > mrs.placed_at THEN 'subscription started after this order'
      WHEN mrs.sub_started_at <= mrs.placed_at AND mrs.sub_ended_at IS NOT NULL AND mrs.sub_ended_at < mrs.placed_at THEN 'active status but already past its end date'
      ELSE 'dates indicate overlap - likely a bug in the original orphan flag'
    END AS category,
    CASE
      WHEN mrs.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN mrs.discount_total
      ELSE mrs.discount_total / er.rate
    END AS discount_amount_eur
  FROM most_recent_sub mrs
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = mrs.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(mrs.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE mrs.rn = 1 AND mrs.sub_status = 'active'
)
SELECT
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_active_bucket,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS distinct_customers,
  ROUND(SUM(discount_amount_eur), 2) AS total_discount_eur
FROM base
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY order_count DESC, category
builds_on: Root cause of the 291 'unexplained' active-bucket orphan orders
Reconciled 2025 orphan population by tenant and subscription status (single pass)
entries.engineer_note: I don't have the prior "orphan order" / tenant-level reconciliation report in hand, so I defined "orphan order" as a 2025 order whose customer has no subscription (of any status) with started_at<=placed_at<=ended_at (or open-ended), i.e. no subscription period covered the order at placement time - please confirm this matches the earlier report's flag logic. "Most-recent subscription" is the one with the latest started_at (ties broken by higher id) per customer. Each row already comes from one order-grain CTE before the GROUP BY, so order_count/customers/EUR total are from an identical order set per category; sum the three rows to get the active-bucket grand total to check against the reconciliation report.

entries.title: Apparel and Footwear: loyalty member vs non-member behavior by tenure
entries.question: Within Apparel and Footwear alone, where 72% of loyalty members sit, do members still look worse off than non-members on orders, revenue and refunds once we also control for how long they have been a customer?
entries.sql:
WITH apparel_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
),
qualifying_users AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id, u.created_at
  FROM users u
  JOIN apparel_tenants t ON t.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM orders o
      WHERE o.user_id = u.id
        AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
        AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    )
),
order_agg AS (
  SELECT
    o.user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS total_order_count,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled') AS non_cancelled_order_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN o.grand_total / er.rate ELSE 0 END) AS total_revenue_eur,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (
      WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
         OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)
    ) AS refunded_order_count
  FROM orders o
  JOIN qualifying_users qu ON qu.user_id = o.user_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at)::date
  GROUP BY o.user_id
),
segmented AS (
  SELECT
    qu.user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la WHERE la.user_id = qu.user_id)
      THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member'
    END AS segment,
    CASE
      WHEN qu.created_at > DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '6 months' THEN 'under 6 months'
      WHEN qu.created_at > DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '12 months' THEN '6 to 12 months'
      WHEN qu.created_at > DATE '2025-12-31' - INTERVAL '24 months' THEN '12 to 24 months'
      ELSE 'over 24 months'
    END AS tenure_band
  FROM qualifying_users qu
)
SELECT
  s.tenure_band,
  s.segment,
  COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
  ROUND(AVG(oa.total_order_count), 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(AVG(oa.total_revenue_eur), 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(oa.total_revenue_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(oa.non_cancelled_order_count), 0), 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(oa.refunded_order_count) / NULLIF(SUM(oa.total_order_count), 0), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM segmented s
JOIN order_agg oa ON oa.user_id = s.user_id
GROUP BY s.tenure_band, s.segment
ORDER BY
  CASE s.tenure_band
    WHEN 'under 6 months' THEN 1
    WHEN '6 to 12 months' THEN 2
    WHEN '12 to 24 months' THEN 3
    WHEN 'over 24 months' THEN 4
  END,
  CASE s.segment WHEN 'loyalty member' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END
builds_on: Loyalty member vs non-member behavior by account tenure
Loyalty member refund rate by merchant vertical
entries.engineer_note: avg_order_value_eur is computed as aggregate (non-cancelled EUR revenue / non-cancelled order count) within each tenure_band x segment cell, not an average of per-customer AOVs, to match the standard order-value definition; avg_lifetime_orders and avg_lifetime_revenue_eur are per-customer averages as specified. Only 8 rows expected (4 tenure bands x 2 segments).

entries.title: Loyalty points redemption rate by enrollment cohort age
entries.question: Is the growing points liability just a 'young programme, redemptions lag issuance' phase that will level out, or do even our oldest member cohorts still show a structurally low redemption rate?
entries.sql:
with cohort_accounts as (
    select
        la.id as loyalty_account_id,
        la.loyalty_program_id,
        cd.year_num,
        cd.quarter_num,
        cd.quarter_start
    from loyalty_accounts la
    join calendar_days cd on cd.calendar_date = cast(la.enrolled_at as date)
    where cd.quarter_start >= date '2023-01-01'
      and cd.quarter_start <= date '2025-10-01'
),

account_currency as (
    select
        ca.loyalty_account_id,
        ca.year_num,
        ca.quarter_num,
        ca.quarter_start,
        lp.points_per_currency,
        lp.currency_code
    from cohort_accounts ca
    join loyalty_programs lp on lp.id = ca.loyalty_program_id
),

transaction_amounts as (
    select
        ac.loyalty_account_id,
        ac.year_num,
        ac.quarter_num,
        ac.quarter_start,
        lt.direction,
        case
            when ac.currency_code = 'EUR' then (lt.points / ac.points_per_currency)
            else (lt.points / ac.points_per_currency) / er.rate
        end as amount_eur
    from account_currency ac
    join loyalty_transactions lt on lt.loyalty_account_id = ac.loyalty_account_id
    left join exchange_rates er
        on er.base_code = 'EUR'
       and er.quote_code = ac.currency_code
       and er.as_of = cast(lt.occurred_at as date)
),

cohort_members as (
    select
        year_num,
        quarter_num,
        quarter_start,
        count(distinct loyalty_account_id) as member_count
    from cohort_accounts
    group by year_num, quarter_num, quarter_start
),

cohort_transactions as (
    select
        year_num,
        quarter_num,
        quarter_start,
        sum(case when direction = 'earn' then amount_eur else 0 end) as total_points_earned_value_eur,
        sum(case when direction <> 'earn' then amount_eur else 0 end) as total_points_redeemed_value_eur
    from transaction_amounts
    group by year_num, quarter_num, quarter_start
)

select
    cast(cm.year_num as varchar) || '-Q' || cast(cm.quarter_num as varchar) as enrollment_quarter,
    cm.member_count,
    (extract(year from date '2025-12-31') - extract(year from cm.quarter_start)) * 12
        + (extract(month from date '2025-12-31') - extract(month from cm.quarter_start))
        as months_since_cohort_quarter_start,
    round(coalesce(ct.total_points_earned_value_eur, 0), 2) as total_points_earned_value_eur,
    round(coalesce(ct.total_points_redeemed_value_eur, 0), 2) as total_points_redeemed_value_eur,
    round(
        case when coalesce(ct.total_points_earned_value_eur, 0) = 0 then null
             else ct.total_points_redeemed_value_eur / ct.total_points_earned_value_eur * 100
        end, 2
    ) as lifetime_redemption_rate_pct
from cohort_members cm
left join cohort_transactions ct
    on ct.year_num = cm.year_num
   and ct.quarter_num = cm.quarter_num
   and ct.quarter_start = cm.quarter_start
order by cm.quarter_start asc
builds_on: Loyalty points and referral reward cost by month
Loyalty programme unit economics: points cost vs revenue per customer
entries.engineer_note: months_since_cohort_quarter_start is computed as an exact calendar-month difference from each cohort quarter's start date to 2025-12-31 (e.g. 2023-Q1 comes out to 35, not the illustrative ~36, since 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31 is 35 full months); redeemed/earned values assume loyalty_transactions.points is stored as a positive magnitude with sign conveyed only by direction, consistent with the earlier unit-economics conversion method.

entries.title: Loyalty transaction order-linkage diagnostic by direction
entries.question: Before retesting the rewards-redemption-without-purchase hypothesis, is order_id even populated on redemption-direction loyalty_transactions, or do we need a different way to connect a redemption to an order?
entries.sql:
select
  direction,
  count(*) as transaction_count,
  count(order_id) as transactions_with_order_id,
  round(100.0 * count(order_id) / nullif(count(*), 0), 2) as pct_with_order_id,
  count(distinct order_id) as distinct_order_ids_referenced
from loyalty_transactions
where occurred_at >= date '2023-01-01'
  and occurred_at < date '2026-01-01'
group by direction
order by transaction_count desc, direction
builds_on: Refund rate on points-redeeming orders vs other member orders
entries.engineer_note: Grain is one row per direction value as requested, covering all tenants and the full 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31 window (upper bound applied as occurred_at < 2026-01-01).

entries.title: Refund rate on orders with a same-day points redemption
entries.question: Using date-proximity matching instead of the unusable order_id link, do loyalty members' orders that coincide with a points redemption on the same calendar day show a different refund rate than their other orders?
entries.sql:
WITH loyalty_user_ids AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM loyalty_accounts
),
eligible_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.placed_at, o.grand_total, o.currency_code, o.status
  FROM orders o
  JOIN loyalty_user_ids lu ON lu.user_id = o.user_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
burn_by_user_day AS (
  SELECT user_id, CAST(occurred_at AS DATE) AS burn_date, SUM(ABS(points)) AS day_points
  FROM loyalty_transactions
  WHERE direction = 'burn'
  GROUP BY user_id, CAST(occurred_at AS DATE)
),
classified_orders AS (
  SELECT
    eo.order_id,
    eo.user_id,
    eo.placed_at,
    eo.grand_total,
    eo.currency_code,
    eo.status,
    bd.day_points,
    CASE WHEN bd.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'same-day points redemption' ELSE 'no same-day points redemption' END AS order_type
  FROM eligible_orders eo
  LEFT JOIN burn_by_user_day bd
    ON bd.user_id = eo.user_id AND bd.burn_date = CAST(eo.placed_at AS DATE)
),
refund_flags AS (
  SELECT
    co.order_id,
    co.order_type,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = co.order_id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
      OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = co.order_id)
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM classified_orders co
),
order_value_eur AS (
  SELECT
    co.order_id,
    co.order_type,
    CASE WHEN co.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN co.grand_total
         ELSE co.grand_total / er.rate END AS grand_total_eur
  FROM classified_orders co
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = co.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(co.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE co.status <> 'cancelled'
),
order_counts AS (
  SELECT order_type, COUNT(*) AS order_count, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS distinct_customers, AVG(COALESCE(day_points,0)) AS avg_points_redeemed_that_day
  FROM classified_orders
  GROUP BY order_type
),
refund_rates AS (
  SELECT order_type, AVG(is_refunded) * 100 AS refund_rate_pct
  FROM refund_flags
  GROUP BY order_type
),
avg_values AS (
  SELECT order_type, AVG(grand_total_eur) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM order_value_eur
  GROUP BY order_type
)
SELECT
  oc.order_type,
  oc.order_count,
  oc.distinct_customers,
  ROUND(rr.refund_rate_pct, 2) AS refund_rate_pct,
  ROUND(av.avg_order_value_eur, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(oc.avg_points_redeemed_that_day, 1) AS avg_points_redeemed_that_day
FROM order_counts oc
JOIN refund_rates rr ON rr.order_type = oc.order_type
JOIN avg_values av ON av.order_type = oc.order_type
ORDER BY CASE WHEN oc.order_type = 'same-day points redemption' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, oc.order_type
builds_on: Loyalty transaction order-linkage diagnostic by direction
Refund rate on points-redeeming orders vs other member orders
entries.engineer_note: Classification uses user_id + calendar date of placed_at vs. loyalty_transactions.occurred_at (direction='burn') as requested, since order_id linkage isn't usable. avg_points_redeemed_that_day sums |points| across all same-day burn transactions for that user before averaging; avg_order_value_eur excludes cancelled orders per the given definition while order_count/refund_rate include all statuses.

entries.title: Apparel order value breakdown: subtotal, discount and total, member vs non-member
entries.question: Is the large average-order-value gap seen among Apparel members (28-40% lower than non-members across every tenure band) explained by heavier discounting at checkout, or do members simply buy cheaper products before any discount is applied?
entries.sql:
WITH apparel_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id, o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.currency_code, o.subtotal, o.discount_total, o.grand_total, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id
  WHERE t.industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
    AND u.is_staff = false
    AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
user_segment AS (
  SELECT ao.*,
    CASE WHEN la.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'loyalty member' ELSE 'non-member' END AS segment
  FROM apparel_orders ao
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM loyalty_accounts) la ON la.user_id = ao.user_id
),
fx_converted AS (
  SELECT us.segment,
    us.subtotal / CASE WHEN us.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS subtotal_eur,
    us.discount_total / CASE WHEN us.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS discount_total_eur,
    us.grand_total / CASE WHEN us.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE er.rate END AS grand_total_eur
  FROM user_segment us
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = us.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(us.placed_at AS DATE)
),
segment_agg AS (
  SELECT segment,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    AVG(subtotal_eur) AS avg_subtotal_eur,
    AVG(discount_total_eur) AS avg_discount_total_eur,
    AVG(grand_total_eur) AS avg_grand_total_eur,
    SUM(discount_total_eur) AS sum_discount_eur,
    SUM(subtotal_eur) AS sum_subtotal_eur
  FROM fx_converted
  GROUP BY segment
)
SELECT
  segment,
  order_count,
  ROUND(avg_subtotal_eur, 2) AS avg_subtotal_eur,
  ROUND(avg_discount_total_eur, 2) AS avg_discount_total_eur,
  ROUND(avg_grand_total_eur, 2) AS avg_grand_total_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * sum_discount_eur / NULLIF(sum_subtotal_eur,0), 2) AS discount_rate_pct
FROM segment_agg
ORDER BY CASE WHEN segment = 'loyalty member' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, segment
builds_on: Apparel and Footwear: loyalty member vs non-member behavior by tenure
entries.engineer_note: Segment is based on ever having a loyalty_accounts row (not tenure-banded, since the request's grain is just member vs non-member); amounts are converted EUR via exchange_rates using the order's placed_at date, with EUR orders passed through unconverted.

entries.title: What distinguishes higher-revenue loyalty members from the rest
entries.question: Among enrolled loyalty members, do the ones who generate the most revenue use the programme differently - redeeming more or less, staying longer, returning less - giving a hint at what a healthier version of the programme would look like?
entries.sql:
WITH loyalty_members AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_accounts
),
population AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.tenant_id, o.user_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN loyalty_members lm ON lm.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND lm.user_id = o.user_id
  WHERE o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
orders_base AS (
  SELECT o.tenant_id, o.user_id, o.id AS order_id, o.status, o.placed_at, o.grand_total, o.currency_code
  FROM orders o
  JOIN population p ON p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND p.user_id = o.user_id
),
payment_refund AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, order_id, MAX(CASE WHEN amount_refunded > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_refund
  FROM payments
  WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY tenant_id, order_id
),
return_flag AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, order_id
  FROM order_returns
),
orders_enriched AS (
  SELECT
    ob.tenant_id, ob.user_id, ob.order_id, ob.status, ob.placed_at,
    CASE WHEN ob.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ob.grand_total
         ELSE ob.grand_total / er.rate END AS grand_total_eur,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(pr.has_refund,0) = 1 OR rf.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM orders_base ob
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = ob.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(ob.placed_at AS DATE)
  LEFT JOIN payment_refund pr ON pr.tenant_id = ob.tenant_id AND pr.order_id = ob.order_id
  LEFT JOIN return_flag rf ON rf.tenant_id = ob.tenant_id AND rf.order_id = ob.order_id
),
member_orders AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id, user_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN status <> 'cancelled' THEN COALESCE(grand_total_eur,0) ELSE 0 END) AS lifetime_revenue_eur,
    COUNT(*) AS lifetime_orders,
    MAX(placed_at) AS last_order_at,
    SUM(is_refunded) AS refunded_orders
  FROM orders_enriched
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
),
tx_value AS (
  SELECT lt.tenant_id, lt.user_id, lt.direction, lt.occurred_at,
    lt.points / lp.points_per_currency AS points_currency_amount,
    lp.currency_code
  FROM loyalty_transactions lt
  JOIN loyalty_accounts la ON la.id = lt.loyalty_account_id
  JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la.loyalty_program_id
  JOIN population p ON p.tenant_id = lt.tenant_id AND p.user_id = lt.user_id
),
tx_value_eur AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id, direction,
    CASE WHEN currency_code = 'EUR' THEN points_currency_amount
         ELSE points_currency_amount / er.rate END AS value_eur
  FROM tx_value tv
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = tv.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(tv.occurred_at AS DATE)
),
member_loyalty AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, user_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN direction = 'burn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ever_redeemed,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'earn' THEN value_eur ELSE 0 END) AS earned_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'burn' THEN value_eur ELSE 0 END) AS redeemed_eur
  FROM tx_value_eur
  GROUP BY tenant_id, user_id
),
member_full AS (
  SELECT
    mo.tenant_id, mo.user_id,
    mo.lifetime_revenue_eur, mo.lifetime_orders, mo.refunded_orders,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (mo.last_order_at - u.created_at)) / 86400.0 AS tenure_days,
    COALESCE(ml.ever_redeemed,0) AS ever_redeemed,
    COALESCE(ml.earned_eur,0) AS earned_eur,
    COALESCE(ml.redeemed_eur,0) AS redeemed_eur
  FROM member_orders mo
  JOIN users u ON u.tenant_id = mo.tenant_id AND u.id = mo.user_id
  LEFT JOIN member_loyalty ml ON ml.tenant_id = mo.tenant_id AND ml.user_id = mo.user_id
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT
    mf.*,
    NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue_eur DESC) AS quartile
  FROM member_full mf
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN quartile = 1 THEN 'Top 25% by lifetime revenue' ELSE 'Remaining 75%' END AS performance_group,
  COUNT(*) AS member_count,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_revenue_eur), 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_orders), 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(AVG(tenure_days), 1) AS avg_tenure_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(ever_redeemed), 1) AS pct_who_ever_redeemed_points,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(redeemed_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(earned_eur), 0), 1) AS own_redemption_rate_pct,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(refunded_orders) / NULLIF(SUM(lifetime_orders), 0), 1) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM ranked
GROUP BY CASE WHEN quartile = 1 THEN 'Top 25% by lifetime revenue' ELSE 'Remaining 75%' END
ORDER BY MIN(quartile)
builds_on: Loyalty programme unit economics: points cost vs revenue per customer
Loyalty points redemption rate by enrollment cohort age
entries.engineer_note: A member is a (tenant_id, user_id) pair since users aren't globally unique across tenants. The "unit-economics" points-to-EUR method isn't in the catalog, so I derived it as points ÷ program.points_per_currency (gives the program's currency amount), then converted to EUR via the daily exchange_rates as_of the transaction date; please flag if the real unit-economics report uses a different conversion. Top/bottom split uses NTILE(4), grouping tile 1 as "top 25%" and tiles 2-4 as "remaining 75%".

entries.title: Apparel: never-redeemed vs ever-redeemed members vs non-members, by tenure
entries.question: Once we separate loyalty members into those who have actually redeemed a point at least once versus those who never have, do the engaged ones match or beat non-members of similar tenure, while the disengaged majority lags behind?
entries.sql:
WITH apparel_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
),
eligible_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT u.id AS user_id, u.tenant_id, u.created_at
  FROM users u
  JOIN apparel_tenants t ON t.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM orders o
      WHERE o.user_id = u.id
        AND o.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
        AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01'
        AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
    )
),
loyalty_group AS (
  SELECT
    eu.user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN la.user_id IS NULL THEN 'non-member'
      WHEN lb.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'ever-redeemed member'
      ELSE 'never-redeemed member'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM eligible_users eu
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM loyalty_accounts) la
    ON la.user_id = eu.user_id
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM loyalty_transactions WHERE direction = 'burn') lb
    ON lb.user_id = eu.user_id
),
tenure AS (
  SELECT
    eu.user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - eu.created_at::date) < 182 THEN 'under 6 months'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - eu.created_at::date) < 365 THEN '6 to 12 months'
      WHEN (DATE '2025-12-31' - eu.created_at::date) < 730 THEN '12 to 24 months'
      ELSE 'over 24 months'
    END AS tenure_band
  FROM eligible_users eu
),
orders_scoped AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.status,
    CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN
      CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
           ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate END
    ELSE NULL END AS revenue_eur,
    CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_noncancelled,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
         OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM orders o
  JOIN eligible_users eu ON eu.user_id = o.user_id AND eu.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
),
user_agg AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    COUNT(*) AS lifetime_orders,
    SUM(is_noncancelled) AS noncancelled_orders,
    SUM(COALESCE(revenue_eur, 0)) AS lifetime_revenue_eur,
    SUM(is_refunded) AS refunded_orders
  FROM orders_scoped
  GROUP BY user_id
),
user_level AS (
  SELECT
    t.tenure_band,
    lg.customer_group,
    ua.lifetime_orders,
    ua.noncancelled_orders,
    ua.lifetime_revenue_eur,
    ua.refunded_orders
  FROM eligible_users eu
  JOIN tenure t ON t.user_id = eu.user_id
  JOIN loyalty_group lg ON lg.user_id = eu.user_id
  JOIN user_agg ua ON ua.user_id = eu.user_id
)
SELECT
  tenure_band,
  customer_group AS "group",
  COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_orders)::numeric, 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_revenue_eur)::numeric, 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND((SUM(lifetime_revenue_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(noncancelled_orders), 0))::numeric, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND((100.0 * SUM(refunded_orders) / NULLIF(SUM(lifetime_orders), 0))::numeric, 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM user_level
GROUP BY tenure_band, customer_group
ORDER BY
  CASE tenure_band
    WHEN 'under 6 months' THEN 1
    WHEN '6 to 12 months' THEN 2
    WHEN '12 to 24 months' THEN 3
    WHEN 'over 24 months' THEN 4
  END,
  CASE customer_group
    WHEN 'non-member' THEN 1
    WHEN 'never-redeemed member' THEN 2
    WHEN 'ever-redeemed member' THEN 3
  END
builds_on: What distinguishes higher-revenue loyalty members from the rest
Apparel and Footwear: loyalty member vs non-member behavior by tenure
entries.engineer_note: Tenure bands are bucketed using day-count thresholds (182/365/730 days) as proxies for 6/12/24 months, since the warehouse has no native month-diff function. avg_order_value_eur and refund_rate_pct are computed as group-level ratios (total revenue/orders), not an average of each customer's own ratio.

entries.title: Loyalty unit economics: ever-redeemed vs never-redeemed members
entries.question: Is the programme's realized cost concentrated entirely in the minority of members who actually redeem, while the disengaged majority sits as pure unclaimed liability rather than real cost?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN m.is_ever_redeemed THEN 'ever-redeemed member' ELSE 'never-redeemed member' END AS "group",
  COUNT(*) AS member_count,
  ROUND(SUM(m.revenue_eur), 2) AS total_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(m.revenue_eur) / COUNT(*), 2) AS revenue_per_customer_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(m.redeemed_cost_eur), 2) AS total_points_redeemed_cost_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(m.earned_liability_eur), 2) AS total_points_earned_liability_eur,
  CASE WHEN SUM(m.revenue_eur) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE ROUND(SUM(m.redeemed_cost_eur) / SUM(m.revenue_eur) * 100, 2) END AS redeemed_cost_pct_of_revenue
FROM (
  SELECT
    u.id AS user_id,
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_transactions lt WHERE lt.user_id = u.id AND lt.direction = 'burn') AS is_ever_redeemed,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
             ELSE o.grand_total / er.rate END
      ), 0)
     FROM orders o
     LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er ON er.base_code = 'EUR' AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code AND er.as_of = CAST(o.placed_at AS DATE)
     WHERE o.user_id = u.id
       AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
       AND o.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
    ) AS revenue_eur,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN lp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ABS(lt2.points) / lp.points_per_currency
             ELSE (ABS(lt2.points) / lp.points_per_currency) / er2.rate END
      ), 0)
     FROM loyalty_transactions lt2
     JOIN loyalty_accounts la2 ON la2.id = lt2.loyalty_account_id
     JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la2.loyalty_program_id
     LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er2 ON er2.base_code = 'EUR' AND er2.quote_code = lp.currency_code AND er2.as_of = CAST(lt2.occurred_at AS DATE)
     WHERE lt2.user_id = u.id AND lt2.direction = 'burn'
    ) AS redeemed_cost_eur,
    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN lp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN ABS(lt3.points) / lp.points_per_currency
             ELSE (ABS(lt3.points) / lp.points_per_currency) / er3.rate END
      ), 0)
     FROM loyalty_transactions lt3
     JOIN loyalty_accounts la3 ON la3.id = lt3.loyalty_account_id
     JOIN loyalty_programs lp ON lp.id = la3.loyalty_program_id
     LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er3 ON er3.base_code = 'EUR' AND er3.quote_code = lp.currency_code AND er3.as_of = CAST(lt3.occurred_at AS DATE)
     WHERE lt3.user_id = u.id AND lt3.direction = 'earn'
    ) AS earned_liability_eur
  FROM users u
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts la WHERE la.user_id = u.id)
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o2 WHERE o2.user_id = u.id AND o2.placed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o2.placed_at < DATE '2026-01-01')
) m
GROUP BY m.is_ever_redeemed
ORDER BY m.is_ever_redeemed DESC
builds_on: Loyalty programme unit economics: points cost vs revenue per customer
What distinguishes higher-revenue loyalty members from the rest
entries.engineer_note: Population = users with a loyalty_accounts row and at least one order (any status) placed 2023-01-01..2025-12-31; revenue is summed over non-cancelled orders in that same window. Points costs/liabilities use points_per_currency and the program's currency, converted to EUR via exchange_rates as of occurred_at; EUR-denominated amounts use the rate=1 identity rather than a self-join lookup.

entries.title: Member order behavior before vs after their first points redemption
entries.question: Among members who have redeemed at least once, does their order frequency and spend actually pick up after that first redemption, or were they already heavy buyers beforehand - i.e. does redeeming look like a cause of engagement or just a marker of customers who were already engaged?
entries.sql:
WITH population AS (
  SELECT 
    t0.id AS user_id,
    t0.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t0.created_at AS user_created_at,
    t1.status AS tenant_status,
    t2.first_redeem_at AS first_redeem_at
  FROM users t0
  JOIN tenants t1 ON t1.id = t0.tenant_id
  JOIN (
    SELECT t3.user_id AS user_id, t3.tenant_id AS tenant_id, MIN(t3.occurred_at) AS first_redeem_at
    FROM loyalty_transactions t3
    WHERE t3.direction = 'burn'
    GROUP BY t3.user_id, t3.tenant_id
  ) t2 ON t2.user_id = t0.id AND t2.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM loyalty_accounts t4
    WHERE t4.user_id = t0.id AND t4.tenant_id = t0.tenant_id
  )
),
base_orders AS (
  SELECT
    t5.id AS order_id,
    t5.tenant_id AS tenant_id,
    t5.user_id AS user_id,
    t5.placed_at AS placed_at,
    t5.status AS status,
    t5.currency_code AS currency_code,
    t5.grand_total AS grand_total,
    CASE WHEN t5.placed_at < t6.first_redeem_at THEN 'before first redemption' ELSE 'after first redemption' END AS period
  FROM orders t5
  JOIN population t6 ON t6.user_id = t5.user_id AND t6.tenant_id = t5.tenant_id
  WHERE t5.placed_at IS NOT NULL
    AND t5.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND t5.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
),
periods AS (
  SELECT 'before first redemption' AS period
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'after first redemption' AS period
),
order_counts AS (
  SELECT
    t7.period AS period,
    COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t7.user_id) AS distinct_customers
  FROM base_orders t7
  GROUP BY t7.period
),
aov AS (
  SELECT
    t8.period AS period,
    AVG(
      CASE WHEN t8.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN t8.grand_total
           ELSE t8.grand_total / t9.rate
      END
    ) AS avg_order_value_eur
  FROM base_orders t8
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates t9
    ON t9.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND t9.quote_code = t8.currency_code
   AND t9.as_of = CAST(t8.placed_at AS DATE)
  WHERE t8.status <> 'cancelled'
  GROUP BY t8.period
),
order_refund_flags AS (
  SELECT
    t10.order_id AS order_id,
    t10.period AS period,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(t11.has_refund, false) OR COALESCE(t12.has_return, false) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM base_orders t10
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT t13.order_id AS order_id, bool_or(t13.amount_refunded > 0) AS has_refund
    FROM payments t13
    WHERE t13.order_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY t13.order_id
  ) t11 ON t11.order_id = t10.order_id
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT t14.order_id AS order_id, true AS has_return
    FROM order_returns t14
  ) t12 ON t12.order_id = t10.order_id
),
refund_rate AS (
  SELECT
    t15.period AS period,
    100.0 * SUM(t15.is_refunded) / COUNT(*) AS refund_rate_pct
  FROM order_refund_flags t15
  GROUP BY t15.period
),
exposure_before AS (
  SELECT
    'before first redemption' AS period,
    t16.user_id AS user_id,
    GREATEST(
      1,
      CAST(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t16.first_redeem_at - COALESCE(t17.first_order_before, t16.user_created_at))) / 86400 AS BIGINT)
    ) AS exposed_days
  FROM population t16
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT t18.user_id AS user_id, MIN(t18.placed_at) AS first_order_before
    FROM base_orders t18
    WHERE t18.period = 'before first redemption'
    GROUP BY t18.user_id
  ) t17 ON t17.user_id = t16.user_id
),
exposure_after AS (
  SELECT
    'after first redemption' AS period,
    t19.user_id AS user_id,
    GREATEST(
      1,
      CAST(
        EXTRACT(
          EPOCH FROM (
            COALESCE(
              CASE WHEN t19.tenant_status = 'churned' THEN t20.last_order_after ELSE TIMESTAMP '2025-12-31 00:00:00' END,
              t19.first_redeem_at
            ) - t19.first_redeem_at
          )
        ) / 86400 AS BIGINT
      )
    ) AS exposed_days
  FROM population t19
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT t21.user_id AS user_id, MAX(t21.placed_at) AS last_order_after
    FROM base_orders t21
    WHERE t21.period = 'after first redemption'
    GROUP BY t21.user_id
  ) t20 ON t20.user_id = t19.user_id
),
exposure_union AS (
  SELECT * FROM exposure_before
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM exposure_after
),
exposure_years AS (
  SELECT
    t22.period AS period,
    SUM(t22.exposed_days) / 365.0 AS exposed_customer_years
  FROM exposure_union t22
  GROUP BY t22.period
)
SELECT
  t23.period AS period,
  COALESCE(t24.distinct_customers, 0) AS distinct_customers,
  COALESCE(t24.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t25.avg_order_value_eur, 0), 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t24.total_orders, 0) / NULLIF(t27.exposed_customer_years, 0), 2) AS orders_per_customer_per_year,
  ROUND(COALESCE(t26.refund_rate_pct, 0), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM periods t23
LEFT JOIN order_counts t24 ON t24.period = t23.period
LEFT JOIN aov t25 ON t25.period = t23.period
LEFT JOIN refund_rate t26 ON t26.period = t23.period
LEFT JOIN exposure_years t27 ON t27.period = t23.period
ORDER BY CASE WHEN t23.period = 'before first redemption' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, t23.period
builds_on: Loyalty member order behavior before vs after enrollment
What distinguishes higher-revenue loyalty members from the rest
entries.engineer_note: Population = users with a loyalty_accounts row and >=1 'burn' loyalty_transactions row; split is on their first burn's occurred_at. For exposure-after's end date, since the schema has no customer-level churn flag, I used the tenant's status: if the merchant tenant has churned, exposed-after runs to the customer's last order after redemption, otherwise it is right-censored at 2025-12-31 (i.e. "still active" = tenant still active on the platform). AOV uses non-cancelled orders converted to EUR via exchange_rates; refund_rate_pct and order counts use all orders (any status) in the period.

entries.title: Order frequency deceleration by customer group: first half vs second half of tenure
entries.question: Does order frequency drop off after a member's first redemption because redeeming specifically reduces engagement, or do non-members and never-redeemed members show the same kind of natural slowdown over their lifetime?
entries.sql:
WITH user_orders AS (
  SELECT o.id AS order_id, o.user_id, o.tenant_id, o.placed_at
  FROM orders o
  JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id AND u.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
),
user_stats AS (
  SELECT user_id, tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, MIN(placed_at) AS first_order, MAX(placed_at) AS last_order
  FROM user_orders
  GROUP BY user_id, tenant_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
),
loyalty_acct AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_accounts
),
loyalty_burn AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id, user_id FROM loyalty_transactions WHERE direction = 'burn'
),
user_group AS (
  SELECT us.user_id, us.tenant_id, us.first_order, us.last_order,
    us.first_order + (us.last_order - us.first_order)/2 AS midpoint,
    CASE
      WHEN la.user_id IS NULL THEN 'non-member'
      WHEN lb.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'ever-redeemed member'
      ELSE 'never-redeemed member'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM user_stats us
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_acct la ON la.tenant_id = us.tenant_id AND la.user_id = us.user_id
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_burn lb ON lb.tenant_id = us.tenant_id AND lb.user_id = us.user_id
),
order_period AS (
  SELECT uo.order_id, uo.user_id, uo.tenant_id, uo.placed_at,
    ug.customer_group,
    CASE WHEN uo.placed_at < ug.midpoint THEN 'first half' ELSE 'second half' END AS period
  FROM user_orders uo
  JOIN user_group ug ON ug.user_id = uo.user_id AND ug.tenant_id = uo.tenant_id
),
payment_refund AS (
  SELECT order_id, tenant_id, MAX(CASE WHEN amount_refunded > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_refund
  FROM payments
  WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY order_id, tenant_id
),
return_flag AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT order_id, tenant_id, 1 AS has_return
  FROM order_returns
),
order_refund AS (
  SELECT op.order_id, op.user_id, op.tenant_id, op.customer_group, op.period,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(pr.has_refund,0) = 1 OR rf.has_return = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_refunded
  FROM order_period op
  LEFT JOIN payment_refund pr ON pr.order_id = op.order_id AND pr.tenant_id = op.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN return_flag rf ON rf.order_id = op.order_id AND rf.tenant_id = op.tenant_id
),
customer_period AS (
  SELECT customer_group, period, user_id, tenant_id,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(is_refunded) AS refund_count
  FROM order_refund
  GROUP BY customer_group, period, user_id, tenant_id
),
customer_period_exposed AS (
  SELECT cp.customer_group, cp.period, cp.user_id, cp.tenant_id, cp.order_count, cp.refund_count,
    CASE WHEN cp.period = 'first half'
      THEN GREATEST(1, CAST(ug.midpoint AS date) - CAST(ug.first_order AS date))
      ELSE GREATEST(1, CAST(ug.last_order AS date) - CAST(ug.midpoint AS date))
    END AS exposed_days
  FROM customer_period cp
  JOIN user_group ug ON ug.user_id = cp.user_id AND ug.tenant_id = cp.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  customer_group AS "group",
  period,
  COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
  SUM(order_count) AS total_orders,
  ROUND(CAST(SUM(order_count) / (SUM(exposed_days) / 365.0) AS numeric), 2) AS orders_per_customer_per_year,
  ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(refund_count) / SUM(order_count) AS numeric), 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM customer_period_exposed
GROUP BY customer_group, period
ORDER BY
  CASE customer_group WHEN 'non-member' THEN 1 WHEN 'never-redeemed member' THEN 2 WHEN 'ever-redeemed member' THEN 3 END,
  CASE period WHEN 'first half' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END
builds_on: Member order behavior before vs after their first points redemption
entries.engineer_note: Grain is customer group x lifetime period (6 rows total), as requested. Note: loyalty_accounts/loyalty_transactions and orders are joined on (tenant_id, user_id) since user_id is only unique per tenant; refund flag combines payments.amount_refunded>0 and presence of any order_returns row for the order, amounts are not currency-converted since this report counts orders/customers/rates rather than summing money.

entries.title: Platform-wide: never-redeemed vs ever-redeemed members vs non-members, by tenure
entries.question: Does the Apparel finding - that engaged (ever-redeemed) members beat tenure-matched non-members while never-redeemed members lag behind - hold up across the whole platform, or was it specific to Apparel?
entries.sql:
WITH eligible_users AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT u.id AS user_id, u.tenant_id, u.created_at
  FROM users u
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id AND o.tenant_id = u.tenant_id
  WHERE u.is_staff = false
    AND o.placed_at >= TIMESTAMP '2023-01-01 00:00:00'
    AND o.placed_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
),
tenure AS (
  SELECT
    user_id, tenant_id,
    CASE
      WHEN created_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' - INTERVAL '6 months' THEN 'under 6 months'
      WHEN created_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' - INTERVAL '12 months' THEN '6 to 12 months'
      WHEN created_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' - INTERVAL '24 months' THEN '12 to 24 months'
      ELSE 'over 24 months'
    END AS tenure_band
  FROM eligible_users
),
loyalty_member AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id, tenant_id FROM loyalty_accounts
),
loyalty_redeemed AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id, tenant_id FROM loyalty_transactions WHERE direction = 'burn'
),
membership AS (
  SELECT
    eu.user_id, eu.tenant_id,
    CASE
      WHEN lm.user_id IS NULL THEN 'non-member'
      WHEN lr.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'ever-redeemed member'
      ELSE 'never-redeemed member'
    END AS customer_group
  FROM eligible_users eu
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_member lm ON lm.user_id = eu.user_id AND lm.tenant_id = eu.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN loyalty_redeemed lr ON lr.user_id = eu.user_id AND lr.tenant_id = eu.tenant_id
),
order_refund_flag AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    CASE
      WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments p WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.amount_refunded > 0)
        OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_returns r WHERE r.order_id = o.id)
      THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS is_refunded
  FROM orders o
),
order_eur AS (
  SELECT
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.user_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.status,
    CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN o.grand_total / er.rate ELSE NULL END AS revenue_eur
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
    AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
    AND er.as_of = CAST(COALESCE(o.placed_at, o.created_at) AS date)
),
customer_orders AS (
  SELECT
    eu.user_id,
    eu.tenant_id,
    COUNT(o.id) AS lifetime_orders,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN oe.revenue_eur ELSE 0 END) AS lifetime_revenue_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.status <> 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_cancelled_order_count,
    SUM(orf.is_refunded) AS refunded_order_count
  FROM eligible_users eu
  JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = eu.user_id AND o.tenant_id = eu.tenant_id
  JOIN order_eur oe ON oe.order_id = o.id
  JOIN order_refund_flag orf ON orf.order_id = o.id
  GROUP BY eu.user_id, eu.tenant_id
),
final AS (
  SELECT
    t.tenure_band,
    m.customer_group,
    COUNT(*) AS customer_count,
    AVG(co.lifetime_orders) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
    AVG(co.lifetime_revenue_eur) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
    SUM(co.lifetime_revenue_eur) / NULLIF(SUM(co.non_cancelled_order_count), 0) AS avg_order_value_eur,
    100.0 * SUM(co.refunded_order_count) / NULLIF(SUM(co.lifetime_orders), 0) AS refund_rate_pct
  FROM tenure t
  JOIN membership m ON m.user_id = t.user_id AND m.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  JOIN customer_orders co ON co.user_id = t.user_id AND co.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  GROUP BY t.tenure_band, m.customer_group
)
SELECT
  tenure_band,
  customer_group AS "group",
  customer_count,
  ROUND(avg_lifetime_orders, 2) AS avg_lifetime_orders,
  ROUND(avg_lifetime_revenue_eur, 2) AS avg_lifetime_revenue_eur,
  ROUND(avg_order_value_eur, 2) AS avg_order_value_eur,
  ROUND(refund_rate_pct, 2) AS refund_rate_pct
FROM final
ORDER BY
  CASE tenure_band
    WHEN 'under 6 months' THEN 1
    WHEN '6 to 12 months' THEN 2
    WHEN '12 to 24 months' THEN 3
    WHEN 'over 24 months' THEN 4
  END,
  CASE customer_group
    WHEN 'non-member' THEN 1
    WHEN 'never-redeemed member' THEN 2
    WHEN 'ever-redeemed member' THEN 3
  END
builds_on: Apparel: never-redeemed vs ever-redeemed members vs non-members, by tenure
entries.engineer_note: Same methodology as the Apparel report (tenure band from users.created_at, non-member/never-redeemed/ever-redeemed groups via loyalty_accounts + 'burn' loyalty_transactions, revenue/AOV from non-cancelled orders converted to EUR via exchange_rates on placed_at, refund = amount_refunded>0 or an order_returns row), just without the industry filter. avg_order_value_eur and refund_rate_pct are computed as group-level totals (sum revenue / sum orders, sum refunded / sum orders) rather than an average of per-customer ratios, to avoid division-by-zero for customers with zero non-cancelled orders.

entries.title: Post-redemption drop-off by how quickly members first redeemed
entries.question: Are members who redeem points very soon after enrolling - likely signup-bonus hunters - disproportionately the ones who never place another order, which would be the clearest sign of rewards given without real repeat purchase behind them?
entries.sql:
WITH member_enroll AS (
  SELECT la.user_id AS user_id, MIN(la.enrolled_at) AS enrolled_at
  FROM loyalty_accounts la
  GROUP BY la.user_id
),
member_first_burn AS (
  SELECT lt.user_id AS user_id, MIN(lt.occurred_at) AS first_burn_at
  FROM loyalty_transactions lt
  WHERE lt.direction = 'burn'
  GROUP BY lt.user_id
),
member_base AS (
  SELECT
    t0.user_id AS user_id,
    t0.enrolled_at AS enrolled_at,
    t1.first_burn_at AS first_burn_at,
    CASE
      WHEN (t1.first_burn_at::date - t0.enrolled_at::date) <= 30 THEN 'within 30 days of enrollment'
      WHEN (t1.first_burn_at::date - t0.enrolled_at::date) <= 180 THEN '31 to 180 days'
      ELSE 'over 180 days'
    END AS bucket
  FROM member_enroll t0
  JOIN member_first_burn t1 ON t1.user_id = t0.user_id
),
orders_after_count AS (
  SELECT
    mb.user_id AS user_id,
    COUNT(o.id) AS orders_after_count
  FROM member_base mb
  LEFT JOIN orders o
    ON o.user_id = mb.user_id
   AND o.placed_at >= mb.first_burn_at
  GROUP BY mb.user_id
),
orders_after_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    mb.user_id AS user_id,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN o.id IS NULL THEN 0
        WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.grand_total
        ELSE o.grand_total / NULLIF(er.rate, 0)
      END
    ) AS revenue_after_eur
  FROM member_base mb
  LEFT JOIN orders o
    ON o.user_id = mb.user_id
   AND o.placed_at >= mb.first_burn_at
   AND o.status <> 'cancelled'
  LEFT JOIN exchange_rates er
    ON er.base_code = 'EUR'
   AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
   AND er.as_of = o.placed_at::date
  GROUP BY mb.user_id
)
SELECT
  mb.bucket AS time_to_first_redemption_bucket,
  COUNT(*) AS member_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(oac.orders_after_count, 0) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_with_no_orders_after_redemption,
  ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(oac.orders_after_count, 0)), 2) AS avg_orders_after_per_customer,
  ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(oar.revenue_after_eur, 0)), 2) AS avg_revenue_after_eur
FROM member_base mb
LEFT JOIN orders_after_count oac ON oac.user_id = mb.user_id
LEFT JOIN orders_after_revenue oar ON oar.user_id = mb.user_id
GROUP BY mb.bucket
ORDER BY
  CASE mb.bucket
    WHEN 'within 30 days of enrollment' THEN 1
    WHEN '31 to 180 days' THEN 2
    WHEN 'over 180 days' THEN 3
  END
builds_on: Member order behavior before vs after their first points redemption
entries.engineer_note: Population is deduplicated by user_id across all tenants (a user's enrollment date is the earliest across any loyalty_accounts row, and 'first redemption' is their earliest burn transaction); revenue excludes cancelled orders and is converted to EUR via same-day exchange_rates, with EUR orders passed through unconverted.

entries.title: Lost B2B Wholesale Deals: When Does Activity Happen Relative to the Deal's Life
entries.question: For deals that eventually get lost, does sales activity cluster early, stay steady throughout, or come in a late flurry right before the deal is given up on — or does it go quiet before the end (stalled and forgotten)?
entries.sql:
WITH scoped_tenants AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf','Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging')
),
new_business_pipelines AS (
  SELECT p.id AS pipeline_id, p.tenant_id
  FROM pipelines p
  JOIN scoped_tenants st ON st.id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE p.name = 'New business'
),
lost_opps AS (
  SELECT o.id AS opportunity_id, o.tenant_id, o.created_at, o.closed_at
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN new_business_pipelines nbp ON nbp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id AND nbp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.is_won = false
),
total_lost AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_lost_opps FROM lost_opps
),
activity_positions AS (
  SELECT
    a.id AS activity_id,
    lo.opportunity_id,
    CASE
      WHEN lo.closed_at IS NULL OR lo.created_at IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN lo.closed_at = lo.created_at THEN NULL
      ELSE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (a.occurred_at - lo.created_at)) / EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (lo.closed_at - lo.created_at))
    END AS relative_position
  FROM activities a
  JOIN lost_opps lo ON lo.opportunity_id = a.opportunity_id AND a.tenant_id = lo.tenant_id
),
bucketed AS (
  SELECT
    activity_id,
    opportunity_id,
    CASE
      WHEN relative_position IS NULL OR relative_position < 0 OR relative_position > 1 THEN 'outside window'
      WHEN relative_position < 0.25 THEN 'Q1 (0-25%)'
      WHEN relative_position < 0.5 THEN 'Q2 (25-50%)'
      WHEN relative_position < 0.75 THEN 'Q3 (50-75%)'
      ELSE 'Q4 (75-100%)'
    END AS lifecycle_quartile
  FROM activity_positions
),
totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_activities_all FROM bucketed
)
SELECT
  b.lifecycle_quartile,
  COUNT(*) AS total_activities_in_bucket,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / t.total_activities_all, 2) AS pct_of_total_activities,
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.opportunity_id) AS opportunities_with_at_least_one_activity_in_bucket,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT b.opportunity_id) / tl.total_lost_opps, 2) AS pct_of_lost_opportunities_with_activity_in_bucket
FROM bucketed b
CROSS JOIN totals t
CROSS JOIN total_lost tl
GROUP BY b.lifecycle_quartile, t.total_activities_all, tl.total_lost_opps
ORDER BY CASE b.lifecycle_quartile
  WHEN 'Q1 (0-25%)' THEN 1
  WHEN 'Q2 (25-50%)' THEN 2
  WHEN 'Q3 (50-75%)' THEN 3
  WHEN 'Q4 (75-100%)' THEN 4
  ELSE 5
END
builds_on: New Business Only: Won vs Lost Opportunity Characteristics
entries.engineer_note: Scoped to the 5 named tenants' 'New business' pipeline, opportunities with is_closed=true and is_won=false. Activities with null/zero-duration relative position, or outside [0,1], are grouped into an 'outside window' bucket per the spec; pct_of_lost_opportunities uses a fixed denominator (total lost opportunities in scope) across all rows.

entries.title: Youssef Meijer: Individual New-Business Opportunities
entries.question: Looking at Youssef Meijer's own deals one by one — which accounts, what sizes, how long open — does his low win rate look like a few bad accounts/territory, or a pattern across all his work?
entries.sql:
WITH polder_tenant AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id
  FROM tenants
  WHERE name = 'Polder Packaging'
),
owner AS (
  SELECT u.id AS user_id
  FROM users u
  JOIN polder_tenant pt ON u.tenant_id = pt.tenant_id
  WHERE u.full_name = 'Youssef Meijer'
),
pipeline AS (
  SELECT p.id AS pipeline_id
  FROM pipelines p
  JOIN polder_tenant pt ON p.tenant_id = pt.tenant_id
  WHERE p.name = 'New business'
),
target_opportunities AS (
  SELECT
    o.id,
    o.account_id,
    o.amount,
    o.currency_code,
    o.is_won,
    o.created_at,
    o.closed_at
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN owner ON o.owner_user_id = owner.user_id
  JOIN pipeline ON o.pipeline_id = pipeline.pipeline_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true
),
with_account AS (
  SELECT
    t.*,
    a.name AS account_name
  FROM target_opportunities t
  JOIN accounts a ON t.account_id = a.id
),
with_rate AS (
  SELECT
    wa.*,
    CASE
      WHEN wa.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN 1.0
      ELSE (
        SELECT er.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er
        WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = wa.currency_code
          AND er.as_of <= wa.closed_at::date
        ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
        LIMIT 1
      )
    END AS eur_rate
  FROM with_account wa
)
SELECT
  account_name,
  CASE WHEN is_won THEN 'won' ELSE 'lost' END AS outcome,
  ROUND(amount / eur_rate, 2) AS amount_eur,
  currency_code,
  (closed_at::date - created_at::date) AS days_open,
  created_at,
  closed_at
FROM with_rate
ORDER BY closed_at ASC, account_name ASC
builds_on: B2B Wholesale: Win Rate and Cycle Time by Sales Rep (New Business) — Corrected
entries.engineer_note: One row per closed opportunity owned by Youssef Meijer at Polder Packaging on the 'New business' pipeline; EUR conversion uses the exchange rate as_of the nearest date on or before closed_at. Expect ~7 rows as noted in the request.

entries.title: Did B2B Wholesale New-Business Pipeline Ever Carry an Open Balance at Month-End?
entries.question: Is the current complete absence of open new-business pipeline a constant feature of the last three years, or did merchants used to carry live open deals and that's changed recently?
entries.sql:
with month_ends as (
    select
        year_num,
        month_num,
        max(calendar_date) as month_end_date
    from calendar_days
    where year_num between 2023 and 2025
    group by year_num, month_num
),
scoped_tenants as (
    select id as tenant_id, name
    from tenants
    where name in (
        'Ballycorran Industrial Supply',
        'Castell Fasteners',
        'Hanse Industriebedarf',
        'Midland Safety Wear',
        'Polder Packaging'
    )
),
new_business_pipelines as (
    select p.id as pipeline_id, p.tenant_id
    from pipelines p
    join scoped_tenants st on st.tenant_id = p.tenant_id
    where p.name = 'New business'
),
scoped_opportunities as (
    select o.id, o.tenant_id, o.created_at, o.closed_at
    from opportunities o
    join new_business_pipelines nbp
        on nbp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id
        and nbp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
),
monthly_open_opportunities as (
    select
        me.month_end_date,
        o.id as opportunity_id,
        (me.month_end_date - o.created_at::date) as age_days
    from month_ends me
    cross join scoped_opportunities o
    where o.created_at::date <= me.month_end_date
        and (o.closed_at is null or o.closed_at::date > me.month_end_date)
)
select
    me.month_end_date,
    count(moo.opportunity_id) as opportunities_open_at_month_end,
    round(avg(moo.age_days)::numeric, 1) as avg_age_days_of_open_opportunities_at_month_end,
    max(moo.age_days) as oldest_age_days_of_open_opportunity_at_month_end
from month_ends me
left join monthly_open_opportunities moo
    on moo.month_end_date = me.month_end_date
group by me.month_end_date

entries.title: B2B Wholesale New-Business Opportunities: Created vs Closed by Month
entries.question: Did new-deal creation actually stop or slow down recently, or did deals just happen to all get closed out right as the data ends — i.e., is the 'zero open pipeline' at Dec 2025 a real freeze or a coincidence of timing?
entries.sql:
WITH target_pipelines AS (
  SELECT p.id AS pipeline_id, p.tenant_id AS tenant_id
  FROM pipelines p
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf','Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging')
    AND p.name = 'New business'
),
months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_start, month_label FROM calendar_days WHERE calendar_date BETWEEN DATE '2023-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
),
created AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', o.created_at)::date AS month_start, count(*) AS cnt
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN target_pipelines tp ON tp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id AND tp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.created_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1
),
closed AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('month', o.closed_at)::date AS month_start, count(*) AS cnt
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN target_pipelines tp ON tp.pipeline_id = o.pipeline_id AND tp.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  WHERE o.is_closed = true AND o.closed_at >= DATE '2023-01-01' AND o.closed_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT m.month_label AS month,
       coalesce(c.cnt,0) AS opportunities_created,
       coalesce(cl.cnt,0) AS opportunities_closed
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN created c ON c.month_start = m.month_start
LEFT JOIN closed cl ON cl.month_start = m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start

entries.engineer_note: Scoped to the five named tenants' 'New business' pipeline as requested; one row per month Jan 2023-Dec 2025 (36 rows), with zero-filled months where no opportunities were created/closed.

entries.title: B2B Wholesale: Dollar-Weighted vs Count-Weighted Win Rate by Rep
entries.question: Is Youssef Meijer's pattern of winning small deals but losing his biggest one a one-off, or do several reps actually perform worse on a dollar basis than their deal-count win rate suggests?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  u.full_name AS rep_name,
  t.name AS merchant,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS count_win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN sub.amount_eur ELSE 0 END), 2) AS total_amount_won_eur,
  ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN NOT sub.is_won THEN sub.amount_eur ELSE 0 END), 2) AS total_amount_lost_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN sub.amount_eur ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(sub.amount_eur), 0), 1) AS dollar_weighted_win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(
    (100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*))
    - (100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN sub.is_won THEN sub.amount_eur ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(sub.amount_eur), 0))
  , 1) AS gap_pct_points
FROM (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    o.owner_user_id,
    o.is_won,
    CASE
      WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
      ELSE o.amount / (
        SELECT er.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er
        WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
          AND er.as_of <= CAST(o.closed_at AS DATE)
        ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
        LIMIT 1
      )
    END AS amount_eur
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN tenants t2 ON t2.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id
  WHERE t2.name IN (
      'Ballycorran Industrial Supply',
      'Castell Fasteners',
      'Hanse Industriebedarf',
      'Midland Safety Wear',
      'Polder Packaging'
    )
    AND p.name = 'New business'
    AND o.is_closed = true
) sub
JOIN users u ON u.id = sub.owner_user_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = sub.tenant_id
GROUP BY sub.owner_user_id, u.full_name, t.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY gap_pct_points DESC, rep_name ASC

Youssef Meijer: Individual New-Business Opportunities
entries.engineer_note: Pipeline scoped by pipelines.name = 'New business' per tenant as requested; amount converted to EUR via the exchange rate on or before closed_at (falls back to the most recent prior rate, consistent with weekend carry-forward). Reps with fewer than 3 closed opportunities in scope are excluded via HAVING.

entries.title: B2B Wholesale: Seasonality of Lost-Deal Cycle Time by Quarter
entries.question: Do lost deals linger longest at particular times of year (e.g., end-of-quarter or holiday periods), or is the ~35-day drag before a deal is given up on roughly constant regardless of when it started?
entries.sql:
with tenant_scope as (
    select id as tenant_id, name
    from tenants
    where name in ('Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf','Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging')
),
pipeline_scope as (
    select p.id as pipeline_id, p.tenant_id
    from pipelines p
    join tenant_scope t on p.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
    where p.name = 'New business'
),
lost_opportunities as (
    select
        o.id as opportunity_id,
        o.created_at,
        o.closed_at,
        (extract(epoch from (o.closed_at - o.created_at)) / 86400.0) as days_open
    from opportunities o
    join pipeline_scope ps
        on o.pipeline_id = ps.pipeline_id
        and o.tenant_id = ps.tenant_id
    where o.is_closed = true
      and o.is_won = false
      and o.closed_at is not null
),
dated as (
    select
        lo.opportunity_id,
        lo.days_open,
        cd.year_num,
        cd.quarter_num
    from lost_opportunities lo
    join calendar_days cd on cd.calendar_date = lo.closed_at::date
)
select
    (year_num || 'Q' || quarter_num) as quarter,
    count(*) as lost_opportunities_count,
    round(avg(days_open)::numeric, 1) as avg_days_open,
    round(percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by days_open)::numeric, 1) as median_days_open
from dated
group by year_num, quarter_num
order by year_num, quarter_num

entries.title: B2B Wholesale: Dollar-Weighted vs Count-Weighted Win Rate by Merchant
entries.question: Does Youssef Meijer's 'wins small deals, loses the big one' pattern show up at the Polder Packaging merchant level too, or is it fully offset by his co-rep (Thijs Dijkstra) once you zoom out?
entries.sql:
WITH opp AS (
  SELECT
    o.tenant_id,
    t.name AS merchant,
    o.amount,
    o.currency_code,
    o.closed_at,
    os.is_won,
    os.is_lost
  FROM opportunities o
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN pipelines p ON p.id = o.pipeline_id AND p.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
  JOIN opportunity_stages os ON os.id = o.stage_id
  WHERE t.name IN (
    'Ballycorran Industrial Supply','Castell Fasteners','Hanse Industriebedarf',
    'Midland Safety Wear','Polder Packaging'
  )
  AND p.name = 'New business'
  AND o.is_closed = true
),
rated AS (
  SELECT
    opp.merchant,
    opp.is_won,
    opp.is_lost,
    CASE
      WHEN opp.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN opp.amount
      ELSE opp.amount / (
        SELECT er.rate
        FROM exchange_rates er
        WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
          AND er.quote_code = opp.currency_code
          AND er.as_of <= opp.closed_at::date
        ORDER BY er.as_of DESC
        LIMIT 1
      )
    END AS amount_eur
  FROM opp
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    merchant,
    COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS won_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_won THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS total_amount_won_eur,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_lost THEN amount_eur ELSE 0 END) AS total_amount_lost_eur
  FROM rated
  GROUP BY merchant
)
SELECT
  merchant,
  opportunities_closed,
  ROUND(100.0 * won_count / opportunities_closed, 2) AS count_win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(total_amount_won_eur, 2) AS total_amount_won_eur,
  ROUND(total_amount_lost_eur, 2) AS total_amount_lost_eur,
  ROUND(100.0 * total_amount_won_eur / NULLIF(total_amount_won_eur + total_amount_lost_eur, 0), 2) AS dollar_weighted_win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(
    (100.0 * won_count / opportunities_closed)
    - (100.0 * total_amount_won_eur / NULLIF(total_amount_won_eur + total_amount_lost_eur, 0)),
    2
  ) AS gap_pct_points
FROM agg
ORDER BY gap_pct_points DESC, merchant ASC
