No minimum-deal filter applied per instructions.

entries.title: Trend of stock-count discrepancies within 2025: steady climb or step change?
entries.question: Did the 24% year-over-year rise in routine stock-count discrepancies climb steadily, or did it step up at a specific point in the year (and is that step explained by more warehouses coming online, or a genuine per-location worsening)?
entries.sql:
WITH periods AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    date_trunc('month', calendar_date)::date AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN day_of_month <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS half
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND calendar_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
adj AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', sa.created_at)::date AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN EXTRACT(day FROM sa.created_at)::int <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS half,
    sa.stock_location_id,
    sa.quantity_delta
  FROM stock_adjustments sa
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sa.stock_location_id
  WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
adj_agg AS (
  SELECT
    month_start, half,
    COUNT(*) AS events,
    SUM(ABS(quantity_delta)) AS abs_units_variance,
    SUM(quantity_delta) AS net_units_variance,
    COUNT(DISTINCT stock_location_id) AS distinct_locations_active
  FROM adj
  GROUP BY month_start, half
),
wh AS (
  SELECT
    date_trunc('month', w.created_at)::date AS month_start,
    CASE WHEN EXTRACT(day FROM w.created_at)::int <= 15 THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS half,
    COUNT(*) AS new_warehouses
  FROM warehouses w
  WHERE w.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND w.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY month_start, half
)
SELECT
  strftime(p.month_start, '%Y-%m') || ' (' ||
    CASE WHEN p.half = 1 THEN '1-15'
         ELSE '16-' || EXTRACT(DAY FROM (p.month_start + INTERVAL '1 month' - INTERVAL '1 day'))::int
    END || ')' AS period_label,
  COALESCE(a.events, 0) AS events,
  COALESCE(a.abs_units_variance, 0) AS abs_units_variance,
  COALESCE(a.net_units_variance, 0) AS net_units_variance,
  COALESCE(a.distinct_locations_active, 0) AS distinct_locations_active,
  ROUND(
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(a.distinct_locations_active, 0) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE a.events::numeric / a.distinct_locations_active
    END, 2
  ) AS events_per_active_location,
  COALESCE(w.new_warehouses, 0) AS new_warehouses_opened_this_period
FROM periods p
LEFT JOIN adj_agg a ON a.month_start = p.month_start AND a.half = p.half
LEFT JOIN wh w ON w.month_start = p.month_start AND w.half = p.half
ORDER BY p.month_start, p.half
builds_on: Monthly volume of stock_adjustments table entries, 2025
Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
entries.engineer_note: Covers all tenants (no tenant_id filter) since the question is platform-wide about discrepancy trend and warehouse rollout; events_per_active_location is NULL for any period with zero active locations to avoid divide-by-zero.

entries.title: Who logs 'Missing - suspected theft' stock adjustments: concentrated among specific staff?
entries.question: Is the 'Missing - suspected theft' reason spread roughly proportionally across everyone who logs stock adjustments, or does it concentrate in a handful of specific staff members — and do their theft entries cluster at a particular time of day (suggesting end-of-shift batch logging rather than individually investigated incidents)?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(u.full_name, 'Unknown/unassigned') AS staff_name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_adjustments_logged,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sa.reason = 'Missing - suspected theft') AS theft_tagged_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sa.reason = 'Missing - suspected theft') / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_theft_of_own_adjustments,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sa.reason = 'Damaged in warehouse') AS damage_tagged_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sa.reason = 'Expired') AS expired_tagged_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sa.reason = 'Cycle count variance') AS cycle_count_variance_count,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(HOUR FROM sa.created_at)) FILTER (WHERE sa.reason = 'Missing - suspected theft'), 1) AS avg_hour_of_day_for_theft_entries,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_staff_with_adjustments_2025
FROM stock_adjustments sa
LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = sa.adjusted_by_user_id
WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY sa.adjusted_by_user_id, u.full_name
ORDER BY theft_tagged_count DESC, total_adjustments_logged DESC, staff_name ASC
LIMIT 50
entries.engineer_note: Report shows top 50 staff by theft-tagged count; the total_staff_with_adjustments_2025 column (a window count over the full grouped result, computed before the LIMIT) tells you how many distinct staff logged >=1 adjustment in 2025 in case it exceeds 50. Not scoped to a single tenant/merchant since the question is about staff behavior generally, not a particular merchant; user ids are globally unique so grouping/joining works correctly across tenants.

entries.title: Where 'Missing - suspected theft' tags concentrate: by warehouse
entries.question: Does the 'Missing - suspected theft' reason concentrate in a handful of specific warehouses/sites, or is it spread evenly across all sites that log stock adjustments?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    w.id AS warehouse_id,
    w.name AS warehouse_name,
    t.name AS tenant_name,
    sa.reason,
    sa.adjusted_by_user_id
  FROM stock_adjustments sa
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sa.stock_location_id
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT
    warehouse_id,
    warehouse_name,
    tenant_name,
    COUNT(*) AS total_adjustments_at_site,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE reason = 'Missing - suspected theft') AS theft_tagged_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT adjusted_by_user_id) FILTER (WHERE reason = 'Missing - suspected theft') AS distinct_staff_logging_theft_here
  FROM base
  GROUP BY warehouse_id, warehouse_name, tenant_name
)
SELECT
  warehouse_name,
  tenant_name,
  total_adjustments_at_site,
  theft_tagged_count,
  ROUND(theft_tagged_count * 100.0 / NULLIF(total_adjustments_at_site, 0), 1) AS pct_theft_of_site_adjustments,
  distinct_staff_logging_theft_here,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_warehouses_with_adjustments_2025
FROM agg
ORDER BY theft_tagged_count DESC, pct_theft_of_site_adjustments DESC, warehouse_name ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Where 'Missing - suspected theft' tags concentrate: by warehouse
entries.engineer_note: Report is capped at 50 warehouses as requested; I added a repeated column total_warehouses_with_adjustments_2025 (a window count computed before the LIMIT) so the analyst can see the full distinct-warehouse count even though only up to 50 rows print.

entries.title: Do B2B wholesale merchants get routine stock counts, or only the annual catch-up?
entries.question: Do the B2B wholesale/office-supply merchants behind the December 31 correction run any routine, day-to-day stock-count activity during the year, or does their stock sit untouched in bulk storage until a single year-end true-up?
entries.sql:
WITH loc AS (
  SELECT sl.id AS stock_location_id, w.tenant_id, sl.kind
  FROM stock_locations sl
  JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name IN ('Deskline Supplies', 'OfficeHub Nordic', 'Kontor24 Bürobedarf', 'Hanse Industriebedarf', 'Castell Fasteners', 'Midland Safety Wear', 'Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'Polder Packaging')
),
loc_agg AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    count(*) AS total_stock_locations,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'bulk') AS bulk_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'pick') AS pick_count
  FROM loc
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
adj AS (
  SELECT l.tenant_id,
    count(*) AS routine_stock_adjustments_2025,
    count(DISTINCT sa.variant_id) AS distinct_variants_with_routine_adjustment
  FROM stock_adjustments sa
  JOIN loc l ON l.stock_location_id = sa.stock_location_id
  WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY l.tenant_id
),
dec31 AS (
  SELECT l.tenant_id,
    sum(abs(sm.quantity)) AS dec31_correction_abs_units,
    count(DISTINCT sm.variant_id) AS dec31_correction_distinct_variants
  FROM stock_movements sm
  JOIN loc l ON l.stock_location_id = sm.stock_location_id
  WHERE sm.kind = 'adjustment' AND sm.occurred_at::date = DATE '2025-12-31'
  GROUP BY l.tenant_id
)
SELECT t.name AS tenant_name,
  la.total_stock_locations,
  round(100.0 * la.bulk_count / la.total_stock_locations, 1) AS pct_locations_kind_bulk,
  round(100.0 * la.pick_count / la.total_stock_locations, 1) AS pct_locations_kind_pick,
  coalesce(adj.routine_stock_adjustments_2025, 0) AS routine_stock_adjustments_2025,
  coalesce(adj.distinct_variants_with_routine_adjustment, 0) AS distinct_variants_with_routine_adjustment,
  coalesce(dec31.dec31_correction_abs_units, 0) AS dec31_correction_abs_units,
  coalesce(dec31.dec31_correction_distinct_variants, 0) AS dec31_correction_distinct_variants
FROM tenants t
JOIN loc_agg la ON la.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN adj ON adj.tenant_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN dec31 ON dec31.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE t.name IN ('Deskline Supplies', 'OfficeHub Nordic', 'Kontor24 Bürobedarf', 'Hanse Industriebedarf', 'Castell Fasteners', 'Midland Safety Wear', 'Ballycorran Industrial Supply', 'Polder Packaging')
ORDER BY dec31_correction_abs_units DESC, tenant_name
builds_on: Which merchants drove the December 31 bulk stock correction
Stock-count discrepancies by storage-location kind, company-wide

entries.title: Apparel/footwear discrepancies by warehouse: scale effect or genuine elevated rate?
entries.question: Is the apparel/footwear concentration in stock-count discrepancies explained by those warehouses simply being bigger (more pick locations), or do specific apparel sites show a genuinely higher discrepancy rate per location?
entries.sql:
SELECT warehouse_name, tenant_name, distinct_pick_locations, total_routine_adjustments_2025,
  ROUND(CASE WHEN distinct_pick_locations = 0 THEN NULL ELSE total_routine_adjustments_2025::numeric / distinct_pick_locations END, 2) AS events_per_pick_location,
  distinct_variants_affected,
  avg_hour_of_day_of_entries
FROM (
  SELECT w.id as warehouse_id, w.name as warehouse_name, t.name as tenant_name,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stock_locations sl2 WHERE sl2.warehouse_id = w.id AND sl2.kind = 'pick') as distinct_pick_locations,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stock_adjustments sa2
       WHERE sa2.stock_location_id IN (SELECT sl3.id FROM stock_locations sl3 WHERE sl3.warehouse_id = w.id)
       AND sa2.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa2.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') as total_routine_adjustments_2025,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sa3.variant_id) FROM stock_adjustments sa3
       WHERE sa3.stock_location_id IN (SELECT sl4.id FROM stock_locations sl4 WHERE sl4.warehouse_id = w.id)
       AND sa3.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa3.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') as distinct_variants_affected,
    (SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(HOUR FROM sa4.created_at)), 1) FROM stock_adjustments sa4
       WHERE sa4.stock_location_id IN (SELECT sl5.id FROM stock_locations sl5 WHERE sl5.warehouse_id = w.id)
       AND sa4.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa4.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01') as avg_hour_of_day_of_entries
  FROM warehouses w
  JOIN tenants t ON w.tenant_id = t.id
  WHERE t.industry = 'Apparel & Footwear'
) sub
ORDER BY events_per_pick_location DESC NULLS LAST, total_routine_adjustments_2025 DESC, warehouse_name ASC, warehouse_id ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Where 'Missing - suspected theft' tags concentrate: by warehouse
Trend of stock-count discrepancies within 2025: steady climb or step change?
entries.engineer_note: Grain is warehouse, restricted to tenants.industry = 'Apparel & Footwear' as specified; distinct_pick_locations counts stock_locations with kind='pick' independent of whether adjustments occurred there, so events_per_pick_location is NULL (shown blank) for any warehouse with zero pick locations. If the true apparel-warehouse count exceeds 50 the report is capped at 50 rows per the house page-length limit; please flag if you need the full count surfaced separately.

entries.title: Which specific products drive discrepancies at the three standout apparel sites
entries.question: At Atlanta (Cragsley Outfitters), Reading (Marrowby & Vane) and Den Haag (Studio Vrij) — the three sites with by far the most stock-count discrepancies — is the problem spread across the catalog, or concentrated in a handful of specific products/size-color variants?
entries.sql:
WITH three_warehouses AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM warehouses
  WHERE name IN ('Atlanta Fulfilment Centre','Reading Fulfilment Centre','Den Haag Fulfilment Centre')
),
adjustments AS (
  SELECT sa.variant_id, sa.reason, sa.created_at, w.name AS warehouse_name
  FROM stock_adjustments sa
  JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sa.stock_location_id
  JOIN three_warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
  WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
variant_info AS (
  SELECT pv.id AS variant_id, pv.sku, pv.name AS variant_name, p.name AS product_name
  FROM product_variants pv
  JOIN products p ON p.id = pv.product_id
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT
    a.warehouse_name,
    vi.product_name,
    vi.sku,
    vi.variant_name,
    COUNT(*) AS adjustment_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.reason = 'Missing - suspected theft' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_theft_reason,
    COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(a.created_at)) AS distinct_days_affected
  FROM adjustments a
  JOIN variant_info vi ON vi.variant_id = a.variant_id
  GROUP BY a.warehouse_name, vi.product_name, vi.sku, vi.variant_name
)
SELECT
  warehouse_name,
  product_name,
  sku,
  variant_name,
  adjustment_count,
  pct_theft_reason,
  distinct_days_affected,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_distinct_variants
FROM aggregated
ORDER BY adjustment_count DESC, warehouse_name ASC, sku ASC
LIMIT 50
builds_on: Where 'Missing - suspected theft' tags concentrate: by warehouse
entries.engineer_note: Grain is warehouse × product variant as requested; adjustment_count/pct_theft_reason/distinct_days_affected are computed per variant per warehouse over 2025 stock_adjustments at the three named sites. Added a total_distinct_variants column (window count before the 50-row cap) so the analyst can see the full count of variants with discrepancies even though only the top 50 by adjustment_count are printed.

entries.title: Is the December 31 correction one single batch event, or genuinely independent per merchant?
entries.question: Did the 407 stock_movements kind='adjustment' events in 2025 all fire at the exact same timestamp (suggesting one system/data event), or do different merchants' corrections have distinct timestamps (consistent with independent, organic annual stocktakes)?
entries.sql:
WITH t0 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT sm0.occurred_at AS occurred_at
  FROM stock_movements sm0
  WHERE sm0.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm0.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm0.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
t1 AS (
  SELECT sm1.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
         COUNT(*) AS event_count
  FROM stock_movements sm1
  WHERE sm1.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm1.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm1.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY sm1.occurred_at
),
t2 AS (
  SELECT sm2.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
         COUNT(DISTINCT sl2.warehouse_id) AS distinct_warehouses
  FROM stock_movements sm2
  JOIN stock_locations sl2 ON sl2.id = sm2.stock_location_id
  WHERE sm2.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm2.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm2.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY sm2.occurred_at
),
t3 AS (
  SELECT sm3.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
         COUNT(DISTINCT w3.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenants
  FROM stock_movements sm3
  JOIN stock_locations sl3 ON sl3.id = sm3.stock_location_id
  JOIN warehouses w3 ON w3.id = sl3.warehouse_id
  WHERE sm3.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm3.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm3.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY sm3.occurred_at
),
t4 AS (
  SELECT sm4.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
         SUM(ABS(sm4.quantity)) AS total_abs_quantity
  FROM stock_movements sm4
  WHERE sm4.kind = 'adjustment'
    AND sm4.occurred_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND sm4.occurred_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY sm4.occurred_at
)
SELECT
  t0.occurred_at AS occurred_at,
  COALESCE(t1.event_count, 0) AS event_count,
  COALESCE(t3.distinct_tenants, 0) AS distinct_tenants,
  COALESCE(t2.distinct_warehouses, 0) AS distinct_warehouses,
  COALESCE(t4.total_abs_quantity, 0) AS total_abs_quantity
FROM t0
LEFT JOIN t1 ON t1.occurred_at = t0.occurred_at
LEFT JOIN t2 ON t2.occurred_at = t0.occurred_at
LEFT JOIN t3 ON t3.occurred_at = t0.occurred_at
LEFT JOIN t4 ON t4.occurred_at = t0.occurred_at
ORDER BY event_count DESC, occurred_at ASC
builds_on: Scale of adjustment-kind stock movements by month, 2025
Do B2B wholesale merchants get routine stock counts, or only the annual catch-up?
entries.engineer_note: Grain is the distinct exact occurred_at timestamp among 2025 adjustment movements; warehouse/tenant joins are used only for the distinct counts, not to filter rows. The report will show however many distinct timestamp values exist (expected to be well under 50); if it turns out to exceed 50, let me know and I'll add a cap or pre-aggregate further.

entries.title: Do the zero-activity 'Warehouse' sites hold real inventory?
entries.question: The apparel merchants' secondary sites named '...Warehouse' (as opposed to '...Fulfilment Centre') showed zero stock-count activity all year — are these empty/inactive shells, or do they hold meaningful live inventory that is simply never being counted (a blind spot)?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  w.name AS warehouse_name,
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(si.quantity), 0)
     FROM stock_items si
     JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = si.stock_location_id
    WHERE sl.warehouse_id = w.id) AS total_stock_on_hand,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT si.variant_id)
     FROM stock_items si
     JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = si.stock_location_id
    WHERE sl.warehouse_id = w.id
      AND si.quantity > 0) AS distinct_variants_stocked,
  ROUND(
    (
      (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(si.quantity), 0)
         FROM stock_items si
         JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = si.stock_location_id
        WHERE sl.warehouse_id = w.id)::numeric
      /
      NULLIF(
        (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(si2.quantity), 0)
           FROM stock_items si2
           JOIN stock_locations sl2 ON sl2.id = si2.stock_location_id
           JOIN warehouses w2 ON w2.id = sl2.warehouse_id
          WHERE w2.tenant_id = w.tenant_id), 0
      ) * 100
    ), 1
  ) AS pct_of_tenant_total_stock_units
FROM warehouses w
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
WHERE (t.name, w.name) IN (
  VALUES
    ('Oakhurst Tailoring', 'Aarhus Warehouse'),
    ('Cragsley Outfitters', 'Boston Warehouse'),
    ('Studio Vrij', 'Brussels Warehouse'),
    ('Cragsley Outfitters', 'Calgary Warehouse'),
    ('Thistlecombe', 'Glasgow Warehouse'),
    ('Studio Vrij', 'Groningen Warehouse'),
    ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Limerick Warehouse'),
    ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Preston Warehouse'),
    ('Rue Lafayette Studio', 'Toulouse Warehouse'),
    ('Velvet Ash', 'Uppsala Warehouse')
)
ORDER BY total_stock_on_hand DESC, warehouse_name
builds_on: Apparel/footwear discrepancies by warehouse: scale effect or genuine elevated rate?
entries.engineer_note: The request names 10 warehouse/tenant pairs but refers to "9 zero-activity sites" — I included all 10 listed pairs since that's the explicit list given; please flag if one should be dropped.

entries.title: Is the ~1.08 adjustments-per-variant ratio apparel-specific or company-wide?
entries.question: Is the near-constant rate of about 1.08 routine stock-adjustments per distinct affected variant per year a quirk of the apparel/footwear vertical, or does it hold across all merchant verticals — i.e., is the whole routine discrepancy stream essentially a flat background rate of roughly one single-unit miss per SKU per year, regardless of product type?
entries.sql:
SELECT t.industry,
  COUNT(*) AS total_routine_adjustments_2025,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sa.variant_id) AS distinct_variants_with_adjustment,
  ROUND(COUNT(*)::numeric / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT sa.variant_id), 0), 3) AS adjustments_per_variant,
  COUNT(DISTINCT t.id) AS distinct_tenants_in_industry
FROM stock_adjustments sa
JOIN stock_locations sl ON sl.id = sa.stock_location_id
JOIN warehouses w ON w.id = sl.warehouse_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = w.tenant_id
WHERE sa.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND sa.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY t.industry
ORDER BY adjustments_per_variant DESC, t.industry ASC
builds_on: Apparel/footwear discrepancies by warehouse: scale effect or genuine elevated rate?
Reasons behind routine stock_adjustments entries, 2025
entries.engineer_note: Grouped by tenants.industry (the free-text field on the tenants table) since that's the only industry/vertical attribute available; adjustment counts are all stock_adjustments rows (table has no distinction between "routine" and other reasons) in 2025, reached via stock_location_id -> stock_locations -> warehouses -> tenants.

entries.title: Staffing load vs. ticket complexity, top merchants benchmark
entries.question: For Marrowby & Vane and Studio Vrij, does their high breach rate look like a staffing shortfall (high tickets-per-agent) or inherently harder tickets (more back-and-forth, higher-priority mix), compared to other top merchants like Cragsley Outfitters?
entries.sql:
WITH target_tenants AS (
  SELECT id AS tenant_id, name AS tenant_name
  FROM tenants
  WHERE name IN ('Cragsley Outfitters','Marrowby & Vane','Studio Vrij','Brennquell Kaffee','Grind Collective','Petalcourt Beauty')
),
tickets_2025 AS (
  SELECT t.id, t.tenant_id, t.priority, t.created_at, t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN target_tenants tt ON tt.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
ticket_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
  FROM tickets_2025
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
message_counts AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, COUNT(tm.id) AS message_count
  FROM tickets_2025 t
  JOIN ticket_messages tm ON tm.ticket_id = t.id
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
),
agent_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS agent_count
  FROM support_agents
  WHERE tenant_id IN (SELECT tenant_id FROM target_tenants)
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
priority_counts AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN priority IN ('high','urgent') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_urgent_count
  FROM tickets_2025
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
resolution_stats AS (
  SELECT tenant_id,
    AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (resolved_at - created_at)) / 60.0) AS avg_resolution_minutes
  FROM tickets_2025
  WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
breach_counts AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT sb.ticket_id) AS breach_count
  FROM tickets_2025 t
  JOIN sla_breaches sb ON sb.ticket_id = t.id AND sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
)
SELECT
  tt.tenant_name,
  tc.ticket_count,
  COALESCE(ac.agent_count, 0) AS agent_count,
  ROUND(tc.ticket_count::numeric / NULLIF(ac.agent_count, 0), 1) AS tickets_per_agent,
  ROUND(COALESCE(mc.message_count, 0)::numeric / NULLIF(tc.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS avg_messages_per_ticket,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(pc.high_urgent_count, 0) / NULLIF(tc.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS pct_high_or_urgent_priority,
  ROUND(rs.avg_resolution_minutes, 1) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(bc.breach_count, 0) / NULLIF(tc.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM target_tenants tt
JOIN ticket_counts tc ON tc.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN agent_counts ac ON ac.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN message_counts mc ON mc.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN priority_counts pc ON pc.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN resolution_stats rs ON rs.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN breach_counts bc ON bc.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
ORDER BY resolution_breach_rate DESC, tt.tenant_name
builds_on: Ticket volume and SLA performance by merchant
Highest-volume merchant + agent-group units
entries.engineer_note: avg_resolution_minutes is computed only over tickets with a resolved_at timestamp (still-open tickets are excluded from that average but still count toward ticket_count, agent ratios and breach rate); agent_count is a simple distinct count of support_agents rows per tenant with no date filter, matching the stated "as used in last week's report" convention.

entries.title: Macro usage_count audit trail reconciliation
entries.question: Can we independently verify what macros.usage_count is actually counting, using the audit trail, before we repeat that number anywhere?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  tm.title AS macro_title,
  tm.usage_count AS current_usage_count,
  COALESCE(ch.event_count, 0) AS logged_update_event_count,
  ch.sum_increment AS sum_of_logged_increments,
  ch.first_update_at AS first_logged_update_at,
  ch.last_update_at AS last_logged_update_at,
  tm.created_at AS macro_created_at
FROM (
  SELECT id, title, usage_count, created_at
  FROM macros
  ORDER BY usage_count DESC, id
  LIMIT 5
) tm
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    entity_id,
    COUNT(*) AS event_count,
    SUM((after_data->>'usage_count')::numeric - (before_data->>'usage_count')::numeric) AS sum_increment,
    MIN(occurred_at) AS first_update_at,
    MAX(occurred_at) AS last_update_at
  FROM change_history
  WHERE entity_table = 'macros'
    AND 'usage_count' = ANY(changed_columns)
  GROUP BY entity_id
) ch ON ch.entity_id = tm.id
ORDER BY tm.usage_count DESC, tm.id
builds_on: Macro usage overview
entries.engineer_note: We don't have last week's report output stored to match macro ids against, so the 5 macros here are today's top 5 by macros.usage_count (tie-broken by id) rather than a literal re-identification of last week's rows — flag if that set needs to match exactly, we'd need the prior report's macro ids. Also note change_history is only filtered by entity_table='macros' and changed_columns containing 'usage_count' (no entity_schema filter was specified/available), and per-macro figures are null for logged_update_event_count fields if no matching change_history rows exist.
warnings: columns sum_of_logged_increments, first_logged_update_at, last_logged_update_at are mostly empty

entries.title: Ticket tag coverage: tagged vs. untagged volume and speed
entries.question: What share of 2025 tickets carry no topic tag at all, and do untagged tickets differ from tagged ones enough to change the topic/breach story from last week?
entries.sql:
WITH ticket_base AS (
    SELECT
        t0.id AS ticket_id,
        t0.created_at AS created_at,
        t0.resolved_at AS resolved_at,
        CASE
            WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ticket_tags_map t1 WHERE t1.ticket_id = t0.id)
            THEN 'Tagged'
            ELSE 'Untagged'
        END AS coverage_status
    FROM tickets t0
    WHERE t0.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND t0.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
counts AS (
    SELECT
        t2.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
        COUNT(*) AS ticket_count
    FROM ticket_base t2
    GROUP BY t2.coverage_status
),
grand_total AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_tickets
    FROM ticket_base t3
),
resolution_time AS (
    SELECT
        t4.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
        AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t4.resolved_at - t4.created_at)) / 60.0) AS avg_resolution_minutes
    FROM ticket_base t4
    WHERE t4.resolved_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY t4.coverage_status
),
resolution_breaches AS (
    SELECT
        t5.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
        COUNT(DISTINCT t6.ticket_id) AS resolution_breach_count
    FROM ticket_base t5
    JOIN sla_breaches t6
        ON t6.ticket_id = t5.ticket_id
        AND t6.breach_kind = 'resolution'
    GROUP BY t5.coverage_status
),
first_response_breaches AS (
    SELECT
        t7.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
        COUNT(DISTINCT t8.ticket_id) AS first_response_breach_count
    FROM ticket_base t7
    JOIN sla_breaches t8
        ON t8.ticket_id = t7.ticket_id
        AND t8.breach_kind = 'first_response'
    GROUP BY t7.coverage_status
)
SELECT
    t9.coverage_status AS coverage_status,
    t9.ticket_count AS ticket_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * t9.ticket_count / NULLIF(t10.total_tickets, 0), 1) AS pct_of_total_tickets,
    ROUND(COALESCE(t11.avg_resolution_minutes, 0), 0) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
    ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t12.resolution_breach_count, 0) / NULLIF(t9.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate,
    ROUND(100.0 * COALESCE(t13.first_response_breach_count, 0) / NULLIF(t9.ticket_count, 0), 1) AS first_response_breach_rate
FROM counts t9
CROSS JOIN grand_total t10
LEFT JOIN resolution_time t11 ON t11.coverage_status = t9.coverage_status
LEFT JOIN resolution_breaches t12 ON t12.coverage_status = t9.coverage_status
LEFT JOIN first_response_breaches t13 ON t13.coverage_status = t9.coverage_status
ORDER BY
    CASE WHEN t9.coverage_status = 'Tagged' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
    t9.coverage_status
builds_on: Ticket volume and speed by topic tag
entries.engineer_note: avg_resolution_minutes is computed only over tickets with a non-null resolved_at (unresolved tickets have no resolution duration); breach rates are the share of each status's tickets with at least one sla_breaches row of that kind.

entries.title: Topic mix and resolution time by tag, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
entries.question: Is Marrowby & Vane's and Studio Vrij's slowness concentrated in specific topics (especially delivery-related ones), or uniformly slow across all topics, compared to Cragsley Outfitters?
entries.sql:
WITH tenant_filter AS (
  SELECT id, name FROM tenants WHERE name IN ('Marrowby & Vane','Studio Vrij','Cragsley Outfitters')
),
ticket_tags AS (
  SELECT t.id AS ticket_id, t.tenant_id, t.created_at, t.resolved_at, st.name AS tag_name
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN ticket_tags_map ttm ON ttm.ticket_id = t.id
  JOIN support_tags st ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id
  JOIN tenant_filter tf ON tf.id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
tenant_totals AS (
  SELECT t.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_tickets
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN tenant_filter tf ON tf.id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY t.tenant_id
),
breaches AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ticket_id FROM sla_breaches WHERE breach_kind = 'resolution'
)
SELECT
  tf.name AS tenant_name,
  tt.tag_name,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / tot.total_tickets, 1) AS pct_of_tenant_tickets,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN tt.resolved_at IS NOT NULL THEN EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tt.resolved_at - tt.created_at)) / 60.0 END)) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN b.ticket_id IS NOT NULL THEN tt.ticket_id END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM ticket_tags tt
JOIN tenant_filter tf ON tf.id = tt.tenant_id
JOIN tenant_totals tot ON tot.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN breaches b ON b.ticket_id = tt.ticket_id
GROUP BY tf.name, tt.tag_name, tot.total_tickets
ORDER BY tf.name, ticket_count DESC, tt.tag_name
builds_on: Staffing load vs. ticket complexity, top merchants benchmark
Ticket volume and speed by topic tag
entries.engineer_note: avg_resolution_minutes is computed only over tickets with a non-null resolved_at (unresolved tickets in the 2025 window are excluded from that average but still counted in ticket_count and the breach-rate denominator); resolution_breach_rate = share of each (tenant, tag) ticket group with at least one sla_breaches row of breach_kind='resolution'. pct_of_tenant_tickets can sum to over 100% per tenant since a ticket may carry multiple tags.

entries.title: Where the delay accumulates: first-response lag vs. post-response handling time
entries.question: For Marrowby & Vane, Studio Vrij, and Cragsley Outfitters, does the slowness happen before an agent first replies (pickup delay) or after the first reply, while the ticket is still being worked (handling/back-and-forth delay)?
entries.sql:
select
  t.name as tenant_name,
  count(*) as ticket_count,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (tk.first_response_at - tk.created_at))/60)::numeric) as avg_first_response_minutes,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (tk.resolved_at - tk.first_response_at))/60)::numeric) as avg_post_response_minutes,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (tk.resolved_at - tk.created_at))/60)::numeric) as avg_resolution_minutes
from tickets tk
join tenants t on t.id = tk.tenant_id
where t.name in ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij', 'Cragsley Outfitters')
  and tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
  and tk.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
  and tk.first_response_at is not null
  and tk.resolved_at is not null
group by t.name
order by avg_post_response_minutes desc, tenant_name
builds_on: Staffing load vs. ticket complexity, top merchants benchmark
entries.engineer_note: Used tenant_id filtering via tenants.name match to the three named merchants; created_at upper bound is exclusive of 2026-01-01 to cover all of 2025-12-31 per the stated window.

entries.title: Monthly ticket volume vs. knowledge-base engagement trend
entries.question: Is there any visible relationship between how much customers engage with the knowledge base and how many tickets we get — even a rough, non-causal signal?
entries.sql:
SELECT m.month_label,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets t WHERE t.created_at >= m.month_start AND t.created_at < m.month_end) AS ticket_count,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM page_views pv WHERE pv.viewed_at >= m.month_start AND pv.viewed_at < m.month_end AND (pv.path ILIKE '%/help%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/kb%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%knowledge%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/faq%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/support%')) AS kb_engagement_count,
       'page_views.path ILIKE any of %/help%, %/kb%, %knowledge%, %/faq%, %/support% (best-guess pattern)' AS kb_engagement_signal_used
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start, (month_start + INTERVAL '1 month') AS month_end
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND calendar_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
) m
ORDER BY m.month_label ASC
entries.engineer_note: My tooling only lets me validate SQL against an empty schema (dry_run never returns real rows/values), so I could not actually inspect which event_name or path values exist in this warehouse before writing the query. I picked page_views.path with a broad set of help/kb/faq/support/knowledge substring patterns as the most plausible, commonly-used signal, aggregated per calendar month via calendar_days; if these patterns don't match real data, kb_engagement_count will read as 0 rather than NULL, so please sanity-check the first few months before circulating and let me know if the events table turns out to have a better-named view event instead.

entries.title: Carrier mix and on-time delivery performance, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
entries.question: Do Marrowby & Vane and Studio Vrij rely on a slower or less reliable carrier than Cragsley Outfitters, which would explain their outsized delivery/where-is-my-order ticket resolution times?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  t.name AS tenant_name,
  s.carrier,
  count(*) AS shipment_count,
  round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) over (partition by t.name), 1) AS pct_of_tenant_shipments,
  round(avg(extract(epoch from (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at)) / 86400.0) filter (where s.delivered_at is not null and s.shipped_at is not null), 1) AS avg_delivery_days,
  round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where s.delivered_at is not null and s.shipped_at is not null and s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at <= interval '3 days')
        / nullif(count(*) filter (where s.delivered_at is not null and s.shipped_at is not null), 0), 1) AS pct_delivered_within_3_days
FROM shipments s
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = s.tenant_id
WHERE t.name IN ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij', 'Cragsley Outfitters')
  AND s.shipped_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
  AND s.shipped_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY t.name, s.carrier
ORDER BY t.name, shipment_count DESC
builds_on: Topic mix and resolution time by tag, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
Where the delay accumulates: first-response lag vs. post-response handling time
entries.engineer_note: pct_of_tenant_shipments is based on all 2025 shipments for the tenant (any delivery status); avg_delivery_days and pct_delivered_within_3_days are computed only over the subset of shipments with both shipped_at and delivered_at populated, as requested.

entries.title: Monthly delivery-topic ticket volume and speed, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
entries.question: Did the delivery/where-is-my-order slowness at Marrowby & Vane and Studio Vrij spike in a specific period (e.g. November-December, matching a known carrier breakdown) or run elevated all year?
entries.sql:
WITH tagged_tickets AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t.id AS ticket_id, t.tenant_id, t.created_at, t.resolved_at
  FROM tickets t
  JOIN ticket_tags_map ttm ON ttm.ticket_id = t.id AND ttm.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  JOIN support_tags st ON st.id = ttm.support_tag_id AND st.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
  JOIN tenants te ON te.id = t.tenant_id
  WHERE te.name IN ('Marrowby & Vane','Studio Vrij','Cragsley Outfitters')
    AND st.name IN ('delivery','where-is-my-order')
    AND t.created_at >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND t.created_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
breaches AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ticket_id FROM sla_breaches WHERE breach_kind = 'resolution'
)
SELECT
  te.name AS tenant_name,
  strftime(date_trunc('month', tt.created_at), '%Y-%m') AS month_label,
  COUNT(*) AS ticket_count,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (tt.resolved_at - tt.created_at))/60) FILTER (WHERE tt.resolved_at IS NOT NULL)) AS avg_resolution_minutes,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.ticket_id IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*), 1) AS resolution_breach_rate
FROM tagged_tickets tt
JOIN tenants te ON te.id = tt.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN breaches b ON b.ticket_id = tt.ticket_id
GROUP BY te.name, date_trunc('month', tt.created_at)
ORDER BY te.name, month_label
builds_on: Topic mix and resolution time by tag, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
entries.engineer_note: avg_resolution_minutes is computed only over tickets that have a resolved_at timestamp (unresolved tickets in a month are excluded from that average but still counted in ticket_count and the breach-rate denominator); resolution_breach_rate is the share of that month's tagged tickets with at least one sla_breaches row of breach_kind='resolution'.

entries.title: Event name inventory for knowledge-base engagement signal
entries.question: Which event_name values in the events table actually correspond to a customer viewing a knowledge-base/help article, so we can build a trustworthy KB-engagement metric next week instead of guessing?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  event_name,
  COUNT(*) AS event_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS distinct_user_count
FROM events
WHERE occurred_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
  AND occurred_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY event_name
ORDER BY event_count DESC, event_name ASC
LIMIT 30
builds_on: Monthly ticket volume vs. knowledge-base engagement trend
entries.engineer_note: Platform-wide, unfiltered inventory of all distinct event_name values in 2025 with their counts, as requested, so the analyst can visually identify KB/article/help-view events; the printed report will show the total distinct event_name count alongside the top-30 rows.

entries.title: Albion Parcel monthly on-time performance at Marrowby & Vane
entries.question: Did Albion Parcel's on-time performance at Marrowby & Vane specifically collapse in November-December 2025, and has it recovered by year end?
entries.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    s.id,
    s.shipped_at,
    s.delivered_at,
    strftime(s.shipped_at, '%Y-%m') AS month_label
  FROM shipments s
  JOIN tenants t ON t.id = s.tenant_id
  WHERE t.name = 'Marrowby & Vane'
    AND s.carrier = 'Albion Parcel'
    AND s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
    AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
),
monthly_shipment_counts AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    COUNT(*) AS shipment_count
  FROM base
  GROUP BY month_label
),
delivered_base AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (delivered_at - shipped_at)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days
  FROM base
  WHERE shipped_at IS NOT NULL
    AND delivered_at IS NOT NULL
),
monthly_delivery_stats AS (
  SELECT
    month_label,
    ROUND(AVG(delivery_days)::numeric, 1) AS avg_delivery_days,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_days <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_delivered_within_3_days
  FROM delivered_base
  GROUP BY month_label
)
SELECT
  c.month_label,
  c.shipment_count,
  d.avg_delivery_days,
  d.pct_delivered_within_3_days
FROM monthly_shipment_counts c
LEFT JOIN monthly_delivery_stats d ON c.month_label = d.month_label
ORDER BY c.month_label ASC
builds_on: Carrier mix and on-time delivery performance, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
Monthly delivery-topic ticket volume and speed, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
entries.engineer_note: Shipment counts include all shipped-in-month shipments for Marrowby & Vane / Albion Parcel; avg_delivery_days and pct_delivered_within_3_days are computed only over the subset with both shipped_at and delivered_at populated, so months with no delivered shipments will show null for those two metrics.

entries.title: Studio Vrij carrier performance by month, May-July focus
entries.question: Which of Studio Vrij's carriers caused the May-July 2025 delivery breakdown, and did its performance fully recover afterward?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  s.carrier AS carrier,
  cd.month_label AS month_label,
  COUNT(*) AS shipment_count,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at)) / 86400.0) FILTER (WHERE s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL), 1) AS avg_delivery_days,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND s.delivered_at - s.shipped_at <= INTERVAL '3 days')
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.delivered_at IS NOT NULL), 0), 1) AS pct_delivered_within_3_days
FROM shipments s
JOIN fulfillments f ON f.id = s.fulfillment_id
JOIN orders o ON o.id = f.order_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
JOIN calendar_days cd ON cd.calendar_date = CAST(s.shipped_at AS date)
WHERE t.name = 'Studio Vrij'
  AND s.carrier IN ('Lowlands Express', 'Polder Post')
  AND s.shipped_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND s.shipped_at < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY s.carrier, cd.month_label
ORDER BY s.carrier, cd.month_label
builds_on: Carrier mix and on-time delivery performance, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
Monthly delivery-topic ticket volume and speed, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
entries.engineer_note: shipment_count reflects all shipments shipped that month for the carrier; avg_delivery_days and pct_delivered_within_3_days are computed only over the subset of those with a non-null delivered_at, as requested. Rows span all 12 months of 2025 (not just May-July) so the analyst can see the before/during/after pattern.

entries.title: Ticket performance with known carrier-incident months excluded
entries.question: Once we strip out the known carrier-incident months, do Marrowby & Vane and Studio Vrij still look worse than Cragsley Outfitters, or does that fully explain the gap?
entries.sql:
SELECT
  tenant_name,
  excluded_period,
  ticket_count_after_exclusion,
  avg_resolution_minutes_after_exclusion,
  resolution_breach_rate_after_exclusion
FROM (
  SELECT
    ft.tenant_name,
    ft.excluded_period,
    count(*) AS ticket_count_after_exclusion,
    round(avg(extract(epoch from (ft.resolved_at - ft.created_at)) / 60.0)) AS avg_resolution_minutes_after_exclusion,
    round(
      100.0 * sum(
        case when exists (
          select 1 from sla_breaches sb
          where sb.ticket_id = ft.ticket_id and sb.breach_kind = 'resolution'
        ) then 1 else 0 end
      ) / count(*),
      1
    ) AS resolution_breach_rate_after_exclusion
  FROM (
    SELECT
      tk.id as ticket_id,
      t.name as tenant_name,
      case
        when t.name = 'Marrowby & Vane' then 'Excludes Nov-Dec 2025'
        when t.name = 'Studio Vrij' then 'Excludes May-Jul 2025'
        else 'None'
      end as excluded_period,
      tk.created_at,
      tk.resolved_at
    FROM tickets tk
    JOIN tenants t ON t.id = tk.tenant_id
    WHERE t.name IN ('Marrowby & Vane', 'Studio Vrij', 'Cragsley Outfitters')
      AND tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-01-01'
      AND tk.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01'
      AND NOT (
        (t.name = 'Marrowby & Vane' AND tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-11-01' AND tk.created_at < timestamp '2026-01-01')
        OR
        (t.name = 'Studio Vrij' AND tk.created_at >= timestamp '2025-05-01' AND tk.created_at < timestamp '2025-08-01')
      )
  ) ft
  GROUP BY ft.tenant_name, ft.excluded_period
) x
ORDER BY resolution_breach_rate_after_exclusion DESC, tenant_name
builds_on: Monthly delivery-topic ticket volume and speed, flagged merchants vs. Cragsley
Staffing load vs. ticket complexity, top merchants benchmark
entries.engineer_note: avg_resolution_minutes_after_exclusion is averaged only over tickets with a non-null resolved_at (unresolved tickets have no resolution time to measure); resolution_breach_rate_after_exclusion is the share of all tickets in the filtered window (resolved or not) that have a sla_breaches row with breach_kind='resolution'.
